title: F-S2.04: TrainConfigS2Full + TrainConfigS2PhaseAOnly + train_config_hash + PhaseAEffectiveConfigHash
description:
Goal
====
Implement TrainConfigS2Full + TrainConfigS2PhaseAOnly + the train_config_hash
and PhaseAEffectiveConfigHash surfaces, including the full Rep-S2-4 hash
field set. Per F-S2 RFC §5 + §10.

Why this matters
================
Reproducibility (Rep-S2-1 byte-equality at every phase boundary) requires
that EVERY field that can perturb training is hashed. The Rep-S2-4 rule
binds D1+D3+D5+D10+D13 plus the loss-unit choice from §1. Splitting
TrainConfigS2 into Full vs PhaseAOnly avoids the ablation-vs-full ambiguity
that would otherwise pollute I-S2-5 (H4 wants the Phase-A-effective hash,
not the full A→D plan).

Scope
=====
Types (in gbf-experiments::s2::schema):

  struct TrainConfigS2Full {
    optimizer_steps: u32 = 10000          // S1 inheritance
    batch_size: u32 = 32
    sequence_length: u32 = 128
    eval_every_steps: u32 = 1000
    eval_subset_size: u32 = 4096
    optimizer: AdamWConfig (lr=1e-3 etc., S1 D10/D13)
    phase_plan: [PhaseA(1..=4000), PhaseB(4001..=5000),
                 PhaseC(5001..=8000), PhaseD(8001..=10000)]
    hardness_ramp: PhaseCRampD2 + PhaseDRampD2
    distill_temp: f32 = 2.0
    lambda_distill_default: f32 = 1.0
    lambda_range: f32 = 0.01
    lambda_zero: f32 = 0.0001
    range_safe_lo: f32 = -1.0
    range_safe_hi: f32 = 1.0
    threshold_init_multiplier: f32 = 0.7
    teacher_freeze_step: u64 = 4000
    rng_kind: Pcg64Mcg
    device_profile: S1CpuDeterministic
    training_loss_unit: nats              // RFC §1; the explicit unit pin
  }

  struct TrainConfigS2PhaseAOnly {
    optimizer_steps: u32 = 4000           // ablation budget
    batch_size, sequence_length, eval_*, optimizer, rng_kind,
    device_profile: same as Full (default S1 values)
    phase_plan: [PhaseA(1..=4000)]
    // no hardness ramp; no distill temp; no thresholds
  }

  type alias TrainConfigHash = Hash256
  fn train_config_hash(cfg: &TrainConfigS2Full | &TrainConfigS2PhaseAOnly,
                      build_kind: S2BuildKind) -> Hash256
    // domain separator "s2_train_config.v1/<build_kind>"
    // includes build_kind-specific overrides (e.g. nodistill sets
    // lambda_distill_default = 0.0 inside the hashed config)

  type alias PhaseAEffectiveConfigHash = Hash256
  fn phase_a_effective_config_hash(cfg: TrainConfigS2Full | TrainConfigS2PhaseAOnly)
    -> PhaseAEffectiveConfigHash
    // domain separator "s2_phase_a_effective.v1"
    // covers ONLY optimizer hyperparameters + batch/seq/eval + rng
    // streams + model_config + corpus hashes + device_profile + PhaseA
    // boundary. Excludes any Phase B/C/D fields. Used ONLY for H4
    // ablation comparator. Full-run reproducibility uses
    // train_config_hash, not this.

Acceptance
==========
- Both TrainConfigS2Full and TrainConfigS2PhaseAOnly serialize via
  S1CanonicalJson and round-trip byte-equal.
- train_config_hash is deterministic across replays and includes EVERY
  field in Rep-S2-4: phase_plan, hardness_ramp_id, distill_temp,
  lambda_distill_default, lambda_range, lambda_zero, range_safe_lo,
  range_safe_hi, threshold_init_multiplier, teacher_freeze_step,
  build_kind overrides, and the phase-effective lambda table.
- PhaseAEffectiveConfigHash explicitly excludes Phase B/C/D plan/ramp/lambda
  fields. Unit test: changing lambda_distill_default in TrainConfigS2Full
  does NOT change PhaseAEffectiveConfigHash but DOES change
  train_config_hash.
- training_loss_unit pin field exists and is set to "nats" by default;
  changing it bumps train_config_hash.

Considerations
==============
- Rep-S2-5 requires bumping pass_version_S2 if any train_config field
  semantics change. This bead does not bump pass_version_S2; that happens
  at first result artifact commit (RFC §10).
- range_safe_lo/range_safe_hi MUST appear in the hash even though they are
  consumed only when lambda_range_effective > 0 (RFC §2 / Rep-S2-4).
- Do NOT include generated_at, host_clock, env vars not in env_exact, or
  any other ephemera in the hash (Rep-S2-8 + O8).

References
==========
F-S2 RFC §5 Run protocol, §10 Reproducibility laws (Rep-S2-4, Rep-S2-5,
Rep-S2-8), §13 O8 No hidden inputs.
Depends on: F-S2.02 (types).
close_reason: Merged into bd-zaoh (F-S2.02 — TrainConfigS2)

title: CI feature matrix: replace --all-features with explicit closure combos; add s5_feature_matrix_check.sh
description:
# Goal

Replace the --all-features CI invocations in §16 and §18.10 with explicit closure feature combinations that respect the workspace's feature mutual-exclusion rules, and add a feature-matrix script that iterates the legal combinations.

# Background / Why

The F-S5 feature contract has at least two mutual-exclusion sets:

  - s5-default XOR s5-no-log (logging on/off)
  - s5-falsify-* are pairwise mutually exclusive (only one falsifier active per build)

Using --all-features enables every flag, which either (a) violates the mutual-exclusion guards (compile-error if the guards work, silent inconsistency if they do not), or (b) builds a code path no real closure run uses, defeating the purpose of CI gating.

# Change

In .github/workflows/ci.yml (or scripts/ci-pre-commit) + scripts/:

  - Replace:
      cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings
      cargo test   --workspace --all-features
    with:
      cargo clippy --workspace --features \"s5-default,qat,burn-adapter\" -- -D warnings
      cargo test   --workspace --features \"s5-default,qat,burn-adapter\"
      scripts/s5_feature_matrix_check.sh
  - Update both occurrences (§16 closure CI gates and §18.10 closure-block list).
  - New script: scripts/s5_feature_matrix_check.sh iterates the legal feature combinations one at a time:
      - { s5-default, qat, burn-adapter }
      - { s5-no-log, qat, burn-adapter }
      - { s5-default, qat, burn-adapter, s5-falsify-N } for N in 1..15 (sample-mode: not all together)
    For each, runs cargo build / test selectively.

# Why this matters

CI is the only mechanical gate that says \"this feature combination builds and passes its targeted tests\". The current --all-features setup either silently fails (no enforcement) or breaks the build whenever a real reviewer turns on a falsifier. The matrix script makes feature combinations explicit and reviewable.

# Considerations

  - Matrix runtime: 15 falsifier variants plus base = 17 cargo build cycles per CI run; bound CPU budget by selecting a representative subset on PR runs and the full matrix nightly.
  - Document the legal combinations in scripts/README.md so future contributors know which flags can coexist.

# Verification

  - Script exits 0 on a clean tree.
  - Manually enabling two mutually-exclusive features (e.g. s5-falsify-13 + s5-falsify-14) fails to compile.
  - Coverage report: every closure feature is exercised by some matrix row.

# Related RFC sections

  §16 CI gates, §18.10 closure-block list, feature matrix table.

# Depends on

  B21 (D14 logging baseline command must match what CI invokes).
close_reason: Completed bd-14sn. Gemini and Claude ACPX reviews both PASS. Verification cited by reviewers: scripts/tests/s5_feature_matrix_check_test.sh; scripts/s5_feature_matrix_check.sh --dry-run/--sample. Live producer falsifier execution remains follow-up bd-q3zo, not claimed here.

title: F-S2.19: s2_report.v1 emitter + R-S2-* validators + O1 preregistration check script
description:
Goal
====
Implement the s2_report.v1 emitter (writes docs/experiments/S2-report.md
with YAML front-matter + markdown body, populates every required field,
enforces R-S2-* validators) AND the operational
scripts/s2_preregistration_check.sh that enforces O1 (predictions_section_
hash + strict-ancestor + first_result_commit non-null result rule).
Per F-S2 RFC §9.9 + §10 + §13 O1 + §16.8.

Why this matters
================
- s2_report.v1 is the artifact bd-1xqf closes against. A clean report
  with all R-S2 validators passing + Decision in {ProceedToS3,
  ProceedToS3WithDistillReview} is the necessary AND sufficient condition
  for S2 closure.
- Pre-registration is the load-bearing scientific commitment: predictions
  must exist in git history BEFORE any result artifact, with no edits
  after.

Scope
=====
Report emitter (gbf-experiments::s2::report):
- struct ReportInputs (gathers verifier records, per-seed artifacts,
  falsification suite, oracle re-run, api drift, predictions linkage).
- fn emit_s2_report(inputs) -> Result<EmittedReport, _>:
    1. dispatch outcome (F-S2.18) + decide (F-S2.18).
    2. Construct YAML front-matter per F-S2.08 schema.
    3. Render body sections (Pre-registered predictions / Observed /
       Hypothesis verdicts / Falsification analysis / Surprises /
       Decision / Reproducibility statement).
    4. Compute report_self_hash via R-S2-Self-Hash construction:
         a. parsed YAML front-matter through S1CanonicalJson
            (generated_at + report_self_hash omitted);
         b. domain separator 's2_report.v1/frontmatter+body';
         c. markdown body bytes exactly as committed.
    5. Run validators R-S2-Decision / R-S2-AllSeeds /
       R-S2-ClosureArtifacts / R-S2-Self-Hash / R-S2-Predictions /
       R-S2-AllHypotheses.
    6. Write file.

scripts/s2_preregistration_check.sh (O1):
- Inputs: predictions_commit, first_result_commit.
- Step 1: extract '## Pre-registered predictions' section at
  predictions_commit; normalize; sha256; compare predictions_section_hash.
- Step 2: git merge-base --is-ancestor predictions_commit
  first_result_commit (STRICT, equal is rejected).
- Step 3: scan every commit in predictions_commit..HEAD; check whether
  it introduces any non-null S2 result artifact self-hash / completed
  run-product / score / verdict.
- Bash strict mode (set -euo pipefail); structured JSON output to
  /tmp/s2-prereg.json (consumed by F-S2.21 workflow).

Logging contract
================
Report emitter:
  INFO at emit entry:
    event="report_emit_start" outcome=<S2Outcome>
      decision=<Decision> per_seed_artifact_count=<u32>
  DEBUG per R-S2 validator:
    event="r_s2_validator_run" id=<&str> passed=<bool>
      remediation=<&str|null>
  INFO at write completion:
    event="report_written" path=<Path> report_self_hash=<hex>
      file_size_bytes=<u64>
  ERROR per validator failure:
    event="r_s2_validator_failed" id=<&str> diagnostic=<json>

Prereg script (emits to stderr as JSON lines; also writes
/tmp/s2-prereg.json):
  event="prereg_stage_start" stage=1 description="extract section + hash"
  event="prereg_section_hash_compare" expected=<hex> observed=<hex>
    matches=<bool>
  event="prereg_stage_start" stage=2 description="strict ancestor check"
  event="prereg_ancestor_check" predictions_commit=<sha>
    first_result_commit=<sha> is_strict_ancestor=<bool>
  event="prereg_stage_start" stage=3 description="non-null result scan"
  event="prereg_commit_scanned" commit=<sha>
    introduces_non_null_result=<bool>
  event="prereg_done" passed=<bool> exit_code=<i32>
  ERROR on violation: event="prereg_violation" stage=<u32>
    detail=<&str>

Unit tests
==========
- File: gbf-experiments/tests/report_emitter_s2.rs
  Scenarios:
    * Clean inputs (all verifiers pass) → emit produces report with
      Decision = ProceedToS3, all R-S2 validators pass.
    * Bundle missing one nodistill checkpoint → R-S2-ClosureArtifacts
      fails with remediation pointing to per_seed_artifacts shape.
    * Re-emitting with same inputs → byte-identical file modulo
      generated_at.
    * Reordering YAML keys (via different serializer) → identical
      report_self_hash.
    * R-S2-Self-Hash: changing generated_at does NOT change hash;
      changing any other front-matter field DOES change hash.

- File: gbf-experiments/tests/preregistration_check_s2.rs (shell-out
  test):
    Uses assert_cmd to invoke scripts/s2_preregistration_check.sh
    against fixture git histories created in tempdir:
    * Clean history (prereg → result) → exit 0.
    * Editing prereg in a later commit → exit 1 (Step 1 mismatch).
    * Earlier result commit not equal to recorded first_result_commit
      → exit 1 (Step 3).
    * Schema-template commit between prereg and result → correctly
      NOT classified as result.

Golden artifacts (insta):
  tests/snapshots/report_emitter__pass_clean.snap (full markdown body)
  tests/snapshots/report_emitter__pass_with_distill_warn.snap
  tests/snapshots/preregistration__clean_history_output.snap

E2E verification
================
- gbf s2 report (F-S2.20) calls emit_s2_report.
- scripts/s2_preregistration_check.sh wraps the prereg validator.
- integration_s2 (F-S2.22) generates a report from synthetic verifier
  records on the tiny fixture and asserts it matches the
  pass_clean golden snapshot.
- Structured log assertion: exactly one event="report_written" per
  closure attempt.

Considerations
==============
- R-S2-Predictions strict-ancestor enforcement is OPERATIONALLY enforced
  by the prereg script; the CONTRACT is in F-S2.08.
- Reproducibility statement body template populated from ReportInputs
  (pass_version_S2 / corpus shas / manifest references).

References
==========
F-S2 RFC §9.9 s2_report.v1, §10 R-S2-*, §13 O1, §15.4 replay commands,
§16.8.
Inherits from F-S1 closed beads: bd-1261 (S1-report.md emitter pattern),
bd-3cpl (F-S1.21 preregistration check script pattern).
Merges (former separate beads): F-S2.43 (emitter) + F-S2.44 (prereg
script).

comments.text:
## Epic A: M0 Foundation Stack

### What this is

This epic is the **M0 milestone** from `history/planv0.md` §"What I would build first" (line 2468). It is the foundation under everything: the assembly eDSL, the hardware contract, the live-execution ABI, the bank-write ABI, the Bank0 cooperative runtime skeleton, and the content-addressed storage / migration infrastructure.

Without M0, none of M1–M6 can begin. The Training-Contract Revision Pass (epic `bd-1rb`) decomposed the **training side** into ~75 beads. M0 is the equivalent decomposition for **the foundation that the compiler, runtime, oracle, and bench all build on top of**.

### Why this matters (overarching project goals)

GBLLM compiles a quantized MoE language model into a Game Boy ROM that executes cooperatively alongside a UI. The five cooperating products from `planv0.md` (training, artifact boundary, oracles, compiler, runtime) all share three contracts: `gbf-hw` (target contract), `gbf-artifact` (durable model contract), `gbf-abi` (live execution contract). M0 produces those three contracts in usable form **plus** the assembly eDSL that is the only legal authoring layer for executable code, **plus** the runtime nucleus that everything else schedules onto.

Every architectural invariant in the plan eventually grounds out in M0:

- "All executable code originates from `AsmIR`" → requires `gbf-asm` to exist (F-A1).
- "ISR code/data is Bank0-resident, proven by `ReachabilityValidation`" → requires `MachineEffect` / `PrivilegeClass` typing in AsmIR (F-A1) plus the Bank0 nucleus modules (F-A5).
- "The `BankLease`/`BankGuard` ABI is the only legal path to MBC writes" → requires F-A4.
- "The runtime is a cooperative kernel centered on Bank0" → requires F-A5.
- "Every build is content-addressed and lazy-loadable" → requires F-A6 (`gbf-store`).

### Scope

Six features:

- **F-A1 — `gbf-asm`**: typed LR35902 eDSL, ISA shapes, `MachineEffect`/`PrivilegeClass`, builder, cycle model, layout/relax, encoder, listing, ROM builder.
- **F-A2 — `gbf-hw`**: `TargetProfile`, verified DMG/MBC5 memory map, MBC5 register semantics, LCD/timing/interrupt constants, joypad, calibration schema (types, not data).
- **F-A3 — `gbf-abi`**: live-execution `#[repr(C)]` types — `AbiVersion`, `InferenceState` with liveness, harness command/result blocks, faults, interrupts, `ResourceLease`, semantic-checkpoint ids, trace events.
- **F-A4 — `BankLease`/`BankGuard` ABI**: the sole legal path to MBC writes, with HRAM bank shadow registers and interrupt-safe acquire/release primitives.
- **F-A5 — Bank0 cooperative runtime skeleton**: boot + IRQ vectors, scheduler with TIMA-armed deadline yielding, joypad, text renderer, keyboard, `video_commit` queue with `UiCommitPlan`, panic screen.
- **F-A6 — `gbf-store` + `gbf-migrate`**: content-addressed blob store, two-level `StageCache`, pinsets/GC, archive transport, host-side migration DAGs.

### What is **not** in scope (deferred to other epics)

- The compiler IR pipeline (Stages 1–12) → Epic B.
- The three oracles (`DenotationalOracle`, `ArtifactOracle`, `ScheduleOracle`) → Epic C.
- The runtime persistence protocol, harness control plane, drift monitor, fault-policy table, `SchedulePack` mode switching → Epic D.
- Calibration *bundle production* (the schema is here in F-A2; producing real bundles is Epic E).
- Build reports, certificates, slow reference impls → Epic F.
- Corpus / lexical / decode pipelines → Epic G.
- Kernel families, emulator adapters → Epic H.

### Decomposition rationale

Why six features and not one giant blob?

- Each feature corresponds to a single crate (or one tightly coupled pair) in `gbf-foundation`/`gbf-asm`/`gbf-hw`/`gbf-abi`/`gbf-runtime`/`gbf-store`+`gbf-migrate`. That makes PR review and test isolation natural.
- Crate boundaries are already drawn by `bd-1bi` (T0.1) which scaffolded the workspace. Every module file currently exists as `//! Module stub.` — these features fill them in.
- The features have a real DAG (F-A1, F-A2, F-A3, F-A6 are independent; F-A4 needs F-A1 + F-A2; F-A5 needs everything earlier). That parallelism matters for staffing this work.

### Critical-path analysis

```
F-A1 (asm) ─────────────────────────────┐
F-A2 (hw) ──────────────────┐           │
F-A3 (abi)                  ├─→ F-A4 ───┤
F-A6 (store/migrate)        │           ├─→ F-A5 (Bank0 runtime)
                            │           │
                       (mbc5 + memory)  │
                                  (BankLease + InterruptPolicy + AsmIR)
```

The longest path is F-A1 + F-A2 → F-A4 → F-A5. F-A3 and F-A6 can land independently.

### Milestone DoD (when this epic is done)

All six features complete AND:

```bash
cargo test --workspace                                    # Everything green
cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings                   # Clean
cargo run -p gbf-cli -- demo-bank0-rom                    # A bring-up ROM exists
```

The bring-up ROM:
1. Boots on a real DMG/MBC5 emulator (SameBoy or BGB).
2. Shows a text screen and keyboard prompt rendered from `gbf-runtime::text` + `keyboard`.
3. Cooperatively yields per the `gbf-runtime::scheduler` + TIMA deadline ABI.
4. Performs at least one bank switch through `BankLease` and one safe-mode panic via `gbf-runtime::panic`.
5. Has a `runtime_nucleus_hash` consistent with the `RuntimeChromeBudget` pinned in the synthetic reference budget (T2.6, `bd-ros`).

That ROM is what M1 (oracles) and M2 (first scheduled inference) build against.

### How this connects to existing beads

- **T0.1 (`bd-1bi`)**, **T0.2 (`bd-yb3`)**, **T0.3 (`bd-1z3`)** are CLOSED and provide the workspace + pre-commit + foundation types this epic builds on.
- **F2 (`bd-1hv`)** `RuntimeChromeBudget` and its children (T2.1–T2.7) consume **F-A2** (`TargetProfileId`, memory map) and **F-A3** (`runtime_nucleus_hash` provenance), and the synthetic reference budget (T2.6, `bd-ros`) is what F-A5's bring-up ROM hash-pins against.
- **F11 (`bd-1i8`)** `CompileProfile + WRAM Layout` defines the `BringUp` profile (T11.2, `bd-ymo`) that the F-A5 runtime imports for WRAM layout constants.
- **F12 (`bd-144`)** `Dual-Path Sequence-State Experimentation` does not depend on M0 directly but its M2 implementation will run on M0's runtime.

### Constitution checkpoints (epic-level)

- **§I.1 Correctness by Construction**: every module here lands typed and exhaustive — no opaque numbers, no untyped MBC writes, no untyped ABI.
- **§II.1 Latency is Tech Debt**: the feature set is sized so a developer can implement one feature per week and still keep the workspace test suite under 2 minutes.
- **§III.1 Compiler-first**: most M0 invariants are **types + tests**. Runtime/encoder bugs surface as failing `cargo test`, not field debugging.
- **§IV.3 Reproducible Builds**: `gbf-store` (F-A6) is content-addressed; `gbf-asm` encoder (F-A1) is bit-stable.
- **§VI.1 Single Source of Truth**: `gbf-hw` is the *only* place hardware constants live. `gbf-asm` is the *only* authoring layer for executable code. `gbf-abi` is the *only* live-execution contract.

### Confidence: HIGH on shape, MEDIUM on Bank0 runtime sizing

The plan specifies F-A1, F-A2, F-A3, F-A4, F-A6 quite tightly — they're mostly schema/types/encoder work. F-A5 (Bank0 nucleus) involves real cooperative-runtime engineering on a constrained 16 KiB Bank 0; the byte budget is tight and may force a second pass. The reference shell module set (Boot, Interrupts, Scheduler, Banking, Joypad, Text, Keyboard, VideoCommit — pinned in T2.4 `bd-37r`) anchors the F-A5 sizing constraint.

### Future-self note

If you (later me) are wondering "why not skip M0 and start at M1 with a stub runtime?": because M1 oracles need a *real* `gbf-abi`, M2 `RomWindowPlan` needs *real* MBC5 register semantics from `gbf-hw`, and the very first compiled ROM needs `gbf-asm`'s encoder. Cutting M0 corners shows up as silent contract drift between the compiler and the runtime later — exactly the failure mode planv0.md was written to prevent (`runtime_nucleus_hash` exists for this reason).

The thirty-eight tasks below are sized so each is one focused PR. Pick them in dependency order with `br ready`.

## M0 scope expanded (2026-04-30): gbf-emu and gbf-debug move into Epic A

### What changed in the plan

`history/planv0.md` was revised. Two new pieces are now M0 deliverables (line 2901):

> **M0**: `gbf-asm`, encoder, symbol map, ROM builder; `gbf-hw` target profiles + calibration schema; `gbf-abi` skeleton (including liveness fields); Bank0 UI/runtime skeleton with VBlank, keyboard, text output, video commit queue, cooperative scheduler, and `BankLease`/`BankGuard` ABI; **`gbf-emu` gameroy adapter with deterministic execution policy and breakpoint/watchpoint primitives; `gbf-debug` session file format and rquickjs-scripted agent CLI so the runtime skeleton is agent-debuggable from the first ROM that boots.**

Two changes underneath this:

1. The previously-sketched two-backend SameBoy+BGB emulator model is **dropped** (planv0.md lines 2715-2720). gameroy passes most mooneye-test-suite accuracy gates and maintaining two adapters in a Rust-only project did not pay for itself.
2. `gbf-debug` is a new crate not in the original plan at all — agent-facing scripted debugger built around the observation that "agents are best at coding, and emulator state is cheap" (planv0.md lines 2722-2731).

### Two new features added to Epic A

- **F-A7** (`bd-3mxe`): `gbf-emu` — gameroy adapter, DeterminismPolicy, breakpoint/watchpoint primitives, snapshot-restore, framebuffer, joypad-injection, registry-driven trap dispatcher, memory-trace normalization, harness-mode plumbing.
- **F-A8** (`bd-1o08`): `gbf-debug` — agent-facing scripted debugger CLI. Stateless CLI (init/exec/inspect) round-tripping through zstd-compressed JSON session files, plus an rquickjs scripting host exposing a `gb` object.

### What this changes about the M0 critical path

The DAG is now:

```
                                M0 done
                                  ▲
                                  │
                      F-A5 (Bank0 runtime) ◄───────────┐
                        │                              │
              ┌─────────┴─────────┐         F-A8 ◄──── F-A7
            F-A4 ────────────► F-A3              │     │
              │                                  │     │
      ┌───────┴───────┐                          │     │
      ▼               ▼                          │     ▼
    F-A1            F-A2          F-A6         depends on F-A1
 (gbf-asm)        (gbf-hw)        (store)      (T-A1.8 sym +
                                                T-A1.9 ROM builder)
```

F-A7 depends on F-A1 (T-A1.9 ROM builder produces .gb that gameroy loads) and F-A3 (TraceEvent types). F-A8 depends on F-A7 (emu API) and F-A1 (T-A1.8 .sym writer for SymbolTable hydration).

### What this changes about M0 milestone DoD

The original DoD was implicitly "a bootable ROM exists." The new DoD is "a bootable ROM exists **and is agent-debuggable from the first boot**." Specifically:

- F-A1 produces a tiny bootable .gb + .sym.
- F-A5 emits the runtime nucleus (boot, ISRs, scheduler, UI) through `gbf-asm::Builder`.
- F-A7 loads the .gb under `DeterminismPolicy` and runs it through gameroy.
- F-A8 forges a `.gbsess` session via `gbf-debug init`, then an agent script can `gb.run_until(gb.symbol("entry"))`, dump CPU registers, and produce structured JSON.

### Cross-references

- F-H3 (`bd-1aqc`) — emulator adapters for SameBoy+BGB — is being **closed as superseded** by F-A7. The single-backend model replaces the two-backend one.
- Epic H (`bd-oov`) is being retitled "Epic H: Kernel" since gbf-emu has left.
- F-E2 (`bd-2ww0`) — PlatformCalibrationBundle production — was blocked by F-H3; that dependency is now redirected to F-A7.

### Why this expansion is M0, not M1+

The plan's clause is load-bearing: "agent-debuggable from the **first** ROM that boots." If we ship M0 without `gbf-debug`, the agent's first interaction with the runtime nucleus is a bespoke shell-out to a non-Rust emulator, and every subsequent debugging session is bespoke. Building `gbf-debug` after M0 means rebuilding the test/calibration/harness layers around it — much more rework than including it in M0.

### Critical-path estimate

Before this change: ~38 child tasks, critical path F-A1 → F-A4 → F-A5 ≈ 20 task-units.

After this change: ~51 child tasks (38 + 6 F-A7 + 7 F-A8). F-A7 can run parallel to F-A4/F-A5 once F-A1's T-A1.9 closes; F-A8 starts when F-A7 has its core API and F-A1 has its .sym writer. Critical path approximately unchanged — F-A5 is still the longest serial run — but total task count grows by ~13.

title: T-A7.5: trace_ring.rs — NormalizedTraceEvent + TraceCursor + BankSnapshot + TraceOrigin + drop policy
description: Module trace_ring.rs (renamed from the trace.rs stub). NormalizedTraceEvent enum: MemoryWrite{addr,value,region:gbf_hw::memory::MemoryRegion,bank:BankSnapshot,origin:TraceOrigin,cycle:ClockCycles} | RomBankSwitch{from,to,source:BankSwitchSource{Bank1Write|Bank2Write},cycle} | SramBankSwitch{from,to,cycle} | IoWrite{reg,value,cycle} | TrapHit{trap_id,kind,cycle} (F-A7-local, NOT F-A3 TraceEvent::TrapHit) | Typed(gbf_abi::trace::TraceEvent) (passthrough so consumers see one stream). BankSnapshot{rom:u16, sram:u8, wramx:u8, vram:u8} attached to every MemoryWrite. TraceOrigin: GuestCpu (default — drained from gameroy-core's io_trace per step) | Dma | HostBus (NEW — for Emulator::bus_read/bus_write side-effecting accesses; advances the clock; see RFC §3.7.1 finding 6) | HostPoke (raw debug; does NOT advance clock; recorded only when explicit debug auditing is enabled). cycle is typed ClockCycles — never raw u64. The adapter DRAINS gameroy-core's io_trace once per interpret_op invocation (never accumulated across instructions — finding 5) and reconstructs each event's ClockCycles from the step's start_clock/end_clock plus per-access ordering, because io_trace's first byte packs (kind | ((clock_count & !3) >> 1)) and is not a full u64. TraceCursor with capacity + TraceDropPolicy{DropOldest|DropNewest|HaltAndError (raises EmuError::TraceCapacityExceeded)} configured via EmulatorConfig at load_rom time. Cursor tracks MBC5 BANK1/BANK2/RAMB shadow registers to derive RomBankSwitch (BANK1+BANK2 9-bit composition) and SramBankSwitch events. record() is pub(crate); consumers see only drain(). Trace cursor preserves every guest-visible event exactly once — no duplicate suppression of identical consecutive guest writes. MemoryRegion classification happens at normalization time via gbf_hw::memory::classify(addr). Consumed by gbf-test diff harness, gbf-bench drift reports, gbf-debug trace ring, and F-D3 trace pipeline.
close_reason: Completed F-A7 trace normalization: NormalizedTraceEvent stream, mapper-aware MBC5 bank tracking, HostBus/HostPoke origins, typed passthrough, packed io_trace cycle reconstruction, restore trace-bank lineage, and expanded trace tests. Gates: full workspace fmt/clippy/test pass.

title: F-S7 v0.2 T3.2: ParetoVerdict 6-variant + H4 closure under byte-equivalence
description:
## Goal

Implement §11.3 ParetoVerdict with six variants (MoE-dominates, dense-dominates, MoE-wins-under-byte-equivalence, Dense-wins-under-byte-equivalence, Incomparable, Tied) and the closure rule that confirms H4 on MoE-dominates OR MoE-wins-under-byte-equivalence.

## Background

Pre-review §11.3 let MoE 'dominate' when its byte count was greater than dense by up to D6 tolerance, which is not Pareto dominance on actual bytes. v0.2 separates strict dominance (every axis ≤; one strict) from byte-equivalence outcomes (|Δ bytes| ≤ tolerance; bpc strict). Under the matched-bytes framing — where the experiment intends bytes to be equal — H4 Confirms on either strict MoE dominance or the byte-equivalence MoE win. Dense-wins-under-byte-equivalence is symmetric: H4 Refuted, and H3 must also be Refuted (dense beat MoE on bpc with bytes equivalent).

## Files

- gbf-experiments/src/s7/pareto.rs (six-variant enum + decision tree)
- gbf-experiments/src/s7/outcome.rs (closure rule wiring)
- gbf-experiments/tests/pareto_six_variants.rs (deterministic verdict for each branch)

## Acceptance

- The decision tree maps deterministically: strict-MoE wins → MoE-dominates; strict-dense wins → dense-dominates; exact tie on both → Tied; bytes-equivalent + MoE bpc strictly lower → MoE-wins-under-byte-equivalence; symmetric for dense; otherwise Incomparable.
- H4 Confirmed iff verdict ∈ {MoE-dominates, MoE-wins-under-byte-equivalence}.
- Dense-wins-under-byte-equivalence triggers H3 also Refuted (the parity gate ran but lost under byte-equivalence; same outcome as dense-dominates).
- F3-pareto-unequal-bytes falsification (bytes differ beyond tolerance, MoE 'wins' bpc) is caught by Incomparable (not a Pareto win) and routed to Fail-pareto.

## Reasoning chain

T3.2 depends on T3.1 (parity verdict computes first; Pareto runs after). T3.2 reads CheckpointFrontierPoints from gbf-train's frontier emission (carry-through from S5).
notes:
## Test Plan & Logging (AGENTS.md addendum)

### Unit tests (gbf-experiments/tests/pareto_six_variants.rs)

Six table-driven test cases, one per variant, each with a synthetic CheckpointFrontierPoint pair:

- MoE_dominates: bpc_moe < bpc_dense (strict) AND bytes_moe < bytes_dense (strict).
- MoE_dominates_strict_bpc_equal_bytes: bpc_moe < bpc_dense, bytes_moe == bytes_dense.
- dense_dominates: symmetric.
- Tied: exact equality on both axes (f64 bit-pattern equality).
- MoE_wins_under_byte_equivalence: bpc_moe < bpc_dense AND |Δbytes| ≤ tolerance AND NOT strict-dominate.
- Dense_wins_under_byte_equivalence: symmetric.
- Incomparable: bpc_moe < bpc_dense AND bytes_moe > bytes_dense + tolerance.

### Closure-rule tests

- h4_confirmed_strict_dominance: MoE_dominates → H4 Confirmed.
- h4_confirmed_byte_equivalence_win: MoE_wins_under_byte_equivalence → H4 Confirmed.
- h4_refuted_dense_under_byte_equivalence: Dense_wins_under_byte_equivalence → H4 Refuted AND H3 also Refuted (test asserts both).
- h4_refuted_tied: Tied → H4 Refuted; S7Outcome = Fail-pareto.
- h4_refuted_incomparable: Incomparable → H4 Refuted; S7Outcome = Fail-pareto.

### Logging

- s7.pareto.verdict INFO event per dispatch: { bpc_moe, bpc_dense, bytes_moe, bytes_dense, tolerance, bytes_equivalent: bool, verdict, h4_status, h3_implication }.

### Reviewer Personas

P5 Detective (always-on), P6 Scope Sentinel (always-on), P7 Numerical & Determinism (f64 bit-pattern equality for Rep-S7-7), P8 Public Contract / Schema Stability (ParetoVerdict variants are §11.3 public).

title: F-B10: RomWindowPlan (Stage 8)
description:
# F-B10 — RomWindowPlan (Stage 8 of the 14-stage compiler pipeline)

**Source RFC:** `history/rfcs/F-B9-F-B10-sram-rom-window-plans.md` (paired RFC with F-B9).

## Why this stage exists (background for future self)

The Game Boy LR35902 sees ROM through two windows: a fixed `Bank 0` (`$0000–$3FFF`) and a switchable `Bank N` (`$4000–$7FFF`). At any instant exactly one switchable bank is visible. Every kernel call, LUT lookup, expert weight access, and embedding/logit fetch must come from a bank that is *visible at that moment*. Without an explicit plan binding each callable artifact to a ROM bank + a window-binding lifetime, the cooperative scheduler has no way to bound `max_bank_switches_per_token`, the backend has no way to legalize far-calls, and Reachability cannot prove ISR safety.

F-B10 is the spatial residency owner for ROM. It is the FIRST stage that decides "kernel K lives in bank B with residency R" — and that decision then becomes a hash-pinned input to OverlayPlan, ArenaPlan, GbSchedIR, the backend's far-call legalizer, and F-B14's bank-switch cost model.

## Pipeline context

**Upstream inputs (pinned into K8 cache key):**
- F-B8 `StoragePlan` — provides `RomConst` materializations (expert weights, router tables, LUTs, embedding/logit/norm constants).
- F-B9 `SramPagePlan` — consumed by hash for audit + for reasoning about ROM/SRAM transitions.
- `KernelSpecRegistry` (Epic H) — list of callable kernels with size + ISR-eligibility metadata.
- `ResolvedCompilePolicy.placement.profile` — `StrictOnePerBank` | `Budgeted` | `PackedExperts` (the load-bearing residency strategy knob).
- `RuntimeChromeBudget` — bank-switches per token cap.
- `TargetProfile` — ROM size, bank count, MBC type.

**Downstream consumers:**
- F-B11 `OverlayPlan` — reads the `WramOverlay` candidates (kernels/LUTs/expert fragments marked for WRAM time-multiplexing).
- F-B12 `ArenaPlan` — consumed by hash for audit.
- F-B13 `GbSchedIR` — mints `RomWindow` leases over `RomWindowBinding`s; ISR-eligibility check.
- F-B14 — bank-switch cost charging.
- F-B15 backend — far-call thunk insertion, bank-assignment legalization, ReachabilityValidation reads residency annotations.

## Core data types (closed enums)

- **KernelResidency** — `Bank0Fixed | WramOverlay | CoResidentSwitchable(BankIndex)` — the three legal residency classes.
- **RomWindowBinding** — `{ binding_id, target: BankIndex | OverlayId, residency: KernelResidency, payload_bytes, isr_eligible: bool, install_source: Option<OverlaySource> }`
- **BankAssignment** — `{ bank: BankIndex, occupants: SortedVec<BindingId>, total_bytes, slack_bytes }`
- **SimultaneousVisibilitySet** — derived predicate: `simultaneously_visible_at(slice_id) -> Set<RomWindowBinding>` — used by OverlayPlan to validate install-event source visibility.
- **RomWindowPlan** — product: `{ identity, bindings: SortedVec<RomWindowBinding>, banks: SortedVec<BankAssignment>, overlay_candidates: SortedVec<OverlayCandidate>, budgets: BankSwitchBudgetTally, profile: PlacementProfile }`

## Algorithm sketch

1. **Enumerate callables** from KernelSpecRegistry + StoragePlan RomConst bindings.
2. **Classify residency** per binding:
   - ISR-reachable kernels (e.g., scheduler tick, panic) → `Bank0Fixed`.
   - Hot kernels marked overlayable → `WramOverlay` candidate (F-B11 finalizes).
   - Everything else → `CoResidentSwitchable(bank)` where bank is chosen by the placement profile.
3. **Bin-pack into banks** under profile rules:
   - `StrictOnePerBank` — each large object gets its own bank; no sharing.
   - `Budgeted` — default; experts alone but small kernels packed by reachability-class compatibility.
   - `PackedExperts` — aggressive packing of small experts into shared banks (tight M3+ deployments).
4. **Emit overlay candidates** for F-B11 — `{ object_id, source: RomBank+offset, payload_bytes, install_event, region_constraint }`.
5. **Compute SimultaneousVisibilitySet** — for each scheduling point, what set of bindings can be visible.
6. **Tally bank-switch budgets** — derive from kernel call graph.
7. **Self-consistency** + self-hash + emit.

**Non-obvious decisions:**
- `KernelResidency` is a public type and propagates intact to F-B13's `Residency::{Bank0, Common, Expert}` mapping at slice level.
- `WramOverlay` residency means "this object will be loaded into WRAM at install time"; OverlayPlan owns the region layout, RomWindowPlan only marks candidates.
- The placement profile is the single most consequential knob in the pipeline — every later stage's cost surface depends on it.

## Invariants (RWP-SC-*)

- RWP-SC-1: Every binding has exactly one residency class.
- RWP-SC-2: ISR-eligible kernels → Bank0Fixed.
- RWP-SC-3: Bank capacity ≥ sum of occupant payload bytes.
- RWP-SC-4: Bank-switch budget ≤ RuntimeChromeBudget cap.
- RWP-SC-5: Every WramOverlay candidate has a valid source (rom_bank + offset).
- RWP-SC-6: No two co-resident occupants of the same bank conflict (alignment, ISR class).
- RWP-SC-7: Canonical sort hash stable.
- RWP-SC-8: No section/codegen leakage.
- RWP-SC-9: No scheduling fields.
- RWP-SC-10: No repair provenance in v1.
- RWP-SC-11: Placement profile correctly applied (per-profile rules witnessed).

## Diagnostic algebra (closed code list)

`RomWindow*`: InputHashMismatch, ResidencyClassImpossible, BankCapacityExceeded, BankSwitchBudgetExceeded, OverlayCandidateInvalidSource, IsrEligibleNotBank0, ProfileViolation, CanonicalSortDrift, ReportRoundTripFailed, SectionRoleLeaked, SchedulingFieldLeaked, RepairProvenanceForbidden, TargetProfileLayoutUnsupported, PolicyProjectionMismatch, KernelSpecRegistryMissing.

All severity `Hard`. Origin: `RomWindowPlanConstruction`.

## Cache key (K8, for F-B17)

```
K8 := DomainHash('gbf-codegen', 'StageCacheKey', 'rom_window_plan', 'v1',
                 CanonicalJson({
                   storage_plan_self_hash,
                   sram_page_plan_self_hash,
                   kernel_spec_registry_hash,
                   runtime_chrome_budget_hash,
                   target_profile_hash,
                   rom_window_plan_policy_projection_hash,  // includes placement profile
                   pass_version: 'stage8/v1',
                   crate_feature_set_hash,
                 }))
```

## Outputs

- `rom_window_plan.json` (ReportEnvelope) with product, summary (bank_count_used, switch_count_per_token, overlay_candidate_count), audit parents.
- Optional `certs/rom_window.cert.v1` — bank-fit witness, residency-class witness, visibility predicate manifest.

## Interaction with F-B16 (BLOCKED on oracle)

Expected proposals when F-B16 lands:
- `AdvancePlacementProfile { to: Budgeted | PackedExperts }`
- `AdvanceKernelResidencyBias { to: PreferCoResident | PreferBank0Streaming | PreferWramOverlay | FitFirst }`
- `AdvanceKernelDuplicationBias { to: DuplicateEntryStubs | DuplicateTinyKernels | DuplicateToSatisfyWindow }`
- `ForceKernelResidency { selector, to }`
- `AuthorizedRelaxation` — once-per-build profile demotion (e.g., PackedExperts → Budgeted).

## Open questions / risks

1. F-B16 lockup; until oracle confirms, profile selection is at build start, no in-loop fallback.
2. PackedExperts requires reachability-class compatibility analysis that depends on F-B15's ReachabilityValidation — chicken-and-egg risk if rules drift.
3. SimultaneousVisibilitySet correctness gates F-B11's install-source visibility check; bugs here propagate.

## Test surface

- Fixtures per residency class × profile (3 × 3 grid minimum).
- Reject fixtures one per RWP-SC-* and one per diagnostic code.
- K8 determinism + cache pinning.
- Profile-promotion semantics witness (when F-B16 unblocks).

## How this serves the overarching goal

F-B10 is the contract that says "every byte of compiled code lives in a known bank with a known residency lifetime, and we can prove the cooperative scheduler will not blow the bank-switch budget." Every downstream proof — overlay install correctness, arena reservation honor, slice lease balance, ISR residency, backend far-call legalization — depends on this contract.
design:
# F-B10 Implementation design

## Crate / module structure
- **Owner crate:** `gbf-codegen`
- **Module:** `gbf-codegen::rom_window_plan` (public), `::core` (pure builder), `::diagnostics`, `::cache` (K8 helpers).
- **Public types:** `RomWindowPlan`, `RomWindowBinding`, `KernelResidency`, `BankAssignment`, `SimultaneousVisibilitySet`, `OverlayCandidate`, `BankSwitchBudgetTally`.
- **Public entry:** `pub fn build_rom_window_plan(inputs: &RomWindowPlanInputs) -> RomWindowPlanProduct`.
- **Cache integration:** `run_rom_window_plan_cached` wraps with `gbf-store::StageCache` per F-B17.

## Implementation phases (ordered, gated)

1. **Phase 1 — Type surface.** `KernelResidency`, `RomWindowBinding`, `BankAssignment`, `SimultaneousVisibilitySet`, `OverlayCandidate`. Gate: serde round-trip; canonical ordering stable.
2. **Phase 2 — Input bundle + K8.** Pin all inputs including `placement.profile` into `rom_window_plan_policy_projection_hash`. Gate: K8 forward+backward+negative injectivity tests.
3. **Phase 3 — ISR-eligibility classifier.** Closed predicate library `is_isr_eligible(KernelSpec)` driven by F-B6 ObservationPlan reachability classes + F-B13's expected `InterruptPolicy` annotations. Gate: any kernel reaching the IRQ vector classifies `Bank0Fixed`.
4. **Phase 4 — Profile-driven bin-packers.** Three packers: `StrictOnePerBank`, `Budgeted` (first-fit), `PackedExperts` (FFD with reachability-class compatibility). All deterministic. Gate: byte-identical bank assignments across 100 shuffled-input runs.
5. **Phase 5 — Overlay-candidate emission.** `WramOverlay` candidates carry `{ object_id, source: RomBank+offset, payload_bytes, install_event, region_constraint }` for F-B11 consumption. Gate: every candidate's source visible at install-event start under `SimultaneousVisibilitySet`.
6. **Phase 6 — Bank-switch budget derivation.** Walk kernel call graph; tally per-token switches; reject if > `RuntimeChromeBudget.max_bank_switches_per_token`. Gate: tally matches hand-computed value on 5 fixture graphs.
7. **Phase 7 — Diagnostic algebra + RWP-SC-1..11.** Closed `RomWindowDiagnostic` enum; one reject fixture per code + invariant. Gate: completeness assertion.
8. **Phase 8 — Report envelope + self-hash + optional cert.** `rom_window.cert.v1` with bank-fit + residency-class witness + visibility predicate manifest.
9. **Phase 9 — Cache integration + failure memos.** Per F-B17.
10. **Phase 10 — E2E verify-packet.** `scripts/review/f-b10/verify-packet.sh`.

## Structured tracing catalog

**Top-level span:** `gbf.compile.stage8_rom_window_plan` with `stage_id=8`, `build_id`, `input_identity_hash`, `placement_profile`, `cache_status`, `outcome`, `bank_count_used`, `overlay_candidate_count`, `bank_switches_per_token`.

**Events:**
- `gbf.compile.stage.start`, `gbf.compile.cache.lookup`, `gbf.compile.stage.complete` — common pattern.
- `gbf.compile.stage.step` — `step_name ∈ {enumerate_callables, classify_residency, bin_pack, emit_overlay_candidates, compute_visibility, tally_budgets}`.
- `gbf.compile.rom_window.bank_assigned` — fields: `binding_id`, `bank`, `bytes`, `slack_bytes`, `residency`.
- `gbf.compile.rom_window.overlay_candidate` — fields: `object_id`, `source_bank`, `payload_bytes`, `install_event`.
- `gbf.compile.rom_window.profile_decision` — fields: `profile`, `co_residency_count`, `slack_bytes_remaining`.
- `gbf.compile.stage.diagnostic` — closed-enum code emission.

## Test plan

### Unit tests
- `tests/stage8_kernel_residency_classifier.rs` — every `KernelSpec` → expected residency; ISR-eligibility honors F-B6 reachability.
- `tests/stage8_bin_packer_determinism.rs` — three packers × shuffled inputs → byte-identical bank assignments.
- `tests/stage8_visibility_predicate.rs` — `SimultaneousVisibilitySet` correctness for hand-crafted call graphs.
- `tests/stage8_bank_switch_budget.rs` — tally matches expected for branching call graphs.
- `tests/stage8_k8_injectivity.rs` — F-B17 conformance (forward+backward+negative).
- `tests/stage8_overlay_candidate_emission.rs` — every `WramOverlay` candidate is a valid input to F-B11.

### Fixture tests (`fixtures/rom_window_plan/`)
- `pass/strict_one_per_bank.json`, `pass/budgeted_basic.json`, `pass/packed_experts.json` — one per profile.
- `pass/isr_eligible_bank0.json` — ISR-reachable kernel forced to Bank0.
- `pass/overlay_candidate_full_cycle.json` — overlay candidate visible at install event.
- `reject/sc_NN_*.json` — one per RWP-SC-1..11.
- `reject/code_<DiagnosticCode>.json` — one per closed code (15 fixtures).
- `reject/profile_packed_experts_residency_class_mismatch.json` — co-residency violates reachability-class compatibility.

### Property tests
- `prop_bin_packer_determinism` — shuffled-input → identical output.
- `prop_visibility_predicate_monotone` — adding a binding only grows visibility set.
- `prop_isr_eligibility_transitive` — kernel reachable from ISR vector → Bank0Fixed.

### Determinism + cache tests
- `determinism_two_runs_byte_identical`.
- `cache_hit_path_byte_identical`.

comments.text:
## F-B8: RomWindowPlan (Stage 8)

### What this is

Essential on MBC5 (`planv0.md` line 1318). Computes which ROM objects must be simultaneously visible under the single-switchable-window rule, selects kernel + LUT residency from `StoragePlan`'s materializations, duplicates or stages tiny hot tables when legal, **rejects impossible code/data placements** before layout.

`KernelResidency` is `Bank0Fixed | WramOverlay | CoResidentSwitchable`. Per planv0.md line 1320, this pass resolves the contradiction: you cannot have "shared micro-kernels in common banks" *and* "expert-local data in expert banks" be the hot-path default simultaneously, because there's only one switchable ROM window.

### Why this matters

The single most important architectural correction in the whole plan was adding this pass (planv0.md line 2554). Without it, bank thrash is silent and deferred to runtime; with it, illegal placements fail loudly at compile time.

### Design sketch

```rust
pub enum KernelResidency {
    Bank0Fixed,
    WramOverlay,
    CoResidentSwitchable,
}

pub struct RomWindowPlan {
    pub kernel_residency: BTreeMap<KernelInstanceId, KernelResidency>,
    pub lut_residency: BTreeMap<LutId, KernelResidency>,
    pub residency_epochs: Vec<ResidencyEpoch>,
    pub bank_switch_cost: BTreeMap<TransitionId, EstimatedCostDelta>,
}
```

Emits `certs/window.cert.json`.

### Cross-feature deps

- F-B6 StoragePlan
- F11 / bd-1i8 CompileProfile (overlay reload policy + max_bank_switches_per_token)
- F-A2.2 Memory map predicates

### Confidence: HIGH

title: F-S3.09: TinyStories.v2 manifest + tiny in-repo CI smoke corpus (KN preconditions met)
description:
## Context

`fixtures/corpora/tinystories.v2.toml` is the manifest pinning the post-charset_v1-normalization train and val character sequences for S3 (RFC D5). It records:
- `raw_train_sha256`, `raw_val_sha256` (pre-normalization, inherited from F-S1's `tinystories.toml`)
- `train_post_sha256`, `val_post_sha256` (post-charset_v1 normalization)
- `charset_v1_sha256` (LexicalSpec_v1 hash from B3)
- `chapter_sha256` for the held-out Accelerando chapter that v0_success prompts are drawn from
- `chapter_char_count` and the fixed prompt offsets

Separately, the CI smoke run uses a tiny in-repo fixture corpus (NOT TinyStories) that **MUST satisfy the KN D-rule preconditions for orders k ∈ {2,3,4,5}: n_1, n_2, n_3 all non-zero** (third-round Patch on tiny CI fixture). Otherwise the smoke test exercises Fail-baseline rather than the intended end-to-end path.

## Why this matters

Without B9, B10 has no train_post to fit the KN baseline on; B18 has no val_post to score against; the v0_success prompts have nowhere to come from; and the contamination check (O-8) has no train_post to scan against.

## Deliverables

1. `fixtures/corpora/tinystories.v2.toml`:
   - All sha256 fields above, computed against the canonical TinyStories raw bytes already pinned in F-S1
   - chapter_sha256 + chapter_char_count + 8 prompt offsets (first 3 = agreement subset)
2. `fixtures/corpora/tiny_corpus_s3/`:
   - `train.bytes`, `eval.bytes`, `manifest.toml` (mirrors `gbf-experiments/tests/fixtures/tiny_corpus_s2/`)
   - Sized so a 5-seed S3 pass completes within the project test timeout
   - **n_1, n_2, n_3 all non-zero for k ∈ {2,3,4,5}** verified by a fixture self-test
3. A `fixtures/corpora/tiny_corpus_s3/preconditions.toml` recording the verified n_1/n_2/n_3 values for each effective order, so future amendments can detect regression.

## Test scaffolding

1. **`gbf-experiments/tests/manifest_sha_s3.rs`** (O-1' part 2) — manifest sha verification:
   - Asserts `sha256(normalize_raw(raw_train_bytes).tokens.canonical_bytes) == train_post_sha256` from `tinystories.v2.toml`
   - Asserts `sha256(normalize_raw(raw_val_bytes).tokens.canonical_bytes) == val_post_sha256`
   - Asserts `sha256(LexicalSpec_v1) == charset_v1_sha256`
2. **`gbf-experiments/tests/tiny_corpus_kn_preconditions_s3.rs`** — fixture self-test:
   - For k ∈ {2,3,4,5}: compute n_1, n_2, n_3 over the tiny corpus
   - Assert all > 0
   - Print the exact values for human inspection (so a future regression is loud)
   - Compare against the pinned values in `preconditions.toml`
3. **`gbf-experiments/tests/manifest_round_trip_s3.rs`** — round-trip the TOML reader
4. **`gbf-experiments/tests/chapter_holdout_s3.rs`** — assert the held-out chapter is structurally absent from train_post (rolling-hash sliding window over train_post; expensive but bounded; runs under `--ignored` flag for nightly only)

## Logging discipline

The manifest reader emits an INFO event:
```
event_name = "s3::tinystories_v2_manifest::loaded"
fields: { raw_train_sha256, raw_val_sha256, train_post_sha256, val_post_sha256,
          charset_v1_sha256, chapter_sha256, chapter_char_count, prompt_count }
target = "gbf_data::manifest"
```

## E2E acceptance script

`scripts/s3_manifest_verify.sh` (test-only helper):
1. Reads `tinystories.v2.toml`
2. Re-computes every sha256 field from the source bytes
3. Asserts every field matches
4. Emits NDJSON to `/tmp/s3-manifest-verify.json`

## Inheritance / non-duplication

- Reuses F-S1's `tinystories.toml` raw byte sha256s.
- F-S2 fixture template: `gbf-experiments/tests/fixtures/tiny_corpus_s2/`.
- DOES NOT modify F-S1's `tinystories.toml`; the v2 manifest references it.

## Considerations

- The held-out Accelerando chapter selection is content work; the human author picks the chapter to satisfy: (a) ≥ chapter_char_count chars, (b) NOT contained in train_post, (c) yields 8 contiguous 64-128-char prompts with sufficient diversity.
- Contamination of the held-out chapter with train_post would silently inflate Q1; O-8 (B18) verifies; but B9 must construct the fixture so contamination is structurally impossible.

## Acceptance

```
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test manifest_sha_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test tiny_corpus_kn_preconditions_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test manifest_round_trip_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test chapter_holdout_s3 -- --ignored
scripts/s3_manifest_verify.sh
```

## Out of scope

- The KN baseline math itself (B10).
- The bpc primitive (B11).
- The contamination check at S3 closure (handled by B18 / O-8 in the runtime path).

## References

- RFC D5; §6.2 "Pinned prompt set"; §16.2 (tiny corpus rule)
- F-S2 fixture template: `gbf-experiments/tests/fixtures/tiny_corpus_s2/`

title: T-B3.25: StageCache K1 (DomainHash form; resolved_blob_index_hash + lowering_manifest_hash; no sequence_semantics_hash)
description:
## What
Implement StageCache key K1 per RFC §11:

```text
K1 := StageCacheKeyHash("quant_graph.v1", schema_version, {
  artifact_validation_self_hash,
  policy_resolution_self_hash,
  artifact_effective_core_hash,
  lowering_manifest_hash,
  resolved_blob_index_hash,
  pass_version_quant_graph,
  crate_feature_set_hash,
  quant_graph_schema_hash
})
```

Plus success-store, failure-memo paths inheriting from F-B2/F-B4 §11
laws (C-Success-Stage1, C-NoFalseSuccess-Stage1, C-FailureMemo-Stage1,
C-PassVersion, C-SchemaVersion, C-FeatureSet).

## Why
K1 is the cache identity for Stage 1. Three deliberate omissions from
earlier drafts:

1. **`sequence_semantics_hash` is NOT in K1** (Ambiguity A45).
   `SequenceSemanticsSpec` is part of `ArtifactCore`; its identity is
   already captured by `artifact_effective_core_hash`. Sidecar
   rebinding is forbidden in v1.

2. **`resolved_blob_index_hash` IS in K1** (Ambiguity A78). Without
   it, two artifacts with the same `ArtifactCore` but different
   blob storage backends could collide on cache hits.

3. **`lowering_manifest_hash` IS in K1** (§8.1). Lowering-manifest
   drift must invalidate the cache because tensor packings depend on
   it.

`pass_version_quant_graph` is bumped on any algorithmic change to
construction logic (e.g. canonical-sort tweak); `crate_feature_set_hash`
captures `cfg(feature = ...)` flags; `quant_graph_schema_hash` is the
schema's own self-hash (every schema bump is a cache miss).

## Inputs
- T-B3.24 (canonical schema is what `quant_graph_schema_hash` hashes).
- T-B3.2a (`ResolvedBlobIndex.self_hash`).
- F-B2/F-B4's existing `StageCacheKeyHash` helper.

## Outputs
- `fn compute_k1(...) -> Hash256` using `DomainHash`.
- StageCache success entry shape (stores `QuantGraphProduct` + report).
- Failure memo shape (stores canonical failure report only).
- Cache laws tests:
  - `success_store_iff_passed`.
  - `no_false_success_on_failure`.
  - `failure_memo_never_used_as_success`.
  - `pass_version_drift_invalidates`.
  - `schema_drift_invalidates`.
  - `feature_set_drift_invalidates`.

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT include `sequence_semantics_hash` (Ambiguity A45).
- DO NOT bitwise-mix sub-hashes; use `DomainHash` (Ambiguity A52).
- DO NOT store a success product when outcome = Failed (proof
  obligation O13).

## Acceptance
- `gbf-codegen::k1_does_not_include_sequence_semantics_hash`.
- `gbf-codegen::k1_includes_resolved_blob_index_hash`.
- `gbf-codegen::k1_includes_lowering_manifest_hash`.
- `gbf-codegen::stage1_cache_failure_memo_distinct_from_success`.

## Refs
- RFC §11 (K1, cache laws), §8.1 (lowering_manifest_hash binding),
  Proof obligation O13, Ambiguity ledger: A45, A52, A78.
- Depends on: T-B3.24, T-B3.2a.
- Blocks: T-B3.26 (fixtures exercise cache), T-B3.27 (driver wires
  cache).

comments.text:
## T-A5.7: Panic screen

**Target crate**: `gbf-runtime`
**Target file(s)**: `gbf-runtime/src/panic.rs`
**Reference**: `planv0.md` line 1646 (panic/debug screen in Bank 0 nucleus).

### Background

When the runtime takes an unrecoverable fault, it disables interrupts, dumps `FaultSnapshot` (T-A3.4) to a known SRAM address (so a power-cut and reboot can read it), renders a "Game Boy halted: <fault code>" screen via direct VRAM write (since normal video_commit may itself be broken), and halts.

Panic is in the reference shell budget reservation but not in the included module set initially — yet bring-up needs at least a basic panic so faults don't silently freeze. **Compromise**: ship a minimal panic in M0 (just halt + on-screen code dump); defer the full FaultSnapshot+SRAM persistence to Epic D.

### Implementation Notes

```rust
pub fn build_panic_section() -> Section;

/// Emit AsmIR for: disable interrupts, dump FaultCode to a known VRAM tile, halt.
pub fn emit_panic<B: Builder>(b: &mut B, code: FaultCode);

/// Bypass video_commit (since it may be broken); write directly to VRAM.
pub fn emit_panic_screen_render<B: Builder>(b: &mut B);
```

Bypassing `video_commit` is one of the rare audited cases where direct VRAM write is legal. The section is `PrivilegeClass::Privileged + InterruptDisabled`. ReachabilityValidation will recognize the panic section as exempt from the "no-direct-VRAM-write" rule.

### Acceptance Criteria

```bash
cargo check -p gbf-runtime
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- panic::emits_di_then_halt
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- panic::renders_fault_code_glyphs
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- panic::section_marked_exempt              # Annotation for ReachabilityValidation
```

### Constitution Checkpoints

- §V.3: Panic dumps fault code to a visible location; not silent.
- §I.1: FaultCode is structured.

## RFC F-A5 alignment - 2026-05-03

Source of truth: history/rfcs/F-A5-bank0-runtime.md section 3G. This comment supersedes earlier bead text where inconsistent.

Corrections:
- M0 panic writes only a FaultCode byte to WRAM_LAST_FAULT_ADDR and renders the fault code on screen. It does not dump FaultSnapshot and does not write SRAM.
- Full FaultSnapshot plus SRAM persistence belongs to F-D1 and is explicitly deferred.
- Panic must wait for VBlank before clearing LCDC.7 so real DMG hardware is not risked.
- The section annotation is ExecutionContext::PanicOnly plus InterruptDiscipline::ImeDisabled plus PanicBypass. Do not describe this as a PrivilegeClass variant.
- Panic is the only non-video_commit direct VRAM writer and is covered by a cross-section acceptance test.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Why this bead exists

F-S1.27 covers per-PR smoke (pass-clean on tiny fixture). F-S1.24 covers
falsification (broken substitutes produce expected verdicts).
NEITHER covers the POSITIVE end-to-end behavior across all S1Outcome
variants on the tiny fixture: pass-clean, pass-with-warning,
fail-substrate, fail-capacity, fail-suspicious, fail-phase, fail-metric.

If those scenarios aren't exercised end-to-end, the dispatcher (F-S1.19)
+ report emitter (F-S1.20) + Decision binding (F-S1.29) could be
individually correct yet fail to compose under realistic inputs.

This bead lands the comprehensive e2e harness with structured logging,
golden artifacts per scenario, and a top-level driver script. It is the
single test the user can point at and say "these prove the system works
end-to-end, with logs we can read".

## Scope

- gbf-experiments/tests/e2e/ directory:
    e2e.rs                          (root harness, gates each scenario)
    scenarios/
      pass_clean.rs                  (all H1..H5 confirm)
      pass_with_warning.rs           (H3 refuted; T12.5 prereq)
      fail_substrate_nan.rs          (NaN injection at step K → H1 R)
      fail_substrate_zero_grad.rs    (gradient-zero hook → H1 R)
      fail_capacity_toytiny.rs       (d_model=2 fixture)
      fail_suspicious_low_bpc.rs     (synthetic over-fit on val → median<0.5)
      fail_phase_ternary_leak.rs     (forces ablation tensor mismatch)
      fail_metric_modulo_shuffle.rs  (broken Fisher-Yates → O-metric-4 R)
    common_scenario.rs               (shared scenario harness)
    golden/
      pass_clean/
        s1_baseline.v1.json
        s1_checkpoint.v1.metadata.json   (per seed)
        s1_run_log.v1.json               (per seed)
        s1_score.v1.json                 (per seed)
        s1_negative_test.v1.json
        s1_ablation.v1.json
        S1-report.md
      pass_with_warning/
        ... (analogous)
      fail_*/
        ... (each with the report ending in the expected Decision)

- Each scenario:
    1. Sets up a fresh TempDir.
    2. Initializes F-S1.30 logging in `Json` profile to a per-scenario
       log file (one NDJSON event per line).
    3. Builds the appropriate substitute/feature set:
        - pass scenarios use the production code paths
        - fail-substrate-nan uses falsify F1 (NaN forward)
        - fail-substrate-zero-grad uses falsify F2
        - fail-capacity-toytiny uses falsify F5 (ToyTiny d_model=2)
        - fail-phase-ternary-leak uses falsify F4
        - fail-metric-modulo-shuffle uses falsify F6
        - fail-suspicious uses a fixture that synthesizes a
          guaranteed-low-bpc trained model (e.g., trains on val).
    4. Runs the full pipeline: baseline → 5-seed train → score →
       neg-test → ablation → oracle → report.
    5. Asserts:
        - Final S1Outcome matches the scenario's expected variant.
        - Decision dispatch matches expected.
        - All produced JSON artifacts byte-equal their golden file
          (or, for hash-bearing fields, equal modulo a documented
          fluctuation envelope which should be EMPTY for deterministic
          tests).
        - The structured log file contains the expected event sequence
          (e.g., for fail-substrate-nan: a `run.divergence` event with
          `observed=non_finite_loss` at the injected step).
    6. On failure: dump the captured log + the JSON diff to stderr.

- Top-level driver: `scripts/s1_e2e.sh`
    Runs every e2e scenario sequentially against the tiny fixture.
    Prints a per-scenario PASS/FAIL summary plus aggregate runtime.
    Optional --scenario flag to run just one.

- Golden update workflow:
    `cargo test -p gbf-experiments --test e2e -- --update-goldens`
    re-pins all goldens. CI uses --no-update; goldens drift = PR
    review surfaces it explicitly.

## Considerations

- The harness is deliberately TINY-FIXTURE-ONLY. Full TinyStories
  e2e is F-S1.28's job; bringing it into PR CI would 10× the cycle.
- Goldens are the single biggest assurance the system is wired
  correctly. Keep them under review like any other code.
- Do NOT use sleeps, network, or wall-clock-dependent assertions.
  Determinism is the contract.
- E2E logs must use F-S1.30's structured format so future tooling
  can ingest them automatically.

## Testing (meta)

- A "self-test" scenario verifies the harness fails as expected when
  given a deliberately-incorrect golden.
- Runtime budget: full e2e suite < 5 minutes wall clock (tiny fixture).
- Each scenario's log file is < 1 MiB.

## Logging requirements

- Every scenario emits a span `s1.e2e.scenario.<name>` at INFO.
- Each phase transition (baseline / train / score / neg / ablation /
  oracle / report) emits an event at INFO with the scenario name as
  a field.
- Final outcome + decision logged at INFO before the assertion
  block runs.

## RFC anchors

- §8 Outcome algebra (every variant exercised here)
- §13 O5 falsification (this harness COMPLEMENTS the unit-level
  falsification suite by exercising end-to-end composition)
- §15.2 test layout (e2e is a new sibling of integration)
- §14 Minimal end-to-end theorem

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Why this bead exists

bd-14d8 (T16.1) lands the corpus + manifest TOML at
`fixtures/corpora/tinystories.toml` and the downloader. F-S1.08 wires that into
the s1 surface: a thin `s1::manifest` module that delegates to gbf-data and
asserts manifest sha256 verification before any byte ever flows to training,
scoring, or baseline code.

Per A26 in the ambiguity ledger, the manifest lives at repo root, not crate-
local, because S4/S8 will share it. This bead does NOT move that file.

## Scope

In `gbf-data` (extending T16.1's loader):
  - `read_tinystories_manifest(path) -> Result<TinyStoriesManifest>`
  - `load_train_bytes(manifest) -> Result<ByteSeq>` and equivalent for val
  - On load: re-hash the on-disk file and assert sha256 equals the manifest
    field. ABORT on mismatch — never return un-pinned bytes.
  - Strict raw-byte policy (D5):
      * No NFC, no charset folding, no <unk>/<bos>/<eos>.
      * `<|endoftext|>` is treated as ordinary 14 input bytes (NOT stripped,
        NOT replaced, NOT interpreted as a semantic boundary).
      * No newline normalization; no archive reserialization.

In `gbf-experiments::s1::manifest`:
  - Re-export / wrap gbf-data's reader. The wrapper exists so the s1 code does
    NOT depend on gbf-data internals beyond the public type.
  - Provides `verified_corpus(manifest) -> { train: ByteSeq, val: ByteSeq }`
    that calls `enforce()` from F-S1.04 first (env profile), then loads + hashes.

Unit tests (against a tiny in-repo fixture corpus, NOT real TinyStories):
  - sha256 mismatch → returns Err with diagnostic
  - byte-for-byte preservation including the `<|endoftext|>` separator
  - load_val_bytes returns the entire val byte sequence with no truncation

## Considerations

- The TinyStories byte length is 2.07 GiB train + 21.5 MiB val. Plan for this
  in tests by using a tiny fixture corpus, not the full file. The full corpus
  is gated behind a separate CI job (§15.2 "The full TinyStories run is gated
  behind a separate CI job").
- Future-self: bd-14d8 evolves over time (S3 adds charset_v1 normalization).
  S1 only consumes the raw-byte loader contract. Don't be tempted to share
  S3's normalized bytes back into S1 — that would invalidate prior comparisons
  per Rule Amendment.

## RFC anchors

- §1 TinyStoriesManifest, S1 canonical TinyStories instance
- §15.1 gbf-data row + s1::manifest module
- §15.4 canonical replay command
- D5 Fixed split
- A26 manifest at repo root
- Rep-3 corpus pinning

title: T-A7.6: Harness-mode execution path — host-side command/result block plumbing
description: Plumbing for F-D2's Harness Control Plane. HarnessChannel reads/writes the F-A3 #[repr(C)] HarnessCommandBlock and HarnessResultBlock at a constructor-supplied HarnessSlot{sram_bank, command_addr, result_addr, doorbell_addr}. Verbs (Emulator::attach_harness / poll_harness / write_harness_result) live on Emulator (not the channel) to dodge borrow-checker issues. Doorbell is an edge signal; the u32 sequence lives in the command block. F-A7 does NOT dispatch HarnessOp variants — that is F-D2's job. M0 uses MBC5-SRAM-DIRECT access via cartridge.ram[bank * 0x2000 + (addr - 0xA000)] indexing — F-A7 does NOT call GameBoy::write and does NOT mutate the emulated MBC5 SRAM bank register (avoids clock advancement, avoids harness-driven RomBankSwitch/SramBankSwitch trace pollution; see RFC §3.7.1 finding 9 and resolved Q42). The HarnessMemory trait exposes read_sram_bank(bank, addr) / read_sram_bank_range(bank, addr, len) / write_sram_bank(bank, addr, value) — NOT switch_sram_bank + peek/poke. Operations must not emit guest MemoryWrite trace events, must not trigger guest memory traps, and must not advance the clock. Wraps F-A3's blocks directly with no local mirror of the byte layout. Errors: HarnessMagicMismatch, HarnessSequenceMismatch, HarnessSramOutOfRange, HarnessSramAccessUnavailable (if the spike confirms cartridge.ram is private at the pinned rev).

title: T2.5: runtime_nucleus_hash CI drift gate between training and production shell
description: CI step that: (1) on every PR touching gbf-runtime, re-emits RuntimeChromeBudget; (2) compares runtime_nucleus_hash to the pinned training-time hash recorded in the active training run manifest (or the canonical reference budget); (3) fails the PR unless the bump is intentional and tagged with a release note that promotes the new hash. Trainer also self-checks at every step that the captured pin is unchanged.
close_reason: Completed runtime nucleus drift gate, v2 budget contract binding, CI workflow, and trainer self-check

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Agent Instructions

**Target**: CI workflow + `gbf-runtime` + `gbf-train`.
**Target file(s)**: `.github/workflows/runtime-nucleus-drift.yml` (new) or equivalent CI config; `gbf-train/src/preflight.rs` (self-check); a reusable `tools/check-nucleus-drift` binary if needed.

**Reference**: bd-1hv 2026-04-26 session comment ("`runtime_nucleus_hash` is load-bearing"), T2.1 refinement (bd-yfv), T2.4 (bd-37r).

### Implementation Notes

Two layers of drift detection, both required:

1. **CI gate (production-shell drift).**
   - Trigger: any PR that modifies `gbf-runtime/`, `gbf-policy/src/budget.rs`, `gbf-policy/src/profile.rs`, `gbf-policy/src/reference_shell.rs`, or anything that ends up in the runtime-nucleus binary.
   - Action: re-emit `RuntimeChromeBudget` from the post-PR shell. Compare `runtime_nucleus_hash` to the value pinned in `artifacts/calibration/pinned_reference_budget.json` (or whatever path the project chooses).
   - Failure mode: PR fails with a diagnostic listing both hashes and per-slot byte deltas. The PR author either (a) reverts the budget-affecting change, or (b) explicitly bumps the pin in the same PR with a release note that promotes the new hash.

2. **Trainer self-check (active-run drift).**
   - At training start, the trainer captures the pinned `runtime_nucleus_hash` into the run manifest.
   - At every checkpoint commit and every export step, the trainer re-reads the active `RuntimeChromeBudget` (synthetic or real) and asserts the hash is unchanged.
   - On drift: trainer halts with a clear error pointing to (i) the pinned hash, (ii) the current hash, (iii) which file change likely caused it (via `git log -p <budget_file>` summary).

### Release-note convention for promoting a new hash

Promotion is a deliberate, reviewable act. The mechanism:
- A dedicated marker file `artifacts/calibration/PINNED_HASH_HISTORY.md` records every pinned hash with date, the modules included, and the reason for promotion.
- CI reads the most recent entry's hash; PRs that change the runtime nucleus must add a new entry to be merged.

### What this task does NOT do

It does not specify the byte-level encoding of `runtime_nucleus_hash` (that's T2.1 / bd-yfv). It does not implement the synthetic budget (that's T2.6 / bd-ros). It composes those.

### Acceptance Criteria

```bash
# Locally:
cargo run -p tools-check-nucleus-drift                         # Exit 0 when in sync
cargo test -p gbf-train -- preflight::nucleus_self_check        # Trainer self-check enforces drift

# CI:
# Verify: a PR adding a new file to gbf-runtime/src/ that ends up in the nucleus fails CI without a pin promotion
# Verify: a PR that promotes the pin (updates PINNED_HASH_HISTORY.md) passes
# Verify: the diagnostic on failure lists both hashes and the offending file paths
```

### Constitution Checkpoints

- §I.4: CI gate is the verifiable reward — exit 0 means no silent drift.
- §IV.3: Reproducible budget — same source produces same hash; CI catches deviations.
- §V.3: Loud failure with structured diff (old hash, new hash, byte deltas) on drift.
- §VI.1: PINNED_HASH_HISTORY.md is the single source of truth for hash promotion.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## T-A5.1: Boot + IRQ vector dispatch

**Target crate**: `gbf-runtime`
**Target file(s)**: `gbf-runtime/src/boot.rs`, `gbf-runtime/src/interrupts.rs`
**Reference**: `planv0.md` line 1626, line 1646 (boot/header/vectors as part of Bank 0 nucleus).

### Background

Boot is the first executable code on the cartridge. After the cartridge header (`$0100`) and the Nintendo logo verification dance, control jumps to the runtime's `main` entry point. From there the runtime initializes:
- HRAM shadow registers (zero them).
- IRQ vectors (point each `INT_VECTOR_*` at the matching ISR entry stub).
- LCD power-up state.
- Joypad register read.
- Cooperative scheduler initial state.

### Implementation Notes

```rust
/// Build the Bank 0 boot section with cartridge header, init sequence, and IRQ vectors.
pub fn build_boot_section() -> Section;

/// Build the IRQ dispatch section. Each vector is a 16-byte slot; they jump to ISR stubs in Bank 0.
pub fn build_irq_vectors_section() -> Section;

/// IRQ entry stubs: minimal AsmIR that saves regs, calls into the corresponding ISR handler,
/// restores regs, RETI.
pub fn build_isr_stubs_section() -> Section;
```

The vector layout (per gbf-hw T-A2.5):
- `$0040` VBlank
- `$0048` LCD STAT
- `$0050` Timer (used by scheduler for yield deadline)
- `$0058` Serial
- `$0060` Joypad

Each ISR stub is `Privileged + InterruptHandler` per T-A1.4; reachability is `Bank0/HRAM/fixed-WRAM`.

The cartridge header bytes are emitted via T-A1.9's `assemble_rom`; this task wires the runtime into those slots.

### Acceptance Criteria

```bash
cargo check -p gbf-runtime
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- boot::cartridge_header_layout         # Bytes at $0100-$014F
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- boot::irq_vector_jumps                 # Vectors jump to ISR stubs
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- boot::shadow_registers_zeroed_at_init
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- interrupts::isr_stubs_are_isr_marked   # Privilege class
```

### Constitution Checkpoints

- §I.1: Boot is structured AsmIR sections, not raw bytes.
- §VI.1: Single boot module.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## RFC F-A5 alignment - 2026-05-03

Source of truth: history/rfcs/F-A5-bank0-runtime.md sections 3A and 5.2. This comment supersedes earlier bead text where inconsistent.

Corrections:
- Do not put the full boot init stream in the cartridge header. The only executable bytes at $0100..=$0103 are NOP; JP runtime_boot_entry. The Nintendo logo and header occupy $0104..=$014F, and runtime_boot_entry starts at $0150 or later.
- Each IRQ vector slot is 8 bytes, not 16 bytes: JP nn plus NOP padding to the next slot.
- ISR stubs use PrivilegeClass::InterruptHandler plus ExecutionContext::InterruptHandler and InterruptDiscipline::ImeDisabled; do not describe this as Privileged + InterruptHandler.
- Normal handlers do not write IF. The CPU acknowledges the serviced interrupt on dispatch; emit_clear_pending_if_bit exists only for intentional pending-request discard and must preserve unrelated IF bits.
- Boot imports hardware constants from gbf-hw and banking-shadow helpers/constants from F-A4. F-A5 must not redeclare them.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Why this bead exists

When F-S1.13 fails on seed 3 at step 7421 in a nightly job, the
debugger's first questions are:
  - was my env clean?
  - did the manifest sha256 verify?
  - which Burn version?
  - what does the failed checkpoint look like?
  - which tensor diverged in ablation?

Without a doctor / inspect CLI, every answer requires bespoke ad-hoc
scripts. This bead consolidates the diagnosis surface so future
debugging is fast.

## Scope

Add to `gbf s1` (extending F-S1.25):

  - `gbf s1 doctor`
      Checks (each with PASS/FAIL + diagnostic):
        - F-S1.04 enforce(S1CpuDeterministic) over current env
        - sha256 of manifest train + val files
        - Cargo.lock dependency_lockfile_sha matches recorded
        - rust_toolchain_hash present + matches expected
        - Burn version pinned via `=` syntax
        - GPU-disabled (no CUDA libs loaded)
        - Disk space for experiments/S1/** > 1 GiB
      Exit code: 0 if all PASS; 1 if any FAIL.
      Output: human-readable table by default; --json for CI ingest.

  - `gbf s1 inspect <artifact>`
      Where <artifact> is any s1_*.v1 JSON file:
        - Pretty-print structured fields
        - Recompute its self-hash and assert match
        - Print which schema (s1_checkpoint.v1 / s1_run_log.v1 / etc.)
        - For run-logs: print per-eval-point bpc table + grad_norm
          summary
      Exit code: 0 if hash matches; 1 if mismatch.

  - `gbf s1 diff-checkpoints <A.safetensors> <B.safetensors>`
      For each tensor (sorted-name canonical order):
        - tensor_name
        - shape
        - byte payload equality
        - first byte_offset of mismatch (if any)
      Exit code: 0 if all tensors equal; 1 otherwise.

  - `gbf s1 print-config`
      Print the resolved TrainConfig + ModelSizeProfile::Toy0
      reference + S1CpuDeterministic profile + active feature set
      + BUILD_KIND. Useful for confirming what a fresh run will use.

## Considerations

- Doctor output is for HUMANS first; --json is secondary. Pretty-print
  with colors when stdout is a TTY.
- inspect must reject malformed JSON loudly (don't silently succeed).
- diff-checkpoints uses F-S1.06's CanonicalTensorPayloadHash type so
  its output is consistent with the H4 ablation comparator.
- All doctor checks are READ-ONLY; never mutate anything.

## Testing

- Unit tests for each subcommand using `assert_cmd` (F-S1.31).
- Golden tests: run inspect on a known artifact and snapshot output.
- Negative tests: tampered self-hash → inspect exit 1 + diagnostic.
- Property tests: random tensor sets → diff-checkpoints reports
  no mismatch when both inputs are identical.

## Logging

- All doctor checks use the structured logging from F-S1.30.
- Subcommand entry/exit logged at INFO with `s1.cli.<sub>` span.
- Failures logged at ERROR with full diagnostic field.

## RFC anchors

- §15.4 canonical replay command (this is the diagnostic counterpart)
- §13 O4 ablation match (diff-checkpoints is the manual analog)
- §1 Hash256 + self-hash rule (inspect verifies these)

## T-A2.1: `TargetProfile` + `ConsoleModel` + `CartridgeProfile` + `CapabilitySet`

**Target crate**: `gbf-hw`
**Target file(s)**: `gbf-hw/src/target.rs`
**Reference**: `planv0.md` line 213.

### Background

`TargetProfile` is the top-level type that bundles "which Game Boy + which cartridge + which capabilities" for a given build. Compile requests (`CompileRequest::target: TargetProfileId`) resolve into a `TargetProfile` early in compilation. This is what tells the rest of the system whether to assume DMG, CGB, or some specific MBC variant.

### Implementation Notes

```rust
pub struct TargetProfile {
    pub id: TargetProfileId,                  // from gbf-foundation
    pub family: TargetFamilyId,
    pub console: ConsoleModel,
    pub cartridge: CartridgeProfile,
    pub timing: TimingProfile,                // populated in T-A2.4
    pub capabilities: CapabilitySet,
}

pub enum ConsoleModel {
    Dmg,                                       // original Game Boy
    Mgb,                                       // Game Boy Pocket — same architecture, different timing trim
    Sgb,                                       // Super Game Boy — DMG mode only
    Cgb,                                       // Game Boy Color
    // Cgb-in-DMG-mode is a CompileProfile choice, not a separate ConsoleModel.
}

pub struct CartridgeProfile {
    pub mbc: MbcType,
    pub max_rom_kib: u32,
    pub max_sram_kib: u32,
    pub has_battery: bool,
    pub has_rtc: bool,
}

pub enum MbcType {
    None,
    Mbc1,
    Mbc2,
    Mbc3,
    Mbc5,
    // future: Mbc6, Mbc7, etc.
}

pub struct CapabilitySet {
    pub double_speed_mode: bool,               // CGB only
    pub vram_dma: bool,                        // CGB
    pub rtc_present: bool,
}
```

Provide a known-good `pub fn dmg_mbc5_8mib_128kib() -> TargetProfile { ... }` constructor for the bring-up profile.
