```bash
cargo check -p gbf-hw
cargo test -p gbf-hw -- target::dmg_mbc5_constructor              # Bring-up profile is well-formed
cargo test -p gbf-hw -- target::serde_round_trip                  # Profile round-trips through JSON
cargo test -p gbf-hw -- target::capability_set_exhaustive          # Each capability has a known semantics
```

### Constitution Checkpoints

- §I.1: `MbcType` and `ConsoleModel` are enumerated.
- §VI.1: `TargetProfile` is the single place that bundles target identity.

title: T10.15: Full regression test script with diagnostic summary
description:
A single entry-point script (cargo test -p gbf-test -- --training-contract or a dedicated binary) that runs ALL training-contract tests in the correct order and produces a structured diagnostic summary.

**Test execution order:**
1. Infrastructure: tiny model fixtures, logging setup
2. Unit tests: QAT modules, byte math, model config, loss terms, router, budget, Pareto
3. Integration tests: phase transitions, temporal smoothness boundaries
4. E2E tests: train-to-export, export determinism, oracle agreement, shadow compile
5. Regression checks: compare against golden values from last known-good run

**Output artifacts:**
- test_results.json: per-test pass/fail/skip with timing, failure messages, and structured diagnostics
- test_summary.txt: human-readable one-line-per-test with [PASS]/[FAIL]/[SKIP] and total counts
- training_metrics.json: loss curves from E2E training test (useful for detecting training regressions)
- artifact_hashes.json: content hashes of all exported artifacts (useful for detecting export regressions)
- byte_counts.json: per-expert byte counts (useful for detecting budget formula regressions)

**CI integration:**
- Exit code 0 if all tests pass, 1 if any fail
- Failed test output includes: test name, assertion that failed, expected vs actual, full structured context
- Summary line: 'Training-contract tests: 47/47 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (12.3s)'
- Optionally: upload test_results.json and training_metrics.json as CI artifacts

**Golden value management:**
- Golden values stored in fixtures/golden/training_contract/
- When REGENERATE_GOLDEN=1, tests overwrite golden values instead of comparing
- Golden values include: artifact hashes, byte counts, phase transition sequences, loss term values for known inputs

**Performance guard:**
- Total test suite should complete in < 60 seconds on CI (tiny model, CPU only)
- Individual slow tests (E2E) are marked with a time budget and warn if exceeded

title: T10.10: Pareto frontier selection correctness tests (F8 coverage)
description:
Unit tests for Pareto frontier tracking and checkpoint selection:

**Dominance relation tests:**
- Point A (quality=0.9, fit=true, cost=100) dominates B (quality=0.8, fit=true, cost=150): verify A dominates B
- Point A (quality=0.9, fit=true, cost=100) vs C (quality=0.85, fit=true, cost=80): verify neither dominates (Pareto-incomparable)
- Point with fit=false is never selected regardless of quality/cost

**Frontier tracking tests:**
- Insert 5 known points, verify frontier contains exactly the non-dominated ones
- Verify frontier size never exceeds keep_frontier limit
- Verify oldest non-frontier points are evicted first when at capacity

**Selection algorithm tests:**
- Given frontier: [(quality=0.9,cost=100), (quality=0.85,cost=80), (quality=0.95,cost=200)]
- After filtering fit=true, verify selected = highest quality point (0.95, cost=200)
- If best-quality point has fit=false, verify next-best is selected
- If all points have fit=false: verify selection returns None with appropriate error

**training_selection.json output:**
- Run selection on known frontier, verify JSON contains: frontier array, selected checkpoint_id, domination relationships, timestamp
- Verify JSON is valid and parseable

**Edge cases:**
- Single point frontier: verify it's selected
- All identical quality: verify any one is selected (deterministic tiebreak)
- Empty frontier: verify error, not crash

title: F-A1x: First-class Game Boy interrupt vector placement
description:
Follow-up from F-B1 review: the F-B1 ROM uses typed `Instr::JpAbs` encoding for the VBlank vector, but applies the vector jump after assembly. That is acceptable for the bringup packet, yet production `gbf-asm` should own Game Boy interrupt-vector bytes as layout items instead of relying on post-link mutation.

Scope: add a first-class vector-placement surface for fixed Bank0 slots such as `$0040` VBlank, `$0048` LCD STAT, `$0050` Timer, `$0058` Serial, and `$0060` Joypad. The API should reserve vector bytes during layout, emit vector stubs through typed instructions/pseudo-ops, attach a symbol/owner to each slot, and make those slots visible to listings, symbol maps, and reachability roots.

Acceptance criteria:
- `gbf-asm` exposes validated vector-slot types or builder APIs rather than raw byte placement.
- vector placement rejects out-of-Bank0 addresses, slot overflow, duplicate owners, and overlap with header/boot glue/reserved ranges.
- emitted vector stubs are encoded through typed instruction lowering, not ad hoc byte arrays.
- listings and symbol maps show vector slot ownership and target labels.
- ReachabilityValidation can treat installed vectors as roots for ISR code/data checks.
- F-B1 can eventually delete its post-assembly `$0040` patch once this lands.

Closure must include an ASM claim-to-gate matrix and cite tests that actually run.

title: F-B15: Backend — AsmIR codegen + ReachabilityValidation + PlacedRom + EncodedRom (Stage 12)
description:
# F-B15 — Backend: AsmIR codegen + ReachabilityValidation + PlacedRom + EncodedRom (Stage 12)

**Source RFC:** `history/rfcs/F-B15-backend.md`.

## Why this stage exists

Stages 0–11 have committed every typed decision at the IR level — values, effects, residencies, banks, overlays, arenas, slices, leases, cost envelopes. F-B15 is the final lowering: the only stage that turns IR into bytes that flash onto a cartridge and boot in a Game Boy emulator/hardware. Four tightly integrated sub-passes ship as one Feature because their typed seams are inseparable:

1. **AsmIR Codegen** — lower SchedulePack slices into typed F-A1 `Vec<Section>` (eDSL).
2. **ReachabilityValidation** — compute transitive reachability classes (six-class lattice) + prove seven hard rules.
3. **PlacedRom** — bank assignment, layout legalization, branch relaxation, far-call thunks under profile-driven strategies.
4. **EncodedRom** — deterministic serialization to `.gb` bytes, `.sym` symbol map, `.lst` listing.

ReachabilityValidation is the load-bearing safety property: every code/data root the runtime can reach must be placed, reachable in the typed sense, and satisfy ISR/yield/fault/lease invariants. It is the typed counterpart to F-B13's annotation-driven `IsrVisibleResidency` check — F-B15 does the whole-program computation, and **F-B15 wins** if they disagree.

## Pipeline context

**Inputs (consumed by hash):**
- F-B13 SchedulePack — keyed by RuntimeMode (slices, ops, yields, continuation targets, leases, live WRAM/SRAM).
- F-B14 ScheduleCostReport — per-mode cycle budgets + bank-switch counts.
- F-A2 TargetProfile — ROM size, MBC type, cartridge profile, memory regions.
- F-B2/F-B4 ResolvedCompilePolicy — placement profile, determinism mode, cartridge metadata.
- F-A5 runtime nucleus sections — Bank0 boot, interrupts, scheduler, panic, with sections pinned as reachability roots.
- Epic H KernelRegistry — compiled kernel sections keyed by `(KernelSpecId, KernelResidency)`.
- F-B10/F-B11/F-B12 spatial plans (overlay install events, arena ranges, residency directives).
- F-B13 Stage 10.5 resource_state.cert.json — lease balance + yield-safety proof.

**Outputs (by hash):**
- `.gb` — Pan-Docs MBC5 cartridge image (32 KiB–8 MiB per profile).
- `.sym` — RGBDS symbol map (`BB:AAAA name` sorted lex).
- `.lst` — Disassembled interleaved listing with provenance.
- `placed_rom_plan.json` — bank assignments, thunks, layout iterations, global constraints, cycle annotations.
- `map.json` — definitive address map (consumed by gbf-debug, gbf-emu, gbf-bench, harness, persistence).
- `reachability_report.json` — per-section class, findings per rule, dead-code summary, F-B13 disagreements.
- `certs/reachability.cert.json` — proof cert with witness hash for independent cross-validation.

**Downstream consumers:** gbf-emu (F-A7), gbf-debug (F-A8), gbf-bench (Epic E), gbf-verify (F-F2 independent walker), F-B16 (may request retry under different PlacementProfile), F-D1 persistence, F-D2 harness, F-F1 build_manifest aggregator.

## Core data types

- **AsmIRBundle** — `{ codegen_sections, nucleus_sections, provenance_map: HashMap<(SectionId, ItemIndex), AsmIRProvenanceEntry>, asmir_bundle_hash }`. SourceKind enum spans SchedOp, KernelBody, ContinuationHeader, EpochTrampoline, ExpertEntryStub, TensorPayload, LutPayload, RuntimeNucleus, CartridgeHeader, BuildIdentityBlock.
- **ReachabilityClassSet** — join-semilattice of six classes: `IsrReachable`, `YieldResumeReachable`, `FaultPathReachable`, `HarnessEntryReachable`, `BankLeaseProtected`, `NormalOnly`. Per-node multi-class membership.
- **ReachabilityCertificate** — `{ roots, class_summary, findings: Vec<{rule: R1..R7, status: Holds|Violated, witnesses}>, validator_witness_hash, cert_self_hash }`.
- **PlacedRom** — `{ bank_assignments, legalized: Vec<LegalizedSection>, symbol_table, layout: LayoutPlan, thunk_pool, placed_rom_self_hash }`.
- **EncodedRom** — `{ gb_bytes (with BuildIdentityBlock.build_hash patched in place), sym_lines, lst_text, identity: { build_hash, encoded_rom_self_hash, encoder_version } }`.
- **PlacementProfile** — `StrictOnePerBank` (bring-up debug; each expert alone) | `Budgeted` (default; experts alone, small kernels packed) | `PackedExperts` (tight M3+; multi-expert co-residency by reachability-class compatibility).

## Sub-pass algorithms

**AsmIR Codegen (§8.8):** Per SchedSlice: emit slice header with AssertBank + liveness bump; one lowering rule per SchedOp variant; kernel binding looks up `(kernel_id, target_residency)` in KernelRegistry, emits in-bank CALL or `LegalizationOp::FarCall` (thunk inserted at PlacedRom time); continuation header emission; epoch trampolines acquire bank lease once at entry, release at exit; expert entry stubs receive BC/return DE; **no raw MBC writes allowed** — all banking via F-A4 `lease_rom_switchable` / `release_bank` helpers.

**ReachabilityValidation (§9.2–§9.3):** Build typed edge graph from LegalizedSection instructions; EdgeKind variants: Call, JumpRelative, JumpAbsolute, FarCallViaThunk, FallThrough, InterruptReturn, PanicJump, RstVector, IndirectJump. Enumerate roots (interrupt vectors, mode continuation entries, fault entries, panic entry, harness polling section). Propagate classes in fixed-point: `O(nodes · edges · 6)` (6 = lattice height). Verify seven rules: R1 IsrReachable in Bank0/HRAM/FixedWram only; R2 no MBC writes outside BankLeaseProtected on privileged paths; R3 MachineEffects match PrivilegeClass; R4 no switchable-bank dependency on ISR/resume paths; R5 no lease reentrancy; R6 every continuation reachable from mode entry; R7 fault-path residency (Bank0/HRAM/FixedWram only).

**PlacedRom (§10.2; nine sub-sub-passes):** (1) bank assignment via profile-driven first-fit (Budgeted) or first-fit-decreasing (PackedExperts); (2) far-call thunk insertion via F-A4 `BankingPreLayoutLowering`, deduplicated per `(target_bank, target_symbol)`; (3) F-A1 iterative monotone branch relaxation (widen JR→JP NZ+JP, NOP padding until convergence); (4) stable symbol naming by role then SymbolName; (5) residency enforcement (KernelResidency directives + ISR rule forces Bank0); (6) bank-switch coalescing (Budgeted/PackedExperts; disabled in StrictOnePerBank); (7) deterministic section ordering per role (Bank0Nucleus < BankingThunk < CommonKernel < ... < ExpertPayload < ConstData < TraceOnly); (8) common-bank vs expert-bank partitioning; (9) continuation-target validity check.

**EncodedRom (§11):** F-A1 ROM builder assembles `.gb` (no choice points); patch BuildIdentityBlock.build_hash in place (zero, hash, overwrite with SHA256); emit `.sym` line-by-line; emit `.lst` instruction-by-instruction; compute `encoded_rom_self_hash = SHA256(full_gb_bytes)`.

## Invariants

**Codegen (§8.6):** every SchedOp emitted exactly once; every MBC write has banking provenance from `gbf-runtime::banking`; every BankLease balanced; every FarCall resolves; every SemanticCheckpointId in schema.

**Reachability (§9):** lattice finite-height; class propagation monotonic; **ISR rule is computed, not declared** — F-B15 classification overrides F-B13 annotation if they disagree.

**PlacedRom (§10.5 global constraints):** no section crosses bank boundary post-relax; all relative branches in range; all expert sections satisfy residency rules; all SRAM/WRAM arenas fit; all continuation targets valid + reachable; **bank packing deterministic** (property-tested byte-equality on regeneration); future-reservation byte ranges respected.

**Named:** BACK-1..7 (ISR safety, banking discipline, continuation validity, placement monotonicity); REACH-1..7 (the seven reachability rules).

## Diagnostic algebra (four closed code families)

**ASM-***: LOWERING-MISSING, NUCLEUS-COLLISION, MBC-RAW-WRITE, MBC-PROVENANCE-VIOLATION, KERNEL-NOT-FOUND, OP-MISSING, LEASE-IMBALANCE, FARCALL-UNRESOLVED, CHECKPOINT-UNKNOWN.

**REACH-***: ISR-BANK-DEPENDENCY, PRIVILEGED-MBC-WRITE, PRIVILEGE-VIOLATION, PRIVILEGED-SWITCHABLE-DEPENDENCY, LEASE-REENTRANCY, VECTOR-NOT-ROOT (deferred to bd-3s0s), CLASS-DISAGREEMENT (F-B15 wins over F-B13), CONTINUATION-UNREACHABLE, DEAD-CODE (Soft unless `no_dead_code` objective set), FAULT-PATH-NONRESIDENT-DATA.

**PLACE-***: EXPERT-TOO-LARGE, EXPERT-COMMON-BANK-PRESSURE, BANK0-PRESSURE, ROM-OVERFLOW, RELAX-FAILED, VECTOR-NOT-FIRST-CLASS, PROFILE-INFEASIBLE (may trigger F-B16 profile promotion), FAR-CALL-RESIDENCY, COMMON-EXPERT-MIX, ISR-NON-BANK0, CONTINUATION-CROSS-BANK, SECTION-CROSSES-BANK, EXPERT-RESIDENCY, ARENA-OVERFLOW-{WRAM,HRAM,SRAM}, CONTINUATION-INVALID, NONDETERMINISM, FUTURE-RESERVATION-COLLISION, COST-DRIFT (Soft in M2, Hard in M3+).

**ENC-***: DRIFT (encoded byte count != PlacedRom expected — catastrophic), NONDETERMINISM (two encoded ROMs of same PlacedRom differ — catastrophic), HEADER-CHECKSUM, BUILD-HASH-PATCH.

## Cache keys (K12–K15)

- **K12 (AsmIRCacheKey)** — schedule_pack_hash, resolved_compile_policy_hash, target_profile_hash, runtime_nucleus_hash, schedule_cost_report_hash, kernel_registry_hash, asmir_codegen_version.
- **K13 (ReachabilityCacheKey)** — asmir_bundle_hash, reachability_walker_version. PROFILE-AGNOSTIC.
- **K14 (PlacedRomCacheKey)** — asmir_bundle_hash, reachability_report_hash, placement_profile, layout_algorithm_version, overlay_plan_hash, arena_plan_hash, rom_window_plan_hash, schedule_cost_report_hash.
- **K15 (EncodedRomCacheKey)** — placed_rom_self_hash, cartridge_header_hash, build_identity_args_hash, encoder_version.

(Note: K-key numbering here is per F-B15 RFC; differs from F-B17 cross-stage K14/K11/K12 numbering — both are internally consistent.)

## Determinism (§2.3, §10.4)

Same SchedulePack + TargetProfile + PlacementProfile ⇒ **byte-identical** `.gb`. Achieved via: canonical sorting (sections by ExpertId, hotness, symbol name); lex-ordered symbol naming per role; first-fit(-decreasing) bin-packing (deterministic given sorted input); property-tested regeneration (two consecutive PlacedRom builds assert byte-equality).

## Interaction with F-B16

F-B15 is OUTSIDE the inner refinement loop (which wraps F-B5–F-B11). F-B16 may request a Stage-12 retry under a different PlacementProfile: `Budgeted` PLACE-EXPERT-COMMON-BANK-PRESSURE → propose `RepairProposal::ProfilePromotion(PackedExperts)`. F-B15 itself never retries — it is idempotent under fixed inputs.

## Open questions / risks

1. MBC5 bank-switch timing — EmulationModel vs hardware latency; F-B15 trusts F-B14's envelope.
2. Cross-bank thunk reentrancy after thunk insertion — F-B13 resource state cert is on pre-thunk graph; F-B15 re-verifies after legalization (R5 defense-in-depth).
3. Vectors as reachability roots deferred to bd-3s0s (T-A1x.2); REACH-VECTOR-NOT-ROOT fires until that lands.
4. Dead-code Soft by default; Hard if `CompileObjective.no_dead_code` set.
5. PLACE-COST-DRIFT Soft in M2; Hard in M3+ when F-B16 drives refinement.

## Test surface (closure gate)

- Fixture ROMs: single-slice, multi-mode, mixed residencies.
- Golden-byte tests: PlacedRom + EncodedRom regeneration assert byte-equality.
- Reachability-forgery tests: inject violations of all 7 rules; validator rejects each.
- Bank-packing determinism property test.
- ReachabilityValidation cross-check via gbf-verify independent walker (two-implementation defense).
- gbf-emu boot smoke (F-A7 territory).
- map.json consumers (gbf-debug breakpoints, harness command-block offset, persistence persistent-page layout).
- Provenance roundtrip with SchedulePack ids.

## Milestone alignment

- **M2 closure**: ReachabilityValidation integrated; `PlacementProfile::Budgeted` emits one shared common-bank kernel + one expert payload bank; encoded `.gb` diffable against ScheduleOracle (once F-C3 lands); map.json/.sym/.lst schemas stable.
- **M3+**: `PlacementProfile::PackedExperts` available for tight multi-expert builds; per-RuntimeMode section sequences support future mode-switch policy (F-D5). No additional Stage-12 work for M3.

## How this serves the overarching goal

F-B15 is the bridge from IR to bytes — the final proof that the entire type stack is safe to deploy. Its four sub-passes are inseparable because ReachabilityValidation reasons about the typed edge graph codegen produces and the bank assignments PlacedRom creates; PlacedRom enforces the residency rules ReachabilityValidation computes; EncodedRom is tiny because all choices are made upstream. Determinism, closed diagnostics, and dual-implementation cross-checks (for reachability certificates) are the load-bearing properties that make the whole pipeline trustworthy in production.
design:
# F-B15 Implementation design (Stage 12 — four sub-passes shipping as ONE bead)

## Crate / module structure
- **Owner crate:** `gbf-codegen`
- **Modules:** `gbf-codegen::backend::asmir_codegen`, `::reachability`, `::placed_rom`, `::encoded_rom`. Shared `::types`, `::diagnostics`, `::cache` (K12–K15).
- **Public types:** `AsmIRBundle`, `ReachabilityCertificate`, `ReachabilityClassSet`, `PlacedRom`, `EncodedRom`, `LegalizedSection`, `SymbolTable`, `ThunkSection`, `LayoutPlan`, `MapJson`, `PlacementProfile`, `EdgeKind`, `ReachabilityFinding`, `ReachabilityRoots`.
- **Public entries:** `build_asmir(...) -> AsmIRBundle`; `validate_reachability(...) -> ReachabilityCertificate`; `place_rom(...) -> PlacedRom`; `encode_rom(...) -> EncodedRom`. Each cache-wrapped under its respective K-key.

## Why four sub-passes ship together

ReachabilityValidation must reason about codegen's typed edge graph; PlacedRom must enforce ReachabilityValidation's rules; EncodedRom only emits what PlacedRom decided. Splitting would break typed seams. They ship as ONE bead but with four explicit per-sub-pass implementation gates (PR-able sub-tasks under one Feature).

## Implementation phases (ordered, all four required for closure)

### Sub-pass 1: AsmIR Codegen

1. **Phase 1.1** — `AsmIRBundle` + `AsmIRProvenanceEntry` with `SourceKind` enum (SchedOp, KernelBody, ContinuationHeader, EpochTrampoline, ExpertEntryStub, TensorPayload, LutPayload, RuntimeNucleus, CartridgeHeader, BuildIdentityBlock).
2. **Phase 1.2** — Per `SchedOp` lowering rule: slice header (AssertBank + liveness bump), kernel binding (`KernelRegistry` lookup; emit in-bank CALL or `LegalizationOp::FarCall`), continuation header emission, epoch trampoline (acquire lease once at entry, release at exit), expert entry stub. **No raw MBC writes** — all banking via F-A4 `lease_rom_switchable` / `release_bank`.
3. **Phase 1.3** — Provenance map: every `(SectionId, ItemIndex)` has one entry. Gate: ASM-OP-MISSING fixture.
4. **Phase 1.4** — K12 (AsmIRCacheKey) integration.

### Sub-pass 2: ReachabilityValidation

5. **Phase 2.1** — Typed edge graph: `EdgeKind` (Call, JumpRelative, JumpAbsolute, FarCallViaThunk, FallThrough, InterruptReturn, PanicJump, RstVector, IndirectJump).
6. **Phase 2.2** — Six-class lattice: `IsrReachable`, `YieldResumeReachable`, `FaultPathReachable`, `HarnessEntryReachable`, `BankLeaseProtected`, `NormalOnly`. Fixed-point closure `O(nodes · edges · 6)`.
7. **Phase 2.3** — Root enumeration: interrupt vectors, mode-level continuation entries, fault entries, panic entry, harness polling. Gate: REACH-VECTOR-NOT-ROOT until bd-3s0s (T-A1x.2) lands first-class placement.
8. **Phase 2.4** — Seven rules: R1 ISR residency, R2 no privileged MBC writes, R3 effect/privilege match, R4 no switchable-bank ISR/resume dep, R5 no lease reentrancy, R6 continuations reachable, R7 fault-path residency. Each rule emits `Holds | Violated` with typed witness.
9. **Phase 2.5** — Disagreement detection vs F-B13 annotation: emit `REACH-CLASS-DISAGREEMENT`; **F-B15 wins**.
10. **Phase 2.6** — `reachability.cert.json` with `validator_witness_hash` for independent cross-validation by `gbf-verify`.
11. **Phase 2.7** — K13 (ReachabilityCacheKey) integration — PROFILE-AGNOSTIC.

### Sub-pass 3: PlacedRom

12. **Phase 3.1** — Bank assignment per `PlacementProfile`: StrictOnePerBank (each expert alone), Budgeted (default; first-fit), PackedExperts (FFD with reachability-class compatibility).
13. **Phase 3.2** — Far-call thunk insertion via F-A4 `BankingPreLayoutLowering`: lease-acquire + CALL + release; deduplicated per `(target_bank, target_symbol)`.
14. **Phase 3.3** — F-A1 iterative monotone branch relaxation: widen JR → JP NZ + JP; NOP padding until convergence. Gate: layout_iterations finite + bounded.
15. **Phase 3.4** — Stable symbol naming: per role then SymbolName; lex order.
16. **Phase 3.5** — Residency enforcement: validate against RomWindowPlan + ISR rule forces Bank0.
17. **Phase 3.6** — Bank-switch coalescing (Budgeted/PackedExperts; disabled in StrictOnePerBank).
18. **Phase 3.7** — Section ordering per role (Bank0Nucleus < BankingThunk < CommonKernel < ... < ExpertPayload < ConstData < TraceOnly).
19. **Phase 3.8** — Continuation-target validity check.
20. **Phase 3.9** — Global constraints §10.5 (no section crosses bank; branches in range; residency rules; arena fits; continuation reachable; bank packing deterministic; future-reservation ranges respected).
21. **Phase 3.10** — K14 (PlacedRomCacheKey) — integrates all spatial plans + profile + cost report.

### Sub-pass 4: EncodedRom

22. **Phase 4.1** — F-A1 ROM builder assembles `.gb` (no choice points).
23. **Phase 4.2** — `BuildIdentityBlock.build_hash` patch-in-place: zero field, `SHA256(rom_bytes)`, overwrite.
24. **Phase 4.3** — `.sym` (RGBDS `BB:AAAA name` lex-sorted).
25. **Phase 4.4** — `.lst` instruction-by-instruction with provenance comments.
26. **Phase 4.5** — `encoded_rom_self_hash = SHA256(full_gb_bytes)`.
27. **Phase 4.6** — `map.json` definitive address map (consumed by gbf-debug, gbf-emu, gbf-bench, harness, persistence).
28. **Phase 4.7** — K15 (EncodedRomCacheKey).

### Final phases

29. **Phase 5 — Cross-stage integration tests.** F-B14 envelopes in budget.json; F-A7 gbf-emu boot smoke; F-A8 gbf-debug map.json consumption; F-D1 persistence reads persistent-page layout; F-F2 gbf-verify independent reachability walker cross-check.
30. **Phase 6 — E2E verify-packet.** `scripts/review/f-b15/verify-packet.sh`.

## Structured tracing catalog

**Top-level spans:**
- `gbf.compile.stage12_asmir_codegen` — `mode`, `section_count`, `provenance_entry_count`, `bundle_hash`.
- `gbf.compile.stage12_reachability` — `roots_count`, `class_summary: {per_class_byte_counts}`, `findings: {rule, status}`, `disagreement_count`, `dead_code_section_count`, `cert_self_hash`.
- `gbf.compile.stage12_placed_rom` — `placement_profile`, `bank_count_used`, `thunk_count`, `layout_iterations`, `global_constraints_summary`, `placed_rom_self_hash`.
- `gbf.compile.stage12_encoded_rom` — `gb_bytes_len`, `build_hash`, `encoded_rom_self_hash`, `sym_lines_count`, `lst_text_len`.

**Events:**
- `gbf.compile.codegen.slice_lowered` — `mode`, `slice_id`, `op_count`, `section_id`.
- `gbf.compile.codegen.kernel_bound` — `kernel_spec`, `target_residency`, `call_kind: InBank|FarCall`.
- `gbf.compile.reach.root_pinned` — `kind`, `symbol`, `address`.
- `gbf.compile.reach.class_propagated` — `section_id`, `class_set`.
- `gbf.compile.reach.rule_finding` — `rule: R1..R7`, `status`, `witness?`.
- `gbf.compile.reach.disagreement` — `section_id`, `f_b13_annotation`, `f_b15_computed`.
- `gbf.compile.place.bank_assigned` — `section_id`, `bank`, `slack_bytes`.
- `gbf.compile.place.thunk_inserted` — `target_bank`, `target_symbol`, `thunk_address`.
- `gbf.compile.place.branch_relaxed` — `section_id`, `byte_offset`, `from`, `to`.
- `gbf.compile.encode.byte_patched` — `field`, `address`, `value`.
- `gbf.compile.stage.diagnostic` — closed-enum emission.

## Test plan

### Unit tests
- `stage12_asmir_lowering.rs` — every SchedOp → expected AsmIR pattern.
- `stage12_provenance_completeness.rs` — every `(section_id, item_index)` has provenance.
- `stage12_no_raw_mbc.rs` — compile-fail test: any raw MBC write → `ASM-MBC-RAW-WRITE`.
- `stage12_reach_edge_graph.rs` — EdgeKind enumeration over all SchedOp lowerings.
- `stage12_reach_lattice.rs` — six-class join; monotone propagation.
- `stage12_reach_seven_rules.rs` — one fixture per rule × {Holds, Violated}.
- `stage12_reach_disagreement.rs` — F-B13 annotation vs F-B15 computed; F-B15 wins.
- `stage12_place_three_profiles.rs` — StrictOnePerBank/Budgeted/PackedExperts byte-identical determinism per profile.
- `stage12_place_thunk_dedup.rs` — same `(target_bank, target_symbol)` shares one thunk.
- `stage12_place_branch_relax.rs` — monotone convergence; bounded iterations.
- `stage12_place_global_constraints.rs` — all 7 invariants checked.
- `stage12_encode_build_hash_patch.rs` — zero/hash/patch round-trip.
- `stage12_encode_map_json.rs` — schema round-trip; symbol resolution; arena byte ranges.
- `stage12_encode_sym_lst.rs` — RGBDS format + listing provenance.
- `stage12_k12_k13_k14_k15_injectivity.rs` — F-B17 conformance per key.

### Fixture tests (`fixtures/backend/`)
- `pass/single_mode_strict_per_bank.json` → .gb → byte-identical regen.
- `pass/budgeted_default.json` → .gb.
- `pass/packed_experts.json` → .gb.
- `pass/multi_mode_section_partitioning.json` → .gb.
- `reject/asm_<code>.json` × 9 (ASM- diagnostics).
- `reject/reach_<code>.json` × ~10 (REACH- diagnostics).
- `reject/place_<code>.json` × ~18 (PLACE- diagnostics).
- `reject/enc_<code>.json` × 4 (ENC- diagnostics).
- `reject/seven_rules_R1.json` … `R7.json` — reachability rule violations.
- `reject/non_deterministic_regen.json` — synthetic non-determinism; verify detection.

### Property tests
- `prop_place_bank_packing_deterministic` — 100-iter shuffled input → identical bank_assignments + legalized + bytes.
- `prop_reach_lattice_monotone` — class propagation only grows.
- `prop_branch_relax_terminates` — bounded iterations per legalized section.
- `prop_thunk_dedup_complete` — every cross-bank call resolves through deduplicated thunk pool.
- `prop_encoded_rom_byte_identical_regen` — two encodes of same PlacedRom byte-equal.

### Determinism + cache tests
- `determinism_per_profile_byte_identical_gb` — 2x build per profile.
- `cache_K12_K13_K14_K15_independent` — each key independently caches.
- `cache_K13_profile_agnostic` — K13 hit across profile changes (PROFILE-AGNOSTIC).
- `cache_K14_profile_sensitive` — K14 misses on profile change.
- `cache_failure_memo_replay` per key.
- `cache_poisoning_recovery` per key.

### Cross-stage integration
- `stage12_from_sched_ir.rs` — slice ops consumed without modification.
- `stage12_from_cost_report.rs` — per-mode envelopes embedded in budget.json.
- `stage12_to_gbf_emu.rs` — encoded ROM loads + boots in gbf-emu (F-A7).
- `stage12_to_gbf_debug.rs` — `.sym` + `.lst` + map.json consumed by gbf-debug.
- `stage12_to_gbf_bench.rs` — cycle annotations consumed.
- `stage12_to_gbf_verify.rs` — independent reachability walker cross-check; certificate matches.
- `stage12_to_persistence.rs` — map.json persistent-page layout matches F-D1 expectations.

### E2E verify-packet (`scripts/review/f-b15/verify-packet.sh`)
1. Run all stage-12 tests.
2. Compile sample LM through full pipeline under each `PlacementProfile`; produce .gb + .sym + .lst + map.json + reachability_report.json + placed_rom_plan.json + certs/reachability.cert.json + budget.json + compiler_feedback.json.
3. Determinism: 2x build per profile; SHA256 byte-equality on every artifact.
4. K12/K13/K14/K15 cache hit/miss equivalence.
5. K13 profile-agnostic check; K14 profile-sensitive check.
6. Independent reachability walker (`gbf-verify reachability check --cert=...`) cross-checks; cert matches.
7. `gbf-emu boot --rom=<.gb>` smoke test: harness boot sequence executes without crash.
8. `gbf debug` map.json consumption: breakpoint resolution by symbol name + address.
9. Synthetic reachability-forgery test: modify cert; verifier rejects.
10. Bank-packing determinism property test: 100-iter shuffled inputs → byte-identical.
11. Emit `f_b15_packet.json` with per-profile artifact hashes, bank counts, thunk counts, layout iterations, reachability summary, build_hash, encoded_rom_self_hash, diagnostics.
12. Exit 0 on green.

## CLI / debug integration
- `gbf compile --stage=backend --profile=<...> --inputs=<dir> --out=<rom_dir>`.
- `gbf compile build --inputs=<dir> --out=<rom_dir>` — full pipeline including Stage 12.
- `gbf debug rom inspect --rom=<.gb>` — pretty-print bank map + symbol table.
- `gbf debug reach inspect --report=<reachability_report.json>` — per-section class + findings.
- `gbf debug reach verify --cert=<reachability.cert.json>` — independent re-validation.
- `gbf debug place inspect --plan=<placed_rom_plan.json>` — bank assignments + thunks + layout iterations.
- `gbf debug encode diff --left=<rom_a.gb> --right=<rom_b.gb>` — byte-diff for non-determinism investigation.
- `gbf debug envelope --stage=backend`.

## Performance budget
- Sub-pass 1 (AsmIR codegen): < 300 ms on M3 sample LM.
- Sub-pass 2 (Reachability): < 200 ms.
- Sub-pass 3 (PlacedRom): < 500 ms.
- Sub-pass 4 (EncodedRom): < 100 ms.
- Total Stage 12 wall-clock: < 1.5 s.
- Combined memory ceiling: < 128 MiB peak.
- Cache hit replays: < 50 ms per key.

comments.text:
## F-B13: Backend — AsmIR codegen + ReachabilityValidation + PlacedRom + EncodedRom (Stage 12)

### What this is

The headline backend stage with four sub-passes (`planv0.md` line 1496):

1. **AsmIR codegen**: lower `GbSchedIR` slices into `AsmIR` sections via `gbf-asm` builders. Compiler-generated code uses `BankLease` pseudo-ops only — no raw MBC writes.
2. **ReachabilityValidation**: compute (not trust) ISR-reachable / yield-resume-reachable / fault-path-reachable / harness-entry-reachable / bank-lease-protected / normal-only classes. Validate ISR locality, no forbidden MBC writes on privileged paths, no switchable-bank dep on ISR or resume paths, no illegal reentrancy through bank guards, no fault path on non-resident data. Emits `certs/reachability.cert.json`.
3. **PlacedRom**: layout via `PlacementProfile::{StrictOnePerBank, Budgeted, PackedExperts}`, branch relax, far-call thunks, bank-switch coalescing, deterministic section ordering, residency enforcement.
4. **EncodedRom**: bytes only. `.gb` + `.sym` + `.lst`. Tiny encoder.

### Why this matters

Backend is where structural correctness becomes a real ROM. ReachabilityValidation is the safety pass that catches bugs that would otherwise survive until cartridge testing.

### Design sketch

```rust
pub fn codegen_asm(sched: &GbSchedIR, kernels: &KernelRegistry) -> Vec<Section>;
pub fn validate_reachability(sections: &[Section]) -> Result<ReachabilityReport, ReachabilityError>;
pub fn place_rom(sections: Vec<Section>, profile: PlacementProfile) -> PlacedRom;
pub fn encode_rom(placed: PlacedRom, header: CartridgeHeader) -> EncodedRom;
```

### Cross-feature deps

- F-A1 (gbf-asm) for AsmIR + encoder
- F-B11 GbSchedIR
- F-A4 BankLease ABI (validated by reachability)
- F-H1, F-H2 KernelRegistry + kernel impls

### Confidence: HIGH on structure, MEDIUM on reachability completeness — getting all six privilege classes right is the engineering challenge.

comments.text:
## Agent Instructions

**Target crate**: `gbf-train` (export pipeline) + relies on T2.3 (bd-27n) preflight.
**Target file(s)**: `gbf-train/src/export.rs` (extend or new), `gbf-train/src/shadow.rs` (re-validation hook).

**Reference**: bd-1hv 2026-04-26 session ("Per-export re-validation"), T2.3 refinement (bd-27n), T2.5 (bd-177).

### Implementation Notes

Add an explicit re-validation stage to the export pipeline that runs the same preflight from T2.3 against the **current** `RuntimeChromeBudget` (not the training-time pinned one).

1. **Inputs.**
   - The just-exported `ArtifactCore` + lowering artifacts.
   - The training-time pinned `RuntimeChromeBudget` (from the run manifest).
   - The current production `RuntimeChromeBudget` (re-emitted from the live shell).

2. **Action.**
   - Compare the two `runtime_nucleus_hash`es. If equal, skip the byte-delta comparison and run the standard export-time preflight against the pinned budget.
   - If they differ:
     - Compute per-slot byte deltas.
     - Re-run the preflight against the **current** budget (this is the authoritative check for what production will actually receive).
     - Emit `BudgetDriftReport`:
       ```rust
       pub struct BudgetDriftReport {
           pub training_hash: Hash256,
           pub current_hash: Hash256,
           pub training_modules: BTreeSet<RuntimeShellModule>,
           pub current_modules: BTreeSet<RuntimeShellModule>,
           pub slot_deltas: Vec<RomBudgetSlotDelta>,
           pub wram_delta: WramReservedDelta,
           pub sram_delta: i32,
       }
       ```
   - If `fits_envelope == false` against the current budget, **block export**. Hard failure.
   - If only `risk_flags` fire, surface them but do not block.

3. **Diagnostic.**

   ```
   Budget drift detected:
     Training-time:  runtime_nucleus_hash=0xAB12...  modules={Boot,…,VideoCommit}
     At export:      runtime_nucleus_hash=0xCD34...  modules={Boot,…,VideoCommit,Persistence}
     ExpertBank.usable_bytes: 15488 -> 15104 (delta -384, persistence module added).
     Re-running preflight against current budget...
     Expert payload demand=14976 bytes. PASS (margin 128 bytes).
   ```

4. **Where it runs.**
   - Phase E (HardenAndSelect) export pipeline.
   - F8 shadow_compile pipeline (so drift is caught early during training, not only at final export).

### Coordination with T2.5

T2.5 prevents the production shell from drifting silently. T2.7 handles the case where drift is intentional and the trainer needs to react. They are complementary, not redundant.

### Acceptance Criteria

```bash
cargo check -p gbf-train                                       # Compiles
cargo test -p gbf-train -- export::revalidation_no_drift        # Same hash: standard preflight runs
cargo test -p gbf-train -- export::revalidation_drift_passing   # Drift but fits: warning, export proceeds
cargo test -p gbf-train -- export::revalidation_drift_blocking  # Drift and breaks fit: export blocked
cargo clippy -p gbf-train -- -D warnings                        # No warnings
# Verify: BudgetDriftReport is emitted as JSON to artifacts/runs/<run_id>/budget_drift.json
# Verify: blocked export returns a non-zero exit code with a structured error
```

### Constitution Checkpoints

- §I.4: Re-validation is the verifiable reward at export — exit 0 means production fit is confirmed.
- §V.1: BudgetDriftReport is JSON.
- §V.3: Diagnostic on block lists both hashes, modules, slot deltas, and the offending preflight failure.
- §III.1: Re-validation runs at shadow_compile too, so drift is caught well before final export.

title: T4.4: Implement logit distillation from frozen teacher
description: During phases C and D, compute KL divergence between the student's logits and the frozen teacher's logits on the same input. Weight by lambda_distill. The teacher forward pass is run in no-grad mode. This provides a stable gradient signal that compensates for the noisy STE gradients from ternary projection. The distillation loss should be logged separately from the LM loss so quality vs distillation tradeoffs are visible.

comments.text:
## T-B1.2: L1 — Request-to-AsmIR pipeline (N = 16, WramSmoke layout)

### Background

L1 isolates **the new IR + codegen path** from banking. It uses a real `ComputeBringupRequest`, a real (skeletal) `MatmulI8Node` IR, and a real codegen lowering — but with the `WramSmoke` operand layout so banking pressure does not muddy the failure signal.

### Why WramSmoke is necessary

The naive draft of this RFC said L1 has "no banking" and that `ComputeBringupRequest` requires "distinct nonzero ROM banks". Those two statements cannot both be true. The `WramSmoke` operand-layout variant resolves the contradiction:

- `OperandLayout::WramSmoke` is allowed only for `matrix_dim = 16`.
- `WramSmoke` is **not** valid for closure artifacts or the L5 report.
- L0 (hand-authored) uses `WramSmoke`-shaped layout implicitly; L1 (codegen) uses the variant explicitly; L2 onwards uses `DistinctRomBanks`.

This keeps the smoke profile out of the closure path while still letting L1 run without F-A4 BankLease pressure.

### What L1 proves

- `ComputeBringupRequest` validation rejects bad shapes, wrong tile sizes, same-bank operands, bank-0 operands.
- `MatmulI8Node` IR validates as a single-node graph.
- The lowering is deterministic — same request hashes to same AsmIR hashes to same ROM bytes.
- The compiled kernel produces the same bytes as L0's hand-authored kernel.

### Failure mode it isolates

If L1 fails after L0 passed: the codegen path itself is wrong, not infra.

### Subtask plan

- **T-B1.2.1** `ComputeBringupRequest` type + validation (incl. `KernelImplId::QuarterSquareTableV1` pin, `TileSize`, `YieldQuantum`, target-profile validation).
- **T-B1.2.2** `OperandLayout` enum + `RomBankId` + smoke restriction validation.
- **T-B1.2.3** `MatmulI8Node` IR (`gbf-ir::infer`) + single-node graph invariant.
- **T-B1.2.4** Codegen lowering — `request → IR → AsmIR` (L1 path, deterministic).
- **T-B1.2.5** L1 emulator test (WramSmoke layout, byte-exact vs reference).

### Acceptance gates

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- f_b1_request_validation_accepts_l1_smoke_layout
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- f_b1_request_validation_rejects_smoke_layout_for_n_gt_16
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- compute_bringup_request_rejects_same_bank
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- compute_bringup_request_rejects_bank0_operand
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- compute_bringup_request_rejects_bad_tile
cargo test -p gbf-ir -- f_b1_matmul_ir_single_node_shape
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- f_b1_l1_lowering_is_deterministic
cargo test -p gbf-emu -- f_b1_l1_compiled_matmul_matches_reference
```

### RFC reference

`history/rfcs/F-B1-compute-bringup.md` §7.3, §7.4, §8.2.

### Dependencies

- T-B1.0 (foundations) — uses shape types, reference, table, fixtures.
- T-B1.1 (L0) — provides the canonical kernel structure.
- F-A1 (gbf-asm) — encoder.

title: F-S3.10: 5-gram Kneser-Ney baseline — KnEffectiveCounts + D-rule + chunked-reset scoring + CanonicalKnCountsWrite + hand-counted oracle fixture
description:
## Context

The 5-gram modified Kneser-Ney baseline (RFC D4) is the comparator for H3 / Q1: `val_bpc_char_fp(s) < bpc_kn5_baseline - 0.05`. RFC §3 KnEffectiveCounts pins that `C_5` is raw surface count, while `C_2..C_4` are continuation counts. Discounts are computed via the D-rule on count-of-counts of those effective tables.

Per third-round Patch 12, the scorer MUST back off to `P_KN_{k-1}` when `c(w_{i-k+1..i-1}) = 0`; per third-round Patch 6, baseline fitting aborts with Fail-baseline when any required `n_1, n_2, n_3` is zero for k ∈ {2,3,4,5}; `n_4` may be zero (D_3+ contributes zero from n_4/n_3).

`CanonicalKnCountsWrite` (RFC §3) pins serialization order/encoding for `counts_blob_sha256`.

## Why this matters

H2 hand-counted oracle gate (1e-12 in f64) is the integrity check on KN math. H3 / Q1 depends entirely on bpc_kn5_baseline being correctly computed. A subtle KN bug (e.g., raw surface counts at lower orders, or wrong continuation-count denominator) would silently invalidate every Q1 verdict.

## Deliverables

1. `gbf-experiments/src/s3/baseline/kn_effective_counts.rs`:
   - `pub fn c5_raw_counts(corpus_train_post: &TextCharSeq) -> BTreeMap<NgramKey<5>, u64>` (raw 5-gram counts)
   - `pub fn c_continuation_counts(corpus_train_post: &TextCharSeq, k: usize) -> BTreeMap<NgramKey<K>, u64>` for k ∈ {2,3,4} (number of distinct left contexts)
   - `pub fn count_of_counts<K>(table: &BTreeMap<NgramKey<K>, u64>) -> BTreeMap<u64, u64>` (n_j table)
2. `gbf-experiments/src/s3/baseline/discounts.rs`:
   - `pub struct KnDiscounts { y_k: f64, d_1: f64, d_2: f64, d_3p: f64 }`
   - `pub fn fit_discounts(coc: &BTreeMap<u64, u64>) -> Result<KnDiscounts, BaselineError>`
   - Pre-fit guard: returns `BaselineError::DiscountPreconditionsViolated { order, missing: Vec<u64> }` if `n_1`, `n_2`, or `n_3` is zero
   - Bound checks: `D_1 ∈ [0,1]`, `D_2 ∈ [0,2]`, `D_3+ ∈ [0,3]`; out-of-bounds → `BaselineError::DiscountOutOfBounds`
3. `gbf-experiments/src/s3/baseline/conditional.rs`:
   - `pub fn p_kn_5..p_kn_1` per RFC §3 KnConditional
   - **Backoff rule**: if `c(w_{i-k+1..i-1}) = 0`, back off directly to `P_KN_{k-1}(w_i | suffix)` with interpolation weight 1.0
   - All probabilities in f64; f32 forbidden in baseline computation (compile-time guard via newtype `BaselineProb(f64)`)
4. `gbf-experiments/src/s3/baseline/operation.rs`:
   - `s3_fit_kn5(KnBaselineInputs) -> Result<KnBaselineProduct, BaselineError>` (RFC §6.3)
   - `KnBaselineProduct { bpc_kn1_val..bpc_kn5_val, discounts: BTreeMap<u64, KnDiscounts>, counts_summary: CountsSummary, counts_blob_sha256: Hash256, baseline_self_hash: Hash256 }`
5. `gbf-experiments/src/s3/baseline/canonical_counts_write.rs`:
   - The `CanonicalKnCountsWrite` encoder (third-round Patch 6 of RFC):
     - Effective count tables `C_2, C_3, C_4, C_5` serialized in ascending order of `(order, context_token_tuple_lexicographic, target_token_id)`
     - Counts encoded as unsigned little-endian u64
     - No hash-map iteration order, host path, timestamp, build duration, or compression metadata
6. `fixtures/baselines/kn_oracle/`: hand-counted ~512-char fixture with hand-computed expected `bpc_char` to 16 significant decimal digits + hand-computed effective continuation counts for orders 2..4 + hand-computed expected D_1/D_2/D_3+ for each order k ∈ {2,3,4,5}
7. `gbf-experiments/src/s3/schema.rs::s3_baseline_kn5.v1` schema (RFC §11.2)

## Test scaffolding

1. **`gbf-experiments/tests/baseline_kn5_s3.rs`** (O-2) — KN math oracle:
   - bpc_char on fixture matches expected to 1e-12 in f64
   - D_1, D_2, D_3+ within `[0,1], [0,2], [0,3]` respectively
   - Y_k ∈ (0,1) for every k ∈ {2,3,4,5}
   - Backoff path exercised on a context with raw count 0 (assert `P_KN_5(unseen_context, w) == P_KN_4(suffix, w)`)
2. **`gbf-experiments/tests/baseline_proptest_s3.rs`** — proptest:
   - Strategy `valid_count_of_counts()`: random `n_1, n_2, n_3, n_4 > 0`; assert `fit_discounts` returns within bounds
   - Strategy `invalid_count_of_counts_n3_zero()`: random `n_1, n_2 > 0`, `n_3 = 0`; assert `fit_discounts` returns `Err(DiscountPreconditionsViolated)`
   - Strategy `arbitrary_continuation_table_with_smooth_distribution()`: assert `Σ_w P_KN_5(h, w) ≈ 1.0` to 1e-9 in f64
3. **`gbf-experiments/tests/baseline_canonical_counts_write_s3.rs`** — `counts_blob_sha256` deterministic across 10 replays; mutation test: insert HashMap with random iteration order; canonical bytes unchanged
4. **`gbf-experiments/tests/baseline_fail_test_s3.rs`** — Fail-baseline path:
   - Construct a corpus where `n_3 = 0` for k=4
   - Assert `s3_fit_kn5` returns `BaselineError::DiscountPreconditionsViolated { order: 4, missing: vec![3] }`
   - Assert no partial product is emitted
5. **`gbf-experiments/tests/baseline_self_hash_determinism_s3.rs`** — `baseline_self_hash` deterministic across 10 replays
6. **`gbf-experiments/tests/baseline_compile_guard_s3.rs`** — compile-only test asserting `BaselineProb` cannot be constructed from f32 (compile failure if attempted)

## Logging discipline

`s3_fit_kn5` emits structured events:
```
event_name = "s3::baseline::fit_started"
fields: { train_post_char_count, vocab_size, order: 5 }

event_name = "s3::baseline::counts_computed"
fields: { c5_unique_count, c4_unique_count, c3_unique_count, c2_unique_count }

event_name = "s3::baseline::discounts_fit"
fields: { d_1_per_order: [f64; 4], d_2_per_order: [f64; 4], d_3p_per_order: [f64; 4], y_per_order: [f64; 4] }

event_name = "s3::baseline::scoring_complete"
fields: { bpc_kn5_val, bpc_kn4_val, bpc_kn3_val, bpc_kn2_val, bpc_kn1_val, baseline_self_hash, counts_blob_sha256 }

event_name = "s3::baseline::aborted"  (only if Fail-baseline)
fields: { reason, order, missing_count_of_counts }

target = "gbf_experiments::s3::baseline"
```
Subscriber-level test `gbf-experiments/tests/baseline_logging_s3.rs` asserts every event fires for the happy path AND `aborted` fires for the Fail-baseline path.

## E2E acceptance script

`scripts/s3_baseline_verify.sh`:
1. Runs `gbf s3 fit-baseline --manifest fixtures/corpora/tinystories.v2.toml --capture-events /tmp/s3-baseline.ndjson`
2. Asserts NDJSON contains every event listed above
3. Asserts emitted `s3_baseline_kn5.v1` JSON has expected schema
4. Diffs `baseline_self_hash` against pinned expected value (once we have one from a real run)

## Inheritance / non-duplication

- F-S1 D4 used 3-gram add-α; B10 implements the new 5-gram KN that supersedes (RFC InheritanceFromS1 D4 amendment).
- DOES NOT introduce f32 anywhere in the baseline path — f64 is normative (RFC D4); compile-time enforcement via `BaselineProb` newtype.

## Considerations

- The hand-counted fixture must include effective continuation counts AS WELL AS raw counts so reviewers can verify the KnEffectiveCounts split. Third-round Patch 6 specifically called this out.
- Hand-counting to 16 significant decimal digits is ~1 day of careful arithmetic; budget accordingly.
- Falsification F2-broken-S3 (B20) replaces KN with uniform-1/|Sigma|. The handler interface must be a clean trait so B20 can swap implementations cleanly.

## Acceptance

```
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test baseline_kn5_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test baseline_proptest_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test baseline_canonical_counts_write_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test baseline_fail_test_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test baseline_self_hash_determinism_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test baseline_logging_s3
scripts/s3_baseline_verify.sh
```

## Out of scope

- bpc_char primitive (B11)
- val_bpc_ternary scoring path (B11 ArtifactScorer)

## References

- RFC D4; §3 "KnEffectiveCounts / KnDiscounts / KnConditional"; §6.3; §11.2
- F-S1 D4 (superseded)

title: F-B8 T18: storage_plan.json emitter — envelope, AbstractLiveRangeJson, input_identity in result, SortedVec<{key,value}> provenance, null summary on failure
description:
# storage_plan.json emitter

## Why every field matters

The v1 emitter dropped typed fields the schema claimed to carry. v2 review caught:

* `StorageBindingJson` missing `live_range` — round-trip lost the alias non-conflict evidence.
* `StoragePlanReportResult` missing `input_identity` — round-trip lost the cache-key identity, and the body-level `input_identity` was the only place it appeared, which made the full typed product non-recoverable from JSON.
* `BTreeMap` with non-string keys appearing as JSON objects — JSON object keys must be strings; v2 replaces with `SortedVec<{key, value}>` entries.

Every typed field on `StoragePlan` must round-trip. If a field is intentionally absent (e.g. a projection), say so in the RFC; otherwise the field is in the JSON.

## Envelope (RFC §12.1)

```json
{
  "schema": "storage_plan.v1",
  "schema_version": "1.0.0",
  "outcome": "Passed" | "Failed",
  "report_self_hash": "<Hash256 hex>",
  "body": {
    "outcome": "Passed" | "Failed",
    "result": null | { ...StoragePlanReportResult... },
    "diagnostics": [ ...ValidationDiagnostic[]... ],
    "input_identity": { ...StoragePlanInputIdentity... },
    "summary":  null | { ...StoragePlanSummary... }
  }
}
```

Equality law on success: `body.result.input_identity == body.input_identity`. Both must populate; the body-level copy is the convenience view consumers read without parsing `result`.

## StoragePlanReportResult fields

* `input_identity: StoragePlanInputIdentityJson`
* `bindings: SortedVec<StorageBindingJson>`
* `alias_classes: SortedVec<AliasClassJson>`
* `persist_pages: SortedVec<PersistPageDeclJson>`
* `commit_groups: SortedVec<CommitGroupDeclJson>`
* `repair_proposals: SortedVec<RepairProposalJson>`
* `provenance: StorageProvenanceJson`

## StorageBindingJson + AbstractLiveRangeJson

```json
StorageBindingJson := {
  value, materialization, alias_class, live_range, justification
}

AbstractLiveRangeJson := {
  def_node, first_use_node: null|NodeId, last_use_node: null|NodeId,
  lifetime_class, checkpoint_stable: bool
}
```

## Provenance maps

`StorageProvenanceJson.{bindings,alias_classes,persist_pages,commit_groups}` are `SortedVec<{key, value}>` shapes — no JSON objects keyed by non-string ids.

## Failure variant

* `result = null` per `R-NoPartialIR-StoragePlan`.
* `diagnostics` non-empty.
* `body.input_identity` populated.
* `summary = null` (no degenerate zeroed summary — v2 cleanup).
* Envelope `report_self_hash` still computed.

## Self-hash law

`report_self_hash = SelfHash(canonical_json(env with report_self_hash = ZERO_HASH))`. Implement as: zero the field, canonicalize, hash, patch back. Document the law in the emitter.

## SC11 emit-side scan

Before serializing, recursively walk the JSON value tree and assert no key or tag from the closed `ForbiddenStage6SpatialSurface` set appears. Failure emits STORE-018.

## Acceptance

* Round-trip test: `parse(emit(plan)) == plan` byte-for-byte on the routed-FFN fixture.
* Equality law test: `body.result.input_identity == body.input_identity`.
* Failure path test: `result = null`, `summary = null`, diagnostics non-empty, envelope hashed.
* SC11 scan test: no forbidden key appears; legal `WramHot`/`SramPaged`/`RomConst` tags pass.
* Schema-unknown rejection: parser rejects unknown fields (R-UnknownReject).

## Anti-patterns

* Do not omit `live_range` or `input_identity` from `result`.
* Do not emit a degenerate zeroed summary on failure; use `null`.
* Do not encode a `BTreeMap` with non-string keys as a JSON object.
* Do not place `report_self_hash` anywhere except the envelope top-level.

Depends on: T15.
design:
## Test Plan

### Envelope structure

* `envelope_top_level_fields` — exactly `{schema, schema_version, outcome, report_self_hash, body}`.
* `body_fields_passed` — `{outcome, result, diagnostics, input_identity, summary}`.
* `result_fields_on_passed` — `{input_identity, bindings, alias_classes, persist_pages, commit_groups, repair_proposals, provenance}`.

### live_range round-trip

* `storage_binding_json_includes_live_range` — synthetic binding → JSON → parse → identical binding.
* `abstract_live_range_json_optional_use_bounds` — `first_use_node = None` → JSON `"first_use_node": null`; round-trip preserves.

### input_identity in result

* `result_input_identity_present_on_passed` — `result.input_identity` matches `body.input_identity`.
* `result_input_identity_absent_on_failed` — `result = null` on Failed; the body-level `input_identity` is the only copy.
* `equality_law_body_result_identity` — when both present, byte-equal.

### SortedVec<{key, value}> for provenance

* `provenance_bindings_encoded_as_sorted_vec` — JSON shape: `[{"key": ValueIdJson, "value": BindingProvenanceJson}, ...]`. NOT a JSON object with non-string keys.
* `provenance_alias_classes_encoded_as_sorted_vec` — same shape.
* `provenance_persist_pages_encoded_as_sorted_vec` — same.
* `provenance_commit_groups_encoded_as_sorted_vec` — same.
* `provenance_sort_stable_across_runs` — two runs produce byte-identical sorted vec ordering.

### Self-hash law

* `report_self_hash_zero_compute_patch` — emitter zeros `report_self_hash`, canonicalizes, hashes, patches the hash back. Test the three-step procedure explicitly.
* `report_self_hash_only_at_envelope_level` — no nested body field is named `report_self_hash`. Trybuild compile-fail on regression.

### Failure variant

* `failed_envelope_result_is_null` — emitter explicitly emits `"result": null`.
* `failed_envelope_summary_is_null` — emitter explicitly emits `"summary": null`. (v2 cleanup: no zeroed degenerate summary.)
* `failed_envelope_input_identity_populated` — even on Failed, `body.input_identity` is populated with the upstream/policy hashes.
* `failed_envelope_diagnostics_non_empty` — at least one Hard diagnostic.
* `failed_envelope_report_self_hash_computed` — envelope still hashed.

### SC11 emit-side scan

* `sc11_emit_side_scan_legal_tags_pass` — happy plan emits envelope; SC11 scan returns OK.
* `sc11_emit_side_scan_forbidden_key_fires_store_018` — synthetic emitter that injects `"byte_offset": 0` → STORE-018; provenance: `json_path`.

### Schema rejection (R-UnknownReject)

* `parse_rejects_unknown_top_level_field` — input JSON with `"extra_field": ...` → parse error.
* `parse_rejects_unknown_body_field` — same shape.

### Round-trip determinism

* `routed_ffn_round_trip_byte_identical` — emit + re-parse + re-emit → byte-identical to original.

### Canonical JSON rules (inherited from F-B2/F-B4)

* `canonical_json_lex_object_keys` — object keys lex-sorted.
* `canonical_json_integers_only` — no float, no NaN, no Inf, no `-0`.
* `canonical_json_arrays_sorted_when_unordered` — provenance vectors sorted by `(key, value)` canonical bytes.

## Logging Plan

Events:
* `f_b8.envelope.serializing` (INFO) — once: `outcome`.
* `f_b8.envelope.self_hash_computed` (INFO) — once: `report_self_hash`.
* `f_b8.envelope.sc11_scan_passed` (DEBUG) — once on success.
* `f_b8.envelope.sc11_scan_failed` (ERROR) — once on STORE-018 detection: `json_path, forbidden_key`.
* `f_b8.envelope.emitted` (INFO) — once: `outcome, report_self_hash, bytes_written`.

`assert_traced!` for the round-trip test:

```rust
let plan = build_storage_plan_core(synth::tiny_routed_ffn()).unwrap();
let json = emit_storage_plan_json(&plan).unwrap();
let parsed = parse_storage_plan_json(&json).unwrap();
let json2 = emit_storage_plan_json(&parsed).unwrap();
assert_eq!(json, json2);  // byte-identical round-trip
assert_traced!([
  { event: "f_b8.envelope.serializing", outcome: "Passed" },
  { event: "f_b8.envelope.self_hash_computed" },
  { event: "f_b8.envelope.sc11_scan_passed" },
  { event: "f_b8.envelope.emitted" }
]);
```
notes:
## Regression checklist

1. `StoragePlanReportResult` includes `input_identity: StoragePlanInputIdentityJson` (v2 addition).
2. `StorageBindingJson` includes `live_range: AbstractLiveRangeJson` (v2 addition).
3. Equality law: `body.result.input_identity == body.input_identity` on Passed.
4. `StorageProvenanceJson` uses `SortedVec<{key, value}>` shape (v2 fix; v1 had BTreeMap with non-string keys).
5. Failed envelope: `result = null`, `summary = null` (not zeroed).
6. Self-hash law: `report_self_hash = SelfHash(canonical_json(env with report_self_hash = ZERO_HASH))`.
7. `report_self_hash` ONLY at envelope top level — no nested duplicate.
8. SC11 emit-side scan uses closed-key set; legal enum tags pass.
9. R-UnknownReject: parser rejects unknown fields.
10. Canonical JSON: integers only, lex-sorted keys, sorted arrays.
11. `BindingJustificationJson` has exactly two tag variants: `DecisionRule` and `ForcedRecompute`. (v2: no `RefinementPromotion`, no `HintBundle`.)
12. `CommitAtomicityClass` JSON: only `"AllOrNothing"`. (v2: no `"OrderedRecoverable"`.)

title: T-B2.5: Stage 0 schema compatibility + semantic-core-hash + manifest invariants
description:
## What
Implement Stage 0 validation classes 1, 2, 3 (schema epoch, semantic core
hash, manifest invariants) plus the §7.0 lossless in-memory compatibility
adapter path.

## Why
These are the structural identity gates that protect every downstream stage
from spending cycles on a malformed artifact. Class 1 is the simplest and
fastest gate; if it fails, nothing else makes sense.

## Inputs
- T-B2.4 ValidatedInputs scaffolding.
- T-B2.3 artifact_validation.v1 schema (for diagnostic emission).
- `gbf-artifact::manifest::ArtifactManifest` schema.
- A typed registry of compatibility adapters (initially empty; expand as
  schema epochs accumulate).

## Outputs
- Class 1 `SchemaEpochUnsupported` — only acceptable epochs pass.
- Class 1 `SchemaCompatibilityAdapterMissing { observed, target }`.
- Class 1 `SchemaCompatibilityAdapterNotLossless { adapter }`.
- Class 2 `SemanticCoreHashMismatch` (recompute canonical hash; compare to
  manifest record).
- Class 2 `ArtifactTransportManifestMismatch` (transport metadata disagrees
  with `core.manifest`).
- Class 3 `ManifestInvariantViolated { invariant }` for feature/component/
  digest violations.
- The lossless adapter path produces a `Cow::Owned(view)` carrying the
  adapter's hash in `compatibility_adapter_hash`; semantic payload hash
  must remain identical pre- and post-adapter.

## Pitfalls
- Class 2 short-circuits classes referencing manifest-derived state if it
  fails; otherwise validate as much as possible to give reviewers complete
  diagnostics.
- A successful adapter MUST preserve `semantic_core_hash`. If it changes,
  fail with `SchemaCompatibilityAdapterNotLossless` and keep `outcome=Failed`.
- Lossy migration is out of scope (`gbf-migrate` deferred to F-A6b).

## Acceptance
- gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_rejects_schema_epoch_unsupported
- gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_accepts_lossless_in_memory_schema_adapter
- gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_lossless_adapter_preserves_semantic_hash
- gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_lossless_adapter_records_source_and_effective_hashes
- gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_rejects_lossy_schema_adapter
- gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_rejects_unregistered_schema_adapter
- gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_rejects_semantic_core_hash_mismatch
- gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_rejects_manifest_invariant_violated
- gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_rejects_transport_manifest_mismatch

## Refs
- RFC §7.3 (validation classes table), §7.0 (compatibility), §2.1 (Amends planv0).
- planv0 §"ArtifactValidationAndUpgrade" line ~1531.
- Blocks: T-B2.11.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## RFC amendments (2026-05-07)

Two §7.3 / §7.0 tightenings affect this task:

**1. 'Same epoch' = 'same SemVer major' (§7.0)**

The compatibility adapter rule narrows: F-B2 accepts only same-major lossless
in-memory adapters. Cross-major schema changes are rejected with
`SchemaEpochUnsupported`. Formal admissibility:

```text
Accept(adapter) ⇔ adapter.from.major == adapter.to.major
                ∧ adapter.lossless
                ∧ SemanticHash(before) == SemanticHash(after)
```

Cross-major support waits for `gbf-migrate` and an explicit RFC amendment.

Test: rename/add `gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_rejects_cross_major_schema_adapter`
to confirm cross-major adapters are rejected even when registered.

**2. Class 3 expanded with `ArtifactForbiddenBuildIdentityField` (§7.3)**

In addition to `ManifestInvariantViolated`, Stage 0 class 3 now also emits
`ArtifactForbiddenBuildIdentityField { field: FieldPath }` when a manifest,
aux, or lowering carries any of the following forbidden field paths:

```text
/build_identity
/build_identity_block
/compatibility_envelope
/encoded_rom_hash
/backend_identity
/stage12_identity
```

These belong to Stage 12/backend output identity, not frozen input artifacts.

New acceptance test:
`gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_rejects_artifact_forbidden_build_identity_field`

Cross-refs: §7.0 same-major rule, §7.3 class 3 expansion + forbidden paths list.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Owner clarification from bd-1dvs review (2026-05-08)

The bd-1dvs schema fix restored `ArtifactCompatibilityDecision::LosslessInMemoryUpgrade`
to the public §7.0 JSON shape: `from_schema`, `to_schema`, `adapter`,
`adapter_hash`. Therefore `artifact_validation.v1` can only validate that the
recorded decision's `adapter_hash` matches `identity.compatibility_adapter_hash`.

The actual lossless-adapter proof obligation remains here in T-B2.5:
`SemanticHash(before) == SemanticHash(after)` must be checked by the Stage 0
compatibility adapter execution path before the decision is emitted. The
existing acceptance gate `gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_lossless_adapter_preserves_semantic_hash`
is the owner for that proof. If the adapter changes semantic core hash, Stage 0
must fail closed with the existing compatibility failure path rather than emit a
successful `LosslessInMemoryUpgrade` decision.

`bd-3j65` records `ValidatedInputHashes.artifact_manifest_hash` from
`ImportedArtifactView.manifest.manifest_self_hash`. That is only a transport of
the manifest's recorded self-hash; this bead owns the real manifest self-hash
recomputation and mismatch validation before manifest-derived gates proceed.

Acceptance clarification: include a focused Stage 0 rejection for a mismatched
`ArtifactManifest.manifest_self_hash` (or fold it into the existing manifest
invariant rejection with a precise diagnostic) before closing T-B2.5.

title: F-S7 v0.2 T2.3: Centered z-loss baseline + DistillRawDiagnostic enum
description:
## Goal

Pin the centered z-loss baseline at mu = log(n_experts) so that the analytical baseline (when all router logits = 0) is exactly 0 in f64 within 1e-12 tolerance. Introduce the DistillRawDiagnostic enum to honestly represent the no-frozen-teacher case in Phase A.

## Background

Two CLAUDE.md training-loss bullets converge here: (i) router z-loss must name its zero point — uncentered vs centered, and (ii) raw helpers must validate finite/non-negative diagnostics even when the configured weight is zero, except where a helper intentionally skips computation (in which case it is a *contribution* helper, not a *raw* helper).

Distillation has no raw loss before the Phase A teacher exists. The pre-review schema declared distill_loss_raw: LossNatsPerByte, which would force a sentinel (0.0 is wrong because it lies about the value; finite-validation would either fire spuriously or hide a real bug). v0.2 makes it an explicit enum NotAvailable { reason, phase } | Value { loss } — never 0.

## Files

- gbf-train/src/loss/router_z.rs (centered z-loss with mu = log(n_experts) constant)
- gbf-train/src/loss/raw_diagnostics.rs (RawLossDiagnostics struct; DistillRawDiagnostic enum)
- gbf-train/tests/centered_zloss_baseline.rs (deterministic baseline-zero check)
- gbf-experiments/tests/distill_raw_phase_a.rs (asserts NotAvailable variant in Phase A; serde rejects 0.0 substitution)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Centered z-loss with all router logits = 0 yields z_loss_centered = 0 within 1e-12 f64.
- F5-z-uncentered falsification ownership is recorded/moved if full H7 outcome wiring is outside this bead.
- RawLossDiagnostics serialization of distill_loss_raw = 0.0 (instead of the NotAvailable variant) is rejected at deserialization (per RH-5).
- Phase A logs distill_loss_raw as NotAvailable; phase C+ logs Value { loss }.

## Reasoning chain

This task pins two scalars from CLAUDE.md ('name the zero point/baseline'; 'distinguish raw TOML config from phase-effective config'). It blocks T2.1's z-loss baseline assertion and Phase A run logging in T5.3 (RunLog).
acceptance_criteria:
- Centered z-loss with all router logits = 0 yields z_loss_centered = 0 within 1e-12 f64.
- F5-z-uncentered falsification ownership is recorded/moved if full H7 outcome wiring is outside this bead.
- RawLossDiagnostics serialization of distill_loss_raw = 0.0 (instead of the NotAvailable variant) is rejected at deserialization (per RH-5).
- Phase A raw diagnostic helper returns/logs distill_loss_raw as NotAvailable; phase C+ helper returns Value { loss }.
- Focused router/distillation/raw-diagnostic tests pass.
notes:
## Test Plan & Logging (AGENTS.md addendum)

### AGENTS.md scalar hyperparameter rule

Tests for scalar hyperparameters such as safe bounds, temperatures, and loss weights must include a non-default/non-1.0 value. This task covers TWO hyperparameters: `mu` (z-loss baseline) and `T_d` (distillation temperature).

### Unit tests (gbf-train/tests/centered_zloss_baseline.rs + distillation_temperature.rs)

- centered_zloss_baseline_zero_at_pinned_mu: with mu = log(n_experts) and all router logits = 0, z_loss = 0 within 1e-12 (default path).
- centered_zloss_nondefault_mu: with mu = 0 (the 'uncentered-looking' default for falsification tests), z_loss = (log n_experts)^2 > 0 at zero logits; documents that the default mu pin is load-bearing.
- centered_zloss_property_nonneg: for arbitrary logits in [-10, 10], z_loss >= 0 (property).
- distill_kl_at_default_temperature: T_d = 1.0, identical teacher/student logits → KL = 0.
- distill_kl_at_nondefault_temperature: T_d = 2.0 (non-default), identical logits → KL = 0; T_d = 0.5 with shifted student logits → KL strictly > KL@T_d=1 (sharper distribution makes KL larger).

### DistillRawDiagnostic discipline

- distill_raw_phase_a_not_available: in Phase A (before teacher freeze), DistillRawDiagnostic emits NotAvailable { reason: "no_frozen_teacher", phase: TrainPhase::A }; serde rejects Value{loss: 0.0} substitution at deserialization (RH-5).
- distill_raw_phase_c_value: in Phase C, DistillRawDiagnostic emits Value { loss: LossNatsPerByte }; finite-validation passes.
- distill_raw_zero_default_rejected: a JSON deserialization with distill_loss_raw: 0.0 (rather than NotAvailable) is REJECTED at parse time.

### Raw vs phase-effective config distinction (AGENTS.md)

- raw_toml_config_does_not_gate: RawTomlLossConfig { lambda_distill: 1.0 } does NOT gate by phase; computing the phase-effective config at step ∈ Phase A produces lambda_distill_eff = 0.0.
- phase_effective_is_distinct_type: RawTomlLossConfig and PhaseEffectiveLossConfig are not interchangeable (compile-time test that From conversion requires a step argument).

### Logging

- s7.loss.zloss.baseline { mu_pinned, observed_at_zero_logits, within_tolerance } at DEBUG.
- s7.loss.distill.diagnostic { phase, variant: "NotAvailable" | "Value", reason } at INFO once per phase boundary.

### Reviewer Personas

P5 Detective (always-on), P6 Scope Sentinel (always-on), P3 AI Researcher (z-loss centering claim is research-load-bearing), P7 Numerical & Determinism (1e-12 tolerance is determinism-sensitive), P10 Observability (subscriber capture for the diagnostic events).

### Project Skills

`.agents/skills/logging-bead-closure/SKILL.md` (subscriber-level capture for the diagnostic event shape; F-C4 named owner for dashboards).

description: The trust layer. 13+ build report files, machine-checkable certificates (range/arena/window/reachability/resource_state) consumed by gbf-verify, independent slow reference implementations (pack/unpack, LUT eval, decode/RNG) used in nightly randomized cross-checks, FailureCapsule with minimization/reduction_log, RunManifest + ReproducibilityManifest.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Epic F: Reports & Verify (`gbf-report`, `gbf-verify`)

### What this is

The trust layer: the 13+ build report files (`map.json`, `provenance.json`, `budget.json`, `slice_report.json`, `trace_schema.json`, `oracle_vectors.bin`, `semantic_checkpoint_schema.json`, `operational_probe_schema.json`, `hint_consumption.json`, `compiler_feedback.json`, `reachability_report.json`, etc.), the machine-checkable certificates (`certs/{range,arena,window,reachability,resource_state}.cert.json`), the slow reference algorithms in `gbf-verify`, and the structured failure capsule + minimization machinery.

### Why this matters

Reports turn "the build worked" into "the build worked, and here's the structured evidence." Certificates make safety-critical passes auditable. `gbf-verify`'s independent slow reference impls prevent the failure mode where a shared bug becomes self-validating (engineering rule 17). `FailureCapsule` + `minimized_workload` makes failures bisectable instead of ephemeral.

### Scope (five features)

- **F-F1 — Build reports**: emit the structured JSON + binary report set per `planv0.md` line 1577. One JSON schema per report; CI tests round-trip them.
- **F-F2 — Certificates**: `certs/range.cert.json`, `certs/arena.cert.json`, `certs/window.cert.json`, `certs/reachability.cert.json`, `certs/resource_state.cert.json`. Each consumed by `gbf-verify` as machine-checkable proofs.
- **F-F3 — Slow reference impls in `gbf-verify`**: pack/unpack, logical LUT eval, decode/RNG — independent re-implementations used in nightly randomized cross-checks against production.
- **F-F4 — `FailureCapsule` + minimization**: capture failed runs with structured state + reduction log; cross-build replay support.
- **F-F5 — `RunManifest` + `ReproducibilityManifest`**: scientific reproducibility plumbing — toolchain pin, lockfile, host triple, deterministic seeds, `study_tag`.

### Critical path

```
F-A6 (gbf-store) ──→ F-F1..F-F4 (reports + capsules go through CAS)
F-B (compiler stages) ──→ F-F1..F-F2 (each stage emits its report + cert)
F-C (oracles) ──→ F-F3 cross-checks; F-F4 captures oracle failures
```

### Confidence: HIGH

Mostly schema + JSON serialization + per-stage emit hooks. The verify reference impls are real engineering — they must be deliberately written to fail differently from production code (e.g., naive LUT eval vs production's tiled SIMD-ish lookup).

## F-D4: RuntimeDriftMonitor

### What this is

Per `planv0.md` correction: `RuntimeDriftMonitor` + `DriftTrigger` + `DriftAction` (`ShrinkSlices` / `DropTrace` / `DemoteMode`). Tracks observed `DriftEnvelope` (slice_cycles_p95, ui_commit_cycles_p95, trace_drop_rate_pct, persist_overrun_rate_pct) against expected; fires actions past threshold.

### Why this matters

Production runtime experiences load it wasn't trained on. Drift monitoring + automatic mode demotion is what keeps the cooperative budget honored even when reality disagrees with calibration.

### Design sketch

```rust
pub struct DriftEnvelope {
    pub slice_cycles_p95: Option<u32>,
    pub ui_commit_cycles_p95: Option<u32>,
    pub trace_drop_rate_pct: Option<u8>,
    pub persist_overrun_rate_pct: Option<u8>,
}

pub enum DriftAction {
    ShrinkSlices,
    DropTrace,
    DemoteMode(RuntimeMode),
}
```

- F-A3 abi InterruptPolicy + ResourceLease
- F-D6 SchedulePack mode switching (DemoteMode target)

title: T-A7.4: Trap dispatcher — registry of PC + memory traps with Predicate{Always|Closure|Source} + TrapAction{HaltAndReport|Continue}
description: Registry-driven TrapDispatcher in trap.rs. TrapKind: Pc{addr:u16} | MemRead{range:AddressRange} | MemWrite{range} | MemRw{range}. AddressRange is a constructor-validated newtype that rejects start>end_inclusive (typed AddressRangeError). MemoryAccessKind = InstrFetch | DataRead | Write — under the io_trace backend, opcode/operand fetches and data reads are folded together at the wire level, so MemRead range traps fire on instruction fetches inside the range (RFC §3.7.1 finding 4 + resolved Q44). PC traps fire BEFORE executing the instruction at the registered address (matches debugger expectation); run_until_pc returns immediately when already at pc. Memory traps under the io_trace backend are POST-INSTRUCTION traps — there is no public per-memory-access callback in gameroy-core that can stop the CPU mid-instruction. They fire at the instruction boundary after the matching access; the reported emulator state is post-instruction. Exact pre-access memory traps are an explicit non-goal for M0 (deferred to a follow-up bead requiring upstream-instrumented gb_read/gb_write — finding 4 + Q32). Predicate enum: Always | Closure(FnMut(&TrapContext) -> Result<bool, TrapPredicateError>; not Send+Sync) | Source(String — opaque to gbf-emu; F-A8 compiles into Closure). TrapContext exposes Regs/pc/MemoryAccess/cycle/EmuReadOnlyView (peek/peek_range only — predicates cannot perturb timers, traps, or cursors; reads through the view inherit the same DebugMemoryUnsupported semantics as Emulator::peek). TrapAction: HaltAndReport (returns TrapHit from step/run_*) | Continue (logs NormalizedTraceEvent::TrapHit which is F-A7-LOCAL — not an F-A3 TraceEvent::TrapHit). BreakpointId returned by add_*; persistence shape TrapSpec{id, kind, action, predicate:PredicateSpec{Always|Source}} via export_persistable_specs() refusing closure-only entries with TrapPersistenceError::ClosureOnly. remove(id) returns bool; remove_entry returns Option<RemovedTrap> (public-only fields). Consumed by gbf-debug, gbf-bench, gbf-test, gbf-codegen, F-D2.

title: T10.4: TernaryWeightPlan byte math and pack/unpack round-trip tests (F3 coverage)
description:
Unit tests for TernaryWeightPlan types and byte computations:

**Byte cost computation tests:**
- PerTensor Q8_8, 128x224: verify exact byte count = ceil(128*224/4) + 2 = 7170
- PerOutputRow Q8_8, 128x224: verify = ceil(128*224/4) + 224*2 = 7616
- PerOutputRow Q8_8, 224x128: verify = ceil(224*128/4) + 128*2 = 7424
- PerGroup(16) Q8_8, 128x224: verify = ceil(128*224/4) + ceil(128*224/16)*2 = 10720
- Full two-matrix expert (128,224) PerOutputRow Q8_8: verify total = 15040 + metadata
- Verify all byte costs are deterministic across runs

**Pack/unpack round-trip tests:**
- Create known float tensor, apply ternary projection, pack via production packer, unpack via production unpacker, verify lossless round-trip
- Test all WeightEncoding variants: Ternary2, SparseTernaryBitplanes, Binary1
- Test boundary cases: all-zero tensor, all-positive tensor, alternating pattern
- Test scale formats: Q8_8, Q4_4, Pow2 round-trip through quantize->dequantize

**Independent reference agreement test:**
- Generate 100 random tensors of varying sizes (4x4 to 256x256)
- Pack with production packer AND with gbf-verify independent reference packer
- Verify byte-identical output for all tensors
- If any diverge: log tensor index, first divergent byte position, expected vs actual in hex

**Artifact hash stability:**
- Export same tiny model twice, verify ArtifactCore content hash is identical
- Export, modify non-semantic field in ArtifactAux, verify ArtifactCore hash unchanged

All failures include: dimensions, encoding, scale granularity, expected byte count, actual byte count, hex dump of first divergent region.

title: T-B2.18: BootstrapCalibrationBundle + bringup-*.chrome_budget.json fixtures
description:
## What
Author and check in deterministic, content-addressed
`BootstrapCalibrationBundle` artifacts and `bringup-*.chrome_budget.json`
variants for each canonical target profile. See RFC §2.13.

## Why
Bringup is a profile selection, not a relaxation surface. Both
calibration absence and reduced reserved-slack are explicit inputs, not
profile-time relaxations. Without these fixtures, calibration/budget tests
cannot exercise the Bringup acceptance path uniformly.

## Inputs
- `gbf-policy::risk::CalibrationConfidenceClass::None`.
- The four target profiles from `gbf-hw::TargetProfile` (DMG/MBC5 default,
  CGB later).
- Calibration bundle schema from `gbf-policy::compile::CalibrationBundleSet`.

## Outputs
- `fixtures/calibration/bootstrap-dmg-mbc5.calibration.json` (or .toml).
- `fixtures/calibration/bootstrap-cgb-mbc5.calibration.json` (later).
- `fixtures/calibration/bootstrap-*.calibration.sha256` content-addressed
  digests.
- `fixtures/runtime-chrome-budget/bringup-dmg-mbc5.chrome_budget.json`
  with reduced `reserved_slack` and one Bank0Free + one ExpertBank slot.
- `fixtures/runtime-chrome-budget/bringup-*.chrome_budget.sha256`.
- Loader helpers in `gbf-test` or `gbf-codegen::test_support`.

## Pitfalls
- The bundle declares `confidence: None` — Default/Trace/Recovery profiles
  reject this via `CalibrationConfidenceTooLow`. That's the design (§2.13).
- The bundle is hash-addressed; any change must be a NEW bundle file with a
  different hash, not an in-place edit of an existing fixture.
- The `bringup-*.chrome_budget.json` is NOT the same as the production
  budget. Its reduced reserved_slack reflects pre-runtime-shell-baseline
  conditions; do not use it for closure-eligible non-Bringup builds.

## Acceptance
- Files exist at canonical paths.
- Content hashes pinned in test fixtures.
- A successful Stage 0 test of T-B2.8 references these fixtures.

## Refs
- RFC §2.13 Bringup-as-profile + explicit fixtures.
- Depends on: T-B2.12.
- Blocks: T-B2.8 (calibration tests need bootstrap bundle), T-B4.10 (chrome budget tests).

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## RFC amendments (2026-05-07)

The Bringup-acceptance condition is now expressed via the renamed/restructured
`RiskPolicy`:

- Bringup is acceptable when
  `profile.risk_policy.calibration_confidence_requirement == NoMinimumConfidence`.
- The bundle's declared `CalibrationConfidenceClass::None` (no measurements)
  passes only against `NoMinimumConfidence`.

These are two distinct enums (RFC §2.8 disambiguation):
- `CalibrationConfidenceClass` lives in `gbf-hw::calibration` (real today;
  `None | Transferred | WithinFamily | Onsite | ...`).
- `CalibrationConfidenceRequirement` lives in `gbf-policy::risk` via
  `RiskPolicy` (T-B2.0 owns); `NoMinimumConfidence` is its weakest variant.

`BootstrapCalibrationBundle` factory output remains identical: a
`CalibrationBundleSet` with each layer's `confidence = None` and
`measurements = None`. The only thing that changes is the profile field
name + variant on the *consumer* side (T-B2.8 dispatcher, T-B2.12
fixtures).

Fixture file paths unchanged. Hash unchanged. T-B2.0f's factory function
signature unchanged.

Cross-refs: §2.8, §2.13, §7.4.
