title: F-S7 v0.2: Default rank formula fix + n=2 ablation lane override
description:
## Description

Fix the default rank formula (which gives rank=0 for n_experts=2) and pin per-lane rank overrides. Old formula: `rank = min(n_experts / 4, 8)`. For n=2, `floor(2/4) = 0`, which is degenerate. v0.2 formula: `rank = max(1, min(ceil(n_experts / 4), 8))`. The S7 OVERRIDES section pins router_rank = 4 for n_experts=4 (production) and router_rank = 2 for n_experts=2 (ablation lane).

## Acceptance Criteria

- D7 default formula: `rank = max(1, min(ceil(n_experts / 4), 8))`.
- D7 OVERRIDES: "n_experts = 4 production lane: router_rank = 4. n_experts = 2 ablation lane: router_rank = 2."
- `gbf-model::LowRankRouter::default_rank` implements the formula; unit test covers default_rank(2)=1, default_rank(4)=1, default_rank(16)=4, default_rank(64)=8.
- ModelTopologyConfig::from_profile honors the S7 override for both MoeTiny lanes.

## Notes

- The `ceil` vs `floor` ambiguity in the old formula was likely an oversight that no one had hit because S7 OVERRIDES short-circuits the formula for MoeTiny. But the formula is part of the public LowRankRouter API for non-S7 callers and S8 will rely on it.
- Depends on T_F8_1 (rationale must be honest before the override discussion makes sense).

title: F-S3.20: F1-broken-S3..F9-broken-S3 falsification suite (gated by unified falsify feature)
description:
## Context

The S3 falsification suite (RFC §14 O-5'') consists of nine deliberately-broken substitutes `F1-broken-S3..F9-broken-S3`, each producing the expected Refuted verdict on its target hypothesis. Per F-S2 convention (`F1-broken-S2..F6-broken-S2`), they are gated by the unified `falsify` feature and selected via `--test falsification_s3`.

The nine broken substitutes and target hypothesis:
1. F1-broken-S3 charset_v1_lossy_normalization → H1 Refuted
2. F2-broken-S3 five_gram_smoothing_uniform → H2 Refuted
3. F3-broken-S3 model_emits_invalid_charset → H3 Refuted
4. F4-broken-S3 artifact_oracle_dropped_quant_resolve → H4 + H6 Refuted
5. F5-broken-S3 bundle_export_nondeterministic_map_iter → H5 Refuted
6. F6-broken-S3 tied_embedding_export_split → H5 Refuted
7. F7-broken-S3 v0_success_repetition_collapse → H3 Refuted
8. F8-broken-S3 oracle_softmax_over_concat_logits → H4 Refuted (via B19's invalid-comparator/conformance pipeline detection; third-round Patch on F8)
9. F9-broken-S3 phase_scheduler_wrong_ramp → H7 Refuted (third-round Patch 18; uses the s3_phase_log emitter from B12 to record the wrong ramp)

## Why this matters

Per RFC Rule Falsification, this RFC is correct only if a deliberately-broken implementation produces the expected Refuted verdict. The S3 falsification suite is the operational cross-check on every closure-gating hypothesis. Falsification-suite failure produces `Fail-falsification` per the §10 dispatcher (Patch 31 round 2).

## Deliverables

1. `gbf-experiments/tests/falsification_s3.rs` — gate harness (mirrors `gbf-experiments/tests/falsification_s2.rs`); discovers the 9 sub-modules and asserts each Refutes its target hypothesis
2. `gbf-experiments/tests/falsification_s3/{f1..f9}.rs` — each broken substitute (mirrors `gbf-experiments/tests/falsification_s2/{f1..f6}.rs` layout):
   - F1: charset case-fold to lower → train_post_sha256 changes; H1 Refuted
   - F2: KN replaced with uniform 1/|Sigma| → bpc_kn5_oracle_fixture mismatch > 1e-12; H2 Refuted
   - F3: decode loop accepts ids 76, 77, 78 in generated text → Q3 fires; H3 Refuted
   - F4: artifact_oracle uses naming resolver against the adversarial fixture from B16 → H4 (agreement) + H6 (QuantSpec resolution) both Refuted
   - F5: HashMap iteration in graph serialize → bundle_self_hash differs across replays; H5 Refuted
   - F6: classifier emitted as separate CanonicalTensor with identical bytes → payload doubles; H5 Refuted
   - F7: decode loop disables max_consecutive_same_token check → Q4 fires; H3 Refuted
   - F8: oracle KL over softmax([prompt_len * vocab]) → B19's CanonicalConformanceWrite returns PromptWideSoftmaxAggregation; H4 Refuted
   - F9: emit ramp Off→Soft→Soft→Hard for expert_qat OR empty Phase C distill_loss histogram → H7 Refuted via the s3_phase_log structured event check
3. `gbf-experiments/src/s3/falsify.rs` (cfg(feature = "falsify")):
   - Hosts the deliberately-broken implementations referenced by the test files
   - `compile_error!` if `falsify` is enabled outside `cfg(test)` (re-affirm B7 guard)
4. `gbf-experiments/tests/falsification_s3_suite_hash.rs` — deterministic falsification suite hash mirroring `falsification_s2_suite_hash` so changes to the broken substitutes themselves require an explicit RFC amendment:
   - `pub const FALSIFICATION_S3_SUITE_HASH: Hash256 = sha256(concat(f1.rs.bytes, f2.rs.bytes, ..., f9.rs.bytes, falsification_s3.rs.bytes))`
   - Snapshot test against pinned value

## Test scaffolding

1. **The falsification suite IS the test scaffolding.** Each f{n}.rs file is a self-contained refutation test.
2. **`gbf-experiments/tests/falsification_s3_compile_guard_s3.rs`** — assert `falsify` outside cfg(test) → compile_error fires (build-time check)
3. **`gbf-experiments/tests/falsification_s3_coverage_s3.rs`** — assert every closure-gating hypothesis (H1..H7) has at least one falsification substitute pointing at it (so no hypothesis is structurally unfalsifiable)
4. **`gbf-experiments/tests/falsification_s3_negative_s3.rs`** — assert that running the suite WITHOUT injecting broken substitutes (i.e., normal code path) produces all Confirmed verdicts (the "test the test" check)

## Logging discipline

```
event_name = "s3::falsify::suite_started"
fields: { substitute_count: 9, suite_hash }

event_name = "s3::falsify::substitute_run"
level = "info"
fields: { substitute_name: "F{N}-broken-S3", target_hypothesis, expected_verdict: "Refuted" }

event_name = "s3::falsify::substitute_complete"
fields: { substitute_name, target_hypothesis, observed_verdict, matches_expected: bool }

event_name = "s3::falsify::suite_complete"
fields: { all_substitutes_refuted_target: bool, suite_passed }

target = "gbf_experiments::s3::falsify"
```
Subscriber-level test `gbf-experiments/tests/falsification_s3_logging_s3.rs` asserts events fire and `matches_expected = true` for every substitute.

## E2E acceptance script

`scripts/s3_falsification_smoke.sh`:
1. Runs `cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real,s3-oracle-adversarial,falsify" --test falsification_s3 -- --nocapture`
2. Captures stderr to /tmp/s3-falsify.ndjson
3. Asserts NDJSON contains all 9 substitute_complete events with matches_expected = true
4. Asserts FALSIFICATION_S3_SUITE_HASH matches the pinned snapshot

## Inheritance / non-duplication

- F-S2's F1-broken-S2..F6-broken-S2 are independent; B20 does NOT re-run them. Per F-S2 AS2-21, F-S2's falsification suite tests S2-binary behaviors; F-S3's tests S3-binary behaviors.
- `falsify` is the unified feature; do NOT introduce `s3-falsify`.
- F4-broken-S3 reuses the H6 adversarial fixture from B16 (linear_0_weight + linear_0_weight_naive_fp32).
- F8-broken-S3 reuses B19's CanonicalConformanceWrite F8-detection mechanism.
- F9-broken-S3 reuses B12's s3_phase_log structured event emitter.

## Considerations

- F4-broken-S3 must use the H6 adversarial fixture from B16; the broken impl resolves by name and gets the wrong logits.
- F8-broken-S3 must produce a conformance envelope with `aggregation_kind: PromptWideSoftmaxForbidden`; B19 returns the rejection, which propagates into H4 verdict.
- F9-broken-S3 uses a structural mask fixture; per F-S2 AS2-6, structural-mask fixtures are the preferred falsifier for QAT/scheduler claims.

## Acceptance

```
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real,s3-oracle-adversarial,falsify" --test falsification_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test falsification_s3_compile_guard_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test falsification_s3_coverage_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real" --test falsification_s3_negative_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features falsify --test falsification_s3_suite_hash
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features falsify --test falsification_s3_logging_s3
scripts/s3_falsification_smoke.sh
```

## Out of scope

- Outcome dispatcher (B21 — consumes the suite verdict)
- Real falsification of any S2-pinned hypothesis (S2 owns)

## References

- RFC §14 O-5''; Rule Falsification
- F-S2 falsification template: `gbf-experiments/tests/falsification_s2.rs`, `falsification_s2_suite_hash.rs`

title: T-B3.5: Routing + ExpertSection + ExpertWeightSlot + FfnPlan + topology tag (absorbs T-B3.6/7/10)
description:
## What
Define `RoutingTable { layers: Vec<RouterLayer> }`, `RouterLayer
{ layer, n_experts, router_weight, router_bias, semantics }`,
`RouterSemantics { Top1Hard { gate_weight, tie_break } }`,
`RouterGateWeightSemantics { One, SelectedScore }`, and `RouterTieBreak
{ LowestExpertId }`. See RFC §8.1.

## Why
Three closed-enum decisions land here together:

1. `RouterSemantics::Top1Hard` is the v1 closed set (Ambiguity A9). Soft
   top-1 routing is a training-side concern; deployed model is hard
   top-1.

2. `RouterGateWeightSemantics::{ One, SelectedScore }` makes gate-weight
   propagation explicit (Ambiguity A54). `One ⇒ weight = 1.0` (gate
   discarded, one path), `SelectedScore ⇒ weight = normalized_scores[top1]`
   (full MoE math). Without this, `eval_canonical_qg` (§8.7) is
   ambiguous about whether the candidate is multiplied or not.

3. `RouterTieBreak::LowestExpertId` (Ambiguity A81). `BitExact` argmax
   requires deterministic tie-break; v1 pins lowest expert id. Future
   amendments may add `HighestScoreFirst` etc. Reject classes
   `QuantGraphRouterGateWeightSemanticsUnsupported` and
   `QuantGraphRouterTieBreakUnsupported` are minted here for any
   non-v1 variant.

`RoutingTable` is `Option<RoutingTable>` on `QuantGraph` (T-B3.1):
`Some` iff at least one layer is routed (SC-4). Dense-only models have
`None`.

## Inputs
- T-B3.1 (`QuantGraph` skeleton).
- `gbf-foundation::{LayerId, ExpertId}`.
- T-B3.2 (TensorId for `router_weight` / `router_bias` references).

## Outputs
- `pub struct RoutingTable { layers: Vec<RouterLayer> }`.
- `pub struct RouterLayer { layer: LayerId, n_experts: u16,
  router_weight: TensorId, router_bias: Option<TensorId>,
  semantics: RouterSemantics }`.
- `pub enum RouterSemantics { Top1Hard { gate_weight: RouterGateWeightSemantics,
  tie_break: RouterTieBreak } }`.
- `pub enum RouterGateWeightSemantics { One, SelectedScore }`.
- `pub enum RouterTieBreak { LowestExpertId }`.

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT add `SoftTop1` / `TopK` / etc. — Ambiguity A9 forbids it in v1.
- DO NOT drop the gate weight by default. Earlier drafts had no consumer
  for `GateWeight` and the routed FFN math was wrong (Ambiguity A54).
- DO NOT collapse `RouterSemantics` into `RouterLayer` directly; the
  enum-on-enum shape lets future amendments add new top-level
  semantics (e.g. `SoftTop1` + matching `gate_weight` rules).
- `n_experts: u16` matches `ModelSpecSummary`; types must be identical
  to support SC-4 cross-check.

## Acceptance
- `gbf-codegen::router_semantics_only_top1_hard_in_v1`.
- `gbf-codegen::router_gate_weight_semantics_carries_one_or_selected_score`.
- `gbf-codegen::router_tie_break_lowest_expert_id_only_in_v1`.

## Refs
- RFC §8.1 (RoutingTable), §8.7 (gate-weight reference semantics), §8.5
  SC-4 (n_experts coverage).
- Ambiguity ledger: A9, A54, A81.
- Depends on: T-B3.1, T-B3.2.
- Blocks: T-B3.17 (RoutingBinding), T-B3.22a (RouterSemantics binding),
  T-B5.2 (RouteTop1 op carries this contract).

comments.text:
## T-B14.2: Define `CompileKnobOverrides` + selector types

**Target crate**: `gbf-policy` (overrides + most selectors), `gbf-asm` (`SectionId`, `ReductionSiteId` if compiler-emitted)
**Target file(s)**: `gbf-policy/src/knobs/overrides.rs`, `gbf-policy/src/knobs/selectors.rs`
**Reference**: F-B14 oracle resolution; T-B14.1 for the parent type.

### Background

Global policy knobs are insufficient. Repair often needs to say "this specific value recomputes" or "this specific kernel must be overlay-resident." Targeted override maps with **typed selectors** carry those decisions. Selectors are typed precisely so proposals don't smuggle untyped strings or pass-local indices.

### Implementation Notes

```rust
pub struct CompileKnobOverrides {
    /// Optional operational probes disabled by trace demotion.
    /// Semantic observations are NEVER listed here.
    pub disabled_optional_probes: BTreeSet<TraceProbeId>,

    /// Per-kernel residency requirements inserted by RomWindowPlan/OverlayPlan repair.
    pub forced_kernel_residency: BTreeMap<KernelSelector, KernelResidency>,

    /// Pure values forced from Materialize to Recompute. Effect-free only.
    pub forced_recompute: BTreeSet<ValueSelector>,

    /// Site-specific range-plan ceilings.
    pub reduction_ceiling_overrides: BTreeMap<ReductionSelector, ReductionPlanCeiling>,

    /// Tile classes remaining legal for a selector after candidate narrowing.
    pub tile_class_overrides: BTreeMap<TileSelector, BTreeSet<TileCandidateClass>>,
}

pub enum KernelSelector {
    KernelSpec(KernelSpecId),
    LayerExpert { layer: LayerId, expert: ExpertId },
    Section(SectionId),
}

pub enum ValueSelector {
    Value(ValueId),
    AliasClass(AliasClassId),
}

pub enum ReductionSelector {
    Site(ReductionSiteId),
    Layer(LayerId),
}

pub enum TileSelector {
    Kernel(KernelSpecId),
    Layer(LayerId),
    SliceClass(SliceClass),
}

pub enum SliceClass {
    Micro,
    Frame,
    TokenBoundary,
    TraceHeavy,
}
```

`SectionId` (gbf-asm T-A1.2) and `ReductionSiteId` (new — emitted by RangePlan in F-B5; introduce here as a typed newtype `pub struct ReductionSiteId(pub u32)` if not already defined). `KernelSpecId` from F-H1; `ValueId` / `AliasClassId` / `LayerId` / `ExpertId` from gbf-foundation / gbf-ir.

### Monotone semantics on overrides

Repair may **insert** new selectors or move an existing selector to a **later value** in its declared order. It may not delete entries or move a selector backward.

For `tile_class_overrides`, monotone means **subset removal**: the new `BTreeSet` ⊆ the previous one. For `disabled_optional_probes`, monotone means **superset addition**.

These rules are implemented in T-B14.6 (loop controller), but document them on the type.

### Acceptance Criteria

```bash
cargo check -p gbf-policy
cargo test -p gbf-policy -- overrides::serde_round_trip
cargo test -p gbf-policy -- overrides::monotone_insert         # Inserting a selector at higher rank is allowed
cargo test -p gbf-policy -- overrides::monotone_no_delete      # Deletion is rejected
cargo test -p gbf-policy -- selectors::id_exhaustive           # SliceClass enum is closed
```

### Constitution Checkpoints

- §I.1: Selectors are typed; no untyped strings reach the repair loop.
- §VI.1: Selector vocabulary defined once in gbf-policy.

title: T-B6T7.C: StageCache K4 + K5 wiring (core-product storage + envelope rewrap on replay)
description:
## What
Land StageCache wiring for K4 (Stage 4) and K5 (Stage 5):

```text
K4 := StageCacheKeyHash("observation_plan.v1", schema_version, {
  infer_ir_self_hash,
  quant_graph_self_hash,
  semantic_checkpoint_schema_hash,
  observation_policy_projection_hash,
  pass_version_observation_plan,
  crate_feature_set_hash,
  observation_plan_schema_hash,
  build_active_semantic_checkpoint_schema_schema_hash,
  operational_probe_schema_schema_hash,
  probe_registry_hash,
  metric_registry_hash,
  trace_event_layout_registry_hash,
})

K5 := StageCacheKeyHash("range_plan.v1", schema_version, {
  infer_ir_self_hash,
  quant_graph_self_hash,
  static_budget_self_hash,
  range_policy_projection_hash,
  pass_version_range_plan,
  crate_feature_set_hash,
  range_plan_schema_hash,
  range_cert_schema_hash,
})
```

**Audit-only parents NOT in K4/K5**:
- `policy_resolution_self_hash`, `compile_request_hash`, `artifact_aux_hash`
- These move audit context without invalidating cache entries.

## Cache laws
- `C-Success-Stage4/5`: cache stores `*CoreProduct` (body, not envelope).
- `C-NoFalseSuccess-Stage4/5`: failed result never stores success product.
- `C-FailureMemo-Stage4/5`: failure memo stores **bodies + diagnostics**,
  not envelopes.
- `C-ReportRewrap-Stage4/5`: on cache hit, driver wraps fresh envelopes
  with current audit parents.
- `C-FailureReportRewrap`: same for failure replay (Patch 9 of 30-patch).
- `C-PassVersion`, `C-SchemaVersion`, `C-FeatureSet`: standard cache-miss
  triggers.

## Subtasks
- [ ] Compose K4 / K5 via `gbf-store::stage_cache::compose_key`
      (matches landed F-B5 pattern).
- [ ] StageCache cells store `*CoreProduct` for success.
- [ ] Failure memos store body + diagnostics; replay rewraps envelopes.
- [ ] `pass_version_observation_plan = "1.0.0"`,
      `pass_version_range_plan = "1.0.0"` (initial; bump on any
      construction-rule change).
- [ ] `crate_feature_set_hash` reflects feature flags that change
      layout/serde/behavior.
- [ ] Tests prove byte-identical replay across two builds with different
      audit parents (compile_request_hash differs only).

## Acceptance
- [ ] K4/K5 cache hit on identical inputs.
- [ ] K4/K5 cache miss on `pass_version_*` bump.
- [ ] Audit-only parents differ → cache hit (with rewrapped envelopes).
- [ ] Failure memo replay rewraps audit parents successfully.

## How this serves the project
Without StageCache, every dev rebuild re-runs Stage 4 and Stage 5 from
scratch. K4/K5 enable iteration-loop speed that is essential for F-B16
FeasibilityRefinementLoop (one knob delta = re-run only the affected
stages).

## RFC anchors
§11 StageCache algebra (K4/K5 definitions, cache laws).

## History
- 41-patch Patches 10, 11: registry hashes in K4 + audit-only fields out
- 30-patch Patch 9: failure memo stores bodies not envelopes
- 41-patch Patch 3: products split from emitted bundles (enabled rewrap)

## Blocked by
T-B6.F (ObservationPlanCoreProduct), T-B7.B (RangePlanCoreProduct),
T-B6T7.A (schema hashes referenced in K).

title: T10.13: Export determinism and cross-backend agreement test
description:
Tests that the export pipeline produces byte-identical artifacts for the same model weights.

**Determinism test:**
- Create a tiny model with fixed random seed
- Export via ExportVisitor -> ModelArtifact, record ArtifactCore content hash H1
- Reset model to same weights (reload from checkpoint)
- Export again -> record hash H2
- ASSERT: H1 == H2

**Serialization round-trip test:**
- Export ModelArtifact to directory form
- Read it back via artifact loader
- Re-export to directory form
- Verify byte-for-byte identical files in blobs/sha256/

**Canonical tensor determinism:**
- For each CanonicalTensor in ArtifactCore: serialize to bytes, hash, deserialize, re-serialize, verify hash unchanged
- Includes ternary weight tensors, scale tensors, embedding tensors, router weights

**Production packer vs independent reference packer:**
- Export tiny model via production ExportVisitor
- For each ternary weight tensor: repack using gbf-verify's independent reference packer
- ASSERT: byte-identical packed output for all tensors
- If ANY diverge: log tensor name, first divergent byte offset, hex context around divergence

**Scale tensor quantization determinism:**
- Export scale tensors in Q8_8 format
- Verify the quantized scale values match: round_to_nearest(float_scale * 256) as u16
- Verify no NaN or Inf values in exported scales

All failures log: artifact hash, tensor name, byte offset of divergence, hex dump.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p gbf-test -- export_determinism passes; Hash equality across runs; Serialization round-trip byte-identical; 100 random packer agreement tests
close_reason:
## QAT Closure Checklist

**Artifact contract:** This bead adds `gbf-test/tests/export_determinism.rs` for the current `ExportedQatArtifact` / `ArtifactCore` boundary. It proves deterministic tiny fixture export, stable serialized `ExportedQatArtifact` JSON bytes for equivalent exports, stable `ArtifactCore::semantic_hash()`, stable `CanonicalTensor::content_hash` after serde round-trip, and reference-packability of exported canonical ternary weight/scale tensors. It also adds a fixture helper so the tiny export traversal can be reused with alternate router/expert sources.

Directory-form artifact transport, content-addressed `blobs/sha256` loading, and production target packed bytes are not implemented by the current export boundary and are not claimed here.

**differentiable Burn path:** This bead does not add a new differentiable training path. It proves the supported Burn adapter handoff path for `Top1RouterBurnQat` and `ExpertBlockBurnQat`: converting the tiny router/expert block through Burn-owned trained state and then exporting through the scalar `ExportVisitor` yields byte-identical `ExportedQatArtifact` output for identical weights. Full train/checkpoint-to-export coverage remains owned by `bd-1wd`.

**Tests proving it:**

- `cargo test -p gbf-test --test export_determinism`
- `cargo test -p gbf-test -- export_determinism`
- `cargo test -p gbf-test --lib fixtures_make_tiny_artifact_is_valid_and_deterministic`
- `cargo test -p gbf-test --test architecture`
- `cargo clippy -p gbf-test -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --check --all`
- `python3 scripts/qat_harness_checks.py`

**Acceptance movement:** Yes. Review found three original acceptance criteria ahead of the current repo surface:

- Original: export/read/re-export directory form and compare `blobs/sha256` files. New owner: `bd-1yd` for archive/directory transport and `bd-1jy` for the content-addressed blob store/integrity layer. Current replacement gate: JSON serde round-trip of `ExportedQatArtifact`.
- Original: compare production packed ternary bytes to the independent reference packer. New owner: `bd-1pc6`, clarified with a moved-acceptance comment, because `ExportVisitor` currently emits canonical `I8`/`U16` tensors and no production target materializer emits comparable packed bytes yet. Current replacement gate: exported canonical ternary tensors are reference-packable and unpack back to the exported payload.
- Original: full cross-backend train/checkpoint/export agreement. New owner: `bd-1wd`. Current replacement gate: supported Burn router/expert trained-state handoff produces byte-identical scalar export for identical tiny weights.

## Support Matrix

| Deterministic tiny fixture export from identical scalar weights | supported | not applicable | supported | `export_determinism_tiny_model_reexports_identical_core_and_bytes` |
| Supported Burn router/expert trained-state handoff for identical tiny weights | supported | supported | supported through scalar `ExportVisitor` | `export_determinism_supported_burn_router_and_expert_handoff_matches_scalar_tiny_export` |
| Embedding/classifier/dense FFN Burn handoff | supported | moved | moved | `bd-1wd` |
| `ExportedQatArtifact` serde JSON round-trip | supported | not applicable | supported | `export_determinism_exported_qat_artifact_json_round_trip_is_byte_identical` |
| Artifact directory/CAS round-trip and `blobs/sha256` byte identity | not applicable | not applicable | moved | `bd-1yd`, `bd-1jy` |
| `CanonicalTensor` serde round-trip and content-hash stability | supported | not applicable | supported | `export_determinism_canonical_tensors_round_trip_and_hashes_are_stable` |

title: F-S7 v0.2 T5.2: LayerId/ExpertId off-by-one fix + RunLog completion-aware + grad_norms
description:
## Goal

Fix two schema off-by-ones (LayerId: 0..n_blocks-1; ExpertId exhaust: 0..n_experts-1). Make RunLog tolerate partial completion (DivergedAt/CollapsedAt) without forcing length = optimizer_steps. Add the grad_norms series H1/H2 require.

## Background

Pre-review LayerId was '0..n_blocks' (range was off-by-one — n_blocks is exclusive upper bound, so legal IDs are 0..n_blocks-1). Same for EPD-4: 'expert_id values exhaust 0..n_experts'. These were silent off-by-ones that would have allowed an ID equal to n_blocks or n_experts to validate.

Pre-review RunLog RL-Length and RL-Eval required full-length logs even when completion was DivergedAt or CollapsedAt. That contradicts the completion field's whole purpose. v0.2 makes RL-Length and RL-Eval completion-aware. Pre-review also lacked grad_norms (H1/H2 require finite gradient norms across all phases).

## Files

- gbf-artifact/src/schemas/ids.rs (LayerId, ExpertId; enforce inclusive range)
- gbf-artifact/src/schemas/run_log.rs (RunLog with completion-aware invariants + grad_norms field)
- gbf-train/src/runtime/run_log.rs (emitter respects partial completion)
- gbf-artifact/tests/run_log_partial.rs (DivergedAt at step 1234 → losses.length = 1234)

## Acceptance

- LayerId / ExpertId reject n_blocks / n_experts at validation (off-by-one fixed in deserialization).
- RunLog with completion = DivergedAt(1234) has losses.length = 1234 and eval_points.length = floor(1234/1000)+1.
- grad_norms field is present in every RunLog; finite for every step on Completed; truncated on partial completion.
- ScoreReport.token_count = length(charset_v1_encode(normalize(val_bytes))) — not raw byte length.

## Reasoning chain

T5.2 is independent of T5.1 and can land in parallel. It is consumed by T2.x (raw diagnostics emission), T4.x (telemetry's layer_id field uses LayerId), and T3.x (closure reads RunLog completion to determine outcome).

title: Falsifier suite: F13 bias-direction; new F14 pareto-broken; new F15 feedback-broken
description:
# Goal

Fix three falsifier cases:

  - F13 (emulator-oracle-disagree): replace bias direction so the argmax actually changes.
  - F14 (pareto-broken): NEW case as a dedicated falsifier for H14, no longer folded into F11.
  - F15 (feedback-broken): NEW case as a dedicated falsifier for H16, no longer folded into F-rule-violation.

# Background / Why

F13 original: \"bias logits by +0.5 on the P2 prompt's predicted token\" -- biasing the predicted token UP preserves argmax agreement, so it does not refute H15. The falsifier must force a different argmax.

F-pareto-broken / F-feedback-broken were originally folded into F11 (shadow stages missing) and F-rule-violation respectively, under merge-rule-8 \"single-case substitute\". That folding is incorrect because:
  - F11 is about \"shadow stages missing\", not about a broken Pareto emitter; the diagnostic surface is wrong.
  - F-rule-violation is about config rule violation; mutating router_state on empty ExpertSlotAffinity is a feedback-implementation bug, not a config violation.

# Change

In gbf-experiments::s5 + Cargo.toml features:

  - F13: patch BoundedKv export path to either (a) bias a non-oracle token above the predicted token, or (b) bias the predicted token below the runner-up.
  - F14: new feature gate s5-falsify-14 that replaces the Pareto emitter with one that always picks the first point. Expected: H14 Refuted, selection_authority=\"manual-override\" required for any allowed closure.
  - F15: new feature gate s5-falsify-15 that mutates router_state on empty ExpertSlotAffinity OR changes one safe_bound update constant. Expected: H16 Refuted.

Scripts:
  - scripts/s5_falsification_suite.sh runs each F-case (1..15) one at a time and asserts the expected verdict.

# Why this matters

F-case fidelity is the entire proof that the closure gates actually gate. Folding two F-cases into unrelated parent cases hides which capability the test is exercising and risks coupling unrelated bugs.

# Considerations

  - Falsification features are mutually exclusive (Cargo features arranged so any pair of s5-falsify-* fails to compile).
  - F14 ties to FrontierRecommendation B (see B04) -- selection_authority manual-override flow must exist.

# Verification

  - F13 with biased logits -> H15 Refuted.
  - F14 with stub Pareto emitter -> H14 Refuted + selection_authority not \"automated\".
  - F15 with mutated router_state -> H16 Refuted.
  - Compile guard: enabling s5-falsify-14 + s5-falsify-15 simultaneously -> compile error.

# Related RFC sections

  §15 F-cases F1..F15, §11 dispatch, H14, H16, H15.

# Depends on

  B04 (FrontierRecommendation B for F14 semantics);
  B08 (Pareto by-name rules for F14 negative case).

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Why this bead exists

§15.2 + §16.6 mandate an end-to-end smoke run on a TINY in-repo fixture
corpus (NOT TinyStories) used in CI to gate determinism (O2) and per-seed
isolation (O9) on every PR.

The full TinyStories run is a separate, slower CI job (§15.2 explicit:
"The full TinyStories run is gated behind a separate CI job"). The tiny-
fixture smoke run gives PR-cycle feedback without spending 10000 steps × 5
seeds on the real corpus.

## Scope

- Author a tiny fixture corpus in `gbf-experiments/tests/integration/fixtures/`:
    train_bytes: ~16 KiB of synthetic UTF-8 text (e.g. tiled Lorem Ipsum)
    val_bytes: ~4 KiB of similar text
    Both with sha256 pinned in a tiny TOML alongside the corpus.
- An integration TrainConfig with REDUCED budgets:
    optimizer_steps: 100  (NOT 10000)
    batch_size: 4
    sequence_length: 32
    eval_every_steps: 25
  Keep AdamW pinned per D10. The reduced budgets are FOR TESTS ONLY and
  are NOT a relaxation of the F-S1 contract — production S1 uses the
  pinned budgets always.
- Test cases in `tests/integration/*.rs`:
    - 5-seed run completes without divergence
    - Two of five seeds produce different final_checkpoint_sha (O9)
    - Replay seed 0 twice → byte-identical safetensors (O2)
    - [0,1] vs [1,0] swap → identical per-seed hashes (O9)
    - The full pipeline writes the expected artifacts under a temp dir.
- Total wall clock budget for the suite: well under the project's standard
  test timeout. Document the actual measured time in the test header.

## Considerations

- This is a smoke test, NOT a closure gate. Closure of bd-12pl requires the
  full TinyStories run + s1_report.v1 (per §15.2).
- The fixture corpus is permanent and small enough to commit. Keep the
  fixture's expected hashes pinned in the test resource so future-self can
  detect drift.
- Future-self: if you reduce `optimizer_steps` in production, you have
  changed the experiment per D3 — that requires an RFC amendment, not just
  a code change.

## RFC anchors

- §15.2 Test layout (integration row)
- §16.6 CI gates (cargo test -p gbf-experiments --test integration)
- §13 O2, O9
- §10 Rep-1, Rep-7
- D3 (production budgets), D10 (optimizer)

title: T-B4.10: RuntimeChromeBudget binding + missing-budget hard reject
description:
## What
Bind `RuntimeChromeBudget` as a Stage 2 invocation input (NOT part of
CompileRequest). When absent, hard-reject with
`BudgetMissingRuntimeChromeBudget` and emit the only Stage-2 report shape
that allows `runtime_chrome_budget_hash = None`. Implement the
effective-cap arithmetic. See RFC §2.9, §2.13 (effective_cap math), §7.9.5.

## Why
RuntimeChromeBudget is emitted by the runtime-shell build, not the
compiler. It's a separate input from CompileRequest because compile
requests are cheap to vary across runtime-shell builds. Missing budget
is fail-closed because we'd otherwise fall into "synthesizing dummy
budgets" — exactly the shift-left antipattern this chunk avoids.

## Inputs
- T-B4.9 BudgetFailure taxonomy (`BudgetMissingRuntimeChromeBudget`,
  `BudgetWramPeakExceeds`, etc.).
- T-B2.18 bringup-*.chrome_budget.json fixtures.
- `gbf-policy::budget::RuntimeChromeBudget`.

## Outputs
- `pub struct CompileInvocationInputs { artifact_ref, compile_request, target_profile, runtime_chrome_budget: Option<RuntimeChromeBudget> }` (added to gbf-policy if not yet present).
- Stage 2 entry point handles `runtime_chrome_budget == None` by emitting
  a static_budget.json with `outcome=Failed`,
  `runtime_chrome_budget_hash = None`, `runtime_chrome_budget = None`,
  `decision.fits = false`, exactly one `BudgetMissingRuntimeChromeBudget`
  diagnostic.
- Effective cap arithmetic: `effective_cap_bytes: i64 = usable_bytes - reserved_slack`.
  No relaxation term (RFC §2.13).
- All operands widened to i64; do not saturate or wrap.

## Pitfalls
- The "no budget" report is the ONLY Stage-2 report shape allowed to set
  `runtime_chrome_budget_hash` to None — see RFC §7.7 invariant.
- DO NOT mutate the source `RuntimeChromeBudget` in flight. Bringup uses a
  *different* budget file (`bringup-*.chrome_budget.json`) per §2.13.
- Underflow: if `reserved_slack > usable_bytes`, the effective cap is
  negative and the relevant placement check fails. Don't saturate to 0.

## Acceptance
- gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_rejects_missing_runtime_chrome_budget
- gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_missing_runtime_chrome_budget_emits_failure_report_without_budget_hash
- gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_uses_reserved_slack_in_effective_cap

## Refs
- RFC §2.9, §2.13 effective_cap, §7.7 missing-budget invariant, §7.9.5 worked example.
- Depends on: T-B4.9, T-B2.18.
- Blocks: T-B4.11.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## RFC amendments (2026-05-07)

Three §2.9 / §7.6 / §7.7 tightenings:

**1. Missing budget records BOTH a Hard diagnostic AND a BudgetFailure (§2.9, §7.7)**

When `runtime_chrome_budget == None`, Stage 2 emits:
- `ValidationCode::BudgetMissingRuntimeChromeBudget` (Hard diagnostic), AND
- `BudgetFailure::MissingRuntimeChromeBudget` (in `decision.failures`).

This preserves the invariant `decision.fits == decision.failures.is_empty()`
(both must be true OR both false). The previous spec only required the
diagnostic; the failure entry is new.

**2. Stage 2 short-circuits BEFORE `to_budget_view()` when budget missing
(§2.1, §7.6)**

If `runtime_chrome_budget == None`, Stage 2 fails the report **before**
calling `QuantGraphBudgetSource::to_budget_view()`. The missing-budget
report shape therefore has `identity.runtime_chrome_budget_hash = None` AND
`identity.quant_graph_hash` may be the recorded value from
`QuantGraphBudgetSource::quant_graph_hash()` (which is cheap; doesn't
require `to_budget_view`).

A new schema invariant: 'if `BudgetMissingRuntimeChromeBudget` is present,
no `QuantGraphBudgetView` conversion was attempted'.

**3. `runtime_chrome_budget` section is a hash-checked excerpt (§7.7)**

When `runtime_chrome_budget.is_some()`, the embedded
`runtime_chrome_budget` section is a canonical review excerpt and must hash
to `runtime_chrome_budget_hash`. The excerpt is NOT the source of truth —
the budget itself lives in its own JSON file.

New acceptance tests:
- `gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_missing_runtime_chrome_budget_records_budget_failure`
- `gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_missing_runtime_chrome_budget_does_not_call_to_budget_view`
- `gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_runtime_chrome_budget_excerpt_hash_matches_input`

Cross-refs: §2.9, §7.6 short-circuit rule, §7.7 excerpt invariant + missing-budget
shape.

title: T-B3.0: quant_graph.v1 ReportEnvelope binding (canonical-JSON + self-hash)
description:
## What
Bind `quant_graph.v1` to the `ReportEnvelope` machinery from F-B2 (T-B2.2):
declare the `QuantGraphReportBody` shape, the `ReportBody` impl with
`SCHEMA_ID = "quant_graph.v1"`, the `outcome ⇔ result` invariant
(QG-2/QG-3), and a canonical-JSON / self-hash round-trip helper
(`quant_graph_canonical_bytes_hash`). See RFC §10.1.

## Why
The next 26 F-B3 tasks all emit fields *into* this body. Pinning the
envelope first stops every later task from re-inventing JSON shape, hash
rules, or outcome semantics. F-B2/F-B4 already paid this cost once
(bd-2xlj); F-B3 inherits, never forks.

A product-bearing report (`body.result.product: QuantGraph`) is the
contract F-C2 (`bd-c4wg`) and StageCache will read by hash — committing
to that contract now pre-empts a `summary-only` vs `product-bearing`
divergence later (Ambiguity A51 in the RFC ledger).

## Inputs
- `gbf-report::ReportEnvelope<R>`, `ReportBody` trait (T-B2.2 / bd-2xlj).
- `gbf-foundation::{Hash256, DomainHash}`.
- `gbf-codegen` schema-version constants.

## Outputs
- `pub struct QuantGraphReportBody { input_identity, result: Option<...>, diagnostics }`
  with placeholder field types for sub-bodies that later tasks fill in.
- `impl ReportBody for QuantGraphReportBody { const SCHEMA_ID = "quant_graph.v1"; ... }`.
- `quant_graph_canonical_bytes_hash` derived via the F-B2/F-B4 `DomainHash`
  convention (Ambiguity A52: bitwise-mixing of sub-hashes is forbidden).
- Round-trip test: `parse → canonicalize → semantic_validate → self_hash`
  is byte-stable on a synthetic empty/passing body.

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT introduce a separate `quant_graph.v1.test` schema variant
  (Ambiguity A44). Use the same schema with explicit `cfg(test)` gating.
- DO NOT mix sub-hashes via XOR or concatenation — only `DomainHash` over
  CanonicalJson is permitted (Ambiguity A52, RFC §8.8).
- The placeholder body must keep `result: Option<...>` and `outcome ⇔ result`
  enforceable (QG-2, QG-3) even before sub-bodies exist — failing reports
  must still be expressible at this stage.

## Acceptance
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_v1_envelope_round_trips_canonically`.
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_v1_outcome_iff_result_passed_invariant`.
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_v1_self_hash_uses_domain_hash_not_bitwise_mix`.

## Refs
- RFC §10.1 (QuantGraphReportBody schema), §11 (DomainHash convention).
- Ambiguity ledger: A51 (product-bearing), A52 (no bitwise mixing), A77
  (hash the raw IR struct, no zeroing).
- Inherits from: bd-2xlj (T-B2.2 ReportEnvelope), bd-5lrn (T-F-S1.05
  CanonicalJson — S1 already exercises the same canonical-JSON helpers).
- Blocks: T-B3.1 (QuantGraph type), T-B3.24 (final schema wire-up).

Gates: cargo test -p gbf-codegen quant_graph_v1, cargo test -p gbf-codegen report::tests, cargo test -p gbf-report quant_graph_v1, cargo fmt --check --all. Reviews: Gemini PASS after logging/canonicalization/self-hash/null-path fixes; Claude PASS-track with null-result coverage added. Triage: sibling-bead scope findings accepted as multi-bead RFC branch behavior, not per-bead blockers.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## §20 amendments (post-PR-#14)

The deployed `gbf-report::ReportBody` trait carries three `&'static str`
constants (REPORT_TYPE / SCHEMA_ID / SCHEMA_VERSION) and a
`validate_semantics(&self, outcome: ReportOutcome) -> Result<(),
Vec<ValidationDiagnostic>>` method that takes outcome as a parameter.
For `quant_graph.v1`: `REPORT_TYPE = "quant_graph"`, `SCHEMA_ID =
"quant_graph.v1"`. The QG-2 / QG-3 outcome ⇔ result invariant is
enforced INSIDE `validate_semantics`, not by a separate cross-check.

`ReportEnvelope { schema, schema_version, outcome, report_self_hash,
body }` — `report_self_hash: Hash256` is set to `Hash256::ZERO` during
canonical-JSON serialization for hashing, then back to the computed
hash via `with_computed_self_hash()`. Use `gbf-report::canonical_json`
helpers (`canonicalize`, `compute_self_hash`, `round_trip_self_hash`)
rather than reinventing.

The raw `QuantGraph` struct still does not carry its own self-hash
(Ambiguity A77 unchanged); the hash lives on the report envelope and
on `QuantGraphProduct`.

See RFC §20.4 for the full deployed signature.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Comprehensive implementation plan (2026-05-10)

### Scope (full public surface)
- `pub struct QuantGraphReportBody { input_identity, result: Option<QuantGraphResult>, diagnostics }`.
- `impl ReportBody for QuantGraphReportBody` with `REPORT_TYPE = "quant_graph"`, `SCHEMA_ID = "quant_graph.v1"`, `SCHEMA_VERSION = "0.1.0"` (or current).
- `validate_semantics(&self, outcome: ReportOutcome) -> Result<(), Vec<ValidationDiagnostic>>` (deployed signature per RFC §20.4).
- `quant_graph_canonical_bytes_hash` derived via `gbf-report::canonical_json::compute_self_hash` (DomainHash convention; raw IR struct never carries its own hash per Ambiguity A77).

### Unit tests (positive)
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_v1_envelope_round_trips_canonically`
  — build a passing `QuantGraphReportBody`, wrap in `ReportEnvelope::new`, call `with_computed_self_hash`, serialize, deserialize, re-canonicalize, assert byte-identical.
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_v1_self_hash_uses_domain_hash_not_bitwise_mix`
  — assert `compute_self_hash` over a fixed body matches a hand-computed `DomainHash("gbf-codegen", "QuantGraph", schema, canonical_json_bytes)` (Ambiguity A52 regression).
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_v1_passed_with_result_some`
  — `outcome = Passed` + `result = Some(_)` + no Hard diagnostics → validates clean.
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_v1_failed_with_result_none_and_hard_diag`
  — `outcome = Failed` + `result = None` + ≥1 Hard diagnostic → validates clean.
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_v1_canonical_field_order_pinned`
  — `serde_json::json!` round-trip pinning every top-level field name in deployed canonical-JSON output.

### Unit tests (negative — outcome ⇔ result invariant)
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_v1_passed_with_result_none_diagnostic`
  — emits `ReportOutcomeMissingResult`.
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_v1_failed_with_result_some_diagnostic`
  — emits `ReportOutcomeUnexpectedResult`.
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_v1_passed_with_hard_diag_diagnostic`
  — emits `ReportOutcomePassedWithHardDiagnostic`.

### Property / regression tests
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_v1_round_trip_idempotent_under_canonicalize_twice`
  — proof obligation O1: `canonicalize(parse(canonicalize(envelope)))` = `canonicalize(envelope)`.
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_v1_self_hash_zero_during_hashing`
  — assert that `compute_self_hash` sees `report_self_hash = Hash256::ZERO` during the hash computation (regression for the A77 self-hash-zeroing convention).
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_v1_schema_id_constant_matches_envelope_field`
  — compile-time + runtime check that `R::SCHEMA_ID` == envelope.schema string.

### Logging requirements (per `logging-bead-closure` skill)
- `tracing::info!("stage1.envelope.bind", schema = "quant_graph.v1")` on body construction.
- `tracing::debug!("stage1.envelope.canonicalize", canonical_bytes_len = ...)`.
- `tracing::debug!("stage1.envelope.self_hash", report_self_hash = %hash)`.
- ERROR span with typed `ReportOutcomeMismatch` codes on outcome ⇔ result drift.
- Reuse the deployed `gbf-report::canonical_json` helpers — do not reimplement.

### E2E touch
This bead is consumed by the chunk-closure e2e bead (`bd-d06f`) which
asserts `quant_graph.json` round-trips byte-identically across runs.
Direct e2e is bd-2sp5 (fixtures) which exercises the envelope on every
synthetic Toy QG.

### Acceptance gate
All 11 listed tests pass. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings` passes (project pre-commit hook).

title: F-S3.23: gbf-experiments::s3::cli + gbf-cli S3Command dispatch (ReplayFull/ReplayFallback/VerifyDeterminism/NormalizeCorpus/FitBaseline/ExportBundle/ExportArtifact/OracleAgreement/OracleReRun/Report)
description:
## Context

The `gbf s3 …` CLI surface mirrors the landed F-S2 `gbf s2 …` (`gbf-experiments/src/s2/cli.rs:42-1189`). S3 introduces the `S3Command` enum with 10 verbs:

```
S3Command :=
  | ReplayFull(args)              ; full S3 run for a build/seed cell
  | ReplayFallback(args)          ; same training, fallback oracle backend
  | VerifyDeterminism(args)       ; replay seed/build twice and byte-compare
  | NormalizeCorpus(args)         ; runs s3_charset_v1 only
  | FitBaseline(args)             ; runs s3_fit_kn5 only
  | ExportBundle(args)            ; runs s3_export_reference_bundle for one seed
  | ExportArtifact(args)          ; runs s3_export_model_artifact for one seed
  | OracleAgreement(args)         ; runs phase-specific surface agreement
  | OracleReRun(args)             ; re-runs S1 + S2 oracle suites under S3 binary
  | Report(args)                  ; emits s3_report.v1
```

Each verb emits machine-readable JSON for CI consumption + structured NDJSON CLI events (mirroring `S2CliLogging`).

**The `report` verb's evidence-file format is pinned via `s3_replay_full_cli.v1` and `s3_export_bundle_cli.v1` etc. schemas** (mirroring F-S2's `s2_replay_full_cli.v1` from `s2_determinism_check.sh:65`) so the report knows exactly what evidence shape to consume.

## Why this matters

The CLI is the canonical replay surface (RFC §16.4). CI scripts (B24) shell into it; the determinism check, isolation check, api-drift check all consume CLI JSON output. Without B23, the CI matrix can't run.

## Deliverables

1. `gbf-experiments/src/s3/cli.rs` (mirrors `s2/cli.rs:42-1189`):
   - `pub enum S3Command { ReplayFull(...), ReplayFallback(...), VerifyDeterminism(...), NormalizeCorpus(...), FitBaseline(...), ExportBundle(...), ExportArtifact(...), OracleAgreement(...), OracleReRun(...), Report(...) }`
   - `pub fn run(cli: S3Cli) -> Result<(), S3CliError>` entrypoint
   - `pub struct S3CliLogging { format, level, log_file, capture_events }` mirroring S2CliLogging
   - All verbs accept `--manifest`, `--workload`, `--chrome-budget`, `--pass-version`, `--seed-list`, `--build-kind`, `--device-profile`, `--export-visitor-id` per RFC §16.4 canonical replay command
   - All verbs emit NDJSON CLI events to `--capture-events` sink for CI assertions
2. `gbf-experiments/src/s3/cli/evidence_schemas.rs` — evidence-file JSON schemas mirroring `s2_replay_full_cli.v1`:
   - `s3_replay_full_cli.v1` — emitted by ReplayFull; contains all per-seed checkpoint hashes + bundle/artifact self-hashes + agreement_self_hash
   - `s3_export_bundle_cli.v1` — emitted by ExportBundle; contains bundle_self_hash + canonical_bundle_payload_sha
   - `s3_export_artifact_cli.v1` — emitted by ExportArtifact; contains artifact_self_hash + canonical_artifact_payload_sha + tied_embedding_alias metadata
   - `s3_oracle_agreement_cli.v1` — emitted by OracleAgreement; contains AgreementProduct
   - `s3_charset_normalize_cli.v1` — emitted by NormalizeCorpus
   - `s3_fit_baseline_cli.v1` — emitted by FitBaseline
3. `gbf-cli/src/main.rs`:
   - Add `GbfCommand::S3 { command: S3Command }` arm
   - Wire `gbf-experiments::s3::cli::run` per `S3` arm (mirrors S2 wiring at lines 33-38, 48-54)
4. The `report` verb consumes evidence files via `--replay-full <path>`, `--export-bundle <path>`, etc., parsing them via the schemas above

## Test scaffolding

1. **`gbf-cli/tests/s3_cli_s3.rs`** (mirrors `gbf-cli/tests/s2_cli_s2.rs`):
   - End-to-end CLI invocation tests for every verb
   - Canonical command from RFC §16.4 reproduces `experiments/S3/**` byte-for-byte
2. **`gbf-experiments/tests/cli_help_snapshots_s3.rs`** — per-verb `--help` snapshot:
   - `gbf s3 replay-full --help` text matches insta snapshot
   - One snapshot per verb (10 snapshots)
3. **`gbf-experiments/tests/cli_evidence_schema_round_trip_s3.rs`**:
   - For each evidence schema (s3_replay_full_cli.v1, etc.), round-trip through canonical JSON
   - Assert reading + re-emitting produces byte-identical output
4. **`gbf-experiments/tests/cli_capture_events_s3.rs`**:
   - For each verb: invoke with `--capture-events /tmp/...`
   - Assert the file contains valid NDJSON with the expected event taxonomy
   - Mirrors `gbf-experiments/tests/cli_scripts_s2.rs` event-shape assertions
5. **`gbf-experiments/tests/cli_canonical_replay_s3.rs`** — full canonical replay command from RFC §16.4 produces `experiments/S3/**` byte-for-byte (uses tiny-corpus fixture for budget)
6. **`gbf-experiments/tests/cli_build_kind_dispatch_s3.rs`** — passing `--build-kind s3_v0_success_fallback_oracle` against a binary built with only `s3-oracle-real` returns a structured runtime error (NOT a panic)

## Logging discipline

Every verb emits a CLI lifecycle event:
```
event_name = "s3::cli::start"
fields: { verb, args, build_kind, pass_version_S3 }

event_name = "s3::cli::stage_start"
fields: { verb, stage_name, stage_index }

event_name = "s3::cli::stage_complete"
fields: { verb, stage_name, stage_index, passed, duration_ms }

event_name = "s3::cli::done"
fields: { verb, exit_code, total_duration_ms }

target = "gbf_experiments::s3::cli"
```
Subscriber-level test `gbf-experiments/tests/cli_logging_s3.rs` asserts events fire for every verb.

## E2E acceptance script

`scripts/s3_cli_smoke.sh`:
1. Iterates through every S3Command verb
2. Invokes with `--help` (snapshot test)
3. Invokes with minimal valid args + `--capture-events /tmp/s3-cli-<verb>.ndjson`
4. Asserts NDJSON contains start + done events at minimum
5. Asserts evidence file emission for verbs that produce one

## Inheritance / non-duplication

- DOES NOT introduce a new logging framework; reuses S2CliLogging shape.
- DOES NOT modify F-S2 CLI; just adds the new `S3` arm.

## Considerations

- `--build-kind s3_v0_success_real_oracle` is the default; specifying `--build-kind s3_v0_success_fallback_oracle` requires the binary to have been built with `s3-oracle-fallback`. The runtime check is needed because feature combos are static at build time.
- The `report` verb consumes JSON evidence files emitted by other verbs (mirroring `gbf s2 report --replay-full <path>` from `s2/cli.rs:247-260`). Pin the evidence-file schemas explicitly so the report knows what to expect.

## Acceptance

```
cargo test -p gbf-cli --features s3-full -- s3_cli_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real" --test cli_help_snapshots_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real" --test cli_evidence_schema_round_trip_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real" --test cli_capture_events_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real" --test cli_canonical_replay_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real" --test cli_build_kind_dispatch_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real" --test cli_logging_s3
scripts/s3_cli_smoke.sh
```

## Out of scope

- CI workflow YAML (B24)
- The actual report markdown body (B21 owns)

## References

- RFC §16.4 "Canonical replay command"; §16.1 gbf-cli Required
- F-S2 CLI: `gbf-experiments/src/s2/cli.rs:42-1189`; `gbf-cli/src/main.rs:1-61`

title: T-A8.7: Predicate persistence — closure-shaped vs stringified-source predicates
description: Two predicate kinds: closure-shaped (JS function reference for in-script breakpoint conditions; lives only for current invocation), stringified-source (text serialized into the session file; re-parsed on next invocation; survives session round-trips). add_breakpoint accepts both; the persistence decision is explicit, not inferred.
close_reason: Implemented in F-A8 gbf-debug PR; gates recorded in closure comments. Parent feature closes in this same PR.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## 2026-05-04 amendment — F-A7 predicate mapping

F-A7 has merged. F-A7's trap dispatcher exposes `Predicate::{Always, Closure(Box<TrapPredicate>), Source(String)}` (see `gbf-emu/src/trap.rs`), but `predicate_matches` returns `TrapPredicateError::SourceRequiresEvaluator` when asked to evaluate `Predicate::Source` directly — F-A7 cannot itself host a JS evaluator. F-A8 therefore uses this mapping (RFC §3.3.5):

- `gb.add_breakpoint(addr)` (no predicate): registers `Predicate::Always` with F-A7; persists as `PersistedPredicate::None`.
- `gb.add_breakpoint(addr, fn)` (closure): wraps the JS closure in a Rust `Box<TrapPredicate>` that calls back into QuickJS, registers as `Predicate::Closure`; **not** persisted (warning emitted).
- `gb.add_breakpoint(addr, "expr")` (string): wraps the source in a Rust closure that re-evaluates the expression in a read-only QuickJS scope on every fire, registers as `Predicate::Closure`; persists as `PersistedPredicate::StringifiedSource(s)`. F-A7's `Predicate::Source` exists for export-friendly persistence shape (see `PredicateSpec::Source`) but F-A8 does not register `Source` directly because F-A7 cannot evaluate it.

The read-only predicate scope is `{ regs, pc, access, cycle, view, symbol(name), symbolInBank(name, bank) }` — F-A7's `TrapContext` carries `regs/pc/access/cycle/view`; `symbol`/`symbolInBank` are F-A8 additions resolving through the in-session `SessionSymbolTable`. `TrapAction` is always `HaltAndReport` (F-A8 always wants the run loop to stop and surface the hit).

comments.author: bkase
comments.text: Closed by F-A8 implementation. Source of truth: RFC §§3.1.5, 3.3.5. Implemented explicit predicate split: no predicate and stringified-source persist; closure predicates are invocation-local, warn with predicate_not_persisted, and never become unconditional persisted breakpoints. run_until_breakpoint now evaluates predicates before surfacing traps; closure predicates see the documented temporary predicate scope and read-only gb view. Gates: cargo test -p gbf-debug --test e2e string_predicate_round_trips_without_becoming_unconditional; cargo test -p gbf-debug --test e2e closure_predicate_is_invocation_local_and_warned; workspace clippy/test.

title: F-S7 v0.2 Implementation Track — verified MoE-beats-dense at matched bytes
description:
## Context

F-S7 ("MoE Beats Dense at Matched Bytes"; slice S7; closure bead bd-2v9r) underwent pre-implementation correctness review on 2026-05-20 and a second-pass diff review on 2026-06-03. Together those reviews surfaced 25 textual fixes that have been applied to history/rfcs/F-S7-moe-beats-dense.md (v0.2 of the contract).

The RFC patches change the *contract* the implementation must honor. This epic tracks the **implementation work** that follows from v0.2 — the code, schemas, tests, harnesses, and CI gates that make bd-2v9r closeable against v0.2 rather than the broken pre-review v0.1.

## Why this epic is mandatory before bd-2v9r begins

S7's deliverable is *verified knowledge*, not just code. Three things only work if the implementation matches the patched RFC:

1. Pre-registration discipline (S1 O1; Rep-S7-8). The RFC's predictions and falsification rules must appear in git history strictly before the first S7 result artifact commit. If implementation begins against a contract that cannot honestly be satisfied (e.g. v0.1's H7 claim that lm_loss reaches LowRankRouter parameters under hard top-1 stop-gradient dispatch — mathematically impossible), the pre-registration is poisoned and bd-2v9r cannot honestly close.
2. Falsification suite (§16 O5). Nine deliberately broken substitutes must each produce the expected Refuted verdict on the corresponding hypothesis. These tests typecheck against v0.2's hypothesis statements; they do not compile against the v0.1 wording.
3. Outcome algebra totality (O7). Every observable combination of H1..H10 verdicts must map to exactly one S7Outcome. v0.1 collapsed bytes-mismatch into Fail-parity (which closes bd-2v9r as DenseOnly — a successful scientific verdict for an *invalid* experiment). v0.2 separates Fail-bytes (Halt) from Fail-parity (DenseOnly).

## The five load-bearing fixes the implementation must honor

1. Router gradient provenance under hard top-1 dispatch. D3 says dispatch is stop-gradient → lm/distill cannot reach LowRankRouter via that path. H7 declares this; O13 asserts it; the loss composer in gbf-train must respect it.
2. "Matched bytes" = total deployed bytes, not FFN payload. Both H3 and H4 now route through B_deployed_total (FFN + router + bias + metadata). The MatchedBytesPin includes b_router_overhead_total and pins a bias_policy.
3. Fail-bytes vs Fail-parity. AggregateParityVerdict has three variants now (Pass-clean, Fail-parity, Fail-bytes). Outcome dispatch sends Fail-bytes to Halt, not DenseOnly.
4. Entropy units = bits, everywhere. RouterStepTelemetry, LambdaSwitchSweepStep, SwitchStatsSummary, guardrail decisions, all use expert_usage_entropy_bits and log2(n_experts). The 1.7-bits floor for n=4 is now self-consistent.
5. Dense byte solver fairness. solve_d_ff_dense minimizes |B_deployed(Dense) − B_deployed(MoE)| with explicit tie-breaks (prefer Dense ≥ MoE, then smaller d_ff). The pre-review smallest-within-tolerance rule systematically biased the experiment toward MoE.

## Scope

Six feature areas decompose the 25 RFC patches into implementation work:
- F1 Byte Accounting & Matched-Bytes Parity
- F2 Router Gradient Provenance & Loss Composition
- F3 Outcome Algebra & Pareto Verdict
- F4 Telemetry, Sweep Harness & H6 Guardrail
- F5 Switch-Stats Schema & Artifact Integrity
- F6 Training Substrate Robustness

## Out of scope

- Pre-implementation RFC text patches (already applied; tracked under bd-2p7g v0.2 patch series).
- S8 production-scale work (bd-218w).
- Real ROM emulation at scale (S5/F-A8 owns the one-token harness; S7 carries through).
- F-C4 dashboard/report adoption of router telemetry.

## Closure

This epic closes when:
- All six features under it are closed.
- bd-2v9r's predicate references F-S7 v0.2 (pass_version bumped in s7_report.v1 before first result artifact commit per O1).
- The 9-test falsification suite passes against v0.2 hypothesis statements.
- O11 standalone matched-bytes CI test passes against the canonical MoeTiny instance.
- O13 gradient-provenance assertion suite passes, including the new lm/distill → LowRankRouter zero-gradient assertions.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## T-B1.0.9: Structured tracing event vocabulary + subscriber-level test capture infra

**Target paths**:
- `crates/gbf-runtime/src/trace/events.rs` (typed event vocabulary)
- `crates/gbf-runtime/src/trace/subscriber.rs` (test-time subscriber + assertion helpers)

### Background

AGENTS.md is explicit: **"Logging helper closure must cite subscriber-level capture for event shape and move real producer/dashboard adoption to a named owner bead when no executable producer exists."**

F-B1's runtime + emulator + harness emit many distinct events:

- **Banking**: `BankLeaseAcquired`, `BankLeaseReleased`, `MbcRegisterWrite`, `BankShadowUpdate`.
- **Yielding**: `YieldCheckpoint`, `LivenessProgressEpochAdvance`, `SchedulerResumed`.
- **Tile lifecycle**: `TileEntered`, `TileCompleteSafePoint`, `HarnessDumpRequested`, `HarnessResumeAcknowledged`.
- **Frame**: `VBlankFired`, `WidgetTickDispatched`, `SchedulerServicedFrame`, `YieldReturnedToScheduler`.
- **Codegen-time**: `ComputeBringupRequestImported`, `LowerToIrComplete`, `LowerToAsmIrComplete`, `RomEmitted`.
- **Validators**: `ValidatorAccepted`, `ValidatorRejected{rule, evidence}`.

Without a typed vocabulary, each producer invents its own field names; consumers (the test subscriber, the realism-report aggregator, the future M1 schedule oracle) end up doing string-matching. AGENTS.md prohibits this.

### Typed vocabulary

```rust
// gbf-runtime/src/trace/events.rs
#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind")]
pub enum FB1TraceEvent {
    BankLeaseAcquired   { bank: u16, mcycle: u64, lease_id: u32 },
    BankLeaseReleased   { bank: u16, mcycle: u64, lease_id: u32 },
    MbcRegisterWrite    { register: u16, value: u8, mcycle: u64 },
    YieldCheckpoint     { mcycle: u64, quantum: YieldQuantumKind, products_completed: u32 },
    LivenessProgress    { mcycle: u64, progress_epoch: u32 },
    TileEntered         { mt: u16, nt: u16, mcycle: u64 },
    TileCompleteSafePt  { mt: u16, nt: u16, mcycle: u64, source_addr: u16 },
    HarnessDumpReq      { mcycle: u64, addr: u16, len: u16 },
    HarnessResumeAck    { mcycle: u64 },
    VBlankFired         { frame: u32, mcycle: u64 },
    WidgetTickDispatched{ frame: u32, mcycle: u64 },
    SchedulerServiced   { frame: u32, mcycle: u64 },
    YieldReturned       { frame: u32, mcycle: u64, remaining_frame_mcycles: u32 },
    ComputeReqImported  { request_hash: String },
    LowerToIrComplete   { ir_hash: String },
    LowerToAsmIrComplete{ asmir_hash: String },
    RomEmitted          { rom_sha256: String, bytes: u32 },
    ValidatorAccepted   { rule: &'static str, scope: String },
    ValidatorRejected   { rule: &'static str, scope: String, evidence: String },
}
```

These are the **structured fields** on `tracing` events; producers emit via:

```rust
tracing::info!(
    target = "gbf::fb1",
    event = "BankLeaseAcquired",
    bank = bank,
    mcycle = mcycle,
    lease_id = lease_id,
);
```

A converter walks captured events back into `FB1TraceEvent` for assertions.

### Test subscriber

```rust
// gbf-runtime/src/trace/subscriber.rs
pub struct CapturedTrace {
    events: Vec<FB1TraceEvent>,
}

impl CapturedTrace {
    pub fn capture<F: FnOnce()>(f: F) -> Self;
    pub fn count(&self, predicate: impl Fn(&FB1TraceEvent) -> bool) -> usize;
    pub fn first(&self, predicate: impl Fn(&FB1TraceEvent) -> bool) -> Option<&FB1TraceEvent>;
    pub fn ordered_pairs(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&FB1TraceEvent, &FB1TraceEvent)>;
    pub fn assert_lease_acquire_release_balance(&self) -> Result<(), TraceAssertionError>;
    pub fn assert_no_yield_while_lease_active(&self) -> Result<(), TraceAssertionError>;
    pub fn assert_widget_tick_per_gated_frame(&self, gated: Range<u32>) -> Result<(), TraceAssertionError>;
}
```

The capture helper installs a `tracing::Dispatch` for the duration of the closure, decodes structured events, and returns them.

### Why this is load-bearing

Every L2..L5 test in F-B1 needs at least one of:

- "exactly N lease acquires happened"
- "no yield happened while a lease was held"
- "widget ticked once per gated frame"
- "the validator emitted ValidatorRejected with rule=X for fixture Y"

Doing this with stringy event field names creates 30+ places where a test could be silently wrong because it's matching the wrong field. Centralizing the vocabulary and the assertion helpers eliminates that whole class of bug.

### Logging discipline (per AGENTS.md)

- Each producer call site uses the typed event helper, never raw `tracing::info!("BankLease…")` strings.
- Subscriber-level capture in tests proves event *shape*, not just event *count*.
- The test that validates the validator-rejection event *includes* the reason string in the captured event and asserts it (subscriber-level capture for event shape).

### Acceptance gates

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- trace::events_serde_round_trip
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- trace::subscriber_captures_emitted_event_shape
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- trace::subscriber_helpers_assert_lease_balance
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- trace::subscriber_helpers_detect_yield_under_lease
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- trace::subscriber_helpers_detect_missed_widget_tick
```

### RFC reference

`history/rfcs/F-B1-compute-bringup.md` §9.1 (frame events), §11.4 (banking correctness).
AGENTS.md (logging-bead guidance).

### Dependencies

- F-A3 (`TraceEvent` infrastructure — base channel).

### Forward links

Consumed by **all** T-B1.x test beads that capture events. Especially:
- T-B1.3.4 (no-yield-under-lease)
- T-B1.3.5 (lease metrics)
- T-B1.5.4 (frame events)
- T-B1.5.5 (frame trace ordering)
- T-B1.6.3 (aggregation)

title: F-S7 v0.2: TransitionEntry directional (from_expert/to_expert)
description:
## Description

Make `TransitionEntry` (§3.3) directional, with `from_expert: ExpertId` and `to_expert: ExpertId` fields. Pre-review schema stored `pair: UnorderedExpertPair` and §3.3.1 said directional entries get aggregated INTO unordered affinity by `a→b + b→a` SUM rule. But if the stored representation is already unordered, you can't recover directional transitions to aggregate. v0.2 keeps the directional info in TemporalSwitchDigest and applies canonicalization only at ExpertSlotAffinity construction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- §3.3 TransitionEntry definition: `from_expert: ExpertId; to_expert: ExpertId; mass_q8_8: u16`.
- TSD-3 uniqueness invariant: "no two TransitionEntry with the same (from_expert, to_expert) pair."
- TSD-5 invariant rewritten: "from_expert and to_expert are directional and are NOT canonicalized. Canonicalization occurs only when constructing ExpertSlotAffinity."
- §3.3.1 SUM aggregation rule unchanged: `aff(a, b) = transition_mass(a→b) + transition_mass(b→a)` for a < b.
- TemporalSwitchDigest deserialization rejects entries with identical from_expert/to_expert pairs (uniqueness).

## Notes

- Directional storage costs nothing extra (same field count, same byte size) but preserves the information needed by both downstream uses: ExpertSlotAffinity (aggregated) and any future bead that wants directional statistics.

title: F-S7 v0.2: Router gradient provenance (H7, §8.3.1/8.3.2, O13)
description:
## Description

The pre-review H7 declared that `distill_loss` and `lm_loss` reach "all student parameters (router, experts, embeddings, sequence-state, norm)." Under D3's hard top-1 stop-gradient dispatch, this is mathematically impossible: the dispatch indicator is one-hot and its gradient is the zero tensor by construction, so the LM/distillation objective does not directly train routing decisions. The router is trained only by `router_z_loss`, `balance_loss` (through `routing_probs`, not through dispatch), and `temporal_switch_penalty`. v0.2 makes this explicit in H7, §8.3.1, §8.3.2, and O13. It also records a "router task-coupling note" calling out the scientific risk: the LM objective doesn't train the router, which is a known limitation of hard-dispatch designs and may show up as a Refuted H3.

## Design

- H7 statement now says lm_loss and distill_loss reach student logits and through them "selected expert parameters, embeddings, sequence-state, and norm" (NOT router).
- New H7 negative-reach assertions: `∂ distill_loss / ∂ LowRankRouter params : ZERO through dispatch`; same for lm_loss.
- §8.3.1 lm_loss "Gradient provenance" section drops "router" from the reach set and adds the explicit zero-through-dispatch clause.
- §8.3.2 distill_loss "Gradient provenance" adds `∂ distill_loss / ∂ LowRankRouter params : ZERO through dispatch`.
- New "Router task-coupling note" in H7's body: documents that under hard dispatch without STE, the LM/distillation objective does not directly train routing decisions; this is an explicit scientific risk and is recorded as an observed limitation if H3 fails.
- O13 gains a new mandatory assertion: lm_loss and distill_loss have exactly-zero gradient on LowRankRouter parameters under hard top-1 stop-gradient dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- H7 statement for lm_loss and distill_loss lists only "selected expert parameters, embeddings, sequence-state, norm" as alive reach paths.
- H7 includes a "Router task-coupling note" naming the scientific risk.
- §8.3.1 and §8.3.2 gradient provenance match H7 word-for-word.
- O13's assertion list includes "lm_loss and distill_loss have exactly-zero gradient on LowRankRouter parameters under hard top-1 stop-gradient dispatch."
- Falsification F4-switch-grad-router-only still makes sense — it tests L_switch's alive path to LowRankRouter, which is unaffected.
- Test `gbf-experiments/tests/loss_provenance_s7.rs` includes new zero-gradient assertions for lm/distill → LowRankRouter.

## Notes

- This change CHANGES the experimental claim: S7 now admits that the LM objective does not directly train the router, which materially affects how a Fail-parity verdict should be interpreted (it's not "MoE lost," it's "MoE under hard-dispatch and these aux losses lost"). The honest framing protects both scientific integrity and the bd-2v9r closure path.
- Implementation discipline: the test in `loss_provenance_s7.rs` must assert exact zero, not approximate.
- Crate: `gbf-train` (loss composer); `gbf-experiments::s7::loss_provenance` (fixture suite).

title: D14 logging-overhead: correct baseline features and add measurement_env controls
description:
# Goal

Fix the D14 logging-overhead baseline so it actually compiles and produces meaningful numbers under the workspace's feature contract.

# Background / Why

D14 said the baseline workload uses:

  --no-default-features --features s5-no-log

But the workspace's qat / burn-adapter features are also required to compile the training surface. Dropping them either fails to build or builds a degenerate path that does not match the instrumented run's binary. The 1% gate measured against a degenerate baseline is meaningless.

Additionally, a 1% wall-clock comparison without environmental noise controls is statistically meaningless on a typical workstation (CPU frequency scaling, cold/warm cache, single-threaded contention).

# Change

In gbf-train (logging instrumentation) and scripts/s5_logging_overhead_check.sh:

  - baseline_kind command:
      cargo build --release -p gbf-train --bin s5_logging_overhead_workload --no-default-features --features "s5-no-log,qat,burn-adapter"
  - instrumented_kind command:
      cargo build --release -p gbf-train --bin s5_logging_overhead_workload --no-default-features --features "qat,burn-adapter"
  - workload JSON guard:
      baseline must report logging_compiled_out=true; instrumented must report logging_compiled_out=false.
  - overhead policy:
      record signed (median_instrumented - median_baseline) / median_baseline; refuse negative-overhead anomalies instead of clamping.
  - measurement_env (new block, normative):
      - CPU governor fixed (performance or userspace at a pinned frequency)
      - single worker thread
      - warm cache after warmup
      - baseline / instrumented runs interleaved or randomized by pair
  - Update §D14 RFC text as D14 gate/report substrate only; full §13.18 workload_self_hash/measurement_self_hash emission remains owned by bd-zy3j.

# Why this matters

D14 is the only F-S5 gate that catches "logging is silently slow" before it ships. A baseline that builds a different binary or measures under variable conditions can either pass when the instrumentation is slow (false pass) or fail when noise dominates (false fail). Either undermines the gate.

# Considerations

  - Workspace CI machine setup may need a documented "benchmark mode" (governor, taskset, etc.).

title: T-B4.2: Per-expert payload byte math (Ternary2/Binary1/SparseTernaryBitplanes)
description:
## What
Implement per-expert payload byte math owned by F-B4 (NOT trusted from
the QuantGraph producer). Computes `payload_bytes = weight_bytes +
scale_bytes + metadata_bytes` from `rows`, `cols`, and `TernaryWeightPlan`
using checked u64 arithmetic. Absorbs `bd-w80` (T3.4 model-side byte math).
See RFC §7.6 byte-math formulas.

## Why
Trusting producer-supplied byte totals lets a buggy export propagate
silent miscalculations into placement. Stage 2's job is to be a validator,
not a data forwarder. Per the bd-w80 handoff, the full multi-expert
StaticBudgetReport lives here; bd-w80 just proved the model-owned single-
expert case.

## Inputs
- T-B4.1 ExpertProjection (rows, cols, metadata_bytes, plan).
- `gbf-artifact::TernaryWeightPlan` (`ScaleGranularity`, `ScaleFormat`).

## Outputs
- `fn expert_payload_bytes(expert: &ExpertProjection) -> Result<ByteBudget, BudgetMathError>`.
- Ternary2: `weight_bytes = ceil(rows * cols / 4)`.
- Binary1: `weight_bytes = ceil(rows * cols / 8)`.
- SparseTernaryBitplanes: `pos_bp + neg_bp + sparse_metadata_bytes`
  per `TernaryWeightPlan`'s sparse layout name.
- Scale bytes by `ScaleFormat`: `Q8_8 = 2`, `Q4_4 = 1`,
  `Pow2 = 1` (target-profile-overridable).
- Scale count by `ScaleGranularity`: `PerTensor = 1`, `PerOutputRow = rows`,
  `PerGroup(g) = ceil(rows / g)`.
- All math uses checked `u64`; report rejects values exceeding declared widths.
- Reuse bd-w80's tests as canonical.

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT use saturating or wrapping arithmetic. Overflow is a real failure
  mode and must be reported as `BudgetMathError::Overflow`, not silently truncated.
- `Pow2 scale_bytes` may be overridden by target profile — read from
  `TargetProfile`, not hardcoded.
- Scale count for `PerGroup(g)` rounds UP; don't truncate.

## Acceptance
- gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_computes_ternary2_payload_bytes_from_shape
- gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_computes_scale_bytes_by_granularity
- gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_rejects_overflow_in_byte_math (with very large rows/cols)

## Refs
- RFC §7.6 byte-math formulas.
- bd-w80 (absorbed; reuse its single-expert tests).
- planv0 model-side expert sizing line ~966.
- Depends on: T-B4.1.
- Blocks: T-B4.3, T-B4.4, T-B4.8.

title: F-S7 v0.2 T5.1: Switch-stats schema discipline pass (transitions + IDs + RunLog + ScoreReport)
description:
## Goal

Consolidate every F5 schema-discipline fix into one delivery: TemporalSwitchDigest's directional TransitionEntry; ExpertSlotAffinity SUM canonicalization with overflow-safe arithmetic; LayerId / ExpertId / EPD-4 off-by-one fixes; RunLog completion-aware invariants with the grad_norms series H1/H2 require; ScoreReport.token_count via charset_v1 normalization (not raw byte length). These are all CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md export-fact discipline items and they share the same review surface (P8 Public Contract Stability).

## Why one task

Five fixes, one review pass. Splitting them spreads the same reviewer persona (P8) across multiple beads with no logical separation: every fix is a schema delta from v0.1 to v0.2; every fix demands the same construction-AND-deserialization discipline; every fix needs the same serde_json::json! shape pinning treatment; every fix lives in gbf-artifact. Combining them keeps the contract surface auditable in one PR.

## Five fixes

### Fix A — TransitionEntry directional + ExpertSlotAffinity SUM canonicalization

Pre-review TemporalSwitchDigest.transition_mass stored UnorderedExpertPair, but §3.3.1 said directional entries (a→b + b→a) were aggregated by SUM. You cannot recover directional transitions from a store that already canonicalized to unordered. v0.2 keeps directional at the digest layer and canonicalizes only at the ExpertSlotAffinity layer. SUM aggregator is overflow-safe (saturating_add into u32 accumulator before clamping back to u16) to avoid u16 wrap on three-or-more layer aggregation.

### Fix B — LayerId / ExpertId off-by-one

Pre-review LayerId was '0..n_blocks' (off-by-one — legal IDs are 0..n_blocks-1). Same for EPD-4: 'expert_id values exhaust 0..n_experts'. Both must reject n_blocks / n_experts in BOTH construction AND deserialization.

### Fix C — RunLog completion-aware invariants

Pre-review RunLog RL-Length and RL-Eval required full-length logs even when completion was DivergedAt or CollapsedAt — contradicts the completion field. v0.2: losses.length matches the last completed step on partial completion; eval_points.length matches the number of eval points reached.

### Fix D — grad_norms series

Pre-review RunLog lacked grad_norms (H1/H2 require finite gradient norms across all phases). Add the field; pair it with the losses series per RL-Length.

### Fix E — ScoreReport.token_count

Pre-review used token_count = byte_length(val_bytes); unsafe when scoring uses charset_v1 normalization. v0.2: token_count = length(charset_v1_encode(normalize(val_bytes))).

## Files

- gbf-artifact/src/schemas/temporal_switch.rs (Fix A — TransitionEntry directional; TSD-3/TSD-5)
- gbf-artifact/src/schemas/expert_slot_affinity.rs (Fix A — canonicalized UnorderedExpertPair + SUM aggregator)
- gbf-artifact/src/schemas/ids.rs (Fix B — LayerId, ExpertId; inclusive range)
- gbf-artifact/src/schemas/expert_payload.rs (Fix B — EPD-4 exhaust 0..n_experts-1)
- gbf-artifact/src/schemas/run_log.rs (Fix C + Fix D — completion-aware + grad_norms)
- gbf-artifact/src/schemas/score.rs (Fix E — token_count via charset encode)
- gbf-train/src/runtime/run_log.rs (Fix C + Fix D — emitter respects partial completion)

## Acceptance

All five fixes satisfy the discipline rule: invariants enforced in BOTH construction and deserialization; public JSON shape pinned by explicit serde_json::json! assertions; aggregate-distribution invariants validated in both paths; overflow-safe arithmetic for newtype conversions.

## Reasoning chain

T5.1 is parallel to F2/F3/F4 work — it's pure schema work in gbf-artifact. T5.1 is consumed by T4.1 (telemetry uses LayerId), T3.1 + T3.2 (closure outcome reads RunLog), and T3.4 (E2E smoke verifies round-trips for every schema).
notes:
## Test Plan & Logging (AGENTS.md addendum)

### AGENTS.md Artifact Export Fact rules applied

- Layer-scoped facts include layer_id; ExpertId is layer-local; documented in schema headers (Fix A, Fix B).
- Distribution-like vectors validate aggregate invariants in BOTH construction AND deserialization (Fix A: transition_mass sum <= 256; Fix B: expert_id exhaust).
- Unordered hint pairs canonicalize (lo <= hi) in BOTH paths (Fix A: ExpertSlotAffinity).
- Rate / probability newtypes reject impossible ratios in both paths; arithmetic is overflow-safe (Fix A: mass_q8_8 in Q8.8; saturating_add into u32 accumulator).
- Public JSON shape pinned by serde_json::json! assertions, not serde round-trip alone (all five fixes).

### Unit tests — Fix A (gbf-artifact/tests/temporal_switch.rs + expert_slot_affinity.rs)

- tsd2_aggregate_construction / _deserialization: sum > 256 rejected in both.
- tsd3_uniqueness_construction / _deserialization: duplicate (from, to) rejected in both.
- tsd5_directionality_preserved: (a, b) and (b, a) distinct entries.

title: F-S7 v0.2: Entropy units normalization (bits everywhere)
description:
## Description

The pre-review RFC alternated between bits and nats. D11's guardrail B required `entropy >= 0.85 * log2(n_experts)` and stated "for n_experts=4, log2(4) = 2.0; floor = 1.7 nats-of-2." But `RouterStepTelemetry` declared `expert_usage_entropy: f32 ; nats; in [0, ln(n_experts)]`. For n=4, `ln(4) ≈ 1.386`, so a 1.7-nats floor is impossible. The contradiction made the guardrail trivially refutable or trivially satisfiable depending on which axis the implementor picked. v0.2 standardizes on bits everywhere: the metric is `expert_usage_entropy_bits`, the range is `[0, log2(n_experts)]`, the n=4 floor is 1.7 bits.

## Design

- Rename `expert_usage_entropy` → `expert_usage_entropy_bits` in: D19, H1, H5, H6, D11 guardrail clauses, GuardrailVerdict reason strings, RouterStepTelemetry schema, RST-1 invariant, §9.3 sweep harness, §10 collapse guardrail decision.
- Replace `ln(n_experts)` with `log2(n_experts)` everywhere except where the natural-log baseline is correct (z-loss mu = log(n_experts) intentionally uses natural log because logsumexp is in natural log; that stays).
- "1.7 nats-of-2" → "1.7 bits".
- FailC reason: "high-lambda 5.0 entropy drop < 0.3 bits".
- H6 statement: "drops by >= 0.3 bits".

## Acceptance Criteria

- Zero remaining occurrences of `expert_usage_entropy` (without `_bits`) in any normative section of the RFC.
- All entropy floors are expressed as `0.X * log2(n_experts)` where X is the documented ratio.
- RouterStepTelemetry.expert_usage_entropy_bits has range `[0, log2(n_experts)]`.
- Implementation in `gbf-train` computes the entropy in base-2 (using `log2`, not `ln`) and emits `expert_usage_entropy_bits` in structured tracing events.
- Test `gbf-experiments/tests/router_step_telemetry.rs` asserts the bits-range invariant for every per-step event.

## Notes

- The natural-log baseline `mu = log(n_experts)` in centered z-loss (§3.2, §8.3.4) is intentional and untouched — the logsumexp baseline is a property of natural log; the formula `log(sum_e exp(0)) = log(n_experts)` only holds in natural log.
- Implementation crate: `gbf-model::Top1RouterQat` (entropy computation), `gbf-train::logging` (telemetry emit).
