title: F-S2.16: Falsification suite — falsify feature harness + F1..F6-broken-S2 implementations + tests
description:
Goal
====
Implement the falsify feature gate + harness scaffolding AND the six
deliberately-broken implementations (F1..F6-broken-S2) with per-test
files. Each broken impl must produce the EXPECTED verifier result
(Refuted on a specific hypothesis OR explicit config-validator rejection).
falsification_s2_passed = true requires all six. Per F-S2 RFC §13 O5
+ §16.6.

Why this matters
================
Falsification is a Rule (RFC §2 Rule Falsification): the RFC is correct
only if deliberately-broken implementations produce the expected verdict.
This bead is the verifier's verifier — if H1..H6 verifiers cannot detect
the corresponding deliberate breakage, the closure proof is empty.

Harness implementation strategy (CLARIFIED — round 5 review)
============================================================
The six broken implementations are COMPILE-GATED via #[cfg(feature =
"falsify")] inside the normal modules, NOT runtime-swapped via dynamic
dispatch. The harness's `install_broken_impl(BrokenKind) -> Guard`
pattern is implemented as a thread-local boolean flag that is set
before the test invokes the gated code path. The gated code path
branches on the flag and selects the broken behavior; releases the
flag on Guard drop. This keeps the broken behavior compile-isolated
(no leak into release builds) while still providing a test-time
activation switch.

Example (illustrative):

  fn detach_for_teacher(...) -> FrozenTeacher {
      #[cfg(feature = "falsify")]
      if falsify::is_active(BrokenKind::F2_UnfreezeTeacher) {
          return FrozenTeacher { requires_grad: true, ... }; // broken
      }
      // ... normal implementation ...
  }

This pattern is inherited from bd-i5tz (F-S1.24, closed) which used the
same strategy for S1's falsification suite.

Scope (gbf-experiments/Cargo.toml + tests/falsification_s2/)
============================================================
- Cargo feature `falsify` on gbf-experiments (test-only, same as S1).
- tests/falsification_s2.rs top-level harness.
- tests/falsification_s2/*.rs per-broken-impl files (6 total).
- Each test compiled ONLY when --features falsify enabled.
- Harness API:
    enum BrokenKind { F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6 }
    struct Guard;
    fn install_broken_impl(BrokenKind) -> Guard
    Guard::drop releases the active flag.
- s2_report.v1 falsification_s2_passed = AND over six.
- falsification_s2_suite_hash covers six test source byte digests +
  CI test result, hashed via S1CanonicalJson.

Six broken implementations:
  F1-broken-S2  phase_b_skips_ternary
    Scheduler advances B→C but never flips expert_qat. Phase log
    records HardnessTriple.expert_qat = Off throughout C/D.
    Expected: H1 Refuted (PL-4 violated; F-S2.11 catches).

  F2-broken-S2  phase_d_unfreezes_teacher
    Teacher freeze reverted at C→D boundary. teacher_requires_grad
    becomes true after step 8000.
    Expected: H1 Refuted (PL-3 violated; F-S2.11 catches).

  F3-broken-S2  distill_temperature_inverted
    distill_temperature = 0.5 instead of 2.0.
    Expected: S2 train-config validator REJECTS run before training
    because D3 pins 2.0. Suite does NOT rely on empirical H2/H3 gap
    failure (round 4 review).

  F4-broken-S2  threshold_per_weight
    ThresholdPlan = OneThresholdPerWeight (forbidden by D4).
    Fixture assigns NON-UNIFORM per-weight thresholds chosen so at
    least one weight is below illegal per-weight threshold but ABOVE
    legal row threshold (and vice versa).
    Expected: H5.4 Refuted because observed gradient mask deviates
    from legal per-row mask (bd-1j7 fixture detects).

  F5-broken-S2  zero_loss_on_already_zero_grad
    zero_loss short-circuits + returns 0.0 without computing L1 sum
    when lambda_zero = 0.
    Expected: H5.4b diagnostic_subcheck (F-S2.13) Refuted because
    raw_loss_computed = false.

  F6-broken-S2  linearstate_grad_dead
    Burn adapter for LinearStateBlock returns all-zero gradient on
    recurrence parameter.
    Expected: H6 Refuted (LS-2 violated; F-S2.14 catches).

Logging contract
================
Per-broken-impl test entry INFO:
  event="falsify_test_start" broken_kind=<&str>
    expected_verdict=<&str>
Per-installed-flag DEBUG:
  event="falsify_flag_active" kind=<BrokenKind>
Per-broken-impl test exit INFO:
  event="falsify_test_done" broken_kind=<&str>
    observed_verdict=<&str> passed=<bool>
ERROR if a broken impl is NOT caught (verifier silently passed):
  event="falsify_verifier_insensitive" broken_kind=<&str>
    remediation="the corresponding verifier (H1/H4/H5/H6) is missing a
    check; see CLAUDE.md 'Training Loss Beads' falsification rule"

Unit tests
==========
- File: gbf-experiments/tests/falsification_s2.rs (top-level harness;
  feature-gated):
    Compiled with --features falsify. Imports each per-test module.
- Files: gbf-experiments/tests/falsification_s2/{f1..f6}.rs:
    Each asserts the EXPECTED verifier result for its broken impl.
    Each emits the structured falsify_test_* events.
    Each test name is `falsify_<kind>_<short_name>` for grep-ability
    in CI logs.

- File: gbf-experiments/tests/falsification_s2_suite_hash.rs
  Scenarios:
    * falsification_s2_suite_hash is deterministic across replays.
    * Modifying a test source file changes the hash.

Golden artifacts (insta):
  tests/snapshots/falsify_s2__suite_passed.snap (the expected report
    when all six broken impls produce expected verdicts)
  tests/snapshots/falsify_s2__suite_failed_one.snap (illustrative)

E2E verification
================
- cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features falsify --test
  falsification_s2 (s2-pr CI step):
    All six tests pass; exit code 0.
- cargo test WITHOUT --features falsify does NOT compile the
  falsification module (no release leakage). Verify with cargo check.
- Structured log assertion: exactly six events of type
  event="falsify_test_done", all with passed=true.

Considerations
==============
- Each broken impl targets ONE hypothesis (no multi-hypothesis bundles).
- F3 deterministic config-validator rejection (no train-luck dependency).
- Harness Guard reliably restores normal impl on drop via RAII.

References
==========
F-S2 RFC §13 O5, §2 Rule Falsification, §16.6 falsify feature, AS2-5.
Inherits from F-S1 closed beads: bd-i5tz (F-S1.24 falsification suite
with `falsify` feature gate — same compile-gating pattern).
Merges (former separate beads): F-S2.36 (harness) + F-S2.37 (broken impls).

title: T-B2.19: policy_resolution.v1 schema + semantic validator + tests
description:
## What
Define `PolicyResolutionReportBody` + sections + semantic validator +
serde derives. Wire `gbf-report::report_schemas::policy_resolution_v1`.
See RFC §7.5.

## Why
This is Stage 0.5's canonical sidecar. Every later stage references
its self-hash. Without the schema, `ResolvedPolicyProduct.report` has
no concrete shape.

## Inputs
- T-B2.2 ReportEnvelope + canonical JSON.
- T-B2.13 ResolvedCompilePolicy (the resolved object).
- T-B2.14 path-level provenance.
- T-B2.17 HintConsumptionSection.
- T-B2.16 (forbidden RepairProposal_).

## Outputs
- `pub struct PolicyResolutionReportBody { artifact_identity, compile_request, result: Option<PolicyResolutionSuccessSection>, hint_consumption, diagnostics }`.
- `pub struct PolicyResolutionSuccessSection { resolved, compile_knobs, provenance }`.
- Section types: `ArtifactIdentitySection`, `CompileRequestSection`,
  `ResolvedSection`, `CompileKnobsSection`, `PolicyProvenanceSection`.
- Semantic validator implementing §7.5 invariants:
  - `outcome == Passed` iff `result.is_some()` and no Hard diagnostic.
  - `outcome == Failed` iff `result.is_none()` and ≥1 Hard.
  - Provenance sorted by `CompileKnobPath`, every chain non-empty.
  - `compile_knobs.bounds` monotone-tighter than target's defaults.
  - Every `HintBundle::preferences` entry appears in `hint_consumption`.

## Pitfalls
- A failed report has `result = None`, NEVER a partial `ResolvedCompilePolicy`.
- `compile_knobs.provenance` is `Vec<CompileKnobProvenanceEntry>`, sorted.
- Forbid `PolicySource::RepairProposal(_)` in this chunk.
- Schema-version field is in the envelope, not the body.

## Acceptance
- gbf-report::f_b2_policy_resolution_v1_schema_accepts_canonical_fixture
- gbf-report::f_b2_policy_resolution_v1_rejects_missing_required_fields
- gbf-report::f_b2_policy_resolution_v1_rejects_repair_proposal_provenance
- gbf-report::f_b2_policy_resolution_v1_self_hash_round_trip
- gbf-report::f_b2_policy_resolution_v1_failure_report_self_hash_round_trip
- gbf-report::f_b2_policy_resolution_v1_hint_consumption_invariant

## Refs
- RFC §7.5 schema, §9.1 JSON example.
- Depends on: T-B2.2, T-B2.14, T-B2.15, T-B2.16, T-B2.17.
- Blocks: T-B2.20, T-B4.11 (Stage 2 references this self-hash).

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## RFC amendments (2026-05-07)

Multiple §7.5 schema tightenings; some change wire shape:

**1. `result` wraps the success-only sub-tree** (§7.5, §9.1)

The JSON top-level schema now puts `resolved`, `compile_knobs`, and
`provenance` under a single `result: Option<PolicyResolutionSuccessSection>`
field rather than as siblings of `hint_consumption` and `diagnostics`:

```json
{
  "schema": "policy_resolution.v1",
  ...
  "compile_request": { ... },
  "result": {
    "resolved": { ... },
    "compile_knobs": { ... },
    "provenance": { ... }
  } | null,
  "hint_consumption": { ... },
  "diagnostics": [ ... ],
  "report_self_hash": "sha256:..."
}
```

`result == null` iff `outcome == Failed`. This makes the partial-resolved
prohibition mechanically obvious.

**2. `CompileRequestSection` non-Optional fields**

```rust
pub struct CompileRequestSection {
    // ...
    pub calibration_set_ref: CalibrationSetRef,    // was Option
    pub calibration_hash: Hash256,                 // was Option<Hash256>
}
```

Calibration is uniformly required (§2.8). A passing build always has a
`CalibrationBundleSet`; failure reports never reach this section anyway.

**3. `PolicyProvenanceSection` non-Optional fields**

```rust
pub struct PolicyProvenanceSection {
    pub target_defaults: Hash256,
    pub profile_defaults: Hash256,
    pub hint_bundle_hash: Hash256,        // was Option
    pub compile_request_hash: Hash256,
    pub calibration_hash: Hash256,        // was Option
```

title: F-S2.29: H2 verifier (gap ≤ 0.5 per-seed + quality sanity bpc_fp ≤ 2.5 / bpc_ternary ≤ 3.0)
description:
Goal
====
Implement the H2 verifier: per-seed gap_ternary_vs_fp(s) <= 0.5 bpc, plus
the absolute quality sanity gate (bpc_fp <= 2.5, bpc_ternary <= 3.0) and
the per-build suspicious-low-bpc sentinel (fp / ternary / nodistill
median bpc < 0.5). H3's nodistill suspicious branch was moved out of H2
to the outcome level (round 4 review). Per F-S2 RFC §3 H2 + §3 D7.

Why this matters
================
H2 is the closure gate that demonstrates "Toy0 ternary survives QAT."
Without an absolute quality gate, both fp and ternary could be
catastrophically bad (e.g. fp=8.0, ternary=8.3, gap=0.3 ≤ 0.5) and H2
would falsely pass. The suspicious sentinel guards against split leakage
and metric breakage.

Scope (in gbf-experiments::s2::verifiers::h2)
=============================================
- fn verify_h2(scores_t: &[S2ScoreReport;5], scores_f: &[S2ScoreReport;5])
    -> H2Verdict
  where H2Verdict { status: HypothesisStatus,
                     gap: [GapBpc;5],
                     hits: Vec<DiagnosticHit> }
- Falsification predicates (each → Refuted):
    H2.a  ∃ s. gap(s) > 0.5
    H2.b  ∃ s. bpc_fp(s) > 2.5     (quality sanity)
    H2.c  ∃ s. bpc_ternary(s) > 3.0 (quality sanity)
    H2.d  median(bpc_fp) < 0.5      (suspicious — drives Fail-suspicious
                                      at outcome layer, but H2 itself
                                      Refuted)
    H2.e  median(bpc_ternary) < 0.5 (same)
- nodistill suspicious sentinel is NOT in H2 (round 4 review): it lives
  at the outcome layer in F-S2.41.
- Predicted sanity ranges (informational, not gating):
    bpc_fp(s)     in [1.4, 1.9]   [ESTIMATE]
    bpc_ternary(s) in [1.6, 2.4]  [ESTIMATE]
    median(gap)   in [0.05, 0.40] [ESTIMATE]
- Surprise (logged, not failed): bpc outside the sanity range but inside
  the quality gate.

Acceptance
==========
- Synthetic scores with one seed gap = 0.7 → Refuted with H2.a hit
  pointing to that seed.
- bpc_fp(2) = 2.6 → Refuted with H2.b hit.
- median(bpc_fp) = 0.4 → Refuted with H2.d hit; downstream layer
  classifies as Fail-suspicious.
- All seeds within bounds → Confirmed.

Considerations
==============
- Per-seed strict: ALL 5 seeds must satisfy gap <= 0.5. Aggregate "mean
  gap" verdicts are explicitly rejected (RFC §3 D7).
- The fp run-config is matched protocol (D6): same A→B→C→D plan, same
  distillation policy with QuantHardness all-Off. Without that, the H2
  comparison is no longer matched.

References
==========
F-S2 RFC §3 H2, §3 D6 / D7, AS2-1, round-4 review §10.
Depends on: F-S2.27 (gap primitives), F-S2.16 (S2ScoreReport).

## Agent Instructions

- No new ArtifactCore lowering is claimed here. LinearState ArtifactCore export materialization remains the completed input owner from `bd-tnb`; future smoke/report adoption remains with `bd-1l7f` / `bd-1xqf`.

differentiable Burn path
- `LinearStateBurnQat::train_forward` composes `NormApproxBurnQat`, `ActFakeQuantBurnQat`, and `TernaryLinearBurnQat` over Burn tensors, carries recurrent state as a differentiable Burn tensor, and returns both activation output and final state.
- `PhaseControlledModel` is implemented for `LinearStateBurnQat`; scheduler controls update expert, activation, norm hardness and threshold schedule progress at the LinearState boundary.
- Dynamic activation ranges are rejected at adapter construction until a later owner introduces Burn-side mutable activation-range state.

- `cargo test -p gbf-train --features burn-adapter,qat -- phase::linear_state_hardness` (2 tests) proves Soft/Hard phase controls and threshold progress reach the adapter boundary, and dynamic activation range is rejected.
- `cargo clippy -p gbf-train --features burn-adapter,qat -- -D warnings` proves the feature-enabled adapter is warning-clean.
- `cargo clippy -p gbf-train -- -D warnings` proves the bead's literal no-feature clippy gate remains clean.
- `cargo test -p gbf-test --test architecture` (3 tests) proves Burn imports remain confined to `gbf-train`.
- `python3 scripts/qat_harness_checks.py` passed before close.

title: T-B2.9: Stage 0 hint-bundle provenance + workload/golden refs
description:
## What
Implement Stage 0 validation classes 8 and 9: HintBundle provenance
self-consistency and workload/golden vector reference resolution.
See RFC §7.3.

## Why
HintBundle is load-bearing per planv0 line ~738: facts/preferences/
constraints have explicit applicability scope, and unscoped or
inconsistent facts mislead downstream stages. Workload and golden vector
refs underpin testing and conformance gates; an unresolved ref is a silent
build hole.

## Inputs
- T-B2.4 ValidatedInputs.
- `gbf-artifact::HintBundle` (`ExportFacts`, `CompilePreferences`,
  `BuildConstraints`).
- Workload/golden ref types from `gbf-workload`.

## Outputs
- Class 8 code: `HintProvenanceInconsistent { fact: TraceProbeId }` —
  fact references an `EvidenceScope` outside the active artifact/workload/
  target/lowering scope.
- Class 9 codes: `WorkloadRefUnresolved { workload }`,
  `GoldenVectorMissing { vector }`,
  `GoldenVectorDigestMismatch { vector, expected, observed }`.

## Pitfalls
- A fact is allowed to reference a *broader* scope than the build (e.g. all
  DMG targets), but never a *narrower* one (e.g. a different model lineage).
- Golden vector digests must be re-verified against actual sidecar bytes.
- `WorkloadManifestRef` resolution is via id, but the resolved manifest's
  hash must match the recorded value.

## Acceptance
- gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_rejects_hint_provenance_inconsistent
- gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_rejects_workload_ref_unresolved
- gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_rejects_golden_vector_missing
- gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_rejects_golden_vector_digest_mismatch

## Refs
- RFC §7.3 classes 8, 9.
- planv0 §"HintBundle is load-bearing" (line ~738).
- Blocks: T-B2.11.

comments.text:
## RFC amendments (2026-05-07)

§7.3 class 9 unchanged in dispatch but the resolver is now explicit (§7.3
ValidateInputs.resolver). T-B2.4's amendment adds the
`ArtifactResolver` trait; T-B2.9's workload-ref and golden-vector-ref
dispatch must consume the resolver via:

```rust
inputs.resolver.resolve_workload(workload_ref)?;
inputs.resolver.resolve_golden_vector(vector_ref)?;
```

Stage 0 must NOT fall back to ambient global store state for ref resolution.
This change is mostly behavior-preserving for the dispatcher; what changes
is the call-site form.

Class 8 (hint provenance) wording unchanged. The HintBundle is now always
present in `ImportedArtifactView` (canonical empty when absent), so the
provenance check has a non-null reference to inspect — no Option matching
needed.

No new acceptance tests strictly required, but may add:
- `gbf-codegen::f_b2_validate_workload_ref_resolution_uses_artifact_resolver_trait`

Cross-refs: §7.3 class 9 + ArtifactResolver, §2.3 hint normalization.

comments.text:
## T-B1.6.2: `gbf-bench::MatmulI8Bringup` workload runner

**Target crate**: `gbf-bench`
**Target file**: `gbf-bench/src/workloads/matmul_bringup.rs`

### Background

The L5 driver. Sweeps `N ∈ {32, 64, 96, 128}`. For each N, builds the appropriate `ComputeBringupRequest`, lowers to ROM, runs under the deterministic emulator with the cooperative scheduler enabled, drives the tile-dump pause/resume protocol, and compares each N's output byte-for-byte against the reference.

### Sweep shape

| N    | Banking                    | UI / scheduler |
|------|----------------------------|----------------|
| 32   | DistinctRomBanks (small)   | full L4 cooperative |
| 64   | DistinctRomBanks           | full L4 cooperative |
| 96   | DistinctRomBanks           | full L4 cooperative |
| 128  | DistinctRomBanks (headline)| full L4 cooperative |

Even smaller-N runs use the full cooperative scheduler so the soft-margin metrics are comparable across the sweep.

### Outputs the runner produces (per N)

- Streamed-output bytes (host-reassembled, byte-exact compared to reference).
- Frame trace (input to T-B1.5.5 metric computation).
- Runtime trace (lease balance, max active leases, MBC writes, yield-while-lease counter).
- Tile-completion timestamps (for cycle-per-output-tile metric).
- Bank0 used/free bytes.
- WRAM/HRAM/SRAM peaks.

These are aggregated by T-B1.6.3 into the final report.

### Determinism

The runner is single-threaded, uses `DeterministicPolicy` from gbf-emu (fixed RTC, RNG seed, audio off). Two consecutive runs on the same host produce identical traces and identical reports.

### Acceptance gates

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-bench -- matmul_bringup_runner_accepts_valid_sweep
cargo test -p gbf-bench -- matmul_bringup_runner_byte_exact_per_n
cargo test -p gbf-bench -- matmul_bringup_runner_is_deterministic
cargo test -p gbf-bench -- --ignored matmul_bringup_full_n128_run
```

### RFC reference

`history/rfcs/F-B1-compute-bringup.md` §10, §14.

### Dependencies

- T-B1.4 cluster (full streamed-output stack).
- T-B1.5 cluster (cooperative scheduler events).
- T-B1.6.1 (report schema).

title: F-B8 StoragePlan (Stage 6) — v2 RFC implementation epic
description:
# F-B8 StoragePlan — the bridge — v2 RFC implementation

## Project context (read this first)

gbllm compiles a tiny language model into an LR35902 Game Boy ROM. The compiler is Epic B and has 14 stages bracketed by a feasibility envelope and wrapped (stages 5–11) by a bounded `FeasibilityRefinementLoop` (F-B16). **F-B8 is Stage 6 — "the bridge."** It is the unique stage that turns value/effect IR (`GbInferIR`, F-B5) into typed *materialization*, *lifetime*, and *aliasing* decisions **without** committing to byte offsets, bank residency, overlay installs, or slice schedules. Concrete bytes belong to F-B12 ArenaPlan; pages/banks to F-B9/F-B10; overlays to F-B11; schedule to F-B13. Every later spatial stage plugs into F-B8's typed surface.

The bridge metaphor is literal: on the input side the pipeline carries pure value/effect semantics; on the output side every later stage either consumes a `StorageBinding` directly or threads it through to a consumer. There is no other place where "is this value materialized, recomputed, or persisted, and if materialized, what storage class and lifetime?" gets answered.

## Why the v2 RFC pass mattered

Two external review passes (one design-level, one PR-style) found the v1 RFC's "typed, mechanically checkable" claim contradicted by the text in many places:

* **Self-hash recursion** — `StoragePlanIdentity.report_self_hash` made K6 depend on the output report's own hash.
* **Dead promotion levels** — `PureResumeWindowValues` / `PureTokenValues` could not affect any binding under the predicate set.
* **Unreachable diagnostics** — `DR-13 predicate: true` made `STORE-001` dead code.
* **Alias examples contradicted alias predicates** — e.g. PingPong cited for HramHot RouterDecision, which `PP-PingPong` rejects.
* **Reserved persistence shapes simultaneously "closed" and "hard error to emit"** — schema carried `OrderedRecoverable`, `ContinuationWithSequenceState`, `HintBundle` while the v1 producer was required to refuse them.
* **Policy field-path drift** — `policy.compile_knobs.global.pressure.*.soft.bytes` vs `StoragePressureBudget.*.soft_bytes` in different sections.
* **Missing live-range evidence** — `LifetimeClass` alone cannot witness alias non-conflict (two Slice values can overlap).
* **JSON schema omitted typed fields** — `live_range` not in `StorageBindingJson`; `input_identity` not in `StoragePlanReportResult`; `policy_hash` referenced but absent from `StoragePlanInputs`.
* **Singleton intent contradiction** — `ScratchReuse` claimed as singleton default but only legal for hot Slice multi-member classes.
* **Mixed-intent union-find** — transitive closure could merge edges admitted under different intents.
* **DR-1b expressed as a "rule" with `binding: none` in a system whose rule type returns `Materialization`.**
* **DR-3 said "persisted in WRAM by default"** — but `Persist` is the SRAM persistence protocol.

The RFC text was patched across the two review passes. **This epic tracks the implementation work that turns those patches into running code** without re-litigating any of the patches.

## Closure

* All child task beads closed.
* M1 degenerate fixture (every value gets a NoAlias singleton class) and the M3 routed-FFN dense fixture both emit byte-identical `storage_plan.json` across two consecutive clean-checkout runs.
* K6 cache hit/miss replay yields identical product; failure memos replay identical diagnostic ordering.
* F-B9 / F-B10 / F-B11 / F-B12 / F-B13 / F-B16 / F-B17 all consume the typed product without re-deriving storage, lifetime, persistence, or aliasing decisions.
* Every rejection class (RC-1..RC-32) has a corresponding `STORE-*` unit test; every proof obligation (PO-1..PO-23) has a named witness.
* SC11 forbidden-key scan passes against both the type module and emitted JSON for both fixtures.

## Milestone alignment

M2 needs F-B8 wired (one shared micro-kernel resolved by F-B10 RomWindowPlan requires Materialize{class:RomConst} bindings on weights/LUTs). M3 needs the full F-B5→F-B6→F-B7→F-B8→F-B9..F-B13 chain for the routed FFN. This epic is on the critical path for both.

## How to use these beads

The DAG is layered: types → predicates/policy view → rule engine → per-rule families → engines (alias, persist, live range) → driver → cache/emitter → fixtures and tests. `br ready` will surface the next unblocked piece. Each child bead is intentionally self-contained: read its description before touching code, and you should not need to re-read the RFC end-to-end.

title: H6 negative-control fixture + SHR-1 healthy/broken split
description:
# Goal

Add an in-closure negative control for shadow_compile_ok: every ordinary Pick-axis run must include at least one shadow_compile invocation on a pinned broken deployable artifact and observe shadow_compile_ok = false with a non-null diagnostic. Update SHR-1 invariant to distinguish healthy and broken samples.

# Background / Why

H6 verifies that shadow_compile_ok is responsive to real failures. The dedicated falsification feature F5 hardcodes it to true, but that only catches the bug when someone explicitly enables the falsifier. A negative control inside ordinary closure runs catches regressions in the API immediately.

SHR-1 originally said:

  stages_executed = S5_SHADOW_PIPELINE_STAGES iff shadow_compile_ok = true.

This is too strong for broken substitutes (which intentionally produce shadow_compile_ok=false) and conflicts with D11's \"MUST exercise every stage\" language for healthy samples.

# Change

In gbf-experiments::s5 fixtures + gbf-policy invariants:

  - Add fixture fixtures/shadow_compile/broken_negative_control.toml that produces a known compile failure (e.g. out-of-WRAM placement).
  - Every Pick-axis closure run executes the broken fixture at least once and asserts shadow_compile_ok == false with a populated diagnostic.
  - Split SHR-1:
      Healthy: stages_executed == S5_SHADOW_PIPELINE_STAGES AND shadow_compile_ok == true.
      Broken: stages_executed records every attempted stage; failure_stage records the first missing or failed stage.
  - Add ShadowCompileSampleReal.failure_stage: Optional<String> if not already present.

# Why this matters

Two-sided coverage. The positive case (\"all stages run, ok=true\") and the negative case (\"first failed stage recorded, ok=false\") together prove the field is not a constant.

# Considerations

  - The broken fixture must be deterministic and small.
  - Compile-time gating: this negative control runs in every Pick-axis test run; ensure it does not bloat CI.
  - Reviewer P5 evidence: negative-control output is a P5 artifact.

# Verification

  - Healthy run: SHR-1 healthy branch passes; broken run: SHR-1 broken branch passes.
  - Manual mutation: remove the diagnostic field from a broken sample -> validator fails.

# Related RFC sections

  §3 H6, §8.2 SHR-1 invariants, §15 F5.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## T-B1.3.2: BankLease/BankGuard integration in matmul lowering

**Target crate**: `gbf-codegen`
**Target file**: `gbf-codegen/src/matmul.rs` (extends T-B1.2.4)

### Background

L2 is F-A4's first real consumer. Every panel copy in the kernel must lease the operand bank, copy the panel into WRAM, then release the lease. The kernel never writes MBC registers directly; it always goes through F-A4's `BankLease`/`BankGuard` ABI.

### Lowering structure (L2, DistinctRomBanks)

```text
section L2Kernel @ Bank0
  for mt in output_tile_rows:                         ; 0..N/16
    for nt in output_tile_cols:                       ; 0..N/16
      zero accumulator[16, 16]

      for kt in k_tiles:                              ; 0..N/16
        // ----- A panel copy under lease -----
        let guard_a = banking::acquire_rom_bank(a_bank);
        copy A[mt:mt+16, kt:kt+16] -> a_panel
        drop(guard_a);                                ; emits BankRelease

        // ----- B panel copy under lease -----
        let guard_b = banking::acquire_rom_bank(b_bank);
        copy B[kt:kt+16, nt:nt+16] -> b_panel
        drop(guard_b);

        // ----- Compute / yield region -----
        ; assert: no BankLease is active here (T-B1.3.4 invariant)
        for kk in 0..16:
          for mm in 0..16:
            for nn in 0..16:
              acc[mm, nn] += quarter_square_mul(a_panel[mm, kk], b_panel[kk, nn])

      ; tile-complete trap (T-B1.4.3 owns full pause/resume protocol)
```

### Why lease, copy, release (not lease-and-hold-during-compute)

If the lease were held during the inner-product loop, yielding under it would be unsafe (the scheduler/ISR would observe ambiguous ROMX state). Copying the panel into WRAM under a short lease, then releasing, gives us:

- A short critical window for the lease.
- All subsequent compute reads from WRAM (`a_panel`, `b_panel`).
- A clean boundary for `T-B1.5.1` to insert yields.

### Acceptance gates

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- f_b1_l2_lowering_uses_banklease_ops
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- f_b1_l2_lowering_releases_lease_before_compute
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- f_b1_l2_lowering_panel_copy_inside_lease
```

### RFC reference

`history/rfcs/F-B1-compute-bringup.md` §7.8 (lowering contract).

### Dependencies

- T-B1.2.4 (codegen lowering core).
- T-B1.3.1 (`BringupRomWindowPlan`).
- **F-A4** (BankLease/BankGuard ABI) — hard external dep.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Epic B: Compiler Pipeline — 14 Stages + Refinement Loop

### What this is

The transform pipeline from `planv0.md` §"The compiler pipeline" (line 1031). It takes a frozen `ArtifactCore` plus a `CompileRequest` and produces a `CompiledBuild` (ROM + reports + certificates). The 14 stages plus the refinement loop are the actual compiler — what most other epics produce inputs for or consume outputs from.

### Why this matters

This is the heart of GBLLM. Training (epic `bd-1rb`) produces artifacts; oracles (Epic C) verify them; M0 (Epic A) provides the target/abi/asm contracts; bench (Epic E) calibrates the cost model — but Epic B is what *compiles a model into a ROM that runs on a Game Boy*. The architectural rigor of planv0.md (validation envelope, refinement loop, three-stratum oracle correspondence) all hangs on these stages working as specified.

### Scope (sixteen features)

Headline pipeline ordering:

```
Policy / feasibility envelope:
  F-B0  ArtifactValidationAndUpgrade + ResolvedCompilePolicy        (stages 0, 0.5)
  F-B1  QuantGraph                                                   (stage 1)
  F-B2  StaticBudgetReport                                           (stage 2)

Transformative stages (wrapped by FeasibilityRefinementLoop):
  F-B3  GbInferIR (value/effect IR)                                  (stage 3)
  F-B4  ObservationPlan                                              (stage 4)
  F-B5  RangePlan                                                    (stage 5)
  F-B6  StoragePlan                                                  (stage 6)
  F-B7  SramPagePlan                                                 (stage 7)
  F-B8  RomWindowPlan                                                (stage 8)
  F-B9  OverlayPlan                                                  (stage 8.5; replaces existing T11.4 stub bd-gmw)
  F-B10 ArenaPlan                                                    (stage 9)
  F-B11 GbSchedIR + ResourceStateValidation                          (stages 10, 10.5)
  F-B12 ScheduleCostAnalysis                                         (stage 11)
  F-B13 Backend (AsmIR codegen + ReachabilityValidation + PlacedRom + EncodedRom)  (stage 12)

Cross-cutting:
  F-B14 FeasibilityRefinementLoop + RepairPolicy + CompileKnobs       (BLOCKED on oracle question)
  F-B15 StageCache integration across all stages
```

### Out of scope (deferred)

- Producing build reports + certificates → Epic F.
- Running oracles against compiler output → Epic C.
- Running bench against compiled ROMs to refine calibration → Epic E.

### Critical path

```
F-B0 → F-B1 → F-B2 → F-B3 → F-B4 → F-B5 → F-B6 → F-B7 → F-B8 → F-B9 → F-B10 → F-B11 → F-B12 → F-B13
                                  └─────── F-B14 wraps stages 5-11 ──────────┘
F-B15 cross-cuts every stage.
```

`F-B14` is **blocked** until the oracle answers the `CompileKnobs` question we drafted (typed surface for `RepairProposal::tighten`, plus per-profile `RepairPolicy` defaults). All other features can proceed.

### Existing beads to absorb / reshape

- **`bd-w80` (T3.4)** — Update `StaticBudgetReport` for `TernaryWeightPlan` byte math. Belongs to F-B2; can be re-parented or its work absorbed.
- **`bd-gmw` (T11.4)** — `OverlayPlan` IR stub. Replaced by F-B9 with the plan's `{regions, installs, share_classes}` shape. T11.4 should be closed-as-superseded once F-B9 lands.
- **`bd-1f7` (T8.3)** — Shadow compile pipeline (under F8 / `bd-2am`). Orchestrates Epic B stages but doesn't implement them.

### Constitution checkpoints

- **§I.1**: Each stage is a typed transform from one IR to the next; no opaque blobs cross stage boundaries.
- **§III.1**: Most regressions get caught by per-stage golden snapshot tests rather than running ROMs.
- **§I.4**: The pipeline's verifiable reward is the certificate set + a passing `conformance.json` against `ArtifactOracle`.
- **§VI.1**: Each pass type lives in `gbf-codegen` (or `gbf-ir` for IR types); no parallel implementations elsewhere.

### Confidence: HIGH on staging, BLOCKED on F-B14

The 13 transform stages are well-specified in planv0.md. F-B14 cannot land without first resolving (a) `CompileKnobs` enumeration and (b) per-profile `RepairPolicy` defaults — both questions are out for oracle review.

### When this epic is done

The compiler can take an artifact + CompileRequest and produce a passing tiny-model ROM end-to-end, with all certificates emitted, with at least one shadow-compile run from training-time succeeding.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Why this bead exists

Determinism law Rep-1 requires byte-identical safetensors under the same
inputs. This is impossible if the run silently picks up `OMP_NUM_THREADS`,
`RAYON_NUM_THREADS`, or any other environment-variable-driven nondeterminism.

§5 `S1CpuDeterministic` and §16.4 "Determinism budgets" turn this into a
contract: **every variable in `env_exact` is set to its pinned value, every
other variable is unset, and violation aborts the run before tensor allocation**.
The crucial detail is `env_forbidden_unless_listed = true` — extra environment
variables are not just informational, they ABORT the run.

C-NoLeakage in §9.1 makes this invariant first-class on the checkpoint.

## Scope

- `S1CpuDeterministic` struct in `s1::device_profile`:
    backend = Burn CPU backend (pinned by lockfile)
    thread_count = 1
    deterministic_reductions = true
    gpu_allowed = false
    network_allowed = false
    host_clock_allowed_for_training_artifacts = false
    env_exact = {
      BURN_NDARRAY_NUM_THREADS: "1",
      BURN_DETERMINISTIC:       "1",
      OMP_NUM_THREADS:          "1",
      RAYON_NUM_THREADS:        "1"
    }
    env_forbidden_unless_listed = true
- `enforce(profile)` runs BEFORE any tensor allocation:
    - Verify every env_exact key is set to its pinned value.
    - Verify NO other environment variable is set in the process.
    - Reject GPU device, reject any network access pre-emptively, reject
      reads of host clock by training artifacts (host clock is allowed only
      for the `generated_at` field of s1_report.v1, see §9.7 + Rep-8).
    - Abort with non-zero exit + diagnostic if any check fails.
- `device_profile_hash`: canonical hash of the profile, used in
  CheckpointMetadata. Same profile bytes → same hash.
- Unit tests:
    - missing env var → enforce returns Err
    - env_exact value mismatch → Err
    - extra env var present → Err
    - all-correct → Ok and hash matches a pinned vector
- The runner (F-S1.13) calls `enforce()` as the very first action before
  loading the model.

## Considerations

- "every other variable is unset" is harsh. Document for the future-self that
  the canonical replay command (§15.4) is meant to be run from a clean
  process-launch context (e.g., `env -i ...`).
- Cross-machine determinism is NOT required (Rep-2). This profile pins
  same-machine reproducibility only.

## RFC anchors

- §5 RunInputs / TrainConfig / S1CpuDeterministic
- §9.1 C-NoLeakage on s1_checkpoint.v1
- §16.4 determinism budgets
- §13 O8 No hidden inputs
- Rep-2, Rep-8

## QAT Closure Checklist

- Artifact contract: This bead does not introduce a new artifact schema. The pre-export contract is that trained Burn-owned expert tensors can be converted back to `gbf_model::qat::ExpertBlockQat` via `to_core_from_trained_state`; existing bd-x75 artifact identity records the expert clipped activation/nonlinearity and activation range. Real end-to-end materialization remains with the existing export/artifact owners rather than this Burn adapter bead.
- differentiable Burn path: `gbf_train::qat::expert::ExpertBlockBurnQat` executes `up_projection -> clipped_activation -> ActFakeQuantBurnQat -> down_projection`, returns `input + selected_expert_delta + shared_dense_delta`, and uses Burn tensors/params for differentiable execution.

- Acceptance movement: Real three-matrix GLU execution/export is intentionally not accepted here. `ExpertMlpVariant::GatedLinearUnit` remains config-only diagnostic in the scalar/model core and is rejected at the Burn config boundary until a future owner implements the executable/export path.

The artifact-facing contract is inherited from bd-x75: supported expert activation semantics are part of export identity, and `gbf-model::qat::export` records the clipped activation kind. title: F-S3.19: s3_conformance.v1 emitter (per-seed envelopes) + CanonicalConformanceWrite encoder
description:
## Context

`s3_conformance.v1` (RFC §11.7) is the per-seed `ConformanceEnvelope` covering PostLogits + PostDecode tolerances and the quantization gap summary. Per third-round Patch 14 (round 2), the envelope is per-seed (Vec<SeedConformanceEnvelope>) rather than seed-0-only. Per Rule LogitsAggregation, per-token / per-vocab-row aggregation is normative; prompt-wide softmax-then-compare is forbidden (the F8-broken-S3 falsifier).

`CanonicalConformanceWrite` (RFC §3): per-prompt agreement records in manifest prompt order; per-checkpoint metric maps with sorted keys; per-metric float values via S1CanonicalJson (shortest round-trip decimal, -0.0 normalized).

`real_owner_bead = bd-35l3` (F-C4 ConformanceEnvelope) is recorded explicitly per Rule ConformanceEnvelopeEmission.

**B19 enforces F8-broken-S3 detection mechanically** via the `AggregationKind` annotation on metric values introduced in B5: any `MetricGate { aggregation_kind: PromptWideSoftmaxForbidden }` triggers a serialization-time error in CanonicalConformanceWrite.

## Why this matters

The envelope IS the closure-quality artifact for v0_success. Without B19 closing, R-Self-Hash for s3_conformance fails, conformance roll-up has no input, and the §10 dispatcher's `Fail-conformance` ladder branch (Patch 15 round 3) cannot be evaluated.

## Deliverables

1. `gbf-experiments/src/s3/conformance.rs`:
   - `pub fn build_conformance_envelope(workload, agreement_products: Vec<AgreementProduct>) -> Result<ConformanceEnvelope, ConformanceError>`
   - Per-seed roll-up: each seed's `SeedConformanceEnvelope { seed, bundle_self_hash, artifact_self_hash, overall, per_checkpoint, per_metric }`
   - `quantization_gap_summary { mean_per_token_max_abs_diff_phase_A, mean_per_token_max_abs_diff_phase_D, mean_per_token_kl }` (per-token KL only; never prompt-wide)
   - `real_owner_bead: "bd-35l3"`
2. `gbf-artifact/src/canonical_conformance_write.rs`:
   - `pub fn canonical_conformance_bytes(envelope: &ConformanceEnvelope) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ConformanceError>`
   - Sorted keys; shortest round-trip f32; -0.0 normalized
   - **F8 detector**: any MetricGate with `aggregation_kind: PromptWideSoftmaxForbidden` triggers `ConformanceError::PromptWideSoftmaxAggregation { seed, prompt_id, metric_id }` (this is the schema-level F8-broken-S3 rejection)
3. Invariants Co-1..Co-4 enforced (RFC §11.7):
   - Co-1: every per_seed[*].per_checkpoint covers PostLogits and PostDecode (PostEmbedding only when ObservationPolicy requests it AND a tolerance is defined)
   - Co-2: every per_seed[*].per_metric includes MaxAbsLogitDiff; PerTokenKL only for aligned logits rows where KL is well-defined
   - Co-3: overall.tolerance ≥ max per_seed[*].overall.tolerance
   - Co-4: conformance_self_hash round-trips
4. `experiments/S3/conformance/conformance.json` is the actual emission target

## Test scaffolding

1. **`gbf-experiments/tests/conformance_round_trip_s3.rs`** (O-5'):
   - Round-trips through canonical JSON with self-hash equality, sorted keys, per-token aggregation preserved
2. **`gbf-experiments/tests/conformance_seed_arity_s3.rs`** — Co-1 + Co-2 + Co-3:
   - per_seed.len() == 5
   - Every per_seed[*] has PostLogits + PostDecode keys
   - overall.tolerance ≥ max(per_seed[*].overall.tolerance)
3. **`gbf-experiments/tests/conformance_f8_aggregation_rejection_s3.rs`** — F8-broken-S3 detection:
   - Construct an AgreementProduct whose metric values were computed via prompt-wide softmax
   - Mark the corresponding MetricGate.aggregation_kind = PromptWideSoftmaxForbidden
   - Run build_conformance_envelope + CanonicalConformanceWrite
   - Assert `ConformanceError::PromptWideSoftmaxAggregation` is returned
   - Negative: same metric values with `aggregation_kind = PerTokenPerVocabRow` succeed
4. **`gbf-experiments/tests/conformance_canonical_snapshot_s3.rs`** — insta snapshot of canonical conformance bytes for a fixed fixture
5. **`gbf-experiments/tests/conformance_self_hash_determinism_s3.rs`** — `conformance_self_hash` deterministic across 10 replays
6. **`gbf-experiments/tests/conformance_per_token_kl_s3.rs`** — Co-2 PerTokenKL invariant:
   - PerTokenKL only emitted for aligned logits rows where KL is well-defined (denominator non-zero)
   - Negative: row with zero-norm logits → PerTokenKL = None (skipped)
7. **`gbf-experiments/tests/conformance_canonical_write_proptest_s3.rs`** — proptest:
   - Strategy `arbitrary_seed_envelope()`: round-trip canonical bytes
   - Strategy `random_key_insertion_order()`: same envelope inserted in different order produces identical canonical bytes (sorted-keys discipline)

## Logging discipline

```
event_name = "s3::conformance::build_started"
fields: { workload_self_hash, agreement_product_count, real_owner_bead: "bd-35l3" }

event_name = "s3::conformance::seed_envelope_built"
level = "trace"  ; per seed
fields: { seed, bundle_self_hash, artifact_self_hash, per_checkpoint_count, per_metric_count }

event_name = "s3::conformance::aggregation_rejected"  ; F8 detector fires
fields: { seed, prompt_id, metric_id, aggregation_kind }

event_name = "s3::conformance::build_complete"
fields: { per_seed_count, overall_passed, conformance_self_hash, real_owner_bead }

target = "gbf_experiments::s3::conformance"
```
Subscriber-level test `gbf-experiments/tests/conformance_logging_s3.rs` asserts events fire including aggregation_rejected when F8 detector triggers.

## E2E acceptance script

`scripts/s3_conformance_emit_smoke.sh`:
1. Loads fixture AgreementProducts (per-seed)
2. Runs build_conformance_envelope; emits experiments/S3/conformance/conformance.json
3. Re-runs; diffs canonical bytes (must be identical)
4. Asserts per_seed.len() == 5
5. Asserts conformance_self_hash matches pinned value

## Inheritance / non-duplication

- The hierarchical roll-up across multiple workloads is owned upstream by F-C4 (bd-35l3); B19 owns only the single-workload v0_success emission.
- DOES NOT introduce S3CanonicalJson; CanonicalConformanceWrite uses S1CanonicalJson for atomic encoding.

## Considerations

- Co-3's `overall.tolerance ≥ max per_seed[*].overall.tolerance` enforces that the cross-seed envelope is at least as loose as any per-seed gate; otherwise a seed that JUST fits its per-seed gate could still violate the overall envelope by virtue of aggregation.
- The F8 mechanical detection via `aggregation_kind` annotation is the cleanest design: CanonicalConformanceWrite refuses to serialize a forbidden value, so corruption can't leak past the schema layer.

## Acceptance

```
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real" --test conformance_round_trip_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real" --test conformance_seed_arity_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real" --test conformance_f8_aggregation_rejection_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real" --test conformance_canonical_snapshot_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real" --test conformance_self_hash_determinism_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real" --test conformance_per_token_kl_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real" --test conformance_canonical_write_proptest_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d,s3-oracle-real" --test conformance_logging_s3
scripts/s3_conformance_emit_smoke.sh
```

## Out of scope

- Outcome dispatch (B21)
- Roll-up across multiple workloads (F-C4 / bd-35l3)

## References

- RFC §11.7 "s3_conformance.v1"; §3 "CanonicalConformanceWrite"; Rule ConformanceEnvelopeEmission; Rule LogitsAggregation

Claude ACPX PASS with low residual risks; denominator/population is derivable from emitted per-token KL MetricGate rows, and no blockers remain.

title: F-D1: Persistence — versioned SRAM record protocol
description: PersistHeader + PersistGroupCommit + PersistKind + PageState. Double-buffered pages; explicit commit boundaries; SRAM-authoritative recovery. Per-record-kind compatibility (semantic_state_hash for SequenceState, resume_abi_hash for Continuation, build_identity_hash for harness/trace).

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## F-D1: Persistence — versioned SRAM record protocol

### What this is

Per `planv0.md` lines 1718–1788. `PersistHeader` + `PersistGroupCommit` + `PersistKind` + `PageState` (`Writing`/`Committed`/`Retired`). Double-buffered pages with explicit commit boundaries (`NeedInput`, `TokenReady`, `Finished`, or compiler-approved checkpoint). Records sharing mutual consistency get a `CommitGroupId` and atomic group-commit manifest. SRAM-authoritative recovery (HRAM caches but SRAM is truth).

### Why this matters

A power cut mid-write must not corrupt the next session. Without this protocol, "save state" becomes a trust nightmare and every schema bump becomes user-hostile.

### Design sketch

Implement `gbf-runtime/src/persistence.rs` (currently a stub). Header layout per planv0.md; CRC verification; per-record-kind compatibility validation (semantic_state_hash for SequenceState, resume_abi_hash for Continuation, build_identity_hash for harness/trace). Boot validates newest committed group.

### Cross-feature deps

- F-A3.4 FaultCode (PersistChecksum, PersistTornWrite, PersistSchemaUnknown)
- F-A2.2 SRAM constants
- F-A5.6 video_commit (persistence runs concurrently with UI)
- F-A6.5 gbf-migrate (StateMigrator integration)

### Confidence: HIGH. Protocol shape is well-specified.

title: F-F4: FailureCapsule + minimization + reduction_log
description: Capture failed runs with structured state (workload, observations, fault snapshot, build identity, run manifest) + minimized_workload + reduction_log. Cross-build replayable. Makes failures bisectable instead of ephemeral.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## F-F4: FailureCapsule + minimization

### What this is

`FailureCapsule` captures failed runs with structured state (workload manifest, observed observations, fault snapshot, build identity, run manifest) plus a `minimized_workload` and `reduction_log`. Cross-build replayable.

### Why this matters

A failure that can't be reproduced is a failure that can't be fixed. Minimization (delta-debug-style reduction of the workload that triggers the failure) makes investigations bisectable.

### Design sketch

```rust
pub struct FailureCapsule {
    pub original_workload: WorkloadId,
    pub minimized_workload: WorkloadManifest,
    pub reduction_log: Vec<ReductionStep>,
    pub fault: Option<FaultSnapshot>,
    pub run_manifest: RunManifest,
    pub conformance_snapshot: ConformanceEnvelope,
}
```

### Cross-feature deps

- F-A3.4 FaultSnapshot
- F-F1 RunManifest
- F-A6.1 gbf-store (capsule archival)

### Confidence: HIGH on capture, MEDIUM on minimization (needs experimentation)

description:
# Goal

Fix the Phase B / Phase C boundary in PhaseScheduler so Phase C ExpertTernaryQat does not begin until step 6002. Phase B RouterWarmup remains the single-step [6001, 6001] no-op.

# Background / Why

The original RFC defined:

  Phase A  StableFp32                      steps 1..  6000
  Phase B  RouterWarmup                    steps 6001..  6001   (no-op for dense)
  Phase C  ExpertTernaryQat                steps 6001.. 12000

Both Phase B and Phase C claimed step 6001, which made phase membership ambiguous at the boundary. D13 also applies feedback at steps 6000 and 6001; without an unambiguous owner, replay determinism is at risk if the scheduler picks differently between runs.

The fix is mechanical: shift Phase C start to 6002.

# Change

In gbf-train PhaseScheduler:

  - Phase C ExpertTernaryQat: steps 6002..12000.
  - Update step-to-phase dispatch lookup.
  - Update D13 feedback-application assignment to be explicit about steps 6000 -> Phase A finalize, 6001 -> Phase B.
  - Update fixtures / docs.

# Why this matters

Phase membership flows into per-phase loss configs (QAT lambdas, router losses, etc.) — a step misassigned to the wrong phase silently breaks the loss curve and any downstream gate that depends on it.

# Considerations

  - Phase boundary tests should pin steps {6000, 6001, 6002, 6003} explicitly.
  - This is a closed-form spec change; no semantic re-interpretation needed.

# Verification

  - PhaseScheduler unit tests for {6000, 6001, 6002}.
  - Replay determinism: same seed, two runs, identical phase-membership stream.

# Related RFC sections

  §D PhaseScheduler table, §D13 feedback boundary.
close_reason: Completed Phase C step-6002 boundary fix with Gemini and Claude PASS reviews.

title: Review fix bd-2phk: exercise tampered verifier CLI paths
description:
Origin: Gemini external review of closed bead bd-2phk; Claude review still in progress at creation time.

Gemini verdict: PASS WITH CONCERNS.

Actionable concerns:
1. `scripts/review/f-b6-f-b7/verify-packet.sh` still treats tampered independent-verifier events as conditional with comments like "tampered ... belongs to verifier beads". bd-2phk is the verifier bead, so final packet coverage must exercise the real `gbf-verify range-cert verify` CLI on tampered cert fixtures and assert the expected failed/tamper NDJSON events.
2. `gbf-verify/src/range_cert/independent.rs` accepts `(ReportOutcome::Failed, CertOutcome::Failed, failed_evidence_count = 0)` as `FailedEvidence`. Tighten this so a failed envelope without at least one failed proof is rejected as an invariant/tamper error.

Deliverables:
- Add or wire concrete tampered cert JSON fixtures, if not already present, for malformed JSON/self-hash mismatch/unsupported plan family/failed witness mismatch and any existing bd-2phk tamper cases that can be driven by the CLI.
- Extend `run-cert-verify.sh`, `verify-packet.sh`, and/or closure-pack logic so the closure packet verifies the emitted passing cert and the tampered cert paths with expected pass/fail outcomes.
- Remove stale "future verifier bead" language for bd-2phk-owned tampered verifier events.
- Add tests for the zero-failed-evidence failed-envelope invariant.
- Run `cargo test -p gbf-verify --all-features`, `cargo test -p gbf-codegen --test coverage_matrix_f_b6_f_b7`, and `scripts/review/f-b6-f-b7/verify-packet.sh`.

Acceptance:
- Final packet evidence contains real independent-verifier CLI telemetry for passing certs and tampered failures.
- A failed `range.cert.json` envelope with no failed proof evidence is rejected.
- bd-2phk review comments can record the concern as addressed before PR.

title: F-S2.02: Core notation types (PhaseKind, GlobalStep, HardnessTriple, RouterTrainMode, S2BuildKind, PhaseEffectiveLambda)
description:
Goal
====
Implement the core S2 notation types in gbf-experiments::s2::schema (per
F-S2 RFC §1 Core notation). These types are consumed by every downstream
bead and pin the public S2 ABI for the rest of the slice.

Why this matters
================
F-S2 inherits Hash256/Seed/TrainStep/BpcValue/GradNorm/Verdict from F-S1
unchanged, but introduces new S2-specific algebra: phase identity (with the
PhaseKindFixture distinction for the D8 integration test), step counters
(global vs phase-local), hardness triple, router-mode (including the
NoRouter Toy0 variant), the phase-effective lambda record, and build-kind.
These types are the load-bearing vocabulary of D1, D2, D5, D10, D13 and the
artifact schemas in §9.

Scope (Rust types in gbf-experiments::s2::schema)
=================================================
- enum PhaseKindS2     { PhaseA, PhaseB, PhaseC, PhaseD }
- enum PhaseKindFixture { PhaseA, PhaseB, PhaseC, PhaseD, PhaseE }
- type alias GlobalStep   = u64    (absolute, monotonic, 1-indexed)
- type alias PhaseLocalStep = u64  (1-indexed within current phase)
- type alias PhaseStep      = GlobalStep
- enum QuantHardness   { Off, Soft, Hard }       (re-export from gbf-model)
- enum RouterTrainMode { NoRouter, SoftTop1, HardTop1 }
- struct HardnessTriple { expert_qat, activation_qat, norm_qat }
- struct PhaseEffectiveLambda {
    lambda_distill, lambda_balance, lambda_zrouter, lambda_switch,
    lambda_range, lambda_zero, lambda_shape, lambda_overflow: f32
  }
- type alias DistillTemperature   = f32 (finite, > 0)
- type alias DistillLossNats      = f32 (finite, recorded value >= 0)
- type alias DistillLossNats64    = f64 (promoted accumulator)
- type alias GapBpc               = f64
- type alias ThresholdScalar      = f32
- type alias Q8_8Scale            = u16
- enum S2BuildKind {
    s2_ternary_full, s2_fp_full, s2_ternary_nodistill, s2_ablation
  }
  (NO s2_phase_a variant — Phase A teacher checkpoints belong to their
  parent build kind; RFC §1.)
- enum FailureKindS2 { Substrate, Gap, Distill, Phase, Metric,
    Suspicious, LinearState, LossGradFlow, PhaseIntegration, ApiDrift,
    Preregistration, Artifact, Incomplete }
  (Used only in verifier diagnostics and report body.)
- enum HypothesisStatus { Confirmed, Refuted, NotEvaluatedDueToPriorGate(String) }

Acceptance
==========
- All types defined with serde derive, S1CanonicalJson round-trip tested.
- HardnessTriple serializes with stable field order; canonical-JSON
  byte-equal across re-serialization.
- PhaseEffectiveLambda has explicit fields (no implicit zero default per
  CLAUDE.md "Training Loss Beads"; the per-field optionality / null
  semantics live in the artifact schemas, not in this type).
- Unit tests: every enum variant round-trips through S1CanonicalJson.
- proptest: arbitrary GlobalStep values round-trip; HardnessTriple
  serialization is deterministic.

Considerations
==============
- This bead introduces no behavior; it is type-only. Behavior beads (06+)
  consume these types.
- PhaseStep is a transparent alias for GlobalStep so existing F-S1
  PhaseStep references compile unchanged.
- Future S2 beads MUST NOT add new build-kind variants without a pass_version_S2
  bump (Rep-S2-5).

References
==========
F-S2 RFC §1 Core notation. CLAUDE.md "Training Loss Beads".
Blocks: everything in s2::*.
close_reason: Merged into bd-ao09 (F-S2.01 — core notation types)

title: T-B4.8a: Static-fit interpretation and necessary-condition decision semantics
description:
## What
Define `StaticFitInterpretation` and pin the contract that `fits = true`
means "passes Stage-2 necessary static checks", NOT final deployability.
See RFC §7.6 / §7.7.

## Why
Without explicit interpretation, `fits` becomes overclaimed. Reviewers
might conclude "the build is final" when in fact `RomWindowPlan` (F-B10)
or `ResourceStateValidation` (F-B13) could still fail. This task is small
but load-bearing: it pins the meaning of the boolean.

## Inputs
- T-B4.3..T-B4.7 (failure modes).

## Outputs
- `pub enum StaticFitInterpretation { PassesNecessaryStaticChecks, FailsNecessaryStaticChecks }`.
- `BudgetDecisionSection.interpretation` field.
- Schema invariant: `fits == true` ⇒ `interpretation = PassesNecessaryStaticChecks`;
  `fits == false` ⇒ `interpretation = FailsNecessaryStaticChecks`.
- Documentation pinning the contract: later passes (F-B10/F-B12/F-B13)
  remain authoritative for final deployability.

## Pitfalls
- Implementation is small (an enum + invariant). The HARD part is the
  documentation: this task's deliverable is mostly the contract pin.
- Don't extend the enum with a "Tentative" or "Pending" variant in
  this chunk — semantics here are binary.

## Acceptance
- gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_fits_means_necessary_checks_only
- gbf-report::f_b4_static_budget_v1_decision_interpretation_invariant

## Refs
- RFC §7.6, §7.7 BudgetDecisionSection, §16.1 forward-compat for F-B10/F-B12/F-B13.
- Depends on: T-B4.8.
- Blocks: T-B4.11.
close_reason: Completed with gates and review wave

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## RFC amendments (2026-05-07)

No changes to the interpretation enum or its semantics. The
`StaticFitInterpretation` invariant
(`fits == true ⇒ PassesNecessaryStaticChecks`,
`fits == false ⇒ FailsNecessaryStaticChecks`) is unchanged.

The `fits == decision.failures.is_empty()` invariant remains, and is now
backed by the new `BudgetFailure::MissingRuntimeChromeBudget` (so a
missing-budget report still satisfies the invariant — T-B4.10 amendment).

Cross-refs: §7.6 StaticFitInterpretation, §7.7 BudgetDecisionSection
invariants.

title: F-S3.05: gbf-artifact ArtifactCore + QuantSpec_S3 + CanonicalTensor + TiedEmbeddingAlias + ConformanceEnvelope + SemanticCheckpointSchema
description:
## Context

`ArtifactCore` is the canonical artifact object S3 exports for the Phase-D hard ternary student. Per RFC §3 + §7, it consists of `ArtifactManifest`, `LexicalSpec_v1`, `ModelSpec_S3`, `QuantSpec_S3` (Map<CanonicalTensorId, WeightQuant>), `SequenceSemanticsSpec`, `Vec<CanonicalTensor>`, `Vec<LogicalLutSpec>` (empty at S3), `DecodeCapabilitySet { Argmax }`, and `Option<TiedEmbeddingAlias>` (added in third-round review).

`QuantSpec_S3::weight_quant` returns `Fp32` for non-deployable reference tensors and `Ternary2 { row_scale, threshold, accumulator: I32, reduction_order: CanonicalIntegerThenScale }` for deployable post-Phase-D tensors. The single Ternary2 reduction policy is the canonical one referenced by D7 Phase-D bitwise equality.

`ConformanceEnvelope` (RFC §11.7) carries per-seed agreement metrics with PostLogits / PostDecode tolerances, including the `aggregation_kind: AggregationKind` annotation on metric values so F8-broken-S3 (prompt-wide softmax) is mechanically detectable.

This bead intentionally bundles 6 tightly-interlinked schema modules (ArtifactCore, QuantSpec, CanonicalTensor, TiedEmbeddingAlias, ConformanceEnvelope, SemanticCheckpoint). Splitting would force cross-bead churn since `TiedEmbeddingAlias` is a field of `ArtifactCore`, `ConformanceEnvelope` references `SemanticCheckpoint`, and `QuantSpec` references `CanonicalTensorId`. Per-module acceptance criteria below ensure reviewer can verify completeness.

## Why this matters

ArtifactCore is the load-bearing object S3 ships. Every Phase-D row of the agreement gate compares the live hard ternary student against the ArtifactOracle output on the artifact. The QuantSpec resolution rule (D12 / Rule QuantSpecResolution) is what H6 protects — bypassing QuantSpec via tensor-id naming is a closure-blocking defect.

## Deliverables (per-module)

### M5.A — `gbf-artifact/src/artifact.rs`

- `ConformanceEnvelope { schema: "s3_conformance.v1", workload_self_hash, per_seed: Vec<SeedConformanceEnvelope>, overall: EnvelopeGate, quantization_gap_summary, real_owner_bead: "bd-35l3", conformance_self_hash }`

`ArtifactCore::new` emits a DEBUG event:

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Why this bead exists

§8 Outcome algebra is the deterministic dispatch from the five hypothesis
verdicts (H1..H5) + per-seed completion + suspicion threshold to ONE of the
seven S1Outcome variants → ONE Decision.

§13 O7 (Outcome algebra totality) makes this a proof obligation: every
combination must map to exactly one variant.

This bead lands the dispatcher AND the totality test. Without this, two
reports could disagree about which Outcome a given run produced.

## Scope

- Types:
    enum Verdict { Confirmed, Refuted }
    enum HypothesisStatus {
        Confirmed, Refuted,
        NotEvaluatedDueToPriorGate(String)
    }
    enum S1Outcome {
        PassClean, PassWithWarning,
        FailSubstrate, FailCapacity, FailSuspicious,
        FailPhase, FailMetric
    }
    enum Decision {
        ProceedToS2, ProceedToS2WithT12_5Prereq,
        Investigate(String),
        Halt(String)
    }
- Dispatch (§8 Combination) — order is mandatory:
    if any seed.completion = DivergedAt(_)        → FailSubstrate
    elif H1 = Refuted                             → FailSubstrate
    elif H5 = Refuted                             → FailMetric
    elif H4 = Refuted                             → FailPhase
    elif median(val_bpc) < 0.5                    → FailSuspicious
    elif H2 = Refuted                             → FailCapacity
    elif H3 = Refuted                             → PassWithWarning
    else                                          → PassClean
- Decision dispatch (§8):
    PassClean        → ProceedToS2
    PassWithWarning  → ProceedToS2WithT12_5Prereq
    FailCapacity     → Investigate(propose-Toy1)
    FailSubstrate    → Investigate(burn-or-autodiff)
    FailPhase        → Investigate(F4-phase-contract)
    FailMetric       → Halt(measurement-broken)
    FailSuspicious   → Halt(audit-split-and-bpc)
- O7 totality test:
    Enumerate every binary combination of (H1..H5 verdicts) × (any-seed-
    diverged: bool) × (suspicion: bool). For each combination, assert the
    dispatcher returns exactly one S1Outcome. Cardinality:
       2^5 * 2 * 2 = 128 combinations. Cover all 128.
    NotEvaluatedDueToPriorGate enters only on early-failure reports;
    closure-candidate reports must use binary Verdict. Test that
    dispatch refuses to assign ProceedToS2 when any closure-required
    hypothesis is NotEvaluated.

## Considerations

- A22: H1 is binary. "Barely confirmed" stays Confirmed. Dispatch does NOT
  reach into prediction ranges.
- A21: the Decision is checked at PR-merge time, NOT just commit time. Halt
  blocks the bd-12pl closure commit's MERGE.
- Future-self: if a new outcome variant is ever needed (e.g. a non-existence
  check that current code doesn't trigger), update §8 in the RFC FIRST,
  then this dispatcher. Don't add variants silently.

## RFC anchors

- §8 Outcome algebra
- §13 O7 Outcome algebra totality
- §3 hypothesis-by-hypothesis verdicts
- §1 HypothesisStatus
- A21, A22

bead, driver bead, schema/cache bead, and closure bead — it is the
substrate that makes "comprehensive unit tests + e2e scripts + great
detailed logging" achievable across the rest of the chunk.

## 2. Synthetic builder API

**stable name** and structured fields. The harness verifies in CI that
no event name drifts and no class skips its event.

### Common fields per event

`diag_code` (when failed), `elapsed_ns` (u64), `event_seq` (monotonic u64).

## 4. NDJSON sink for closure-pack telemetry

`f_b6_f_b7_ndjson_sink` is a `tracing_subscriber::Layer` impl that writes
one JSON line per event to a configurable path. Used by all e2e scripts.

Default closure-pack output directory:
```
/tmp/f-b6-f-b7-closure/<build_id>/
├── stage4-run.ndjson
├── stage5-run.ndjson
├── verify-packet.ndjson
├── closure-checklist.ndjson
├── stage4_diagnostics_coverage.ndjson
├── stage5_diagnostics_coverage.ndjson
└── meta.json   # build_id, git rev, fixture set
```

Line schema (illustrative):
```json
{"ts":"2026-05-14T...", "event":"stage4.observation_plan.semantic_selection",
 "level":"INFO", "fields":{"selected_count":7, "mandatory_count":3,
 "workload_required_count":2, "workload_optional_count":2,
 "skipped_workload_required":[]}, "span":{...}}
```

## 5. E2E scripts (under `scripts/review/f-b6-f-b7/`)

| Script | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `stage4-run.sh` | Build a fixture, run `run_stage4`, emit 3 reports, dump NDJSON |
| `stage5-run.sh` | Build a fixture, run `run_stage5`, emit `range_plan.json` + `range.cert.json`, dump NDJSON |
| `run-cert-verify.sh` | Run `gbf-verify` on the emitted `range.cert.json`, dump NDJSON |
| `coverage-pack.sh` | Iterate every reject fixture and assert the expected diagnostic fires |
| `closure-pack.sh` | Stage4 → Stage5 → cert-verify → coverage; bundle into `closure-packet.tar.gz` |
| `verify-packet.sh` | Top-level entry: runs `closure-pack.sh` and `scripts/review/f-b6-f-b7/check-checklist.sh` to assert every §18a item |

All scripts emit structured tracing via the NDJSON sink. Each script
exits non-zero with a readable diagnostic on failure.

## 6. Coverage matrix harness

`gbf-codegen/tests/coverage_matrix_f_b6_f_b7.rs`:
- Iterates the closed enumeration of diagnostic codes from RFC §12.
- For each non-reserved code, asserts at least one fixture under
  `reject/stage4/<code>/` or `reject/stage5/<code>/` exists and the
  fixture's `expected_diag.json` matches.
- Reserved codes (e.g. `OBSERVATION-METRIC-ID-UNKNOWN` in v1) are
  explicitly listed as EXCLUDED and the harness fails if they appear in
  an emitted report.

## 7. Builder convention + CLAUDE.md pointer

- All fixture types derive `PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize` so
  goldens are diffable.
- Default-builder returns the smallest valid case; setters chain.
- `expect_emit()` writes canonical JSON to a temp dir, returning the
  path. Used by e2e scripts to materialize fixtures on demand.
- CLAUDE.md adds a short pointer to `scripts/review/f-b6-f-b7/`.

## Acceptance

      green AND fails when a fixture is missing for a non-reserved code
- [ ] Every builder produces byte-identical canonical JSON twice in a
      row (determinism property test)
- [ ] `scripts/review/f-b6-f-b7/verify-packet.sh` exits 0 on the dense
      and MoE accept fixtures and bundles a tarball

- [ ] Telemetry-name drift CI check: every closed event name in §3 is
      present in the emitted NDJSON at least once when the corresponding
      construction class is exercised

## How this serves the project
This bead is what lets every downstream bead say "tested" with a
straight face. Without it:
- 20 construction beads each invent their own fixture builder
- Diagnostic coverage rots silently
- The §18a closure checklist becomes a manual audit
- Reviewers cannot grep for stable event names across debugging sessions
- gbf-verify (F-F1) cannot exercise tampered-cert fixtures consistently

Lands the F-B6/F-B7 review-packet pattern that future RFCs (F-B8, F-B13,
F-B14) will copy. The pattern itself echoes the F-A5 and F-S2 closure
packs that already exist in this repo.

## RFC anchors
§14 task DAG (this bead pre-Wave-2), §18a closure checklist (this bead
ships the harness that runs it).

## History
- All four review passes (42-fix, 41-patch, 45-patch, 30-patch) asked
  for per-rejection-code fixtures and closure checklists.
- F-A5 (gbf-runtime) verify-packet under `scripts/review/f-a5/` is the
  precedent.
- F-S2 (QAT survives) closure-pack pattern is the precedent for NDJSON
  and §18a-style checklists.
- F-B3/F-B5 already use per-class `tracing::event` (e.g.
  `stage3.types.bind_gb_infer_ir`); this bead extends to F-B6/F-B7
  with a closed event vocabulary.

those types to compile.

title: F-S2.35: H5.4b diagnostic_subcheck (lambda_zero=0 raw honesty against F5-broken short-circuit)
description:
Goal
====
Implement the H5.4b diagnostic_subcheck inside the H5.4 FixtureResult:
verifies that the zero_loss helper (F-S2.11) honestly computes raw_loss
when lambda_zero = 0.0 (ComputedDisabled), and that weighted_loss is
exactly 0.0. NOT a sixth fixture — this is a DiagnosticSubcheckResult
attached to H5.4. Per F-S2 RFC §11 H5.4b + §13 O13 + LGF-5 invariant.

Why this matters
================
F5-broken-S2 short-circuits the zero_loss helper when lambda_zero = 0
and returns 0.0 without computing the L1 sum. Without this subcheck the
short-circuit is invisible from the artifact. LGF-2 ("every fixture
uses non-default lambda") would otherwise forbid the lambda=0 case;
LGF-5 exempts diagnostic subchecks.

Scope (in gbf-experiments::s2::loss_grad_flow::synthetic_zero)
==============================================================
- Subcheck name: "lambda_zero_raw_honesty_at_zero_weight"
- lambda_value: 0.0
- Same synthetic 4x8 matrix + per-row thresholds + below/above-threshold
  pattern as H5.4 main fixture.
- Invoke zero_loss helper (F-S2.11) directly.
- Assertions captured into DiagnosticSubcheckResult:
    raw_loss_computed: bool   — true iff helper actually computed the L1
                                sum (must be true; F5-broken returns
                                false)
    raw_loss_finite:   bool   — true; finite and >= 0
    weighted_loss_value: 0.0
    passed: raw_loss_computed AND raw_loss_finite AND
            weighted_loss_value == 0.0
- Attach this subcheck to the H5.4 FixtureResult via
  diagnostic_subchecks list (per F-S2.18 schema).

Acceptance
==========
- Subcheck passes for an honest zero_loss helper.
- Subcheck fails for an F5-broken helper that short-circuits.
- LGF-5 invariant (H5.4 FixtureResult MUST include this subcheck)
  enforced at validate-time.
- LGF-2 (non_default_value_used) is NOT failed by the lambda=0
  subcheck (exemption rule).

Considerations
==============
- This bead is the runtime/test side of the policy. The schema
  (DiagnosticSubcheckResult + LGF-5) lives in F-S2.18.
- F5-broken-S2 (F-S2.37) is the canonical falsification: implementer of
  zero_loss with the short-circuit bug should fail this subcheck.

References
==========
F-S2 RFC §11 H5.4b, §9.4 LGF-5, §13 O5 F5-broken-S2, §13 O13.
Depends on: F-S2.11 (zero_loss helper), F-S2.18 (schema).

## F-H1: KernelSpec + signatures + compatibility ids

### What this is

`gbf-kernel` schema types: `KernelSpec`, `KernelSpecId`, signatures, calling conventions, `KernelCompatSpec`, autotune dimensions. Schema only — implementations are F-H2.

### Why this matters

Per planv0.md line 189: `gbf-codegen` selects kernels and `gbf-runtime` links them, but neither redefines kernel signatures. Without this central spec, kernel signature drift between compiler and runtime is silent.

### Design sketch

```rust
pub struct KernelSpec {
    pub id: KernelSpecId,
    pub family: KernelFamily,                      // MatVec, Residual, Norm, Route, Decode, ...
    pub signature: KernelSignature,                // input/output value kinds + quant formats
    pub calling_convention: CallingConvention,
    pub autotune_dims: Vec<AutotuneDim>,
    pub compat: KernelCompatSpec,
}
```

### Cross-feature deps

- F-A1 gbf-asm (signatures reference AsmIR types)

### Confidence: HIGH

comments.text:
## T-B1.6.3: Report aggregation logic + cycle attribution

**Target crate**: `gbf-report`
**Target file**: `gbf-report/src/aggregation.rs`

### Background

Takes the raw trace + runtime metrics from `gbf-bench::MatmulI8Bringup` and produces a `realism_report.v1` document. Cycle-attribution rules are applied here; this is the bead that turns "the emulator told us X cycles passed" into "X cycles per product-accumulate."

### Cycle-attribution rules (canonical)

- `cycles_per_product_accumulate` is computed from emulator cycle deltas over known product-count regions (kernel inner-loop body). Tile-dump pause is excluded.
- `cycles_per_output_tile` is the cycle delta from "first product of tile" to "tile-complete safe point" — does not include the dump pause.
- `cycles_per_full_matmul` is end-to-end from "kernel entry" to "final tile dump complete." Includes ISR, dump-pauses, scheduler service. This is the wall-clock-equivalent number.
- `wall_clock_seconds_at_gb_clock_f64` is derived: `cycles_per_full_matmul / (4_194_304.0 * 4.0)` for M-cycles, since `1 M-cycle = 4 T-cycles` and `1 T-cycle ≈ 1 / 4.194 MHz`.
- `effective_*_bandwidth_*_f64` is `bytes_read / wall_clock_seconds_at_gb_clock_f64`.

### Aggregation outputs

For each N, the aggregator produces:

- `compute_costs` — distribution stats (min/mean/max/p99) over per-product-accumulate cycles, per-tile cycles, and the scalar `cycles_per_full_matmul`.
- `memory_bandwidth` — Bank0 table-read bytes, ROMX operand-read bytes, effective bandwidths, WRAM/HRAM/SRAM peaks.
- `rom_layout` — Bank0 used/free bytes, ROMX operand bank size.
- `banking` — logical-switch counts, MBC-write counts, lease acquire/release/balance/max-active, yield-while-lease counter.
- `scheduling` — frames-to-completion, gated-frame count, vblank count, widget-update count, scheduler-service count, frame-service-misses, max-no-progress, worst-case interrupt latency, cycles-remaining-at-widget-tick distribution, cycles-remaining-at-scheduler-service distribution.
- `conformance` — byte-exact-match flag, reference-source hash, fixture hash, expected-output hash.

### Acceptance gates

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-report -- aggregation::cycle_attribution_excludes_dump_pause
cargo test -p gbf-report -- aggregation::wall_clock_seconds_derived_from_dmg_clock
cargo test -p gbf-report -- aggregation::distributions_have_min_mean_max_p99
cargo test -p gbf-report -- aggregation::frame_service_misses_zero_in_passing_run
cargo test -p gbf-bench -- f_b1_report_aggregation_known_fixture
```

### RFC reference

`history/rfcs/F-B1-compute-bringup.md` §9.1 (cycle attribution rule), §10.

### Dependencies

- T-B1.6.1 (schema).
- T-B1.6.2 (runner provides traces).
- T-B1.5.5 (frame trace ordering metrics).
- T-B1.3.5 (lease metrics).

**Target crate**: `gbf-model`

**Reference**: `history/planv0.md` — search for "NormApproxQat", "NormPlan", "AffineClipLut", "TileRmsThenAffineClip".

| Burn norm gradients flow through input, affine params, and clip bounds | `cargo test -p gbf-train --features burn-adapter -- qat::norm` | `burn-adapter` | Includes focused autodiff tests for AffineClipLut and TileRmsThenAffineClip. |
| Burn adapter exports the same `NormExportParams` contract as the scalar core | `cargo test -p gbf-train --features burn-adapter -- qat::norm` | `burn-adapter` | `burn_norm_export_matches_artifact_contract_from_owned_tensors`. |
| Burn imports remain confined to `gbf-train` | `cargo test -p gbf-test --test architecture` | none | Architecture sensor protects `bd-1mv` boundary. |
| QAT closure constraints are satisfied | `python3 scripts/qat_harness_checks.py` | none | Harness passed before closure. |

## No Future Variant Acceptance

`NormApproxPlan` accepts only `AffineClipLut` and `TileRmsThenAffineClip`; no future norm plans, dynamic LUT training modes, or implicit LayerNorm lowering variants are accepted. Invalid scalar contracts are rejected by constructors, Burn ragged tile inputs are rejected before reshape, and Burn export revalidates trained affine and clip tensors before producing artifact parameters. `NormPlan::None` remains an artifact-level "no norm module" value, not an accepted `NormApproxQat` training variant.

description: Validation envelope at the head of the pipeline. Verify schema, semantic core hash, manifest invariants, lowering round-trip, calibration freshness. Resolve CompileRequest into ResolvedCompilePolicy with PolicyProvenance. Emit policy_resolution.json.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## F-B0: ArtifactValidationAndUpgrade + ResolvedCompilePolicy (Stages 0, 0.5)

### What this is

The validation envelope at the head of the compiler pipeline (`planv0.md` line 1152, 1037). Stage 0 verifies the artifact's schema, semantic core hash, manifest invariants, required-feature set, self-consistency of canonical tensors / LUTs / quant spec / sequence semantics / decode capabilities / lexical spec / interaction bundle / hint bundle / workload references / golden vectors. Validates `TargetDataLoweringArtifact` packer round-trips. Validates `CompileRequest` against the resolved `TargetProfile`, required-feature set, and any referenced calibration bundles in the `CalibrationSetRef`.

Stage 0.5 (`ResolvedCompilePolicy`) records the fully resolved policy with `PolicyProvenance` (target_defaults, profile_defaults, hint_bundle_hash, compile_request_hash, calibration_hash). Every build emits `policy_resolution.json`.

### Why this matters

Most "the build worked but produced garbage" failures trace back to compiling against an artifact whose schema doesn't match the compiler's expectations or against stale calibration. Catching them here is cheap; catching them later means redoing scheduling, layout, encoding.

### Design sketch

```rust
pub fn validate_artifact(core: &ArtifactCore, manifest: &ArtifactManifest, aux: &ArtifactAux)
    -> Result<(), ValidationError>;
pub fn validate_lowerings(core: &ArtifactCore, lowerings: &[TargetDataLoweringArtifact])
    -> Result<(), ValidationError>;
pub fn resolve_policy(req: &CompileRequest, target: &TargetProfile)
    -> Result<ResolvedCompilePolicy, PolicyResolutionError>;
```

Output: `policy_resolution.json` with the fully resolved policy and provenance.

### Cross-feature deps

- F-A2.1 (TargetProfile)
- F-A6.2 (StageCache: validation results are cached)
- gbf-artifact (existing) for ArtifactCore types
- gbf-policy (existing) for CompileRequest, ResolvedCompilePolicy, RepairPolicy

### Confidence: HIGH

Mostly schema validation + serde + provenance hashing.
