title: T-A1.7: Encoder — the only path from Instr to bytes
description: The only Instr → bytes path. Consumes &LegalizedSection (SoA: labels/instrs/data_blocks/alignments only — un-legalized input is a compile error, not a runtime error) plus &PlacedSection (concrete alignment padding from layout). No &SymbolTable argument. CB-prefix encoding is exhaustively verified across all 256 opcodes. Bit-stable across runs. Three-variant EncodeError; OpNotLegalized / UnresolvedSymbol / RelativeOffsetOutOfRange are eliminated structurally and operationally upstream.
design:
## T-A1.7: Encoder — the only path from `Instr` to bytes

**Target crate**: `gbf-asm`
**Target file(s)**: `gbf-asm/src/encoder.rs`
**Reference**: `history/rfcs/F-A1-gbf-asm.md` §3, §8.

### What changed vs the original sketch

The encoder **does not lower structured ops** under the RFC. It consumes a
`&LegalizedSection`, which physically does not contain `pre_layout_ops`,
`legalization_ops`, or `branches` arrays. Lowering is owned by `lowering.rs`
(pre-layout) and `relax.rs` (placement-dependent legalization, including
`SymbolicBranch` resolution and far-call thunk operand rewriting). The
encoder is thus a total function over four typed item arrays, exhaustive at
compile time. There is no `EncodeError::OpNotLegalized`,
`UnresolvedSymbol`, or `RelativeOffsetOutOfRange` — those failure modes are
eliminated structurally and operationally upstream.

### Public surface (RFC §8.1)

```rust
pub struct EncodedSection {
    pub id: SectionId,
    pub bytes: Vec<u8>,
    pub item_spans: Vec<EncodedItemSpan>,
}

pub struct EncodedItemSpan {
    pub order: ItemOrder,
    pub kind:  EncodedItemKind,            // Instr | DataBlock | AlignmentPadding
    pub offset: u16,
    pub len:    u16,
}

pub fn encode_section(
    section: &LegalizedSection,
    placed: &PlacedSection,
) -> Result<EncodedSection, EncodeError>;

pub fn encode_instr(instr: &Instr) -> Result<SmallVec<[u8; 4]>, EncodeError>;
```

No `&SymbolTable` argument. Symbol resolution is finished by relax; the
encoder receives concrete operand bytes only.

### `EncodeError` (RFC §8.3)

```rust
pub enum EncodeError {
    EncodedLengthMismatch { expected: u8, actual: u8, instr: Instr },
    MissingAlignmentPlan { section_id: SectionId, order: ItemOrder },
    NonRomSectionEncoded { section_id: SectionId, space: AddressSpace },
}
```

`MissingAlignmentPlan` fires when `placed.alignment_padding` lacks an entry
for an `Align` item. The encoder reads concrete padding from layout — it
does not recompute alignment, because divergence between the two
computations would silently break layout/listing/ROM agreement.

### Per-array iteration

`encode_section` merges the four arrays of `LegalizedSection` by `ItemOrder`
and emits:

- `instrs[k]` → `encode_instr(&item.data)`.
- `data_blocks[k]` → `Bytes` pass through; `Words` little-endian.
- `alignments[k]` → `placed.alignment_padding[&item.order]` 0xFF bytes.
- `labels[k]` → 0 bytes (no entry in `item_spans`).

### CB-prefix coverage (RFC §14 q7)

All 256 CB-prefixed opcodes are generated by bitwise logic
`(op, bit, target) → u8` and asserted byte-for-byte against a
Pan-Docs-derived table. CB encoding is exhaustive, not spot-checked.

### Bit-stability

Two specific risks:
- Symbol resolution order — handled upstream (already `BTreeMap`).
- SoA merge order — `ItemOrder::seq_index` is a globally monotone `u32`; the
  k-way merge over four arrays is total and deterministic.
acceptance_criteria:
```bash
cargo check -p gbf-asm
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- encoder::known_opcodes                  # ≥30 Pan-Docs spot-checks
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- encoder::cb_exhaustive                  # all 256 CB encodings
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- encoder::byte_len_matches               # encoder bytes == Instr::byte_len()
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- encoder::bit_stable                     # 100× LegalizedSection round-trip
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- encoder::halt_is_one_byte               # [0x76]
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- encoder::alignment_padding_comes_from_layout_plan
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- encoder::public_api_has_no_symbol_table_argument
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- section::legalized_section_drops_unencoded_arrays_at_the_type_level
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- relax::all_symbolic_operands_are_concrete_after_legalization
```

Mirrors RFC §8 + the §16 claim-to-gate matrix entries for encoder
correctness, structural elimination of un-legalized input, exhaustive
CB-prefix coverage, alignment provenance, and the missing
`&SymbolTable` argument.
notes:
### Constitution Checkpoints (RFC §2.5)

- §I.1 — `EncodeError` is exhaustive, three variants only; un-legalized input is eliminated structurally.
- §III — bit-stability is a property test; CB-prefix coverage is exhaustive at test time.
- §IV.3 — encoder output is reproducible bit-for-bit.
- §VI.1 — encoder is the only path from `Instr` to bytes.

### PR shape (RFC §12)

Pairs with the cycle model into PR1: `cycle_model + encoder`. The encoder
takes `&LegalizedSection`, so curated test fixtures must produce that
type — listing and ROM tests reuse the same fixture builders.

### Open follow-ups (not blocking F-A1)

- Disassembly mnemonic formatter lives in `listing.rs` (T-A1.8), not here.
close_reason:
Completed F-A1 encoder bead across PR1 plus PR2 legalization dependency.

ASM checklist:

-  remains the only Instr -> bytes function; layout/relax size using Instr::byte_len, not byte lowering.

comments.text:
## T-A1.7: Encoder

**Target crate**: `gbf-asm`
**Target file(s)**: `gbf-asm/src/encoder.rs`
**Reference**: `planv0.md` §"Assembly eDSL", §"Engineering rules" rule 2 ("Only the encoder translates legal instructions to bytes").

### Background

The encoder is the **only** module that turns `Instr` into bytes. It must be deterministic, bit-stable across runs (so blob hashes are stable per `§IV.3`), and exhaustive over the ISA defined in T-A1.1.

### Implementation Notes

```rust
pub struct EncodedSection {
    pub id: SectionId,
    pub bytes: Vec<u8>,
    pub instr_offsets: Vec<(InstrIdx, u16)>,    // for listings + provenance lookup
}

pub fn encode_section(
    section: &Section,
    placed: &PlacedSection,
    symbols: &SymbolTable,
) -> Result<EncodedSection, EncodeError>;

pub fn encode_instr(instr: &Instr, here: u16, symbols: &SymbolTable) -> Result<SmallVec<[u8; 4]>, EncodeError>;
```

Pseudo-ops are lowered here:
- `BankLease { ... }` → calls into the F-A4 acquire primitives (the actual bytes are the runtime's banking module entry-point + arguments).
- `FarCall { target, lease_chain }` → either an in-bank `CALL` or a far-call thunk (depending on T-A1.6 relaxation result).
- `Yield { kind }` → call into `gbf-runtime::scheduler::yield_with(kind)`.
- `TraceProbe { id, level }` → call into trace-emit primitive (no-op when trace is disabled).
- `AssertBank` → debug-build-only; release build emits no bytes.
- `Db(u8)` / `Dw(u16)` → straight bytes.

Determinism: every encoding decision must be data-dependent only — no hash-map iteration order, no SystemTime, no thread-local state.

### Acceptance Criteria

```bash
cargo check -p gbf-asm
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- encoder::known_opcodes               # ~30 spot-checks vs Pan Docs
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- encoder::round_trip                   # encode -> decode (where decoder exists) preserves Instr
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- encoder::bit_stable                   # Encoding the same Section twice yields identical bytes
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- encoder::pseudo_op_lowering           # BankLease/FarCall/Yield/TraceProbe lower correctly
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- encoder::assert_bank_release_noop     # AssertBank emits 0 bytes in release builds
```

### Constitution Checkpoints

- §I.1: `EncodeError` enumerates exact failure modes.
- §IV.3: Bit-stability is asserted by test.
- §VI.1: The encoder is the only path to bytes.

title: F-S3.25: F-S3 closure orchestration + F4 (bd-3w2) closure via H7 carry-through
description:
## Context

This is the closure-orchestration bead for F-S3 + F4. It blocks the existing F-S3 closure bead `bd-3k8o` and is the trigger for closing F4 (`bd-3w2`) via H7's carry-through verdict.

Per RFC §13 closure protocol, S3 closure requires 10 ordered conditions:
1. All 5 seed runs Completed through Phase D (D9)
2. s3_report.v1 emitted with R-Predictions verified by git history
3. Decision ∈ {ProceedToS4, ProceedToS4-with-deferred-clause}
4. charset_self_hash, baseline_self_hash, workload_self_hash, conformance_self_hash, v0_success_self_hash recorded
5. Phase-specific exported-surface agreement gate (D7) passes for every seed at Phase A and Phase D on the pinned three-prompt subset
6. v0_success per-seed composite (D6 Q1..Q6) holds for every seed

title: T9.2: Implement StructuredWidthGates supernet training (M6)
description: M6 research: train experts with max d_ff, but each (row_group x col_group) block has a learnable sigmoid gate. During training, the gate values are annealed from 1.0 toward 0.0 using a temperature schedule. The lambda_shape penalty encourages gates to close (producing sparser experts). The lambda_overflow penalty penalizes total exported bytes exceeding the bank budget. The gradient flows through the gate values and the STE-projected ternary weights.
acceptance_criteria: cargo check passes; Gates are learnable parameters; Sigmoid annealing sharpens over steps; Pruning produces valid smaller experts

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Agent Instructions

**Target crate**: `gbf-model` + `gbf-train`
**Target file(s)**:
- `gbf-model/src/qat/expert.rs` (extend with width gates)
- `gbf-train/src/supernet.rs` (new — supernet training logic)

**Reference**: `history/planv0.md` — search for "StructuredWidthGates", "supernet", "learnable sigmoid gates", "M6 research".

### Implementation Notes
- M6 research mode: train experts with max d_ff, with learnable sigmoid gates per block group.
- Gates: `sigmoid(alpha_k)` per group of `col_group` columns; during training, multiply expert activations by gate values.
- Annealing: gradually sharpen sigmoid (increase temperature) during training to force gates toward 0/1.
- Loss terms: lambda_shape (penalize non-binary gates), lambda_overflow (penalize experts exceeding bank budget).
- After training: prune blocks with gate < threshold, yielding variable-size experts.

### Acceptance Criteria
```bash
cargo check -p gbf-model                       # Compiles
cargo check -p gbf-train                       # Compiles
cargo test -- supernet                          # Tests pass
# Verify: gates are learnable parameters
# Verify: sigmoid annealing sharpens over steps
# Verify: pruning produces valid smaller experts
```

### Constitution Checkpoints
- §I.1: ExpertShapePolicy::StructuredWidthGates is the only entry point for this behavior
- §II.3: This is M6 research — keep it isolated from the main training path

title: T-B6.I: ObservationPlan finalize (anchor table, provenance, schema re-emit, budget projection, self-consistency, sort)
description:
## What
Implement construction classes 13-19 of `build_observation_plan_core`:

13. **AnchorTableBinding** — populate `AnchorAttachmentTable`:
    - `semantic: BTreeMap<SemanticCheckpointId, SemanticAttachment>`
    - `probes:   BTreeMap<ProbeInstanceId, ProbeSource>`
    - `metrics:  BTreeMap<MetricId, MetricSource>`
14. **ProvenanceBinding** — populate `ObservationProvenance` keyed by
    `ProbeInstanceId` (NOT `TraceProbeId`).
15. **SchemaReEmit** — build the `BuildActiveCheckpointSchema` payload:
    `Vec<ReEmittedCheckpointEntry>` carrying id, role,
    `original_checkpoint_metadata`, encoding, source, attachment_node_id,
    attachment_anchor, canonical_provenance_tuple.
16. **OperationalProbeSchemaEmit** — build `OperationalProbeSchema` body:
    probes, metrics, `per_class_probe_weight_total`,
    `per_class_metric_weight_total`, `per_class_total_weight`.
17. **InvariantBudgetCheck** — compute `TraceBudgetProjection
    { projected_max_events_per_slice, projected_max_bytes_per_frame,
    fits_declared_budget }`. Under Invariant mode, bust ⇒ Hard
    `OBSERVATION-INVARIANT-MODE-BUDGET-BUSTED`. Under Flexible, bust is
    recorded as a non-diagnostic field in the plan.
18. **SelfConsistency** — cross-class checks `OP-SC-1..19`.
19. **CanonicalSort** — sort all BTreeMaps + Vecs in canonical order.

## Why
Closes the construction pipeline. The 30-patch review's Patch 7 split
metric vs probe weight totals; the 41-patch Patch 28/29 introduced
`TraceBudgetProjection`. SchemaReEmit must include source + original
metadata so F-C2 ArtifactOracle can do checkpoint-aligned diffing.

- [ ] `ReEmittedCheckpointEntry` carries `source: ObservationSource`
      (45-patch Patch 22).

      per_class_total_weight[c]` post-condition.
- [ ] Under Flexible mode, `TraceBudgetProjection.fits_declared_budget =
      false` is allowed.
- [ ] Trace cost projected from `frequency_bound × event_shape.max_payload_bytes`
      per probe (Patch 29 frequency bounds).
- [ ] `R-NoReportHashCycles` enforcement: do not refer to own report's
      report_self_hash from the body.

## Audit amendment — landed-code reconciliation (2026-05-14)

### `ReEmittedCheckpointEntry` references landed CheckpointEntry
Per RFC §20.2, the landed `gbf-abi::checkpoint::CheckpointEntry` is the
canonical "per-checkpoint metadata" carrier. The RFC's
`original_checkpoint_metadata` field on `ReEmittedCheckpointEntry`
should be typed against the landed struct:

```rust
pub struct ReEmittedCheckpointEntry {
    pub id: SemanticCheckpointId,                // wire string
    pub kind: SemanticCheckpointKind,            // helper; for fast pattern
    pub artifact_role: SemanticCheckpointRole,   // derived from stratum
    pub original_checkpoint_metadata: CheckpointEntryView,
    pub encoding: ObservationEncoding,
    pub source: ObservationSource,
    pub attachment_node_id: NodeId,
    pub attachment_anchor: SemanticAnchor,
    pub canonical_provenance_tuple: CanonicalProvenanceTuple,
}

pub struct CheckpointEntryView {
    pub compact: CompactCheckpointId,
    pub stratum: SemanticStratum,
    pub source_op: Option<String>,
}
```

`CheckpointEntryView` is just `CheckpointEntry` minus `semantic`
(redundant with the outer `id`). This keeps the wire JSON compact and
ensures the re-emit faithfully reflects the original schema entry.

### `AnchorAttachmentTable.semantic` uses string keys
Since `SemanticCheckpointId` is a transparent string newtype, the map
`BTreeMap<SemanticCheckpointId, SemanticAttachment>` serializes as a
native JSON object (NOT the sorted-list rule for complex keys). This
is a small but important canonical-JSON simplification:

```json
{
  "semantic": {
    "layer.5.post_router": { "anchor": "...", "source": {...} },
    "post_decode":         { "anchor": "...", "source": {...} },
    ...
  }
}
```

T-B6T7.A's canonical-JSON sorted-list rule applies only to maps with
non-string-newtype complex keys (`ProbeInstanceId`, `ReductionSelector`,
etc).

### Acceptance addition
- [ ] `ReEmittedCheckpointEntry` carries `CheckpointEntryView` reflecting
      the landed `CheckpointEntry`
- [ ] `AnchorAttachmentTable.semantic` uses native string-key JSON
      object encoding (not sorted-list)
- [ ] Re-emit byte-stable across two runs and identical to the original
      schema's checkpoints (minus build-active filtering)

comments.text:
## T-B1.0.3: Deterministic operand fixture generators

**Target crate**: `gbf-verify`
**Target file**: `gbf-verify/src/matmul/fixtures.rs`

### Background

Every test, bench, and review-packet artifact compares against the same operand matrices. The fixtures are pure-arithmetic functions of `(i, j)` — not RNG-backed — so they reproduce exactly across host architectures and toolchain versions. The fixture hash is one of the identity fields in `realism_report.v1.json`.

### Canonical formulas (these are canonical, not examples)

```text
A[i, j] = (((73*i + 37*j + 19) mod 256) - 128) as i8
B[i, j] = (((29*i + 91*j + 11) mod 256) - 128) as i8
```

### Implementation note

Compute the formula in at least `i32`/`u32`, subtract 128 in a signed type, then convert to `i8`. Do **not** rely on accidental unsigned underflow or implementation-defined wrap-around.

```rust
pub fn deterministic_matrix_a(dim: SquareDim) -> Vec<i8> {
    let n = dim.n() as i32;
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(dim.elem_count());
    for i in 0..n {
        for j in 0..n {
            let v = (73 * i + 37 * j + 19).rem_euclid(256);  // 0..256
            let signed = v - 128;                              // -128..128
            out.push(signed as i8);
        }
    }
    out
}

// Similarly for matrix_b with constants (29, 91, 11).
```

### ROM serialization

Two's-complement `i8 as u8`, row-major. No padding. The serialized fixture hash is `operand_fixture_hash` in the realism report.

### Acceptance gates

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-verify -- matmul::fixtures::generation_is_stable
cargo test -p gbf-verify -- matmul::fixtures::known_n16_first_row_a
cargo test -p gbf-verify -- matmul::fixtures::known_n16_first_row_b
cargo test -p gbf-verify -- matmul::fixtures::values_in_i8_range
cargo test -p gbf-verify -- matmul::fixtures::serialization_round_trip
```

### RFC reference

`history/rfcs/F-B1-compute-bringup.md` §7.1.1.

### Dependencies

- T-B1.0.1 (`SquareDim`).

comments.text:
## REVISION PASS — RFC fixture-ownership patch (2026-05-03)

The RFC was patched to fix an inconsistency where production crates needed operand bytes but `ComputeBringupRequest` had no fixture spec and only `gbf-verify` knew the formulas (would have forced `gbf-codegen` to depend on `gbf-verify`, contradicting T-B1.0.7).

### Bead scope after patch

This bead now owns **two** materializers, not one:

1. **Verifier materializer** in `gbf-verify::matmul::fixtures` — `deterministic_matrix_a`/`_b` from RFC §7.1.1 reference subsection. Used by the reference and by the test that compares production vs verifier bytes.
2. **Production materializer** in `gbf-codegen::fixtures::materialize_operand_fixture` (per RFC §7.1.1 production subsection) — consumes `OperandFixtureSpec::DeterministicAffineV1` (introduced by T-B1.2.1) and emits the A/B ROM byte payloads.

Independence rule:

* the two materializers must not call the same helper;
* a parity test asserts byte equality of the production and verifier outputs for every F-B1 review-packet size (`N ∈ {16, 32, 64, 96, 128}`);
* production crates must not depend on `gbf-verify` to build operand ROM payloads — T-B1.0.7's dep-direction lint enforces this mechanically.

### New acceptance gate

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- operand_fixture_matches_verify_for_review_sizes
```

This gate joins the existing `quarter_square_table_matches_verify` parity test as a second instance of the same independence pattern.

### Why the RFC was wrong before

The original RFC said "production crates must not depend on `gbf-verify`," but production crates needed operand bytes to build a closure ROM, and only `gbf-verify` knew the canonical formulas. There was no production-neutral fixture spec at all. The patch resolves this by introducing `OperandFixtureSpec` (in `gbf-abi`/`gbf-ir`) and giving `gbf-codegen` an independent materializer.

### Logging discipline

The production materializer emits `FB1TraceEvent::ComputeReqImported { fixture_hash }` (from T-B1.0.9) when a request is imported. Hash is over the materialized A/B bytes, not the spec name — so a future `DeterministicAffineV2` or alternative fixture format hashes differently even if the spec discriminant looks similar.

title: F-S7 RFC v0.2: Pre-implementation correctness patch series
description:
## Description

F-S7 ("MoE Beats Dense at Matched Bytes"; slice S7; closure bead bd-2v9r) underwent a pre-implementation correctness review on 2026-05-20. The review surfaced 25 distinct issues that, left unfixed, would have made the experiment either unfair (matched bytes wouldn't actually be matched because the dense solver was biased toward MoE), non-falsifiable (the outcome algebra collapsed a bytes-mismatch into Fail-parity, which closes bd-2v9r as DenseOnly — a successful scientific verdict for an invalid experiment), or impossible to pass for the wrong reasons (the original H7 claimed lm_loss and distill_loss reach LowRankRouter parameters, but D3's hard top-1 stop-gradient dispatch blocks exactly that path; an honest implementation would have failed H7 while a dishonest one — straight-through estimator, soft-leaked-into-training — could have passed parity via a phantom path).

All 25 textual patches have been applied to `history/rfcs/F-S7-moe-beats-dense.md`. This epic tracks the v0.2 patch series itself plus the implementation discipline each patch implies, so that bd-2v9r's eventual implementation matches v0.2's contract rather than the pre-review draft.

### The five load-bearing blockers

1. **Router gradient provenance under hard top-1 dispatch.** D3 says dispatch is stop-gradient, so lm/distill cannot reach LowRankRouter via that path. H7 must declare this explicitly and O13 must assert it.
2. **"Matched bytes" semantics.** Original D6 said matched-bytes is FFN-payload only, but H4 used `deployed_bytes_total`. MoE could pass H3 by FFN payload alone while failing Pareto because the router exists. v0.2 routes both H3 and H4 through `B_deployed_total` (FFN + router + bias + metadata).
3. **Fail-bytes vs Fail-parity.** Bytes-mismatch is not a scientific falsification of the MoE-wins claim; it is an invalid experiment. v0.2 separates Fail-bytes (Halt) from Fail-parity (DenseOnly).
4. **Entropy units.** RFC alternated bits and nats; the n=4 floor of "1.7" is impossible in nats (ln 4 ≈ 1.386). v0.2 standardizes on bits everywhere.
5. **Dense byte solver fairness.** Original solver picked the *smallest* d_ff_dense within tolerance — systematically biasing toward MoE. v0.2 minimizes |B_deployed(Dense) − B_deployed(MoE)| with explicit tie-breaks.

### Why pre-implementation patches matter

S7's deliverable is *verified knowledge*, not just code (like S1, S3, S4). The pre-registration discipline (S1 O1; Rep-S7-8) requires that the RFC's predictions and falsification rules are committed strictly before any result artifact. If we begin implementation against the broken v0.1 RFC, the pre-registration is anchored to a contract that cannot honestly be passed, and the bd-2v9r closure path is poisoned. Fixing the RFC now is a one-shot cost; fixing it after first results requires bumping `pass_version` and re-running every (topology, seed) pair from scratch.

### Scope

Twelve thematic features cover the 25 issues:

- F1: Byte accounting reform (D6, §6.2 solver, MatchedBytesPin, bias policy)
- F2: Outcome algebra & closure routing (Fail-bytes, Pass-with-warning removal, §21)
- F3: Router gradient provenance (H7, §8.3.1/8.3.2, O13)
- F4: Entropy units normalization
- F5: H6 guardrail logic & divergence handling
- F6: Temporal smoothness window semantics
- F7: Lambda sweep cadence & H3 decoupling
- F8: LowRankRouter rank rationale
- F9: Pareto verdict byte-equivalence variants
- F10: State machine internal teacher freeze
- F11: Schema discipline (consolidated small fixes)
- F12: H10 emulator comparison & D16 collapse halt robustness

## Acceptance Criteria

- All 12 child features under this epic are closed.
- `history/rfcs/F-S7-moe-beats-dense.md` reflects v0.2 of the contract (already applied as of 2026-05-20).
- bd-2v9r's predicate references F-S7 v0.2 (pass_version bumped before any S7 result artifact commit per O1).
- A reviewer signs off on the dependency graph end-to-end (no orphan Refute path; no orphan Halt path).
- The 9-test falsification suite in §16 O5 still typechecks against v0.2's hypothesis statements.

## Notes

- RFC: `history/rfcs/F-S7-moe-beats-dense.md`
- Closure bead: `bd-2v9r`
- Parent epic: `bd-1rb` (training-contract revision pass)
- Inherits unchanged from S1..S5: seeds [0..4], AdamW config, S1CpuDeterministic, charset_v1, Gutenberg manifest, KN-5 baseline, LinearState multi-timescale, F8 frontier, EncodedRom + emulator one-token.
- This epic does NOT own the implementation of S7 itself (gbf-experiments::s7::*, gbf-policy::DenseMatchedBytesPolicy, gbf-model::Top1RouterQat, etc.); those remain in bd-2v9r's dependency chain.
- Review transcript captured 2026-05-20 by Sonnet-4.7 (1M context) review pass; transcript is not committed (the patches in this epic ARE the reviewable artifact).
close_reason:
Closed bd-2p7g after Gemini and Claude ACPX reviews passed.

All 12 direct child features are closed; audited one-level implementation/audit children are closed; RFC text carries the v0.2 contract corrections; O5 falsification harness typechecked during engineering; bd-2v9r has a clarification comment binding final closure to the v0.2 production predicate.

No v0.1 Pass-with-warning, FFN-only matched-byte gate, entropy-nats metric, adjacent-only smoothness shortcut, or stale H10 training-log comparator is accepted.

title: T-B7.H: gbf-verify independent verifier for range.cert.json
description:
## What
Implement an independent verifier in `gbf-verify` (F-F1) that consumes
`certs/range.cert.json` and re-verifies each `CertifiedReduction`:

```text
Independent_Verify_Range_Cert(cert.json):
  parse cert.json
  verify report_self_hash round-trips
  for each certified in certificates:
    if certified.proof is Failed:
      pass-through (failure is its own evidence)
    else:
      re-run verifies(certified.proof, certified.plan, certified.facts)
      assert it holds
```

This is the load-bearing claim of the whole F-B7 effort: a typed
certificate that can be independently re-checked from the JSON alone.

## Why
The 42-fix review Item 15 made each `CertifiedReduction` carry its own
`plan`, `facts`, and `proof` precisely so the cert is self-contained.
This bead is what proves the design works end-to-end: a separate crate
(gbf-verify) reads only the JSON file and reaches the same yes/no
verdict as Stage 5 did internally.

## Subtasks
- [ ] Implement `Independent_Verify_Range_Cert` in `gbf-verify`.
- [ ] Re-implement `verifies` predicate from RFC §9.6 (port from
      `gbf-codegen` types but DO NOT re-use the codegen impl —
      independence is the point).
- [ ] Re-implement `renorm_recurrence_verifies` (independent module).
- [ ] Round-trip property: codegen-side certificate → JSON →
      gbf-verify-side `verifies` → same yes/no as codegen-side.
- [ ] Fixtures for each plan family (SingleI16, ChunkedI16, RenormLoop
      non-BitExact only) and `Failed` variant.
- [ ] Negative fixture: a tampered cert JSON (e.g. lowered slack) must
      fail verification.

## Acceptance
- [ ] gbf-verify ↔ codegen agreement across all positive fixtures.
- [ ] Tampered fixtures are rejected.
- [ ] gbf-verify has zero dependency on `gbf-codegen` internals — only
      reads JSON and types from `gbf-policy` + shared report types.

## How this serves the project
The conformance story: the deployed ROM behaves like the trained model
because the build emits certificates that an independent verifier can
re-check. Without this verifier, the certificate is just a JSON blob; with
it, every build of every model is provably accumulator-safe.

## RFC anchors
§9.6 verifier predicate (closed match), §10.5 cert schema,
§17 end-to-end theorem item 11.

## History
- 42-fix Item 15: CertifiedReduction packs everything for independence
- 42-fix Item 40: theorem strengthened around range.cert.json
- 30-patch Patch 22: cert is the load-bearing PROOF artifact

## Blocked by
T-B7.F (range.cert.json emission must exist before verifier reads it).

  the codegen-side `verifies` and gbf-verify-side
  `independent_verify` reach the same yes/no.

title: F-S7 v0.2: LayerId & EPD-4 off-by-one (0..N-1 not 0..N)
description:
## Description

Fix off-by-one errors in §3.1 and §3.5. Pre-review LayerId was `u8 ; 0..n_blocks` but n_blocks=4 means valid layer ids are 0..3, not 0..4. Same for §3.5 EPD-4 `expert_id values exhaust 0..n_experts` — for n_experts=4, valid ids are 0..3. v0.2 makes both ranges `0..N-1` per the canonical inclusive-start, inclusive-end convention used in S1 NumberOfBlocks discussion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- §3.1 LayerId definition: `u8 ; 0..n_blocks-1`.
- §3.5 EPD-4 invariant: `expert_id values exhaust 0..n_experts-1 (no missing or duplicate)`.
- ModelTopologyConfig::from_profile validates that ffn_path_per_block has length n_blocks (the length itself is n_blocks; layer ids index it 0..n_blocks-1).
- ExpertPayloadDigest construction validates the n_experts-1 range.

## Notes

- These are textual conventions; the implementation likely already uses 0..N-1 conventions (Rust ranges are half-open by default). The fix protects against a deserialization-time off-by-one.

## RFC published: F-B2 + F-B4 paired RFC

The detailed design for this feature plus its sibling F-B2 lives at:

`history/rfcs/F-B2-F-B4-pipeline-entry-validation.md`

The RFC supersedes the design sketch in this bead's earlier comments. Highlights:

- F-B4 consumes a `QuantGraphBudgetSource` trait that yields a validated
  `QuantGraphBudgetView` (RFC §7.6). F-B3 implements the trait later. F-B4
  may ship and be tested with synthetic impls before F-B3 lands.
- Per-expert payload byte math is owned by F-B4, not trusted from the
  QuantGraph producer. Canonical formulas for Ternary2/Binary1/SparseTernaryBitplanes
  are in RFC §7.6.
- `static_budget.json` is a *necessary-condition* gate, not a final
  deployability proof (RFC §7.7 `StaticFitInterpretation`).
- Three deterministic placement models (`StrictOnePerBank`,
  `BudgetedFirstFit`, `PackedExpertsFirstFitDecreasing`) drive reproducible
  per-bank occupancy.
- Switch counts use `ProjectedSwitchCount { upper_bound, expected_q16_16,
  decision_value, source }`. Bringup/Default/Trace v1 use `upper_bound` for
  budget decisions.
- Missing `RuntimeChromeBudget` is a hard `BudgetMissingRuntimeChromeBudget`
  rejection with a special report shape (RFC §7.7, §7.9.5).
- No floats in v1 reports; fractional quantities use `_q8_8` / `_q16_16`.

Task graph: 14 tasks (T-B4.1 .. T-B4.13, including T-B4.8a). See bead labels
`f-b2-f-b4,chunk1` for the full set, or RFC §12 for the dependency-ordered list.

`bd-w80` (T3.4) byte math is absorbed into T-B4.2.

title: T-B5.14: ProvenanceBinding + AnchorBinding (DomainHash anchors with QG self-hash; total provenance maps)
description:
## What
Implement `ProvenanceBinding` (IIRClass 7) and `AnchorBinding`
(IIRClass 8): fill `g.provenance.{nodes, values, effects}` and
construct `NodeAnchorMap` with serialized `SemanticAnchor` ids.

## Why
ProvenanceBinding fills the three single-source-of-truth maps
(Ambiguity A74):
- `nodes`: every NodeId → typed `QuantGraphEntityRef` identifying
  which QG entity the node corresponds to (e.g.
  `ExpertSection { layer, expert }`,
  `NormPlan(norm_plan_id)`).
- `values`: every ValueId → `ValueProducerRef::{Node | External}`.
- `effects`: every EffectId → `EffectProvenance::{ExternalRoot |
  NodeOutput}`.

AnchorBinding constructs `NodeAnchorMap` with each anchor =
`DomainHash("gbf-codegen", "SemanticAnchor", "v1",
  CanonicalJson({ quant_graph_self_hash, node_id, op_tag,
                  canonical_provenance_tuple }))`. The anchors are
opaque from F-B5's perspective; F-B6 attaches checkpoints later
(Ambiguity A16).

The `canonical_provenance_tuple` (Ambiguity A72) includes
`(op_tag, layer?, expert?, slot?, norm_site?, state_slot?,
residual_site?, occurrence_index)` — the same key used for canonical
sort in T-B5.15.

## Inputs
- T-B5.13 (ReductionSiteBinding output).
- T-B5.7 (`InferIrProvenance` shape).
- T-B5.8 (`NodeAnchorMap`, `SemanticAnchor`).

## Outputs
- `fn bind_provenance(nodes, values, effects, qg) ->
  Result<InferIrProvenance, Vec<ValidationDiagnostic>>`.
- `fn bind_anchors(nodes, qg, qg_self_hash) ->
  Result<NodeAnchorMap, Vec<ValidationDiagnostic>>`.
- Diagnostic mapping: `InferIrSemanticAnchorMissing` when any node
  lacks an anchor.

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT inline provenance on `ValueDecl` / `EffectDecl` (Ambiguity
  A74).
- DO NOT compute the anchor id without `quant_graph_self_hash` in the
  tuple — anchors must distinguish across QGs.
- The `canonical_provenance_tuple` ordering must match the canonical
  sort key (T-B5.15) so anchors and node order are aligned.

## Acceptance
- `gbf-codegen::iir_provenance_binding_total_image`.
- `gbf-codegen::iir_anchor_binding_includes_qg_self_hash`.
- `gbf-codegen::iir_provenance_no_inline_on_value_or_effect_decl`.

## Refs
- RFC §9.3 (Classes 7-8), §2.12 (anchors are opaque ids), §13.3 (F-B6
  handshake), Proof obligations O5, O15, Ambiguity ledger: A16, A72,
  A74.
- Depends on: T-B5.13, T-B5.7, T-B5.8.
- Blocks: T-B5.15 (CanonicalSort).

title: F-S3.14: ExportVisitor → ModelArtifact (s3_export_model_artifact) + CanonicalArtifactWrite + tied alias preservation
description:
## Context

`s3_export_model_artifact` (RFC §7) consumes the FrozenStudent (step-10000 snapshot from B12) and runs the same `ExportVisitor` identity (B13) to produce a canonical `ModelArtifact`. The `CanonicalArtifactWrite` encoder (RFC §3) lives in gbf-artifact and is the only normative implementation of artifact canonical bytes.

`QuantSpec_S3::weight_quant` covers every Linear/Embedding/Classifier tensor in the canonical logical form; the Ternary2 reduction policy is the single pinned policy (RFC §3 + D7 Phase D bitwise rule). Tied embedding/classifier sharing is preserved with `classifier_view: SameTensor | TransposedView` (RFC §3 / Patch 28 round 2).

## Why this matters

The artifact is the input to the ArtifactOracle (B16) and the Phase-D side of the agreement gate (B17 / H4). Without B14, H4 Phase-D cannot be evaluated; H5 (artifact determinism) cannot be tested; H6 (QuantSpec resolution) has no canonical artifact to evaluate against; v0_success (B18) has no artifact to score val_bpc_ternary on; bd-3bf1's artifact-side contract is unverifiable.

## Deliverables

1. `gbf-artifact/src/canonical_artifact_write.rs`:
   - `pub fn canonical_artifact_bytes(artifact: &ModelArtifact) -> Vec<u8>`
   - Identical canonical-write rules to bundle (B13) but applied to ModelArtifact
   - ArtifactAux mutable sidecars excluded from artifact_self_hash; summarized by `canonical_aux_payload_sha` instead
   - Tied embedding alias written once with `classifier_view` metadata (never duplicated payload)
2. `gbf-train/src/export_visitor.rs` (extension; reuses ExportVisitor from B13):
   - `pub fn visit_for_artifact<M: HardTernaryStudentModel>(&self, frozen: &FrozenStudent<M>) -> ModelArtifact`
   - Emits `CanonicalTensor` per Linear/Embedding/Classifier with `payload_role: PayloadRole::DeployableWeight` or `DeployableQuantParam`
   - Honors tied alias with `classifier_view: SameTensor | TransposedView`
3. `gbf-experiments/src/s3/artifact.rs`:
   - `pub fn s3_export_model_artifact(ArtifactExportInputs) -> Result<ArtifactExportProduct, ArtifactExportError>` per RFC §7
   - Ae-Pre-1 (FrozenStudent at step 10000) through Ae-Ok-4 (tied alias preserved) preconditions/postconditions
   - `ArtifactValidationReport`:
     - QuantSpec coverage (every Linear/Embedding/Classifier resolved via QuantSpec::weight_quant; Ae-Ok-2)
     - Tied-embedding alias preserved (Ae-Ok-4)
     - Per-tensor weight_resolution_log entries
   - `artifact_deployable_bytes` derivation per RFC §9 third-round Patch:
     - Sum of byte_length of every tensor whose `payload_role ∈ { DeployableWeight, DeployableQuantParam }`
     - Plus canonical metadata bytes required to resolve those tensors through QuantSpec
     - ArtifactAux sidecars and ReferenceFp32 tensors EXCLUDED
4. `gbf-experiments/src/s3/schema.rs::s3_artifact.v1` (RFC §11.4) emitter, including the new `tied_embedding_alias` block in metadata (Patch 14 round 2)

## Test scaffolding

1. **`gbf-experiments/tests/artifact_determinism_s3.rs`** (O-3') — replay-pair byte equality for ALL 5 seeds:
   - For each seed s ∈ {0..4}: export the same FrozenStudent twice; canonical_artifact_payload_sha and artifact_self_hash byte-equal across replays
2. **`gbf-experiments/tests/artifact_tied_embedding_s3.rs`** (O-3''):
   - TiedEmbeddingAlias preserved on artifact; classifier_view round-trips for both `SameTensor` and `TransposedView`
3. **`gbf-experiments/tests/artifact_quantspec_resolution_s3.rs`** — every Linear/Embedding/Classifier tensor in the canonical logical form has a weight_quant entry; missing tensor → ArtifactExportError::QuantSpecCoverageMissing
4. **`gbf-experiments/tests/artifact_deployable_bytes_s3.rs`** — exact derivation:
   - Construct a fixture artifact with: 100 KB DeployableWeight + 10 KB DeployableQuantParam + 50 KB ArtifactAux sidecar + 200 KB ReferenceFp32
   - Assert artifact_deployable_bytes == 100 KB + 10 KB + (small metadata overhead)
   - Negative: add another 50 KB sidecar; assert artifact_deployable_bytes UNCHANGED
   - Negative: add 100 KB ReferenceFp32; assert artifact_deployable_bytes UNCHANGED
5. **`gbf-experiments/tests/artifact_canonical_snapshot_s3.rs`** — insta snapshot of canonical_artifact_payload_sha for a fixed Toy0 fixture
6. **`gbf-experiments/tests/artifact_no_naming_resolution_s3.rs`** — `weight_resolution_summary.tensors_resolved_via_naming == 0` invariant; F4-broken-S3 detector
7. **`scripts/s3_no_naming_resolution_check.sh`** (referenced from RFC §17.7):
   - Greps every emitted s3_artifact.v1 metadata file for `tensors_resolved_via_naming` and asserts value is 0
   - Fails CI if any artifact has non-zero naming resolution

## Logging discipline

`s3_export_model_artifact` emits structured events:
```
event_name = "s3::artifact_export::started"
fields: { seed, frozen_student_storage_fingerprint, export_visitor_hash, quant_spec_hash }

event_name = "s3::artifact_export::tensor_emitted"
level = "trace"
fields: { tensor_id, payload_role, byte_count, weight_quant_kind, alias_target: Option<CanonicalTensorId> }

event_name = "s3::artifact_export::quantspec_validated"
fields: { total_tensors, tensors_resolved_via_quant_spec, tensors_resolved_via_naming }

event_name = "s3::artifact_export::tied_alias_recorded"
fields: { embedding_canonical_id, classifier_canonical_id, shared, classifier_view }

event_name = "s3::artifact_export::complete"
fields: { seed, artifact_self_hash, canonical_artifact_payload_sha,
          artifact_deployable_bytes, tied_alias_present }

target = "gbf_experiments::s3::artifact"
```
Subscriber-level test `gbf-experiments/tests/artifact_export_logging_s3.rs` asserts events fire and `tensors_resolved_via_naming = 0` invariant.

## E2E acceptance script

`scripts/s3_artifact_export_smoke.sh`:
1. Trains a tiny ternary student through Phase D on the tiny corpus (uses B12 freeze_student path)
2. Runs `gbf s3 export-artifact --seed 0 --capture-events /tmp/s3-artifact.ndjson`
3. Asserts NDJSON contains every export event
4. Re-runs the export; diffs canonical_artifact_payload_sha (must be identical)
5. Asserts `weight_resolution_summary.tensors_resolved_via_naming == 0`
6. Runs `scripts/s3_no_naming_resolution_check.sh` against the produced metadata; passes

## Inheritance / non-duplication

- Reuses ExportVisitor from B13 (same export_visitor_hash for both bundle and artifact).
- Falsification F4-broken-S3 (B20) tests the QuantSpec bypass path; F6-broken-S3 tests tied alias split.

## Considerations

- The artifact's canonical logical graph (NOT a ReferenceProgram graph; that lives in the bundle) is what tied_embedding_alias references. Patch 29 (round 2 Ae-Ok-4) explicitly disambiguated this.
- `artifact_deployable_bytes` excludes ArtifactAux sidecars and non-deployable reference tensors; the chrome budget gate (Q6) compares against this, not against canonical_bytes (Patch 13 round 1).

## Acceptance

```
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d" --test artifact_determinism_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d" --test artifact_tied_embedding_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d" --test artifact_quantspec_resolution_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d" --test artifact_deployable_bytes_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test artifact_canonical_snapshot_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d" --test artifact_no_naming_resolution_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features "s3,s3-phase-d" --test artifact_export_logging_s3
scripts/s3_no_naming_resolution_check.sh
scripts/s3_artifact_export_smoke.sh
```

## Out of scope

- ArtifactOracle evaluation (B16)
- ArtifactDecoder for autoregressive generation (B16)
- s3_run_v0_success runner (B18)

## References

- RFC §3 "ArtifactCore / CanonicalArtifactWrite"; §7 "Artifact export contract"; §11.4
- bd-3bf1 (tied embedding sharing)

title: T10.8: Router and temporal smoothness tests (F7 coverage)
description:
Unit tests for router training features:

**Temporal smoothness boundary handling:**
- Sequence of 8 tokens, all routing to expert 0: verify L_switch = 0
- Sequence of 8 tokens, alternating expert 0 and 1: verify L_switch ≈ 1.0
- Two sequences in same batch (tokens [0-3] = seq A, [4-7] = seq B): verify no cross-sequence penalty
- First token of each sequence: verify no penalty (no previous token to compare against)
- Gradient: verify gradient flows through the router softmax for tokens 1+ but not token 0 of each sequence

**Expert dropout tests:**
- Set dropout rate 0.5, run forward 100 times: verify each expert is dropped ~50% of the time (within 3σ)
- Dropout rate 0.0: verify no experts dropped
- Dropout disabled at eval time: verify eval() forward never drops experts
- Gradient through dropped experts: verify gradient is zero for dropped, non-zero for active

**Low-rank factorization tests:**
- Full-rank router (d_model=8 -> n_experts=4): compute output
- Low-rank router (d_model=8 -> rank=2 -> n_experts=4): verify shape is correct
- Verify low-rank param count < full-rank param count
- Gradient flow: verify gradients reach both low-rank matrices

**Temporal switch digest collection:**
- Run model on tiny corpus, collect TemporalSwitchDigest
- Verify same_expert_rate is between 0 and 256 (Q8.8 format)
- Verify transition_mass entries sum to ≤ 256
- Verify n_layers digests are produced

All tests log: n_experts, routing distribution per token, switch rate, dropout mask when applicable.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p gbf-test -- router_tests passes; Temporal buffer handles boundaries; Dropout matches config; Low-rank matches full-rank within tolerance

title: T10.5: Model config and instantiation tests (F6 coverage)
description:
Unit tests for model architecture construction:

**Block structure tests:**
- Config with alternating(start=0, stride=2) on 4 layers: verify blocks 0,2 have MoE FFN, blocks 1,3 have shared dense FFN
- Config with middle(first=1, last=2) on 4 layers: verify blocks 1,2 have MoE, others don't
- Config with explicit([1,3]) on 4 layers: verify exactly blocks 1,3 have MoE
- All configs: verify sequence-state path is always shared (never MoE)

**Tied embedding tests:**
- Create model with tied=true: verify embed.weight and classifier.weight are the same Tensor object (not just equal values)
- Forward through embed then classify: verify gradient flows to both paths through a single weight
- Gradient test: compute loss, backward, verify embed.weight.grad is non-zero and reflects both embedding and classifier contributions
- Untied config: verify two separate weight tensors, different gradients

**Two-matrix expert structure tests:**
- Create ExpertBlockQat: verify it contains exactly up + down projections (no gate projection)
- Forward shape: input [batch, d_model] -> output [batch, d_model]
- GLU config with warning: verify GLU=true emits a log warning about bank fit

**Expert byte budget formula tests:**
- compute_expert_bytes(d_model=128, d_ff=224, Ternary2, PerOutputRow, Q8_8): verify = 15040 + metadata
- compute_expert_bytes must equal TernaryWeightPlan::compute_byte_cost(up) + compute_byte_cost(down) + metadata_bytes
- Cross-check: the two independent paths to computing byte cost must agree

All tests log: model config summary, block structure, parameter counts, byte costs.

title: F-S3.07: gbf-experiments::s3 module skeleton + S3BuildKind / S3Outcome / S3Decision / S3VerifierBundle / S3RngStreams / S3EnvironmentHash type taxonomy
description:
## Context

The `gbf-experiments::s3` module tree mirrors the landed F-S2 module shape (`s2/{schema, run, score, ablation, oracle_re_run, falsify, environment, rng, gap, verifiers, report, cli, manifest}`). B7 lays down the empty module skeleton + the S3-specific type taxonomy needed by every later S3 bead, **plus the shared test scaffolding** (`tests/common_s3/mod.rs`, `tests/common/proptest_strategies_s3.rs`) that F-S2 has and that S3's tests depend on.

Per RFC §3, S3 introduces `S3BuildKind`, `S3Outcome` (15 variants), `S3Decision`, `S3VerifierBundle` (mirrors S2VerifierBundle for §10 dispatch), `S3Hypothesis` (H1..H7), `S3Completion`, `OracleFallbackTag` (Vec instead of comma-encoded string per third-round Patch 9), and `S3EnvironmentHash` (extends S2EnvironmentHash with `oracle_backend_identity`).

S3RngStreams is declared as identical to S2RngStreams (no new RNG sub-stream domains; per RFC §3 + Rule InheritanceFromS2).

## Why this matters

These types are the structural backbone for §10 outcome dispatch (B21), §10.1 verifier bundle (B21), §17 build matrix (B24), s3_report.v1 emission (B21), and all artifact metadata `build_kind` tags (B14, B18, B19, B21). The shared test scaffolding is what enables every later bead's proptest / NDJSON capture / fixture-builder tests to be written without re-inventing helpers.

## Deliverables

### M7.A — Module skeleton
`gbf-experiments/src/s3/mod.rs`:
```
pub mod {schema, run, score, oracle_re_run, environment, rng, charset, baseline, bundle, artifact, oracle, conformance, falsify, report, cli, manifest, workload, preregistration};
static MODULE_LOADED: Once = Once::new();
pub fn ensure_module_loaded() { ... emit "s3::module_loaded" event ... }
pub const TYPE_COUNT: u64 = ...;
pub const SCHEMA_COUNT: u64 = ...;
pub const S3_LOG_TARGET: &str = "gbf_experiments::s3";
```

### M7.B — `gbf-experiments/src/s3/schema.rs` (S3 type taxonomy)
- `pub enum S3BuildKind { s3_v0_success_real_oracle, s3_v0_success_fallback_oracle, s3_oracle_adversarial }` with serde rename to kebab-case (mirrors `S2BuildKind` from `gbf-experiments/src/s2/schema.rs:354-367`)
- `pub enum S3Outcome` with all 15 variants from RFC §10 + serde rename (`Pass-clean`, `Pass-with-fallback-oracle`, `Fail-charset`, ..., `Fail-incomplete`); `pub const ALL: [Self; 15]`
- `pub enum S3Decision` (tagged enum; mirrors `S2Decision` shape):
   ```
   ProceedToS4 |
   "ProceedToS4-with-deferred-clause" |
   Investigate { reason: String } |
   Halt { reason: String }
   ```
- `pub enum S3Hypothesis { H1..H7 }` with `pub const ALL: [Self; 7]`
- `pub enum S3Completion { Completed, DivergedAt { step: GlobalStep }, NotReached }` (PascalCase tagged)
- `pub enum OracleFallbackTag { S3DenotationalFallback, S3ArtifactFallback }`
- `pub struct S3VerifierBundle` (RFC §10.1 fields) + `pub fn closure_candidate() -> Self` constructor (mirrors `S2VerifierBundle::closure_candidate` from `gbf-experiments/src/s2/schema.rs:2660-2676`)

### M7.C — `gbf-experiments/src/s3/environment.rs`
- `pub struct S3EnvironmentHash { build_config_hash, rust_toolchain_hash, dependency_lockfile_hash, oracle_backend_identity }` (mirrors `S2EnvironmentHash` from `gbf-experiments/src/s2/environment.rs:13-20`, adds `oracle_backend_identity: Hash256`)
- `pub fn compute_environment_hash() -> Result<S3EnvironmentHash, S1SchemaError>` (mirrors S2 cache pattern with OnceLock)
- `pub fn build_config_hash_for_features(active: Vec<&'static str>) -> Result<Hash256, _>` (mirrors S2)

### M7.D — `gbf-experiments/src/s3/rng.rs`
- Re-export `S2RngStreams` (`pub use crate::s2::rng::S2RngStreams as S3RngStreams`)
- `pub fn assert_no_new_rng_domains()` — runtime audit asserting no new domain tags beyond `{init, batch, shuffle, threshold_init}`; called from a unit test

### M7.E — Compile guards in `s3/mod.rs`
- `compile_error!` if both `s3-oracle-real` and `s3-oracle-fallback` enabled
- `compile_error!` if `falsify` enabled outside `cfg(test)`
- (NOTE: B2 already stubs these; B7 enriches the surrounding module body)

### M7.F — **Shared test scaffolding** (mirrors F-S2's `gbf-experiments/tests/common/`)
1. `gbf-experiments/tests/common_s3/mod.rs` — fixture builders (Toy0 model factory, FixedKnFixture, MockArtifact, NDJSON capture sink, tracing test subscriber, BuildKind matrix iterator).
2. `gbf-experiments/tests/common_s3/proptest_strategies_s3.rs` — proptest strategies for `S3BuildKind`, `S3Outcome`, `S3Decision`, `S3Completion`, `OracleFallbackTag`, `S3VerifierBundle`, `HardnessTriple`, `PhaseKindS2` (re-exported from S2 strategies where applicable).
3. `gbf-experiments/tests/common_mod_compiles_s3.rs` — re-affirms F-S2's compile-only test pattern, ensuring the common module compiles for every feature combo S3 supports.
4. `gbf-experiments/tests/common_mod_self_test_s3.rs` — self-tests for the helpers: NDJSON sink writes valid NDJSON, tracing subscriber captures expected events, etc.

## Test scaffolding (B7's own tests; not the shared layer)

1. **`gbf-experiments/tests/types_proptest_s3.rs`** — proptest for round-trip serde on `S3BuildKind`, `S3Outcome`, `S3Decision`, `S3Completion`, `OracleFallbackTag`, `S3VerifierBundle`. Asserts:
   - `S3Hypothesis::ALL.len() == 7`
   - `S3Outcome::ALL.len() == 15`
   - `S3BuildKind` round-trips via serde JSON
2. **`gbf-experiments/tests/canonical_json_s3.rs`** (initial slice — schema-bead-by-schema-bead growth) — round-trips `S3BuildKind` / `S3Outcome` / `S3Decision` / `S3VerifierBundle` through canonical JSON; mirrors `canonical_json_s2.rs`.
3. **`gbf-experiments/tests/env_hash_s3.rs`** — re-affirms `S3EnvironmentHash` is deterministic across 10 replays; the fields {build_config, rust_toolchain, dependency_lockfile, oracle_backend} change → hash changes (sensitivity test).
4. **`gbf-experiments/tests/rng_disjointness_s3.rs`** — asserts S3RngStreams ≡ S2RngStreams; assert_no_new_rng_domains() succeeds.
5. **`gbf-experiments/tests/inert_discipline_s3.rs`** — asserts B7's modules compile but emit no producer events without the `s3-phase-d` runtime feature (mirrors F-S2's inert discipline).
6. **`gbf-experiments/tests/module_loaded_logging_s3.rs`** — subscriber-level test asserting `s3::module_loaded` fires exactly once per process.

## Logging discipline

`ensure_module_loaded` event:
```
event_name = "s3::module_loaded"
fields: { schema_count, type_count, s3_enabled, s3_phase_d_enabled, s3_oracle_real_enabled, s3_oracle_fallback_enabled }
target = "gbf_experiments::s3"
```
The tracing test subscriber in common_s3 captures this for assertions across all later beads' integration tests.

## Inheritance / non-duplication

- DOES NOT introduce S3CanonicalJson; reuse S1CanonicalJson per RFC §3.
- DOES NOT redefine `S2RngStreams` — re-export it.
- DOES NOT redefine `Verdict` or `HypothesisStatus` — those come from F-S1 / F-S2 and are inherited.
- The shared test scaffolding is the F-S3 mirror of F-S2's `tests/common/`; do NOT duplicate F-S2 helpers — re-use them where applicable.

## Considerations

- The S3VerifierBundle mirrors S2VerifierBundle (`gbf-experiments/src/s2/schema.rs:2637-2658`) so the §10 outcome dispatcher in B21 can be implemented as a structurally identical `match` against the S3 type.
- F-S2 outcome variants use PascalCase + serde rename to kebab-case. S3 does the same.
- `oracle_backend_identity` enters S3EnvironmentHash because fallback-vs-real oracle changes observations, agreement reports, and conformance hashes (third-round Patch 30 / D8).

## Acceptance

```
cargo build -p gbf-experiments --features s3
cargo test  -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test types_proptest_s3
cargo test  -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test canonical_json_s3
cargo test  -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test env_hash_s3
cargo test  -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test rng_disjointness_s3
cargo test  -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test inert_discipline_s3
cargo test  -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test module_loaded_logging_s3
cargo test  -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test common_mod_compiles_s3
cargo test  -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test common_mod_self_test_s3
```

## Out of scope

- The dispatcher logic itself (B21).
- The actual verifier checks (every S3 bead contributes one `*_passed` field).
- Falsify module body (B20).

## References

- RFC §3 "S3BuildKind / S3Outcome / S3Decision / S3RngStreams / S3EnvironmentHash"; §10 "Outcome algebra"; §10.1 "S3VerifierBundle"
- F-S2 reference: `gbf-experiments/src/s2/schema.rs:354-367, 2540-2632`; `s2/environment.rs:13-20`; `s2/rng.rs:8-90`; `tests/common/mod.rs:1-419`

comments.text:
## T-A3.2: `InferenceState` + liveness counters

**Target crate**: `gbf-abi`
**Target file(s)**: `gbf-abi/src/continuation.rs`, `gbf-abi/src/liveness.rs`
**Reference**: `planv0.md` line 1795 (liveness contract), line 2507 (every slice participates in liveness).

### Background

`InferenceState` is the continuation record — the durable state that carries across yields. It lives in WRAM during a session and is checkpointed to SRAM at semantic checkpoints. The liveness counters (`progress_epoch`, `last_checkpoint`, `no_progress_frames`) are how the runtime detects livelock at the slice/checkpoint level.

### Implementation Notes

`liveness.rs`:

```rust
#[repr(C)]
pub struct LivenessCounters {
    pub progress_epoch: u32,                  // monotonic; bumped on each successful checkpoint
    pub last_checkpoint: SemanticCheckpointId,
    pub no_progress_frames: u16,              // number of UI frames with no checkpoint advance
    pub livelock_threshold_frames: u16,       // configurable threshold
}

impl LivenessCounters {
    pub fn record_progress(&mut self, cp: SemanticCheckpointId);
    pub fn note_idle_frame(&mut self);
    pub fn is_livelocked(&self) -> bool;
}

pub struct LivenessFault {
    pub at_checkpoint: SemanticCheckpointId,
    pub no_progress_frames: u16,
}
```

`continuation.rs`:

```rust
#[repr(C)]
pub struct InferenceState {
    pub abi: AbiVersion,
    pub schema: u16,                          // versioned per-build state schema
    pub session_id: u32,
    pub token_count: u32,
    pub slice_id: SliceId,
    pub liveness: LivenessCounters,
    pub last_fault: Option<FaultCode>,
    // followed by build-specific tail of sequence-state bytes; opaque here.
}
```

`InferenceState` is a *layout* exposed to the runtime; concrete shape (especially the build-specific tail) is decided per-build. Tests assert at-least invariants (size, alignment, field offsets) for the fixed prefix.

### Acceptance Criteria

```bash
cargo check -p gbf-abi
cargo test -p gbf-abi -- continuation::layout                  # InferenceState prefix is layout-stable
cargo test -p gbf-abi -- liveness::livelock_threshold          # Threshold check fires correctly
cargo test -p gbf-abi -- liveness::progress_advance             # record_progress bumps epoch and resets idle frames
```

### Constitution Checkpoints

- §I.1: Liveness is a typed counter, not a comment.
- §VI.1: Single InferenceState type.

comments.text:
## F-A5: Bank0 Cooperative Runtime Skeleton

### Background

Per `planv0.md` line 1626, `gbf-runtime` is authored as Rust builders over `AsmIR`. This feature implements the Bank0 nucleus modules: boot, interrupts, scheduler, joypad, text, keyboard, video_commit, panic. These are exactly the modules the **pinned reference shell** (T2.4 `bd-37r`) commits to: `{Boot, Interrupts, Scheduler, Banking, Joypad, Text, Keyboard, VideoCommit}`, the minimal+UI set.

Persistence, trace, harness — the runtime modules NOT in the reference shell — are deferred to Epic D.

### How this serves overarching project goals

- Bank 0 is 16 KiB and contains the scheduler, ISRs, and UI. The model's compiled inference program runs *cooperatively alongside* this nucleus — it does not own the CPU.
- `runtime_nucleus_hash` is computed over the encoded Bank 0 nucleus + `CompileProfile` + version stamp. Models trained against a synthetic budget pin against this hash; CI catches drift (T2.5 `bd-177`).
- The `RuntimeChromeBudget` (F2 / `bd-1hv`) is *emitted from this feature's compiled output*. Sizing F-A5 within Bank 0 budget is the load-bearing constraint.

### The problem this solves

Without F-A5:
- Nothing boots. The compiler has no nucleus to schedule against.
- Cooperative yielding has no `yield_requested` flag location, no TIMA arming, no scheduler return path.
- The model has no way to render a single character of output.
- The pinned-reference-shell concept is vacuous — there's no shell.

### Design

Module-level layout:

```
gbf-runtime/src/
  boot.rs          # cartridge header, boot-time IRQ vector wiring, init sequence
  interrupts.rs    # IRQ dispatch table, ISR entry points, IF acknowledgement
  scheduler.rs     # cooperative scheduler, TIMA-armed deadline, HRAM yield_requested
  joypad.rs        # button-state polling
  text.rs          # font + glyph blitting + scrollback
  keyboard.rs      # on-screen keyboard layout + chord input
  video_commit.rs  # UiCommitPlan + commit queue + LCD-mode-gated stages
  panic.rs         # panic screen + fault-code dump
```

### Cooperative-yield mechanism (planv0.md line 1790)

> The compiler inserts safe points; the runtime may arm a soft deadline using TIMA, and the timer ISR sets a `yield_requested` flag in HRAM. Generated code polls that flag only at declared safe points.

So:
1. Scheduler arms TIMA before dispatching an inference slice.
2. TIMA ISR (in `interrupts.rs`) sets `yield_requested = 1` in HRAM.
3. Inference code polls that flag at every safe point (instruction emitted by the compiler, inside `Yield` pseudo-op handling).
4. On observed yield: save continuation, return to scheduler.

### Bank 0 budget realism

Bank 0 has 16384 bytes. The reference shell modules must fit within that budget MINUS the slack reserved for future modules (Persistence, Trace, Harness, Panic — ROM bytes per `T2.4`'s `FutureReservation` table). The bring-up estimate is ~8 KiB for the minimal+UI nucleus, leaving ~8 KiB for compiled "Bank0Free" use (expert hot kernels, etc.). If F-A5 lands above 8 KiB:
- First, audit text/font for size (fonts are typically the biggest contributor).
- Second, consider moving font/glyph data to a CommonBank (relocates UI bytes out of Bank 0).
- Third, only then revisit reserved_slack.

### Children (T-A5.1 ... T-A5.7)

1. **T-A5.1** Boot + IRQ vector dispatch.
2. **T-A5.2** Cooperative scheduler with TIMA + yield_requested HRAM flag.
3. **T-A5.3** Joypad reader.
4. **T-A5.4** Text renderer + font.
5. **T-A5.5** Keyboard input + layout.
6. **T-A5.6** `video_commit` + `UiCommitPlan`.
7. **T-A5.7** Panic screen.

### Dependencies on other Epic A features

- F-A1: every F-A5 module emits AsmIR.
- F-A2: hardware constants for IRQ vectors, LCD modes, joypad register, etc.
- F-A3: `InterruptPolicy`, `FaultCode`, `SemanticCheckpointId` (ISR/panic flow).
- F-A4: `BankLease` is required for any cross-bank far-call from the runtime.

### Confidence: MEDIUM

Cooperative runtime sizing is the real risk. We can absorb a 30% overshoot of Bank 0 budget in v1 (by relocating glyph data to a CommonBank), but a 2× overshoot would force feature reductions or a second pass on text/keyboard.

## Agent Instructions (Feature)

**This is a feature bead.** Implement via child tasks T-A5.1–T-A5.7.

### Feature Definition of Done

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-runtime                                              # All module tests pass
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- scheduler::yield_round_trip               # Inference slice yields, scheduler returns
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- video_commit::lcd_mode_gating             # No VRAM/OAM commit outside legal LCD modes
cargo run -p gbf-cli -- demo-bank0-rom                                 # Boots in SameBoy/BGB; renders text + keyboard
# Bank 0 size assertion (set as an explicit test):
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- nucleus_fits_bank0_budget                 # Encoded nucleus + slack <= 16384
```

## RFC F-A5 alignment - 2026-05-03

Source of truth: history/rfcs/F-A5-bank0-runtime.md. This comment supersedes earlier bead text wherever it conflicts with that RFC.

Key corrections:
- F-A5 ships as one PR that closes T-A5.1 through T-A5.7 plus the small upstream additions in RFC section 1.1.x.
- Banking is F-A4-owned and already shipped; F-A5 consumes only lower_banking_shadow_zero_init, HRAM banking-shadow constants, and InterruptSafetyTable helpers. F-A5 emits no MBC register writes and performs no cross-bank far-calls.
- runtime_nucleus_hash is over the normalized Bank0 image with BuildIdentityBlock hash fields zeroed plus the runtime ABI version. CompileProfile identity is explicitly excluded.
- RuntimeShellModule lives in gbf-abi, not gbf-policy, and every build_*_section function emits a typed annotation.
- The reference shell is Boot, Interrupts, Scheduler, Banking, Joypad, Text, Keyboard, VideoCommit. Panic ships as an M0 audited bring-up exception; persistence, trace, and harness remain Epic D.
- Current budget expectation is approximately 4.7 KiB for F-A5 modules plus 1.4 KiB future reservations, not the older 8 KiB estimate. The hard gate remains 16 KiB minus FutureReservation ROM bytes.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## T-B1.3: L2 — Cross-bank operands via BankLease (N = 64)

### Background

L2 puts F-A4's BankLease ABI under real cross-bank load. A is in ROM bank P, B is in ROM bank Q (P ≠ Q, both nonzero). The matmul kernel is in Bank 0, the multiply table is in Bank 0; each panel copy must lease, copy, release. Generated code may not write MBC registers directly.

### Why N = 64 (not yet 128)

N = 64 lets us exercise the cross-bank pattern without yet committing to the full N = 128 tile schedule. If F-A4 has a bug, it surfaces here at small size first; we're not paying full N = 128 wall-clock for every iteration.

### What L2 proves

- `BringupRomWindowPlan` validates: kernel + table are `PermanentBank0`; A and B are `SwitchableRom` with distinct nonzero banks.
- The codegen lowering inserts BankLease/BankGuard around every panel copy.
- Generated compute sections contain no raw MBC writes — only the audited runtime banking implementation does.
- Lease acquire/release balance is zero over the whole run.
- **No yield occurs while a BankLease is active.** This is the load-bearing safety invariant added during the design pass: yielding under a lease lets the scheduler/ISR observe ambiguous ROMX state.
- Bank0 used/free byte count is reported (catches "kernel too large for Bank 0" early).

### Failure mode it isolates

F-A4's BankLease ABI under realistic compute pressure. L1 ran without F-A4; L2 is F-A4's first real consumer.

### Subtask plan

- **T-B1.3.1** `BringupRomWindowPlan` + `RomResidency` enum + Bank0 used/free byte reporting.
- **T-B1.3.2** BankLease/BankGuard integration in matmul lowering (depends on F-A4).
- **T-B1.3.3** No-raw-MBC-writes static checker (codegen-side).
- **T-B1.3.4** No-yield-while-banklease-active invariant + checker (codegen + runtime trace).
- **T-B1.3.5** BankLease balance tracking (acquire == release; max active leases recorded).
- **T-B1.3.6** L2 emulator test (N=64, cross-bank, byte-exact).

### Acceptance gates

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- f_b1_rom_window_plan_distinct_banks
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- f_b1_l2_lowering_uses_banklease_ops
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- f_b1_l2_generated_code_has_no_raw_mbc_writes
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- f_b1_l2_banklease_balance
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- f_b1_l2_no_yield_while_banklease_active
cargo test -p gbf-emu -- f_b1_l2_cross_bank_matmul_matches_reference
```

### RFC reference

`history/rfcs/F-B1-compute-bringup.md` §7.5, §8.3.

### Dependencies

- T-B1.2 (L1) — codegen path is now real.
- **F-A4** (BankLease/BankGuard ABI) — hard external dependency.

title: Add RuntimeNucleusHash union type (sha256 | SYNTHETIC_REFERENCE-tagged)
description:
# Goal

Define a schema-level type that admits both real and synthetic chrome nucleus hashes so D10 (synthetic-vs-real sentinel) and RV-3 (BlockExport on synthetic-vs-real mismatch) can actually be expressed.

# Background / Why

D10 mandates synthetic runtime-chrome reports tag their nucleus hash with the prefix \`SYNTHETIC_REFERENCE:\` (e.g. \`SYNTHETIC_REFERENCE:sha256:<hex>\`). However the RuntimeChromeBudget struct typed the field as Hash256 whose regex (\`^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$\`) rejects that prefix. The schema was internally inconsistent: the sentinel D10 required could not be serialized into the type that carried it.

# Change

In gbf-policy + gbf-artifact:

  - Add type:
      RuntimeNucleusHash := Hash256 | /^SYNTHETIC_REFERENCE:sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$/
  - Replace \`runtime_nucleus_hash: Hash256\` with \`RuntimeNucleusHash\` in RuntimeChromeBudget and any consumer struct.
  - Implement validation that rejects malformed strings (must match either branch exactly).
  - Update D10 fixture / regen scripts so the synthetic chrome budgets actually carry the prefix.

# Why this matters / Risk if unfixed

The D9-vs-D10 distinction (real chrome budget vs synthetic reference) is load-bearing for re-validation: see RV-3 (BlockExport on synthetic-vs-real mismatch). Without the tagged form, every chrome budget looks real to the validator, and the synthetic flag is implicit / fragile.

# Considerations

  - Equality semantics: synthetic == real is always BlockExport at the RV layer; do not relax to Warn.
  - Print/debug should show the prefix so log scrapers (\`grep SYNTHETIC_REFERENCE\`) work per A21.
  - Migration: D10 fixture currently encodes synthetic by some other convention; replace with the prefix.

# Verification

  - Round-trip golden for both branches.
  - Negative tests: \`SYNTHETIC_REFERENCE:foo\`, missing prefix, double prefix all reject.
  - D10 fixture round-trips and the resulting RV report dispatches BlockExport.

# Related RFC sections

  §1 (RuntimeNucleusHash, RuntimeChromeBudget), §D10, §D18, RV-3, §A21.

# Blocks

  B20 (RV-3 closure) depends on this type existing.
close_reason: Completed RuntimeNucleusHash union type and threaded RuntimeChromeBudget consumers/fixtures. Gemini and Claude ACPX reviews PASS; focused budget/runtime chrome tests passed.

title: F-S7 v0.2 T6.2: Internal teacher-freeze state machine per (topology, seed)
description:
## Goal

Implement the s7_train_run state machine such that T3/T4 (MoE/dense train) transition from BaselineMatched directly (not from a separate TeacherFrozen state); the teacher freeze is an INTERNAL boundary inside each run at Phase A's end, producing a per-(topology, seed) teacher_checkpoint_sha.

## Background

Pre-review §5 had T2 freeze teachers BEFORE T3/T4 trained, but D4 said each s7_train_run contains Phase A (DenseTeacherWarmup) internally. That reads like Phase A runs twice (or outside the run). Pre-review also had dense_teacher_checkpoint_per_topology[2] — not per-seed, while everything else in S7 is per-seed.

v0.2 inlines the freeze: Phase A runs inside each s7_train_run; at the Phase A boundary the teacher checkpoint for that (topology, seed) is frozen; Phases C/D/E distill against the SAME (topology, seed) teacher. No cross-seed teacher sharing — the matched-bytes parity is a TOPOLOGY parity, not a teacher parity. The dense student MUST distill from a dense teacher of the same topology so the comparison is over architectural choice alone, not teacher-quality differential (A20 in §20 ambiguity ledger).

## Files

- gbf-experiments/src/s7/run.rs (s7_train_run state machine; internal freeze boundary)
- gbf-experiments/src/s7/state.rs (TrainAttempted, TeacherFrozen states scoped per-(topology, seed))
- gbf-experiments/tests/teacher_freeze_per_seed.rs (replay (MoE, seed=0) twice → byte-identical teacher; (MoE, seed=0) ≠ (MoE, seed=1) teacher)

## Acceptance

- s7_train_run produces a deterministic per-(topology, seed) teacher_checkpoint_sha.
- (MoE, seed=0) and (MoE, seed=1) produce distinct teacher checkpoints.
- (MoE, seed=0) and (Dense, seed=0) produce distinct teacher checkpoints (different topology).
- The run logs Phase A's teacher freeze as an explicit boundary event under structured tracing.
- F2-bytes-unscaled remains compatible — the dense teacher still exists; only d_ff_dense is wrong.

## Reasoning chain

T6.2 unblocks T2.3 (DistillRawDiagnostic::NotAvailable in Phase A — before the freeze; Value after the freeze) and T2.1 (gradient provenance assertions assume a frozen teacher exists for distill_loss).
notes:
## Test Plan & Logging (AGENTS.md addendum)

### Unit tests (gbf-experiments/tests/teacher_freeze_per_seed.rs)

- teacher_freeze_internal_to_run: a single s7_train_run produces the teacher_checkpoint_sha at the Phase A boundary; the sha is exposed via the run's TrainAttempted state.
- teacher_freeze_same_topology_same_seed_deterministic: replay (MoE, seed=0) twice → byte-identical teacher_checkpoint_sha.
- teacher_freeze_seed_isolation: (MoE, seed=0) and (MoE, seed=1) produce DISTINCT teacher_checkpoint_sha (proves no global mutable teacher state).
- teacher_freeze_topology_isolation: (MoE, seed=0) and (Dense, seed=0) produce DISTINCT teacher_checkpoint_sha (proves the matched-bytes parity is a topology parity, not a teacher parity; per A20).
- teacher_freeze_cross_seed_no_share: enabling a 'cross-seed teacher share' code path is rejected at construction (this is a falsification probe similar to F1-router-top-k-ge-2 — wrong configurations must not compile clean).
- teacher_freeze_distill_phase_c_uses_frozen: in Phase C, the distillation forward consumes the SAME teacher_checkpoint_sha that was frozen at Phase A end of the same (topology, seed) run.

### Cross-cutting hook to T4.4 (Determinism)

- The teacher_checkpoint_sha is one of the determinism axes (D-A in T4.4); a non-deterministic teacher freeze cascades into every downstream artifact and fails Rep-S7-1. T6.2's tests are a *necessary* condition; T4.4's full-pipeline replay is the *sufficient* condition.

### Logging
