  `PolicyProvenance`, `ConstraintProvenance`, `ConstraintOperation`,
  `MonotoneKnob` trait.

- **This task (T-B16.1)** is recast as: extend `CompileKnobs` with any
  refinement-only fields F-B16 needs that don't fit the M1 surface (e.g. any
  `KnobDelta`-adjacent state or oracle-driven extensions discovered when the
  oracle question for bd-3ix resolves). Pure-schema responsibilities have moved.

If the F-B16 oracle resolution turns out to need no additional schema fields
beyond what T-B2.0 ships, this task may close as a no-op when F-B16 unblocks.

title: F-S2.21: Reproducibility hash surface + determinism / isolation / api-drift / distill-determinism CI scripts

Goal
====
Implement (a) the strict reproducibility hash surface — build_config_hash,
rust_toolchain_hash, dependency lockfile hash, and (b) the CI shell
script set under scripts/: s2_determinism_check.sh (O2),

+ §13 O2 / O8 / O9 / O11 / O12 + §16.9.

Why this matters
================
Reproducibility is the foundational claim of S2. Round 2 review added
build_config_hash + rust_toolchain_hash + lockfile_hash to O8 hidden
inputs.

Scope
=====

CI shell scripts (scripts/) — all use bash strict mode, exit 0 on pass /

# Goal

These do not change behavior but they confuse careful readers and reviewer-persona harnesses that follow internal references.

In the RFC text (already patched) and in any code-level docstrings or invariant names that cite these references:

  - §D8: \"the H15 emulator one-token agreement check\" (was H14).

Track any new cross-reference issues uncovered during implementation of the other 23 beads and add them here as comments.

# Why this matters

Cross-reference accuracy is part of the RFC's reviewability surface. Persona P6 (RFC Scope Sentinel) checks numbering coherence; persona P5 (Proof-of-Work Detective) relies on cross-references when verifying claim-to-gate matrices.

# Considerations

  - Low-risk; one-line edits.

# Verification

  - grep for H14 in D8 context returns no hits in the RFC.
  - grep for D12/D14 in S5CanonicalJson context returns no hits.
  - Persona P6 review notes no remaining cross-reference issues.

title: F-S1.17: Ablation comparator + s1_ablation.v1 (H4 seed-0 normative)
description: Implement seed-0 ablation comparator + s1_ablation.v1 emitter per F-S1 §3 H4+§9.5+§13 O4+I-S1-4. comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Why this bead exists

H4's verdict (§3): for seed 0, phase A's canonical_tensor_payload_sha must
equal the ablation build's canonical_tensor_payload_sha. If not, "Phase A
is contaminated by later-phase code. This is a Phase contract bug, not a
numerical issue. Block S2 until F4's phase scheduler is fixed."

This is the *seed-0-only* normative comparison. A23: closure requires only
seed 0; other seeds are informational.

## Scope

- `s1::ablation::compare(phase_a_ckpt, ablation_ckpt) -> AblationReport`:
    1. Load both checkpoints (each via the SafeTensors reader).
    2. Verify both have build_kind tags matching their build (S1-build-A and
       S1-build-B per §16) — the metadata sidecar carries this.
    3. Extract trainable tensors as `CanonicalTensor[]` (using F-S1.06's
       type) — strip optimizer state, strip loss-history sidecars.
    4. Compute canonical_tensor_payload_sha for each.
    5. phase_a_eq_ablation = (sha_phase_a == sha_ablation)
    6. If false: produce `first_mismatch = { tensor: name, byte_offset: u64 }`
       by scanning sorted-tensor sequence for the first divergence.
    7. Emit s1_ablation.v1 (§9.5) with all fields including
       phase_a_checkpoint_sha, ablation_checkpoint_sha,
       phase_a_tensor_payload_sha, ablation_tensor_payload_sha,
       phase_a_eq_ablation, first_mismatch, ablation_self_hash.

## Considerations

- I-S1-4: the ablation checkpoint MUST use the same seed, train_config_hash,
  corpus_*_sha, model_config_hash, device_profile, and rng stream
  definitions as the phase_a checkpoint. Only the QAT codepaths differ.
  Surface this as preflight asserts on the metadata sidecars.
- Whole-file safetensors byte equality is reported separately if the writer
  is canonicalized (F-S1.14). The H4 decision is on tensor payloads, not
  whole-file bytes — H4 is about phase contamination, not container
  metadata bugs.
- A7: NO ulp tolerance. Phase A is a no-op claim; any drift is a contract
  violation.
- A23: seeds 1..4 may be reported optionally; a follow-up bead can extend
  the suite if S2 needs more confidence.

## RFC anchors

- §3 H4 Phase A cleanliness
- §9.5 s1_ablation.v1
- §13 O4 Ablation match
- §1 CanonicalTensorPayloadHash
- I-S1-4
- A7, A23

### Implementation Notes
- Canonical expert byte formula for the default two-matrix Ternary2 PerOutputRow Q8_8 expert:
```rust
pub fn compute_expert_bytes(plan: &TernaryWeightPlan, d_model: u32, d_ff: u32) -> ByteCost {
    let up = plan.compute_byte_cost(d_model, d_ff);   // d_model -> d_ff
    let down = plan.compute_byte_cost(d_ff, d_model);  // d_ff -> d_model
    up + down  // plus any metadata overhead
}
```
- Must be **consistent** with `TernaryWeightPlan::compute_byte_cost()` — uses it, doesn't reimplement it.
- Include metadata overhead estimate (tile headers, alignment padding).
- This function is used by both the trainer (preflight) and compiler (StaticBudgetReport).

```bash
cargo check -p gbf-model                          # Compiles
cargo test -p gbf-model -- budget                  # Tests pass

#   down: ceil(512*256/4) + 512*2 = 32768 + 1024 = 33792 bytes

```

comments.text:
## F-E5: Cycle-model drift reports

### What this is

Compare `gbf-asm` static cycle model predictions to measured kernel runs; emit drift reports per kernel. When drift exceeds threshold, the cycle model needs revision.

### Why this matters

The static cycle model (T-A1.5) is the load-bearing input for every cost estimate. Drift goes silent unless we test for it.

### Design sketch

```rust
pub struct CycleModelDriftReport {
    pub kernel: KernelSpecId,
    pub configuration: KernelConfigKey,
    pub predicted_cycles: u32,
    pub measured_cycles_p50: u32,
    pub drift_pct: f32,
    pub samples: u32,
}
```

### Cross-feature deps

- F-A1.5 cycle model
- F-E3 KernelCalibrationBundle

### Confidence: HIGH

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Why this bead exists

F-S1.27 (the integration smoke test) was previously responsible for both
authoring a tiny fixture corpus AND running tests against it. Those are
two distinct deliverables: the corpus is a static asset; the test is
what consumes it.

Splitting the corpus authoring out:
  - clarifies ownership (corpus is data, test is code)
  - lets F-S1.36 (e2e harness) reuse the same fixture without taking
    on F-S1.27's gating semantics
  - lets the corpus be regenerated deterministically if its sha256 ever
    has to change (e.g., a future RFC alteration)

## Scope

- Path layout:
    gbf-experiments/tests/fixtures/tiny_corpus/
      train.bytes               (~16 KiB)
      val.bytes                 ( ~4 KiB)
      manifest.toml             (mirrors fixtures/corpora/tinystories.toml
                                  fields, but for the tiny corpus)
      generation_recipe.md      (human-readable doc of how it was made)

- Generation script:
    scripts/s1_generate_tiny_fixture.sh
      Inputs: a fixed master_seed (default 0xC0FFEE) and
              total byte counts (16384 + 4096).
      Algorithm: deterministic byte stream produced by:
        1. seed an InitRng(master_seed)  (F-S1.03 primitive)
        2. for each byte: draw uniform_u64_inclusive(rng, 0, 255) → u8
        Exception: ensure the byte stream contains at least
        one occurrence of the literal `<|endoftext|>` separator
        (D5-style) at a known offset, so tests can exercise that
        path without TinyStories.
      Outputs: train.bytes + val.bytes + manifest.toml with
        train_sha256, val_sha256, val_shuffle_deadeef_sha256
        computed and pinned.
      The script is idempotent: re-running with the same master_seed
      reproduces byte-identical files.

- Manifest fields (TOML; mirror §1 TinyStoriesManifest where
  applicable):
    schema           = "tinystories_manifest.v1"
    source_name      = "synthetic-tiny-fixture"
    decompression    = "none"
    raw_byte_policy  = "post-decompression bytes; no normalization"
    train_path       = "train.bytes"
    val_path         = "val.bytes"
    train_byte_length = 16384
    val_byte_length   =  4096
    train_sha256     = sha256:...    (pinned)
    val_sha256       = sha256:...    (pinned)
    val_shuffle_deadeef_sha256 = sha256:...   (pinned via F-S1.15)

- The script is checked in alongside the generated bytes; CI runs it
  as a sanity check and asserts the regeneration matches the pinned
  bytes (catches accidental edits to the script or RNG primitives).

## Considerations

- KEEP THE FIXTURE TINY. ~20 KiB total. The whole point is fast
  iteration in PR CI.
- Re-pinning the fixture (e.g., after F-S1.03 RNG primitives ever
  change) requires explicit acknowledgement: bump a fixture_version
  field in the tiny manifest and update consuming tests.
- This fixture is also used by the falsification suite (F-S1.24)
  and the e2e harness (F-S1.36). Don't make it specific to one
  consumer.

## Testing

- Regeneration test: scripts/s1_generate_tiny_fixture.sh produces
  byte-identical output across two invocations.
- sha256 verification test: gbf-data manifest reader (F-S1.08)
  loads the tiny manifest and confirms sha256s match the on-disk files.
- Multiset test: `<|endoftext|>` separator is present at the
  documented offset.
- Shuffle pin test: applying F-S1.15 Fisher-Yates with
  ShuffleRng(0xDEADBEEF) reproduces the pinned val_shuffle_deadeef_sha256.

## Logging

- Generation script logs (via F-S1.30 if invoked from Rust; bash
  echoes otherwise): byte counts, sha256s, generation duration.

## RFC anchors

- §1 TinyStoriesManifest (mirrored shape)
- §15.2 Test layout (integration row)
- D5 raw byte policy
- D7 O-metric-4 (val_shuffle_deadeef_sha256 pin generalization)

title: F-B12: ArenaPlan (Stage 9)
description:
# F-B12 — ArenaPlan (Stage 9 of the 14-stage compiler pipeline)

**Source RFC:** `history/rfcs/F-B11-F-B12-overlay-arena-plans.md` (paired RFC with F-B11).

## Why this stage exists

After F-B8 decides *what* is materialized, after F-B9 binds *which page* persistent values live on, after F-B10 binds *which bank* code lives in, and after F-B11 *reserves* WRAM bytes for overlays — every materialized value still has no concrete address. F-B12 is the byte-range allocator: it assigns one closed-enum `NamedArena` family + a `ByteRange { start, len }` to every `Materialize` binding and every `Persist` page pair. It is the FIRST stage where addresses become concrete, and the LAST stage before scheduling (F-B13) starts referencing those addresses as `ArenaSlot` ids.

The reservation handshake with F-B11 is the load-bearing safety boundary: arenas reserve overlay bytes EXACTLY (no over-reserve, no under-reserve, no overlap). The "named arena" enum is the public contract that F-C3 ScheduleOracle binds emulator harness state against.

## Pipeline context

**Upstream inputs (pinned into K12 cache key):**
- F-B8 `StoragePlan` — `StorageBinding { value, materialization, alias_class }` for all values; LifetimeClass preserved verbatim; AliasClassId defines slot-sharing equivalence.
- F-B9 `SramPagePlan` — persistent pages with `(PersistPageId, CommitGroupId, SequenceStreamId, payload_bytes)` and `PersistentPageGeometry`.
- F-B10 `RomWindowPlan` — by hash only (audit).
- F-B11 `OverlayPlan` — **critical**: regions[*].bytes, regions[*].constraint, reservation total + per-region.
- `ResolvedCompilePolicy` projected to `ArenaPlanPolicyProjection { arena_alignment_default, arena_zerofill_policy, persistent_page_geometry }`.
- `RuntimeChromeBudget` — bank0_wram_bytes, hram_usable_bytes.
- `TargetProfileSummary` — WRAM/SRAM/HRAM memory map.

**Downstream consumers:**
- F-B13 GbSchedIR — `live_wram` / `live_sram` are `Vec<ArenaSlotRef>`; never invents slots.
- F-B14 — implicit arena access cost.
- F-B15 Backend — emits sections matching arena byte ranges; symbols resolve to ArenaSlot offsets.
- F-C3 ScheduleOracle — binds emulator state to named arenas.
- Epic D Runtime — persistence producer/consumer reads persistent page byte map.

## Core data types (closed v1 surface)

- **NamedArena** (closed enum) — WRAM: `WramActivationsPingA`, `WramActivationsPingB`, `WramAccumScratch`, `WramRouteScratch`, `WramDecodeScratch`, `WramContinuationRecord`, `WramOverlayRegion(OverlayId)`. SRAM: `SramSequenceStatePages(SequenceStreamId)`, `SramTracePages`, `SramHarnessCommandBlock`, `SramHarnessResultBlock`, `SramPersistedTranscript`, `SramColdSpill`. HRAM: `HramFrameFlags`, `HramBankShadow`, `HramFaultCode`, `HramSchedulerScratch`, `HramYieldRequested`. New variants require RFC amendment.
- **ArenaId**, **ByteRange { start: u16, len: u16 }**.
- **ArenaInstance** — `{ id, named, byte_range, backing: WRAM|SRAM|HRAM, alignment, zerofill, slots: SortedVec<ArenaSlot> }`.
- **ArenaSlot** — `{ id, byte_offset, size_bytes, alias_class_id, lifetime_class, binding_kind, binding_ref }`.
- **SlotBindingKind** — `MaterializedValue | PersistentPageA(page,cg) | PersistentPageB(page,cg) | OverlayMember(OverlayId, OverlayResidentId) | RuntimeFixed(RuntimeFixedKind) | TraceRing(TraceRingId)`.
- **ArenaBindings** — `{ materialize_to_slot, persist_to_slot_pair, overlay_to_arena }` (three maps).
- **OverlayReservationHonor** — proof: `{ total_bytes == OverlayPlan.reservation.total_bytes, per_region with exact byte_range }`.
- **ArenaPlan** — product: `{ identity, wram_arenas, sram_arenas, hram_assignments, overlay_reservation, arena_bindings }`.

## Algorithm sketch

1. **arena_for(StorageBinding) → NamedArena family** — closed mapping from `(StorageClass, LifetimeClass)` to allowed arena family. Unmapped classes are hard rejects.
2. **honor_overlay_reservation(op, wram_arenas)** — for each region: allocate WRAM arena of size = region.bytes; mint one ArenaSlot per member at byte_offset 0 (time-sharing overwrite); check byte_range.len exact match; check disjointness from non-overlay WRAM.
3. **Allocate persistent pages** — for each `(page, commit_group)` in SramPagePlan: compute page_size = header + payload + commit_word; allocate two slots (slot_a, slot_b) in `SramSequenceStatePages(stream_id)`; same alias_class_id for both; different byte_offsets (double-buffering).
4. **FFD allocation for non-overlay arenas** — initialize free intervals; collect slots; canonical sort by (descending size, ascending alias_class, ascending lifetime priority, ascending binding_kind discriminant, ascending binding_ref); for each slot pick first free interval with `iv.len ≥ round_up(size, alignment)`; verify MustOverlap alias classes get same offset+size.
5. **Validate F-Addr-1..14 address invariants**.

**Non-obvious decisions:**
- **FFD determinism**: closed sort key + sorted-vec bookkeeping (never hashmaps). Two builds produce identical byte_offsets.
- **Overlay members at offset 0**: time-sharing overwrites the same WRAM bytes.
- **Persistent-page A/B NOT in MustOverlap**: same arena, different offsets; runtime tracks active via commit-group manifest.
- **Recompute bindings get no slot** — pure expressions have no materialized state (AP-SC-3, AP-SC-21).

## Invariants (AP-SC-1..25)

AP-SC-1 Materialize coverage. AP-SC-2 Persist coverage. AP-SC-3 Recompute non-allocation. AP-SC-4 Pure expression non-allocation. AP-SC-5 AliasClass equality on shared slot. AP-SC-6 AliasClass inequality forces disjointness. AP-SC-7 LifetimeClass preserved verbatim from StorageBinding. AP-SC-8 LifetimeClass admissible for arena (mapping check). AP-SC-9 Persistent-page geometry valid. AP-SC-10 Overlay reservation honored exactly. AP-SC-11 Overlay arena disjoint from non-overlay WRAM. AP-SC-12 SRAM no-span (fits 8 KiB window). AP-SC-13 Harness arena no-leak. AP-SC-14 HRAM page bound. AP-SC-15 Continuation record sized to InferenceState. AP-SC-16 Bank0 WRAM/HRAM caps honored. AP-SC-17 No section/codegen leakage. AP-SC-18 No scheduling fields. AP-SC-19 No repair provenance. AP-SC-20 Canonical sort hash stable. AP-SC-21 Pure expression no-slot. AP-SC-22 Cross-arena slot uniqueness. AP-SC-23 TraceRing placement in SramTracePages. AP-SC-24 Reservation entry size equality. AP-SC-25 Reservation honor count.

## Cross-stage invariants (F-Addr-1..14, joint OverlayPlan × ArenaPlan)

F-Addr-1 materialize coverage. F-Addr-2 persist coverage. F-Addr-3 alias-class total-or-disjoint. F-Addr-4 lifetime preservation. F-Addr-5 overlay byte equality. F-Addr-6 overlay disjointness. F-Addr-7 overlay member start-of-region. F-Addr-8 SRAM no-span. F-Addr-9 HRAM page bound. F-Addr-10 continuation sized. F-Addr-11 harness disjoint. F-Addr-12 persistent-page header aligned. F-Addr-13 slot id unique. F-Addr-14 binding_ref resolves.

## Diagnostic algebra (32 closed codes, all Hard)

Arena{InputHashMismatch, AllocationFailed, CapacityExceeded, UnmappedStorageClass, LifetimeClassMismatch, AliasClassDisagreement, AliasClassMustOverlapDisagreement, SlotIdDuplicate, PersistentPageGeometryMismatch, PersistentPageStreamMismatch, CrossStreamPageSharing, SramSpanForbidden, HarnessLeakDetected, ContinuationRecordSizeMismatch, HramOutOfRange, Bank0WramOverflow, HramUsableCapExceeded, OverlayReservationOverflow, OverlayReservationUnderflow, OverlayReservationOverlap, OverlayReservationCountMismatch, OverlayReservationCapDrift, CanonicalSortDrift, ReportRoundTripFailed, SectionRoleLeaked, SchedulingFieldLeaked, RepairProvenanceForbidden, TargetProfileLayoutUnsupported, PureExpressionAllocated, TraceRingMisplaced, PolicyProjectionMismatch, CertAddressInvariantFailed}.

## Cache key (K12, for F-B17)

```
K12 := DomainHash('gbf-codegen', 'StageCacheKey', 'arena_plan', 'v1',
                  CanonicalJson({
                    storage_plan_self_hash,
                    sram_page_plan_self_hash,
                    rom_window_plan_self_hash,
                    overlay_plan_self_hash,    // pinned: reservation handshake
                    runtime_chrome_budget_hash,
                    target_profile_hash,
                    arena_plan_policy_projection_hash,
                    pass_version: 'stage9/v1',
                    crate_feature_set_hash,
                  }))
```

K11/K12 cascade: K11 miss ⇒ K12 miss (overlay_plan_self_hash differs).

## Outputs

- `arena_plan.json` (ReportEnvelope).
- **Mandatory** `certs/arena.cert.v1` (always emitted on success): address_invariants flags F-Addr-1..14, reservation_honor, persistent_page_geometry pages list, harness_no_leak.

## Interaction with F-B16 (BLOCKED on oracle)

Knobs read in v1: arena_alignment_default, arena_zerofill_policy, persistent_page_geometry. Future repairs: capacity adjustments, alignment policy changes (when oracle unblocks).

## Open questions / risks

1. F-B16 lockup.
2. HRAM rigid 5-register enum — ABI changes require enum amendment.
3. PersistentPageGeometry mirrors `gbf-abi::PersistHeader`; size drift is a silent contract break.
4. FFD stability — closed sort key is the determinism guarantee; any future best-fit/worst-fit must preserve byte-identical outputs.

## Test surface

- `pass/`: single Materialize + Persist + Overlay; multiple slots FFD; persistent-page double-buffer; reservation honor; alias-class sharing.
- `reject/`: one per AP-SC-* and one per diagnostic code.
- F-Addr-1..14 fixtures; any false flag reduces result to `None`.
- F-B13 readiness: synthetic SchedSlice references ArenaSlot ids; validation passes.

## How this serves the overarching goal

Every byte the runtime touches has to live SOMEWHERE addressable, alignment-correct, and lifetime-honest. F-B12 is the contract that turns "we have these values" into "these values live at WRAM offset 0x42 with WramAccumScratch lifetime"; without it F-B13 can't schedule, F-B15 can't emit symbols, F-C3 has nothing to bind, and the persistence subsystem has no byte map.
design:
# F-B12 Implementation design

## Crate / module structure
- **Owner crate:** `gbf-codegen`
- **Modules:** `gbf-codegen::arena_plan` (public), `::core` (FFD allocator), `::reservation_honor` (handshake with F-B11), `::persistent_pages`, `::diagnostics`, `::cache` (K12 helpers).
- **Public types:** `NamedArena`, `ArenaId`, `ByteRange`, `ArenaInstance`, `ArenaSlot`, `SlotBindingKind`, `SlotBindingRef`, `ArenaBindings`, `OverlayReservationHonor`, `ArenaPlan`.
- **Public entry:** `pub fn build_arena_plan(inputs: &ArenaPlanInputs) -> ArenaPlanProduct`.

## Implementation phases (ordered, gated)

1. **Phase 1 — `NamedArena` closed enum + types.** All 20 v1 variants (7 WRAM + 6 SRAM + 5 HRAM + `WramOverlayRegion(OverlayId)` + `SramSequenceStatePages(SequenceStreamId)`). Gate: serde round-trip + canonical ordering.
2. **Phase 2 — Input bundle + K12.** Pin all 7 upstream hashes including `overlay_plan_self_hash` (reservation handshake). Gate: F-B17 §9.6.2 conformance; K11→K12 cascade (K11 miss ⇒ K12 miss).
3. **Phase 3 — `arena_for(StorageBinding)` closed mapping.** `(StorageClass, LifetimeClass) → allowed arena family` per RFC §2.6. Gate: unmapped classes hard-reject `ArenaUnmappedStorageClass`.
4. **Phase 4 — `honor_overlay_reservation`.** Allocate WRAM arena per `OverlayPlan.regions`; mint one ArenaSlot per member at `byte_offset = 0`; check exact-byte equality + disjointness from non-overlay WRAM. Gate: AP-SC-10/11/13.
5. **Phase 5 — Persistent-page allocator.** For each `(page, commit_group)` in F-B9: compute page_size = header + payload + commit_word; allocate two slots (A, B) in `SramSequenceStatePages(stream_id)`; same `alias_class_id`, different `byte_offset`. Gate: AP-SC-9.
6. **Phase 6 — FFD allocator.** Canonical sort (descending size, ascending alias_class, ascending lifetime priority, ascending binding_kind discriminant, ascending binding_ref); free-interval bookkeeping via sorted-vec (never hashmap); round_up alignment; MustOverlap alias-class equality check. Gate: shuffle-input determinism property test (100 iter).
7. **Phase 7 — F-Addr-1..14 cross-stage address invariants.** All 14 invariants checked; certificate emits boolean flag per invariant; any `false` reduces result to `None`.
8. **Phase 8 — Diagnostic algebra (AP-SC-1..25 + 32 closed codes).** Reject fixtures per code + invariant.
9. **Phase 9 — Mandatory `arena.cert.v1` emission.** Always emitted on success; pins reservation_honor + persistent_page_geometry + harness_no_leak + all 14 F-Addr flags.
10. **Phase 10 — Cache integration + failure memos.**
11. **Phase 11 — E2E verify-packet.** `scripts/review/f-b12/verify-packet.sh`.

## Structured tracing catalog

**Top-level span:** `gbf.compile.stage9_arena_plan` with `stage_id=9`, `build_id`, `input_identity_hash`, `cache_status`, `outcome`, `wram_arena_count`, `sram_arena_count`, `hram_assignment_count`, `materialize_slot_count`, `persist_slot_pair_count`, `overlay_reservation_total_bytes`.

**Events:**
- Common: start/cache/complete.
- `gbf.compile.stage.step` — `step_name ∈ {classify_arenas, honor_overlay_reservation, allocate_persistent_pages, ffd_allocate, validate_address_invariants}`.
- `gbf.compile.arena.allocated` — fields: `arena_id`, `named` (NamedArena string), `byte_range: {start, len}`, `backing`, `slot_count`.
- `gbf.compile.arena.slot_placed` — fields: `slot_id`, `arena_id`, `byte_offset`, `size_bytes`, `alias_class_id`, `lifetime_class`, `binding_kind`.
- `gbf.compile.arena.reservation_honored` — fields: `overlay_id`, `arena_id`, `bytes`, `byte_range`, `disjoint_from_count`.
- `gbf.compile.arena.persistent_page_emitted` — fields: `page_id`, `commit_group`, `stream_id`, `slot_a_offset`, `slot_b_offset`, `page_size_bytes`.
- `gbf.compile.arena.f_addr_check` — fields: `invariant_code: F-Addr-N`, `holds: bool`.

## Test plan

### Unit tests
- `tests/stage9_named_arena.rs` — closed enum coverage; round-trip; `WramOverlayRegion(OverlayId)` parameterization.
- `tests/stage9_arena_for_mapping.rs` — every `(StorageClass, LifetimeClass)` pair → expected family or hard-reject.
- `tests/stage9_overlay_reservation_handshake.rs` — exact-byte equality with F-B11 reservation; disjointness from non-overlay WRAM.
- `tests/stage9_persistent_page_allocator.rs` — A/B slots same arena, different offsets, same alias_class.
- `tests/stage9_ffd_determinism.rs` — 100-iteration shuffled-input property test.
- `tests/stage9_alias_class_sharing.rs` — MustOverlap → same byte_range; different alias_class → disjoint.
- `tests/stage9_lifetime_preservation.rs` — `ArenaSlot.lifetime_class == StorageBinding.materialization.lifetime` verbatim.
- `tests/stage9_address_invariants.rs` — F-Addr-1..14, one test each; any false → result=None.
- `tests/stage9_k12_injectivity.rs` — F-B17 conformance; K11→K12 cascade.

### Fixture tests (`fixtures/arena_plan/`)
- `pass/single_materialize_persist_overlay.json`.
- `pass/ffd_multi_slot_one_arena.json`.
- `pass/persistent_page_double_buffer.json`.
- `pass/alias_class_sharing.json` (MayOverlap slots in same range).
- `pass/reservation_honor_multi_region.json`.
- `reject/ap_sc_NN_*.json` × 25.
- `reject/code_<DiagnosticCode>.json` × 32.
- `reject/f_addr_NN_violation.json` × 14 (one per cross-stage invariant).

### Property tests
- `prop_ffd_shuffled_input_byte_identical`.
- `prop_alias_class_total_or_disjoint`.
- `prop_persistent_page_geometry_consistent`.
- `prop_overlay_reservation_byte_equality`.

### Determinism + cache tests
- `determinism_two_runs_byte_identical`.
- `cache_hit_path_byte_identical`.
- `cache_invalidation_on_overlay_plan_change` — `overlay_plan_self_hash` change → K12 miss.
- `cache_invalidation_on_storage_plan_change`.
- `cache_failure_memo_replay`.

### Cross-stage integration
- `tests/stage9_from_overlay_plan.rs` — F-B11 reservation honored byte-for-byte.
- `tests/stage9_to_sched_ir.rs` — F-B13 references ArenaSlot ids; live_wram/live_sram resolution succeeds.
- `tests/stage9_to_backend.rs` — F-B15 emits sections matching arena byte ranges (synthetic).
- `tests/stage9_to_runtime_persistence.rs` — F-D1 persistence reads page byte map; geometry matches `gbf-abi::PersistHeader` size.

### E2E verify-packet (`scripts/review/f-b12/verify-packet.sh`)
1. Run all stage-9 tests.
2. Compile sample LM through Stage 9.
3. Determinism: 2x build byte-identical.
4. Cache hit/miss equivalence; K11→K12 cascade verified.
5. Reservation handshake: every F-B11 region honored exactly.
6. F-Addr-1..14 all `true` in `arena.cert.v1` for the sample.
7. Cross-stage smoke: F-B13 schedules over slot ids without errors.
8. Emit `f_b12_packet.json` with arena geometry, slot counts, reservation honor, cert hash, F-Addr flags.
9. Exit 0 on green.

## CLI / debug integration
- `gbf compile --stage=arena_plan --inputs=<dir>`.
- `gbf debug arena inspect --plan=<plan.json>` — pretty-print arenas with byte ranges + slot map + reservation honor.
- `gbf debug arena diff --left=<a.json> --right=<b.json>` — compare two ArenaPlans for non-determinism investigation.
- `gbf debug envelope --stage=arena_plan`.

## Performance budget
- Wall-clock target: < 80 ms on M3 sample LM (≤ 100 slots).
- Memory ceiling: < 8 MiB peak.
- Cache hit: < 10 ms.
acceptance_criteria:

- [ ] `NamedArena` closed enum: all 20 v1 variants serialized + round-trip; `WramOverlayRegion(OverlayId)` + `SramSequenceStatePages(SequenceStreamId)` parameterization tested.
- [ ] `arena_for((StorageClass, LifetimeClass))` mapping complete; unmapped → `ArenaUnmappedStorageClass` Hard.

- [ ] Persistent-page A/B slots: same arena, different offsets, same `alias_class_id`; page_size = header + payload + commit_word matches `gbf-abi::PersistHeader`.
- [ ] FFD allocator determinism: 100-iter shuffled-input property test byte-identical.

notes:
## Reviewer personas

Always-on: P5, P6.

Conditional:
- **P1 Architecture & Boundary Steward** (claude + codex) — `NamedArena` is a public, closed enum forming the oracle/runtime contract surface; review for completeness + boundary correctness.
- **P2 Code Cleanliness** (claude + codex + gemini) — FFD allocator + closed-enum discipline.
- **P7 Numerical & Determinism** (codex + gemini) — FFD determinism is the load-bearing property; canonical sort.
- **P8 Public Contract / Schema Stability** (gemini + claude) — `arena_plan.v1` consumed by F-B13/F-B15/F-C3/F-D1; lockstep discipline.
- **P9 Performance & Resource Reviewer** (gemini + claude) — Bank0 WRAM + HRAM caps enforced; tight 8KiB WRAM.

## Related beads
- **Blocks (upstream):** bd-2k0 (F-B8), bd-3ns (F-B9), bd-15n (F-B10), bd-140 (F-B11).
- **Blocked by F-B12:** bd-9ae (F-B13), bd-18d (F-B15), bd-3ix (F-B16).
- **Cross-cuts:** bd-1g7k (F-B17), F-D1 persistence (Epic D), F-C3 ScheduleOracle (Epic C).
- **ABI coupling:** `gbf-abi::PersistHeader` size must match `PersistentPageGeometry.header_bytes`. Pin via `cargo test -p gbf-abi --test persist_header_size_eq_arena`.

## Known risks
1. F-B16 BLOCKED — no in-loop arena resizing/reordering yet. v1 plans immutable. Plan: forward-compat schema hooks.
2. HRAM rigid 5-register enum — ABI changes require enum amendment. Plan: cross-crate size test.
3. `PersistentPageGeometry` mirrors `gbf-abi::PersistHeader`; size drift silent. Plan: pinned compile-fail test.
4. FFD stability — closed sort key is the determinism guarantee; any future best-fit/worst-fit experimentation must preserve byte-identical outputs. Plan: shuffle-input property test gates merges.
5. `WramOverlayRegion` slot allocation at byte_offset 0 is the time-sharing contract; future fragment-and-resume modes (post-M4) may need offset != 0; v1 schema accepts but enforces 0.

## Future amendments
- v2: F-B16 repair levers (currently none touch arenas, but capacity adjustments are plausible).
- v2: Additional `NamedArena` variants as runtime control plane grows (e.g., per-mode trace pages).
- v3: Best-fit / worst-fit FFD experiments behind a feature flag, gated on determinism preservation.

comments.text:
## F-B10: ArenaPlan (Stage 9)

### What this is

Concrete byte ranges to materialized values selected by `StoragePlan`, plus reservation of WRAM regions selected by `OverlayPlan` (`planv0.md` line 1346). Allocates only `StoragePlan`-materialized values, not pure expression nodes directly.

Named arenas: ping-pong activations, accum scratch, route scratch, decode scratch, continuation record (with liveness), persistent sequence-state pages, trace pages, harness command/result blocks.

### Why this matters

Arenas are named so later stages — scheduling, placement, trace, runtime, `ScheduleOracle` — agree on the same storage geometry. Without that, debugging a slice means reverse-engineering byte offsets.

### Design sketch

```rust
pub struct ArenaPlan {
    pub wram_arenas: Vec<WramArena>,
    pub sram_arenas: Vec<SramArena>,
    pub hram_assignments: Vec<HramAssignment>,
    pub overlay_reservation: Option<OverlayReservation>,
}
```

Emits `certs/arena.cert.json`.

### Cross-feature deps

- F-B6 StoragePlan
- F-B9 OverlayPlan
- F11 / bd-h04 WramReserved (hot_arena_floor must be respected)

### Confidence: HIGH

title: T-B4.8: Deterministic static placement models by PlacementProfile
description:
## What
Implement `StaticPlacementModel`: `StrictOnePerBank`, `BudgetedFirstFit`,
`PackedExpertsFirstFitDecreasing`. Each is deterministic and reproducible
across runs. The active model is recorded in `static_budget.json`. See RFC §7.6.

## Why
Per RFC §2.10, Stage 2 is per-bank, not just per-expert. Without a NAMED
deterministic placement model, two valid implementations could produce
different `per_bank_occupancy` and both would be "correct" — the report
would lose its diff-against-baseline value. The named model rule fixes that.

## Inputs
- T-B4.1 QuantGraphBudgetView (sorted experts).
- T-B4.2 expert_payload_bytes.
- The active `PlacementProfile` from ResolvedPolicyProduct.

## Outputs
- `pub enum StaticPlacementModel { StrictOnePerBank, BudgetedFirstFit, PackedExpertsFirstFitDecreasing }`.
- Each model implementation:
  - StrictOnePerBank: fail if any expert can't fit a distinct ExpertBank slot.
  - BudgetedFirstFit: experts in (layer, expert) order; first-fit by
    `effective_cap_bytes`; signed residual recorded.
  - PackedExpertsFirstFitDecreasing: sort by descending payload, then
    (layer, expert); deterministic first-fit.
- Common kernels/LUTs/optional shared dense FFN go to common-bank-eligible
  slots only. Bank0Free for explicitly Bank0-compatible components.
- Active model is recorded in `BudgetDecisionSection.placement_model`.

## Pitfalls
- "Deterministic" is the load-bearing word. Test with a fixture that
  has multiple equally-good placements and verify byte-identical output
  across runs.
- BudgetedFirstFit's order is `(layer, expert)`, not declaration order.
- PackedExpertsFirstFitDecreasing's tie-break is `(layer, expert)`.
- Don't backtrack — first-fit means first-fit. Backtracking would change
  the determinism story.

## Acceptance
- gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_strict_one_per_bank_deterministic
- gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_budgeted_first_fit_is_byte_stable
- gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_packed_experts_descending_then_layer_expert
- gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_rejects_placement_profile_infeasible

## Refs
- RFC §7.6 StaticPlacementModel, §2.10.
- Depends on: T-B4.1, T-B4.2.
- Blocks: T-B4.3, T-B4.8a, T-B4.11.

comments.text:
## RFC amendments (2026-05-07)

§7.6 pins the resolved-PlacementProfile → StaticPlacementModel mapping in v1:

| `PlacementProfile`        | `StaticPlacementModel`                 |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| `StrictOnePerBank`        | `StrictOnePerBank`                     |
| `Budgeted`                | `BudgetedFirstFit`                     |
| `PackedExperts`           | `PackedExpertsFirstFitDecreasing`      |

This makes the choice of static model deterministic from the resolved
`PlacementProfile` (which lives in T-B2.0's `CompileKnobValues::placement`).
The dispatcher in this task must implement exactly this mapping; later RFCs
amend by adding rows.

The active model is recorded in `BudgetDecisionSection.placement_model`.

Implementation note: the mapping is one-shot; do NOT consult
`ResolvedPolicyProduct` for any other field when picking the static model.
A reviewer should be able to predict the model from the placement profile
alone.

New acceptance test:
- `gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_static_placement_model_matches_pinned_mapping`

Cross-refs: §7.6 mapping table.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Why this bead exists

§13 O1 (Pre-registration provability) is enforced by a CI script, NOT by the
emitter alone. The emitter records claims; the CI script proves them against
git history.

Without an external check, an attacker (or an over-eager developer) could
edit the predictions section after seeing results, leaving the section-hash
field internally consistent but invalidating the falsifiability of the whole
RFC. §13 O1 is the structural defense.

## Scope

`scripts/s1_preregistration_check.sh` (per §16.5):
  1. Read `predictions_section_hash` from the report front-matter.
  2. Recompute the section's normalized hash:
       - extract the "## Pre-registered predictions" section verbatim
       - normalize using S1CanonicalJson byte rules where applicable for
         any embedded structured data; otherwise compare body markdown
         BYTE-IDENTICALLY (exact byte equality of the section content)
     and ASSERT that recomputed hash == predictions_section_hash recorded
     for the predictions_commit.
  3. ASSERT predictions_commit is a STRICT GIT ANCESTOR of
     first_result_commit (use `git merge-base --is-ancestor A B`).
  4. ASSERT first_result_commit is the EARLIEST commit that introduces any
     of: checkpoint_self_hash, score_self_hash, negative_self_hash,
     ablation_self_hash, baseline_self_hash, derived from S1 execution.
     (Walk the git history of `experiments/S1/**` and the report's
     per_seed_artifacts.)
  5. Exit non-zero with a clear diagnostic on any violation.
  6. Closure of bd-12pl is FORBIDDEN while this script exits non-zero.

## Considerations

- This script is invoked by §16.6's CI matrix.
- The script does NOT prove that no uncommitted local run occurred before
  predictions_commit (§13 O1 explicit caveat). It enforces repository
  pre-registration order only.
- Bash is fine; if logic gets gnarly, write it in Rust as a small CLI in
  `gbf-experiments/src/bin/preregistration_check.rs` and invoke from the
  shell wrapper. Either way, the EXIT CODE is the contract.
- Future-self: if the section-hash normalization rules ever drift (e.g. an
  editor inserts trailing whitespace), the script will reject the report.
  That's the point — fix the file, don't relax the check.

## RFC anchors

- §13 O1 Pre-registration provability
- §16.5 Pre-registration CI
- §9.7 R-Predictions
- A16

title: F-S7 v0.2 T6.1: D16 rolling-window collapse halt with grace period
description:
## Goal

Implement D16's collapse halt with router_collapse_grace_steps = 500 (post-Phase-B), entropy_window_steps = 100 (rolling mean), entropy_for_step = min over layers of expert_usage_entropy_bits, and entropy_floor_bits = 0.5 * log2(n_experts). Halt only when the rolling mean drops below the floor AFTER the grace period.

## Background

Pre-review D16 halted on a single production-lambda step that dipped below the floor — a single noisy step in early Phase B could kill an otherwise healthy run. v0.2 layers in three robustness mechanisms: a grace period to let the router settle after Phase B begins; a rolling window so single noisy steps cannot trigger halt; a layer-aggregation rule (min) so collapse means every layer is sick, not one.

## Files

- gbf-train/src/runtime/collapse_halt.rs (rolling window + grace + min-over-layers)
- gbf-train/tests/collapse_halt_grace.rs (single low step in grace does NOT halt; sustained collapse after grace DOES halt)
- gbf-train/tests/collapse_halt_rolling.rs (a single dip below floor with rest of window above does NOT halt)

## Acceptance

- A single step with entropy below the floor within the grace window does not halt.
- A 100-step rolling mean below entropy_floor_bits AFTER step (phase_b_start + 500) halts with completion = CollapsedAt(step).
- The halt fires across all five seeds and is reproducible per (topology, seed) pair (see F6 reasoning).
- Phase A entropy is reported but not asserted (per H1 statement).

## Reasoning chain

T6.1 is independent of T6.2 and T6.3. It is read by T3.x (the closure outcome uses CollapsedAt to route Fail-router-collapse). The grace period must be measured from Phase B start, not from training step 0, because Phase A's teacher warmup may not exercise the router at all.
notes:
## Test Plan & Logging (AGENTS.md addendum)

### Unit tests (gbf-train/tests/collapse_halt_*.rs)

- collapse_halt_single_dip_in_grace_no_halt: single step with entropy below floor at step (phase_b_start + 1) does NOT trigger halt.
- collapse_halt_single_dip_after_grace_no_halt: single step below floor at step (phase_b_start + 800) does NOT halt (rolling-mean still above floor).
- collapse_halt_sustained_collapse_after_grace_halts: rolling mean below floor for 100 consecutive steps after grace → completion = CollapsedAt(step).
- collapse_halt_layer_min_aggregation: layer 0 collapsed, layer 1 healthy → min-over-layers is collapsed → halts iff sustained.
- collapse_halt_phase_a_no_op: Phase A entropy is reported but does NOT contribute to the halt computation (router not warmed).
- collapse_halt_reproducible_per_seed: replay (MoE, seed=0) twice with deliberately-collapsing config → CollapsedAt(step) identical between runs.

### Synthetic training fixture (gbf-train/tests/collapse_halt_integration.rs)

- A 2000-step synthetic training fixture exercises the halt logic end-to-end:
  - 0..4000 Phase A: entropy random, halt MUST NOT fire (Phase A is no-op for the halt check).
  - 4000..4500 Phase B grace window: synthetic entropy oscillates below floor at some steps, MUST NOT halt.
  - 4500..4600 sustained collapse: rolling-mean drops below floor for 100 consecutive steps, MUST halt at step 4600 with completion = CollapsedAt(4600).
- The fixture is small enough to run as a unit test (no Burn forward pass); it injects entropy values directly into the rolling-window aggregator.

### Logging

- s7.collapse_halt.tick DEBUG per step: { step, phase, entropy_per_layer, entropy_for_step (min), rolling_mean, floor, fired: bool }.
- s7.collapse_halt.fired ERROR on the halt step: { step, rolling_mean, floor, last_100_entropies }.
- s7.collapse_halt.summary INFO at end of training: { halted: bool, halt_step: Option<u64>, lowest_rolling_mean_observed }.

### Reviewer Personas

P5 Detective (always-on), P6 Scope Sentinel (always-on), P3 AI Researcher (entropy floor is a research-tunable; sensitivity must be honest), P7 Numerical & Determinism (rolling-mean is path-dependent), P4 QA / Test Engineer.

title: T-B3.9: ClassifyHead + DecodeSpecRecord (absorbs T-B3.8)
description:
## What
Define `ClassifyHead { kind: ClassifyHeadKind, weight: TensorId, bias:
Option<TensorId>, logit_format: QuantFormat }` and `ClassifyHeadKind
{ Tied, Untied }`. See RFC §8.1.

## Why
Three things land:

1. **Tied/Untied as explicit enum** (Ambiguity A11). `ArtifactCore.model.
   classify_head_kind` carries it explicitly; Stage 1 binds it through.
   Tied means `classify_head.weight = embedding_table.tensor_id` (SC-15);
   Untied means a separate weight tensor.

2. **`bias: Option<TensorId>`** is independent of weight tying
   (Ambiguity A24). A Tied head may still have its own bias.

3. **`logit_format`** (renamed from `output_format` to make the
   semantics explicit, Ambiguity A79) is a `QuantFormat` constrained
   to `{ I8, I16, Q8_8, Q4_4 }` (SC-15a). It names the boundary at
   which `Classify`'s output is clamped/rounded; this is the
   `ClassifyLogitBoundary` referenced in §8.7 and §9.7 op signatures.
   The Tied rule (SC-15 / Ambiguity A41) constrains only weight
   identity, not logit_format — the artifact may legitimately declare
   a different logit format than the embedding format.

## Inputs
- T-B3.1 (`QuantGraph` skeleton).
- T-B3.2 (`TensorId`, `QuantFormat`).

## Outputs
- `pub struct ClassifyHead { kind, weight, bias: Option<TensorId>,
  logit_format: QuantFormat }`.
- `pub enum ClassifyHeadKind { Tied, Untied }`.

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT default `logit_format` to `ExactAccumulator` and clamp later
  (Ambiguity A79). The artifact already declares a logit format;
  honor it as a named numeric boundary.
- DO NOT couple `bias` to `kind`. A Tied head with its own bias is
  legal (Ambiguity A24).
- DO NOT enforce `logit_format = embedding_format` even when Tied
  (Ambiguity A41 — that is too strong; the artifact can widen the head
  at the named boundary).

## Acceptance
- `gbf-codegen::classify_head_kind_tied_or_untied_only`.
- `gbf-codegen::classify_head_logit_format_only_in_activation_set`.
- `gbf-codegen::classify_head_bias_independent_of_kind`.

## Refs
- RFC §8.1 (ClassifyHead), §8.5 SC-15 (Tied weight equality), SC-15a
  (logit format set), §8.7 (ClassifyLogitBoundary).
- Ambiguity ledger: A11, A24, A41, A79.
- Depends on: T-B3.1, T-B3.2.
- Blocks: T-B3.19 (ClassifyHeadBinding), T-B3.22 (SC-15/SC-15a),
  T-B5.2 (Classify op output predicate).

title: T-B5.16: SelfConsistency cross-class (SC-1..SC-18; reachability, gate-weight, op-signature, sequence-slot)
description:
## What
Implement `SelfConsistency` (IIRClass 10): cross-class checks SC-1
through SC-18 from §9.6, including reachability, gate-weight
consumption, op-signature predicate, and sequence-slot coverage.

## Why
Like F-B3's SelfConsistency, this consolidates the 18 SC rules into
one bead so closure gating is a single place. The checks (RFC §9.6):

- IIR-SC-1: ValueId, EffectId, NodeId unique.
- IIR-SC-2: Every input ValueId is the output of some earlier node
  (except the unique InputToken).
- IIR-SC-3: Effect chain SSA — non-root effects_in is the effects_out
  of exactly one earlier node.
- IIR-SC-4: No cycles.
- IIR-SC-5: ValueDecl.format consistent with op output predicate.
- IIR-SC-6: Norm{plan} formats match QG.norm_plans[plan].
- IIR-SC-7: ExpertMatVec{layer, expert, slot} has a matching expert
  section.
- IIR-SC-8: RouteTop1{layer} requires Top1Hard semantics.
- IIR-SC-9: Dense-vs-routed shape (no Router*/Select* on dense).
- IIR-SC-10: DecodeToken plan binding + Rng chain semantics; Classify
  pure w.r.t. RNG.
- IIR-SC-10a: SequenceRead/Write per slot; SequenceStep inputs sorted
  by StateSlotId.
- IIR-SC-11: EffectDecl.class ∈ v1 closed set; no SemanticCheckpoint /
  TraceProbe.
- IIR-SC-12: Topological order matches §9.4.
- IIR-SC-13: Reachability — every non-terminal value consumed by at
  least one later node; only terminal is DecodedToken.
- IIR-SC-14 / 14a: token_inputs.len() = 1; embedding's input value_id
  equals TokenInput.value_id.
- IIR-SC-15: GateWeight consumed by exactly one SelectExpertTop1.
- IIR-SC-16: RouterDecision consumed by exactly one SelectExpertTop1.
- IIR-SC-17: op_histogram totals match node count.
- IIR-SC-18: every node satisfies op_signature (closed match).

Diagnostic codes from §12 are minted here (one per SC rule).

## Inputs
- T-B5.15 (canonical-sorted IR).
- T-B5.12a (op signature predicate).

## Outputs
- `fn check_self_consistency(g: &GbInferIR, q: &QuantGraph) ->
  Result<(), Vec<ValidationDiagnostic>>` (collects all hard
  diagnostics; never short-circuits).

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT short-circuit (collect all diagnostics).
- DO NOT skip SC-13 reachability — orphaned nodes are a regression
  magnet.
- DO NOT silently coerce mismatched router semantics; emit
  `InferIrNonV1RouterSemantics` (cross-link to T-B3.22a's QG-side
  check).

## Acceptance
- `gbf-codegen::iir_self_consistency_collects_all_diagnostics`.
- `gbf-codegen::iir_self_consistency_table_every_sc_has_counterexample`
  (18 SC rules + 36 IIR-Reject-* fixtures from T-B5.20).

## Refs
- RFC §9.6 (every IIR-SC), §12 (diagnostic taxonomy), Proof
  obligation O4 (rejection completeness).
- Depends on: T-B5.15, T-B5.12a.
- Blocks: T-B5.17 (SemanticEquivalenceCheck).

comments.text:
## Why this bead exists

§16 pins the two cargo invocations that participate in the F-S1 contract:

  S1-build-A "Phase A run":
    cargo build --release -p gbf-experiments
    → gbf-experiments/default → gbf-experiments/phase-a
    → gbf-train/qat + gbf-train/burn-adapter
    → CheckpointMetadata.build_kind = "phase_a"

  S1-build-B "Ablation":
    cargo build --release -p gbf-experiments --no-default-features --features ablation
    → gbf-experiments/ablation → gbf-train/qat-ablation + gbf-train/burn-adapter
    → CheckpointMetadata.build_kind = "ablation"

The two builds are the ONLY two configurations under which an S1 checkpoint
may be produced. Any other configuration is invalid for closure.

This bead wires the feature forwards in `gbf-experiments/Cargo.toml` and the
build_kind tag plumbing into CheckpointMetadata.

## Scope

- gbf-experiments/Cargo.toml features (per §16.3):
    [features]
    default = ["phase-a"]
    phase-a = ["gbf-train/qat", "gbf-train/burn-adapter"]
    ablation = ["gbf-train/qat-ablation", "gbf-train/burn-adapter"]
    falsify = []  # test-only, gates F1..F6 broken substitutes
- BUILD-TIME constant `BUILD_KIND` in gbf-experiments:
    #[cfg(feature = "phase-a")]   const BUILD_KIND: &str = "phase_a";
    #[cfg(feature = "ablation")]  const BUILD_KIND: &str = "ablation";
- `s1_train_run` (F-S1.13) must read this constant and embed it in
  CheckpointMetadata.build_kind.
- CI matrix (§16.6): both builds compile.
    cargo build -p gbf-experiments
    cargo build -p gbf-experiments --no-default-features --features ablation
- Negative test (mutual exclusion at gbf-train level):
    cargo build -p gbf-train --features qat,qat-ablation
    must fail with the F-S1.02 compile_error!.

## Considerations

- A25 ledger: explicit `qat-ablation` (not just `--no-default-features`) is
  the chosen path. This bead is the consumer of that contract.
- The `falsify` feature MUST NOT be enabled in either S1-build-A or
  S1-build-B. It exists only for `cargo test --features falsify --test
  falsification` (§16.6 / §15.2).
- Future-self: if a new build (e.g., GPU benchmark) is ever added, it CANNOT
  be used to produce a checkpoint that flows into bd-12pl closure. The
  build_kind tag and the H4 comparator are the gate.

## RFC anchors

- §16 Build configurations and feature flags (entire section)
- §16.6 CI gates that block bd-12pl closure
- §9.1 s1_checkpoint.v1 build_kind field
- A25

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## T-B1.5.4: gbf-emu frame events — VBlankFired, WidgetTickDispatched, SchedulerServicedFrame, YieldReturnedToScheduler

**Target crate**: `gbf-emu`
**Target file**: `gbf-emu/src/frame_events.rs`

### Background

The emulator records four kinds of frame-aligned events into its trace channel. These are **host/emulator report events**, not new ROM ABI types. The realism report and the L4 hard gate consume them post-run.

### Event types

```rust
pub enum FrameEvent {
    VBlankFired {
        frame: u32,
        mcycle_since_boot: u64,
    },
    WidgetTickDispatched {
        frame: u32,
        mcycle_since_boot: u64,
    },
    SchedulerServicedFrame {
        frame: u32,
        mcycle_since_boot: u64,
    },
    YieldReturnedToScheduler {
        frame: u32,
        mcycle_since_boot: u64,
        remaining_frame_mcycles: u32,
    },
}
```

### Why `SchedulerServicedFrame` is load-bearing

Without it, the L4 hard gate could be satisfied by an ISR-driven widget update **even if the cooperative scheduler is starving**. That would prove the wrong thing. `SchedulerServicedFrame(F)` is emitted only when the cooperative loop actually services frame F, so the gate distinguishes "ISR poked the widget" from "the cooperative runtime did real work."

### Cycle attribution rule (recorded in companion artifact)

- `cycles_per_product_accumulate` is computed from emulator cycle deltas over known product-count regions (kernel tile-loop body).
- Tile dump pause time is **excluded** from compute-cost fields and reported separately as harness overhead if measured.
- VBlank ISR time is included in end-to-end frame counts, but compute micro-cost fields must state whether ISR cycles were excluded or included.

### Acceptance gates

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-emu -- frame_events_emit_vblank_fired_at_ly_144
cargo test -p gbf-emu -- frame_events_emit_widget_tick_dispatched
cargo test -p gbf-emu -- frame_events_emit_scheduler_serviced_frame
cargo test -p gbf-emu -- frame_events_emit_yield_returned
cargo test -p gbf-emu -- frame_events_mcycle_monotonic
cargo test -p gbf-emu -- cycle_attribution_rule_excludes_dump_pause
```

### RFC reference

`history/rfcs/F-B1-compute-bringup.md` §9.1.

### Dependencies

- F-A7 (gbf-emu adapter base).
- F-A5 (cooperative scheduler — emits the cooperative-side events).

comments.author: bkase
bkase
comments.text:
## REVISION PASS — RFC §9.1 frame-event patch (2026-05-03)

Three structural changes to the frame-event emitter.

### 1. `FrameEventEnvelope` wraps every event with a sequence number

```rust
pub struct FrameEventEnvelope {
    pub seq: u64,
    pub event: FrameEvent,
}
```

`seq` is monotonically increasing across the run. It gives a deterministic total order for events with the same `mcycle_since_boot` (which can happen when an ISR fires at exactly the same cycle as a runtime yield). Frame-order checks (T-B1.5.5) use lexicographic `(mcycle_since_boot, seq)` ordering.

### 2. `YieldReturnedToScheduler` margin is signed

Was:
```rust
remaining_frame_mcycles: u32,
```

Now:
```rust
remaining_frame_mcycles_i32: i32,
completed_quantum_products: u16,
compute_progress_epoch: u32,
```

Signed `i32` lets the emitter report a **negative** margin when the runtime services a frame **late** instead of underflowing or being clipped to zero. Negative margins are exactly what a failure post-mortem needs to see.

`completed_quantum_products` records how much compute completed in the just-ended quantum (16, 64, or 256 depending on `YieldQuantum`). `compute_progress_epoch` is captured at the yield point so the realism report can correlate yields to compute progress.

### 3. New event type `ComputeProgressEpochAdvanced`

```rust
ComputeProgressEpochAdvanced {
    frame: u32,
    mcycle_since_boot: u64,
    compute_progress_epoch: u32,
}
```

Distinguishes "the compute kernel made forward progress" from "the widget ticked." Without this, a hung compute kernel that still has its ISR poking the widget could pass the L4 gate. T-B1.5.6's hard gate uses this event, not just the widget event.

### Updated acceptance gates

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-emu -- f_b1_frame_event_seq_is_monotonic
cargo test -p gbf-emu -- f_b1_frame_event_yield_remaining_can_be_negative
cargo test -p gbf-emu -- f_b1_compute_progress_epoch_advances_event_emitted
```

### Cycle-attribution wiring

The aggregator (T-B1.6.3) now consumes `compute_progress_epoch` separately from `vblank_count`. The realism report's `scheduling.scheduler_service_count` is computed from `SchedulerServicedFrame` events; `cycles_remaining_at_scheduler_service` uses signed differences.

### Logging discipline

Every emitted `FrameEvent` is wrapped in `FrameEventEnvelope`. T-B1.0.9's typed vocabulary now imports `FrameEventEnvelope` directly (not just `FrameEvent`) so the run-log capture (T-B1.6.11) records `seq` and uses it for stable cross-run diff.

title: T-B4.11: static_budget.v1 schema + semantic validator + tests
description:
## What
Define `StaticBudgetReportBody` + sections + semantic validator + serde.
Wire `gbf-report::report_schemas::static_budget_v1`. See RFC §7.7.

## Why
The chunk's third and final report. Once this lands, F-B4 is feature-
complete from a contract standpoint — only StageCache wiring and the
review packet remain.

## Inputs
- T-B2.2 ReportEnvelope + canonical JSON.
- T-B4.3..T-B4.10 (everything that contributes to the report).

## Outputs
- `pub struct StaticBudgetReportBody` with sections: `identity`, `policy`,
  `runtime_chrome_budget: Option<RuntimeChromeBudgetSection>`, `projections`,
  `decision`, `diagnostics`.
- `BudgetIdentitySection.runtime_chrome_budget_hash: Option<Hash256>` —
  None ↔ outcome=Failed ↔ exactly one BudgetMissingRuntimeChromeBudget.
- `RuntimeChromeBudgetSection` with `RuntimeMemoryCapSection` (per RFC §7.7).
- `BudgetProjectionSection` — `ProjectedSwitchCountSection` for switch
  counts (preserves upper_bound + decision_value + source).
- `BudgetDecisionSection { fits, interpretation, placement_model, failures }`.
- Semantic validator implementing every §7.7 invariant.

## Pitfalls
- No floats anywhere; reject any float JSON number at the canonicalizer level.
- `decision.fits == decision.failures.is_empty()` (a function-of, not just
  a coincidence; the validator enforces it).
- Failure 1:1 invariant from T-B4.9.
- Per-bank occupancy covers every slot in active RuntimeChromeBudget when
  budget is Some.
- When `decision.fits == false`, unassigned experts must either appear in
  a failure OR carry an explicit `UnassignedBecause` field.

## Acceptance
- gbf-report::f_b4_static_budget_v1_schema_accepts_canonical_fixture
- gbf-report::f_b4_static_budget_v1_rejects_missing_required_fields
- gbf-report::f_b4_static_budget_v1_self_hash_round_trip
- gbf-report::f_b4_static_budget_v1_failure_report_self_hash_round_trip
- gbf-report::f_b4_static_budget_v1_rejects_float_values
- gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_emits_canonical_json
- gbf-codegen::f_b4_budget_is_deterministic_for_same_inputs

## Refs
- RFC §7.7 schema, §9.2 JSON example.
- Depends on: T-B2.2, T-B4.3, T-B4.4, T-B4.5, T-B4.6, T-B4.7, T-B4.8, T-B4.8a, T-B4.9, T-B4.10.
- Blocks: T-B4.12, T-B4.13.

comments.text:
## RFC amendments (2026-05-07)

§7.7 `StaticBudgetReportBody` semantic invariants tightened:

**1. Missing-budget shape requires BOTH diagnostic + failure**

```text
runtime_chrome_budget_hash.is_none() iff
  runtime_chrome_budget.is_none() iff
  outcome == Failed
  AND contains exactly one BudgetMissingRuntimeChromeBudget diagnostic
  AND exactly one BudgetFailure::MissingRuntimeChromeBudget
```

(Was: 'exactly one primary BudgetMissingRuntimeChromeBudget diagnostic'.)

**2. Excerpt invariant**

When `runtime_chrome_budget.is_some()`, the embedded `runtime_chrome_budget`
section is a canonical review excerpt and MUST hash to
`runtime_chrome_budget_hash`. The excerpt is not the source of truth.

**3. View-conversion-attempted invariant**

If `BudgetMissingRuntimeChromeBudget` is present, no `QuantGraphBudgetView`
conversion was attempted. (Schema-level enforcement: missing-budget reports
must not carry per-expert payload values, per-bank occupancy, accumulator
maxima, or anything else derived from the view.)

**4. Reject Soft diagnostics**

The validator rejects any diagnostic carrying `severity = Soft`.

**5. `expected_q16_16: Option<u32>` and `shared_dense_ffn_bytes: Option<...>`**

Added to the §2.5 explicit nullability allow-list. The validator must reject
`null` in any other field of `static_budget.v1`.

New acceptance tests:
- `gbf-report::f_b4_static_budget_v1_missing_budget_includes_failure`

title: F-S7 v0.2: D6 byte accounting + MatchedBytesPin schema (B_ffn vs B_deployed; bias_policy)
description:
## Description

D6 reform AND MatchedBytesPin schema extension. The pre-review D6 said matched-bytes is "FFN-payload only" while H4 used `deployed_bytes_total`; that asymmetry meant MoE could pass FFN-payload parity while losing Pareto because the router has no dense analogue. v0.2 routes both H3 and H4 through a single `B_deployed_total` measure (FFN + router + bias + metadata) AND extends the MatchedBytesPin schema (§13.6) to carry the new fields so matched_bytes.json self-describes the v0.2 byte accounting. The bias_policy enum was introduced because experts and dense FFNs train with biases but the original byte formula ignored them entirely.

## Design

- D6 declares two byte measures: `B_ffn_payload_total` (diagnostic) and `B_deployed_total` (the gate measure used by H3 and H4).
- `compute_linear_deployed_byte_cost(linear) = compute_weight_byte_cost(linear) + bias_byte_cost(linear, bias_policy)` pinned in §6.2 D-Ok-1.
- `bias_policy ∈ {"not_deployed", "folded", "q8_8_per_output", "fp16_per_output"}`; canonical S7 placeholder = `"<PIN_ME>"` until reviewer chooses.
- Linear shape convention: `Linear[out_rows, in_cols]`; per-output-row Q8_8 scales.
- §13.6 MatchedBytesPin schema gains: `bias_policy`, `b_router_overhead_total`, `b_deployed_total_moe`, `b_deployed_total_dense`.
- The `[ESTIMATE 416]` prose pin for d_ff_dense was removed; v0.2 forbids prose estimates because metadata/policy/bank semantics can shift the exact integer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- D6 prose defines `B_ffn_payload_total` and `B_deployed_total` separately; H3 and H4 reference the deployed measure.
- §6.2 names `compute_linear_deployed_byte_cost`; bias_policy enum and placeholder pinned.
- §13.6 MatchedBytesPin carries all four new fields plus existing ones.
- matched_bytes.json self-describes the byte accounting with deterministic hashes.
- No prose estimate of d_ff_dense exists anywhere in the RFC; the only source is `experiments/S7/profile/matched_bytes.json`.

## Notes

- D6 tolerance unchanged: `max(0.10 * B_deployed_total(MoE), 4 * one_bank_bytes)`.
- Implementation crate: `gbf-policy::DenseMatchedBytesPolicy`.
- This task is the foundation for F2 (Fail-bytes), F7 (H3 decoupling), and F9 (Pareto byte-equivalence).

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## T-B1.5.2: Liveness counter integration — `progress_epoch` advances per yield quantum

**Target crate**: `gbf-runtime`
**Target file**: `gbf-runtime/src/liveness.rs`

### Background

F-A3 provides `LivenessCounters` in WRAM (12 bytes). One field, `progress_epoch`, must monotonically advance whenever the matmul kernel is making forward progress. The cooperative scheduler uses this to detect a starved/looping kernel.

This bead wires `yield_check` (from T-B1.5.1) to bump `progress_epoch` and, on resume, lets the scheduler observe the increment.

### Liveness contract

- `progress_epoch` advances at least once per yield quantum.
- The scheduler's `no_progress_frames` counter increments only when an entire frame elapses without a `progress_epoch` advance.
- `max_no_progress_frames` is reported in the realism report; the L4 hard gate requires it to be `<= 1`.

### Why per-quantum, not per-tile

Tile-granularity progress would produce ~64 advances per N=128 matmul. Frame-granularity scheduling at ~1,100 frames means many frames would have *zero* advances, which would wrongly trip the no-progress signal. Per-quantum gives the scheduler a fine-grained signal that the kernel is alive.

### Acceptance gates

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- liveness_advances_per_yield_quantum
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- liveness_no_progress_frames_bounded_under_compute
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- liveness_progress_epoch_monotonic
```

### RFC reference

`history/rfcs/F-B1-compute-bringup.md` §8.5 (L4), §11.5 (scheduler claims).

### Dependencies

- T-B1.5.1 (yield insertion provides the bump points).
- F-A3 (`LivenessCounters`).
- F-A5 (cooperative scheduler).

title: T-B3.16: LayerNormsBinding (per-layer pre_sequence + pre_ffn; Final standalone)
description:
## What
Implement `LayerNormsBinding` (QGClass 6 in §8.3): bind
`q.layer_norms: BTreeMap<LayerId, LayerNorms>` from per-layer
NormPlanRecord sites (LayerSequence / LayerFfn). Final remains
standalone. Asserts every layer has both `pre_sequence` and `pre_ffn`
populated.

## Why
With `NormPlanBinding` having produced `NormPlanRecord`s with `site`
fields, this class projects them into the per-layer
`LayerNorms { pre_sequence, pre_ffn }` records via SC-20:
- For every layer ℓ, `q.layer_norms[ℓ].pre_sequence` resolves to the
  unique record with `site = LayerSequence { layer: ℓ }`.
- Same for `pre_ffn = LayerFfn { layer: ℓ }`.
- Final stays standalone (looked up via `q.norm_plan(NormSite::Final)`).

SC-18 (every layer present) and the more granular
`QuantGraphLayerNormsIncomplete` (LayerNorms exists but `pre_sequence`
or `pre_ffn` missing) are minted here.

## Inputs
- T-B3.15 (NormPlanBinding output).

title: F-S7 v0.2 T1.2: solve_d_ff_dense + MatchedBytesPin emitter + O11 standalone CI
description:
## Goal

Implement the d_ff_dense fair solver, the MatchedBytesPin schema with all eight v0.2 fields, the matched_bytes.json emitter, and the O11 standalone CI test that verifies the canonical S7 instance matches the pinned JSON without running any training. This task combines algorithm, public artifact, and CI gate because they are one cohesive contract: the solver is the *only* producer of the pin, and O11 is the *only* verifier.

## Why this is a single task

T1.1 supplies the byte-cost primitives. The solver consumes them to choose d_ff_dense. The pin is the canonical-JSON serialization of the solver's output. The O11 CI test loads the pin and re-runs the solver against the canonical instance to detect drift. Splitting these creates a synthetic boundary — every change to the solver requires a coordinated change to the pin schema and the CI test anyway.

## Background — solver fairness

The pre-review solver picked the *smallest* d_ff_dense within D6 tolerance, systematically biasing the experiment toward MoE (a smaller dense baseline is easier to beat). v0.2's solver minimizes |B_deployed_total(Dense[d_ff]) − B_deployed_total(MoE)| over admissible integer d_ff values in [d_model, 4096], with explicit tie-breaks: prefer Dense ≥ MoE (so any residual byte advantage goes to dense, not MoE); if still tied, prefer smaller d_ff.

B_deployed_total now includes router overhead, bias bytes, and quantization metadata explicitly — not the FFN-payload-only formula v0.1 used.

## Pin schema (v0.2)

```
MatchedBytesPin {
  formula_version:           SemVer
  d_ff_dense_resolved:       u16
  bias_policy:               String   // one of: not_deployed | folded | q8_8_per_output | fp16_per_output
  b_experts_total:           u64
  b_router_overhead_total:   u64
  b_dense_ffn_total:         u64
  b_deployed_total_moe:      u64
  b_deployed_total_dense:    u64
  tolerance_bytes:           u64
  matched_bytes_self_hash:   Hash256  // DomainHash over canonical JSON with self_hash omitted
}
```

## Files

- gbf-policy/src/matched_bytes.rs (solve_d_ff_dense; integer search)
- gbf-artifact/src/matched_bytes_pin.rs (schema + serde)
- gbf-experiments/src/s7/baseline_match.rs (pin emitter)
- gbf-experiments/tests/matched_bytes_formula.rs (O11; runs WITHOUT any training artifact)
- experiments/S7/profile/matched_bytes.json (committed; pre-registration)
- scripts/s7_matched_bytes_check.sh (CI wrapper for O11)

## Pre-registration timing (critical)

matched_bytes.json must be committed in the same commit as (or strictly before) the predictions_section of s7_report.v1 (predictions_commit per O1 / Rep-S7-8). Any modification before first_result_commit bumps pass_version and re-triggers pre-registration.

## Acceptance

- Solver returns a deterministic d_ff_dense for the canonical MoeTiny instance given F-A4 metadata + bias_policy.
- Solver rejects unsolvable instances with MatchedBytesInfeasible (D-Fail-1).
- Pin round-trips through canonical JSON with self-hash equality.
- Pin emitter is deterministic: same (MoeTiny config, F-A4 metadata, bias_policy) → byte-identical JSON across 100 runs.
- O11 CI test passes against pinned matched_bytes.json AND fails if either bias_policy or F-A4 metadata change without a pin update.
- F2-bytes-unscaled falsification (dense hardcodes d_ff=128) fires AggregateParityVerdict = Fail-bytes per T3.1.

## Reasoning chain

T1.1 (byte helpers) → T1.2 (solver+pin+CI) → T3.1 (Fail-bytes routing reads the pin's tolerance and totals) and T3.2 (Pareto verdict reads bytes) and T4.4 (determinism axis D-E verifies the pin is deterministic).
notes:
## Test Plan & Logging (AGENTS.md addendum)

### Unit tests (gbf-policy/tests/solver.rs)

- solver_picks_min_abs_delta_canonical: canonical MoeTiny + F-A4 metadata → documented d_ff_dense.
- solver_tie_break_prefers_dense_ge_moe: synthetic tie → solver returns Dense ≥ MoE candidate.
- solver_tie_break_smaller_d_ff_last: two candidates with Dense > MoE → solver returns smaller d_ff.
- solver_infeasible_returns_err: no d_ff in [d_model, 4096] within tolerance → MatchedBytesInfeasible.

### Pin schema tests (gbf-artifact/tests/matched_bytes_pin.rs)

- pin_round_trip: serialize → hash → deserialize → re-serialize → re-hash; bytes and hash both equal.
- pin_emitter_deterministic: 100 emissions byte-identical (no host clock; no allocator nondeterminism).
- pin_self_hash_excludes_self: re-hashing the file with self_hash present must NOT equal stored hash.
- pin_json_shape_explicit: serde_json::json!({ ... }) literal containing all eight v0.2 field names deserializes successfully.

### Falsification fixtures (paired with T2.4)

- F2-bytes-unscaled: dense topology hardcodes d_ff=128; AggregateParityVerdict fires Fail-bytes (not Fail-parity — line is critical for §21 line-12 protection).
- F-solver-biased-smallest: override solver to pick smallest within tolerance; T3.1 must still correctly judge it Fail-bytes when the override misalignment triggers v0.2 tolerance check.

### O11 CI logging (scripts/s7_matched_bytes_check.sh)

- One s7.solver.candidate DEBUG per (d_ff, b_deployed_total_dense, delta, in_tolerance).
- One s7.solver.choice INFO at end: { d_ff_chosen, delta, tie_break_reason }.
- One s7.solver.mismatch ERROR if recomputed values disagree with the pin: side-by-side hash table.
- One s7.pin.emit INFO when the pin is regenerated: full eight-field digest.

### Reviewer Personas

P5 Detective (always-on), P6 Scope Sentinel (always-on), P3 AI Researcher (fairness of dense baseline is a research-integrity claim), P7 Numerical & Determinism, P8 Public Contract / Schema Stability (pin is the public artifact).

### Project Skills

`.agents/skills/fixture-bead-closure/SKILL.md` (canonical fixture instance committed and sha-pinned).

title: T-B5.20: Synthetic dense + routed IIR fixtures + 36 IIR-Reject-* counterexamples + BitExact closure gate
description:
## What
Author the synthetic dense and synthetic routed `GbInferIR` fixtures
under `fixtures/infer_ir/` covering every IIR-Reject-* class
(1–36 per §15.2). Each reject class has its own counterexample
fixture under `fixtures/infer_ir/reject/`.

## Why
Closure of F-B5 requires every IIR-Reject-* class to be exercised by
a fixture (proof obligation O4). The 36 classes from §15.2 cover
selectively:

- Single-token convention: InferIrEmbeddingNotUnique,
  InferIrDecodeNotUnique, InferIrClassifyNotUnique.
- Coverage: InferIrExpertCoverageMismatch,
  InferIrRouteCoverageMismatch.
- Disallowed constructs: InferIrSemanticCheckpointEmittedHere,
  InferIrFaultBoundaryEmittedV1Forbidden,
  InferIrSequenceSemanticsUnsupportedV1.
- Effect chain: InferIrEffectChainNotLinear,
  InferIrEffectIdEdgeTokenViolation.
- Topology: InferIrTopologicalOrderMismatch, InferIrCycleDetected,
  InferIrUnreachableNode, InferIrDisconnectedComponent.
- Format: InferIrValueFormatMismatch, InferIrNormFormatMismatch,
  InferIrResidualBoundaryMismatch.
- RNG: InferIrDecodeRngBindingMismatch,
  InferIrUnexpectedRngEffectOnPureOp.
- Storage: InferIrForbiddenStorageMetadata.
- Routing: InferIrNonV1RouterSemantics,
  InferIrRouterMatVecMissingForRoutedLayer,
  InferIrRouterPresentForDenseLayer, InferIrRouterScoreOrphaned.
- Anchors: InferIrSemanticAnchorMissing.
- Op signature: InferIrOpSignatureMismatch.
- FFN flow: InferIrFfnActivationMissing,
  InferIrExpertSelectionMissing, InferIrGateWeightNotConsumed.
- Token ingress: InferIrTokenIngressAmbiguous,
  InferIrInputTokenValueIdMismatch.
- Reduction: InferIrReductionSiteMissing.
- Histogram: InferIrOpHistogramTotalMismatch.
- Sequence (reserved): InferIrSequenceSlotCoverageMismatch,
  InferIrSequenceStateNextOrphaned.
- Semantic equivalence (fixture-only):
  InferIrSemanticEquivalenceFailed.

The **passing** dense and routed fixtures must:
- Round-trip via canonical JSON.
- Self-hash round-trip.
- Be cache-hittable.
- Pass `FixtureSemanticEquivalence` for BitExact (the chunk closure
  gate, proof obligation O11).

## Inputs
- T-B5.19 (StageCache K3 wired).
- T-B3.26 (matching QG fixtures from F-B3).

## Outputs
- `fixtures/infer_ir/dense_toy0/`: minimal dense FFN matching F-B3's
  fixture.
- `fixtures/infer_ir/routed_basic/`: routed FFN (RouterGateWeightSemantics
  variants, expert-coverage parity).
- `fixtures/infer_ir/mixed_topology/`.
- `fixtures/infer_ir/reject/<class>/`: each of 36 reject classes.
- Canonical-bytes-hash + self-hash + topological_order_hash golden
  files for passing fixtures.

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT skip the BitExact + mid-reduction-saturation reject case.
- DO NOT use a real exported model — fixtures should be smallest
  artifact exercising the path (project rule).
- DO NOT skip the C-ReportRewrap-Stage3 test (cache hit replays
  byte-identical product with refreshed audit parents).

## Acceptance
- `gbf-codegen::fixture_infer_ir_dense_toy0_self_hash_round_trip`.
- `gbf-codegen::fixture_infer_ir_routed_basic_self_consistency`.
- `gbf-codegen::fixture_infer_ir_every_reject_class_typed_diagnostic`
  (36 classes, table-driven).
- `gbf-codegen::fixture_infer_ir_fixture_semantic_equivalence_bit_exact`
  (proof obligation O11).
- `gbf-codegen::fixture_infer_ir_cache_hit_replays_with_audit_rewrap`.

## Refs
- RFC §15.2 (reject classes), §16 (proof obligations O1, O2, O4, O11,
  O13, O15).
- Project skill: `.agents/skills/fixture-bead-closure/SKILL.md`.
- Depends on: T-B5.19, T-B3.26.
- Blocks: T-B5.21 (driver split), T-B5.22 (review packet).

title: Add ShadowEmissionId type; fix Phase-E cadence path collision
description:
# Goal

Add a discriminated emission identifier to ShadowCompileSampleReal so that the Phase E final shadow_compile emission is distinct from the cadence step-20000 emission. Eliminate the silent file-overwrite hazard at experiments/S5/runs/seed-{seed}/shadow/.

# Background / Why

D11 specifies cadence samples at {4000, 8000, 12000, 16000, 20000} PLUS one Phase E final emission = 6 samples per seed. The original schema used \`step: ShadowStep\` so both the cadence emission at step 20000 and the Phase E final emission would have written to step-20000.json — silent clobber, undetected by replay.

The fix is a tagged union at the schema level so producers and consumers cannot accidentally treat the Phase E final as just another cadence row.

# Change

In gbf-policy + gbf-artifact (schema crates):

  - Add type ShadowEmissionId = ShadowStep | PhaseEFinal (tagged union; serde-tagged in JSON).
  - In ShadowCompileSampleReal, rename field 'step' -> 'emission_id' typed ShadowEmissionId.
  - Update producer in gbf-experiments::s5 to emit PhaseEFinal at the Phase E hand-off (HardenAndSelect).
  - Update path resolver: cadence -> 'step-{N}.json'; PhaseEFinal -> 'phase-e-final.json'.
  - Update gbf-policy consumers that iterate samples (frontier coverage check, H13 dispatch, audit log).

# Why this matters / Risk if unfixed

Without distinct emission IDs, one of the two step-20000 records would be lost. H13 falsification reads |shadow_at_20000 - final.encoded_rom_byte_cost| and needs both values to exist on disk for replay. The closure PR would fail integrity checks intermittently depending on emission order.

# Considerations

  - JSON: ShadowEmissionId serializes either as {"step": N} or {"phase_e_final": true} (or a string variant). Choose representation that round-trips cleanly under S5CanonicalJson (sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace).
  - Replay determinism: the 6 emissions must be ordered (cadence asc, Phase E last) and the artifact write order must match.
  - No live data exists yet; no migration required.

# Verification

  - Unit: ShadowEmissionId round-trip golden under S5CanonicalJson.
  - Integration: a seed run emits exactly 6 ShadowCompileSampleReal records on disk with distinct paths.
  - Pre-existing H13 boundary fixtures must continue to read shadow_at_20000 correctly.

# Related RFC sections

  §1 (ShadowStep / ShadowEmissionId / ShadowCompileSampleReal), §6.3 (shadow contract), §8.2 (SHR invariants), §13 (paths), §15 (O10).

# Blocks / Depends-on

  - Blocks B13 (H13 threshold) and B19 (ER-7) because both reference the Phase E final emission as a distinct record.

title: T-B4.13: F-B4 review-packet sub-bundle + chunk regen/verify scripts
description:
## What
Author the F-B4 portion of the chunk review packet under
`docs/review/f-b2-f-b4/`. Add `static_budget.{golden,failure.golden}.json`
+ sha256 + fixture. Implement the chunk-level `regen.sh` and
`verify-packet.sh` scripts. See RFC §13, §13.1.

## Why
F-B4 is the final piece of the chunk. The shared regen/verify scripts
must run all three reports' goldens, including the failure goldens for
all three stages. Without these, the reproducibility story has gaps.

## Inputs
- T-B4.11 static_budget.v1 schema + emitter.
- T-B4.12 StageCache (so verify-packet.sh validates cache behavior).
- T-B2.21 (F-B2 review-packet sub-bundle scaffolding).
- RFC §13, §13.1 markdown contents.

## Outputs
- `docs/review/f-b2-f-b4/artifacts/static_budget.golden.json` + `.sha256`.
- `docs/review/f-b2-f-b4/artifacts/static_budget.failure.golden.json` + `.sha256`.
- `docs/review/f-b2-f-b4/artifacts/static_budget.fixture.toml`.
- `scripts/review/f-b2-f-b4/regen.sh`:
  1. Cleans artifacts dir.
  2. Runs synthetic fixture through Stage 0 → Stage 0.5 → synthetic QuantGraphBudgetSource → Stage 2.
  3. Canonicalizes all three success reports.
  4. Writes them and SHA-256 sidecars.
  5. Exits non-zero on failure.
- `scripts/review/f-b2-f-b4/verify-packet.sh`:
  1. Recomputes all three success reports.
  2. Compares byte-for-byte against goldens.
  3. Validates each golden against its semantic validator.
  4. Validates each golden's report_self_hash round-trip.
  5. Runs intentionally failing Stage 0, Stage 0.5, Stage 2 fixtures.
  6. Compares failure reports byte-for-byte against failure goldens.
  7. Exits non-zero on any mismatch.
- `bead-map.md` with T-B*X → bead ID lookup (final, including this task).

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT hand-edit goldens — only the regenerator produces them.
- The fixture must be tiny so reviewers can read the entire report.
- CI runs verify-packet.sh on every PR; regen.sh runs only on intentional
  schema bumps.

## Acceptance
- ./scripts/review/f-b2-f-b4/regen.sh on a clean checkout produces zero
  diff after running.
- ./scripts/review/f-b2-f-b4/verify-packet.sh exits 0.

## Refs
- RFC §13, §13.1, §14 risks (golden rot).
- Depends on: T-B4.11, T-B4.12, T-B2.21.
- Blocks: F-B4 closure (bd-2ps).
