comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## F-B3: GbInferIR (value/effect IR, Stage 3)

### What this is

The hardware-aware **value/effect IR** (`planv0.md` line 1181). Storage-free but **not effect-free**: sequence-state mutation and RNG progression are explicit `EffectId`s, not hidden in buffer aliasing. Typed by **value kind**, **quant format**, and **effect class**. Concrete address space, concrete buffers, tiling, accumulator scratch belong to later stages.

### Why this matters

This is the IR `ArtifactOracle` (Epic C) compares against op-for-op. Getting the value/effect split right is what lets schedule equivalence be reasoned about.

### Design sketch

```rust
pub struct GbNode {
    pub op: InferOp,
    pub inputs: Vec<ValueId>,
    pub effects_in: Vec<EffectId>,
    pub outputs: Vec<ValueId>,
    pub effects_out: Vec<EffectId>,
}

pub enum InferOp {
    Embedding { token_src: TokenSrc },
    SequenceRead { slot: StateSlotId },
    SequenceWrite { slot: StateSlotId },
    RouteTop1 { layer: LayerId },
    ExpertMatVec { layer: LayerId, expert: ExpertId },
    CombineResidual,
    Norm { plan: NormPlan },
    Classify,
    DecodeToken { plan: DecodeSpec },
}
```

### Cross-feature deps

- F-B1 QuantGraph (consumed)
- F-A3.6 SemanticCheckpointId (annotations)

### Confidence: HIGH

title: F-S2.13: InertLossDiscipline trichotomy (ComputedDisabled / StructurallyInert / Enabled) + logging policy
description:
Goal
====
Implement the InertLossDiscipline trichotomy
(ComputedDisabled / StructurallyInert / Enabled) and the per-eval-point
LossTermEvalPoint logging contract. Per F-S2 RFC §2 Rule
InertLossDiscipline + §9.3 LossTermEvalPoint.

Why this matters
================
"lambda = 0" is overloaded. It can mean (a) the helper is intentionally
invoked and weighted out (ComputedDisabled — nodistill in Phase C/D),
(b) the helper does not apply on this topology at all (StructurallyInert —
router losses on Toy0), or (c) the helper is on with a tiny nonzero weight.
Without an explicit trichotomy, a raw=0.0 entry can mean "I computed
zero" or "I didn't compute anything," which destroys the audit trail.
CLAUDE.md "Training Loss Beads" mandates this distinction explicitly.

Scope (in gbf-experiments::s2::loss_logging)
============================================
- enum InertClassification {
    ComputedDisabled { raw: f32, weighted: f32 },
    StructurallyInert,
    Enabled         { raw: f32, weighted: f32 },
  }
- fn classify(term: &str, raw_opt: Option<f32>, lambda: f32,
              applies_to_topology: bool) -> InertClassification:
      if !applies_to_topology  -> StructurallyInert  (raw = null,
                                                       weighted = null)
      else if lambda == 0.0    -> ComputedDisabled { raw = raw_opt.unwrap(),
                                                       weighted = 0.0 }
      else                     -> Enabled { raw, weighted = lambda * raw }
- Serde representation of StructurallyInert: both raw and weighted fields
  in the artifact JSON are literal `null`, NOT `0.0` (so a future bug that
  skips a real computation cannot masquerade as a zero).
- s2_distillation_log.v1's LossTermEvalPoint schema (owned by F-S2.17)
  consumes this classification.
- Toy0 topology table:
    lambda_balance, lambda_zrouter, lambda_switch:
      StructurallyInert on s2_ternary_full / s2_fp_full / s2_ternary_nodistill
      / s2_ablation (no router on Toy0).
    lambda_distill on s2_ternary_nodistill Phase C/D:
      ComputedDisabled (raw helper still invoked).
    lambda_range, lambda_zero per the F-S2.08 phase-effective table.
- A literal 0.0 raw value is allowed only when classify produces Enabled
  and the mathematical raw loss is genuinely zero.

Acceptance
==========
- Unit test: nodistill Phase C with raw=2.5, lambda=0 →
  ComputedDisabled { raw=2.5, weighted=0.0 } serializes with raw=2.5,
  weighted=0.0 (not null).
- Unit test: router losses on Toy0 → StructurallyInert serializes with
  raw=null, weighted=null.
- Unit test: a "missing raw computation" bug (raw_opt=None when
  applies_to_topology=true) is a hard error, not silently turned into 0.0
  or null.
- Unit test: AS2-15 cross-check — the ambiguity ledger says "Present in
  config, with explicit ComputedDisabled vs StructurallyInert logging
  semantics"; the InertClassification enum implements that.

Considerations
==============
- The trichotomy is mirrored at the helper level: F-S2.11 zero_loss helper
  must compute raw even when lambda_zero = 0, so ComputedDisabled is real.
  F-S2.17 (distillation log) writes the JSON.
- This bead defines POLICY; the schema (F-S2.17) and the runtime composer
  (F-S2.12) consume it.

References
==========
F-S2 RFC §2 Rule InertLossDiscipline, §9.3 DL-3, §17 AS2-15,
CLAUDE.md "Training Loss Beads".
Depends on: F-S2.09, F-S2.10, F-S2.11, F-S2.08.

title: F-B8 T13: Alias-class engine — pair predicates, intent-tagged union-find, mixed-intent rejection (STORE-031), cardinality (STORE-032), fingerprint + dense id (STORE-035)
description:
# Alias-class engine

## Why this engine is its own bead

The alias-class layer is what F-B13 ResourceStateValidation reasons about. Getting it wrong here means F-B13 can't prove resource safety. The v2 review surfaced three mistakes the v1 engine could make:

1. **Mixed-intent merge** — union-find over pair predicates can fold edges admitted under different intents into a single equivalence class (e.g. `A~B` via ScratchReuse, `B~C` via PingPong; transitive closure yields one class with no single valid intent). STORE-031.
2. **Cardinality violation** — PingPong requires 2 members; PersistRotation requires a rotation pair. STORE-032.
3. **Hash-truncated id collision** — v1 used u32 collision-retry; v2 wants fingerprint+dense-id with explicit collision diagnostic (STORE-035).

## Construction order (matches §8.7 step 6)

```text
6a. Seed every binding with a fresh singleton AliasClassId.
6b. Collect candidate alias edges from §11.4 pair predicates;
    each edge is tagged with EXACTLY ONE AliasIntent.
6c. Reject any connected component whose edges carry more than
    one AliasIntent (STORE-031).
6d. For ScratchReuse: require pairwise AbstractLiveRange
    disjointness across the WHOLE component, not just along edges.
6e. For PingPong (2 members) and PersistRotation (rotation pair):
    enforce cardinality constraints before unioning (STORE-032).
6f. Canonicalize: sort connected components by
    (AliasClassFingerprint, CanonicalJson({members, intent})) and
    assign dense AliasClassIds in that order.
    On fingerprint collision over distinct payloads: STORE-035.
```

## Pair predicates (closed v1)

* `PP-ScratchReuse(v_a, v_b)`: both hot Slice, scratch/accum roles, **AbstractLiveRange disjoint in topological order** (not byte-range, not lifetime-class).
* `PP-PingPong(v_a, v_b)`: WramHot, same role ∈ {Activation, FfnIntermediate}, `IsPingPongPair(GbInferIR, v_a, v_b)` typed predicate.
* `PP-ResumeOverlap(v_a, v_b)`: yield-boundary pair via `ResumeBoundary(GbInferIR, v_a, v_b)`.
* `PP-PersistRotation(v_a, v_b)`: same kind, same commit group, distinct page ids, runtime declares the rotation pair.

Note: `PP-PersistRotation` consults `SP.persist_pages`. The driver (T16) must build persist pages **before** running the alias engine. This is the v2 reordering.

## Singleton ⇒ NoAlias

Every singleton class gets `intent = NoAlias`. Recompute bindings are always singleton (SC5). RomConst bindings are always singleton. The "default ScratchReuse" pattern from v1 is removed.

## AliasClassFingerprint discipline

```text
AliasClassFingerprint(A) :=
  DomainHash("gbf-codegen", "AliasClassId", "v1",
             CanonicalJson({ members: SortedVec(A.members),
                             intent:  A.intent }))
```

Use the full Hash256. Do not truncate to u32. Do not retry on collision; emit STORE-035 instead.

## Acceptance

* Unit test: union-find over a 3-node component with edges tagged ScratchReuse / PingPong produces STORE-031, not a silent merge.
* Unit test: PingPong with 3 candidate members rejects to STORE-032.
* Unit test: ScratchReuse component with overlapping `AbstractLiveRange` across any pair rejects to STORE-014.
* Unit test: singleton produces `intent = NoAlias`.
* Unit test: same alias class in two runs produces identical `AliasClassFingerprint`; dense `AliasClassId` may differ if other classes change.

## Anti-patterns

* Do not use byte-range overlap as the disjointness witness for ScratchReuse — that is F-B12's job. Use `AbstractLiveRange`.
* Do not assign dense `AliasClassId` before sorting by fingerprint.
* Do not silently retry on fingerprint collision.

Depends on: T2, T4, T12.
design:
## Test Plan

### Pair predicate tests

* `pp_scratch_reuse_admits_disjoint_live_ranges` — two hot Slice scratch values with disjoint AbstractLiveRange → PP-ScratchReuse admits.
* `pp_scratch_reuse_rejects_overlapping_live_ranges` — overlapping → rejected.
* `pp_ping_pong_admits_wram_hot_activation_pair` — two WramHot Activations with `IsPingPongPair=true` → admitted.
* `pp_ping_pong_rejects_hram_hot` — HramHot RouterDecision pair → rejected (PP-PingPong is WramHot-only).
* `pp_ping_pong_rejects_accumulator_role` — Accumulator pair → rejected (PP-PingPong is Activation/FfnIntermediate-only). **Regression for v1 Example C bug.**
* `pp_resume_overlap_admits_yield_boundary_pair` — `ResumeBoundary(iir, v_a, v_b) = true` → admitted.
* `pp_persist_rotation_admits_same_kind_same_group_distinct_pages` — admitted.
* `pp_persist_rotation_reads_persist_pages_built_first` — confirms construction order: persist pages must exist before alias edges are collected.

### Union-find with intent tagging

* `intent_tagged_edges_collected_correctly` — each candidate edge carries exactly one AliasIntent.
* `mixed_intent_component_rejected_with_store_031` — synthetic 3-node component with edges (A~B, ScratchReuse) and (B~C, PingPong) → STORE-031; provenance: `component_members=[A,B,C]`, `intents_seen={ScratchReuse, PingPong}`, `candidate_edges=[...]`.
* `single_intent_component_unions_correctly` — same component but all edges tagged ScratchReuse → one alias class with 3 members.
* `scratch_reuse_pairwise_disjointness_across_component` — 3-member ScratchReuse: even if pairs (A,B) and (B,C) are disjoint, (A,C) must also be disjoint. Violation → STORE-014.
* `ping_pong_cardinality_violation_3_members` — 3-member PingPong → STORE-032; provenance: `intent=PingPong, members.len()=3`.
* `persist_rotation_cardinality_must_be_pair` — non-pair PersistRotation → STORE-032.

### Fingerprint + dense id

* `fingerprint_stable_across_two_runs` — same env → byte-identical fingerprint per class.
* `dense_id_assigned_by_fingerprint_sort` — two runs with different class-ordering hashes produce same dense ids if fingerprints sort identically.
* `dense_id_differs_when_unrelated_class_changes` — adding a new alias class with smaller fingerprint shifts other classes' dense ids by one. Documented; fingerprints unchanged.
* `tie_break_on_canonical_payload` — synthetic identical fingerprint with distinct payloads → tie-break on `CanonicalJson({members, intent})`.
* `store_035_fingerprint_collision` — mock `DomainHash` that produces forced collision → STORE-035; provenance: both canonical payloads.

### Singleton handling

* `every_singleton_class_intent_is_no_alias` — exhaustive: every binding whose alias class has 1 member has intent NoAlias.
* `recompute_binding_in_no_alias_singleton` — Recompute binding's class is NoAlias singleton (SC5).
* `rom_const_binding_in_no_alias_singleton` — RomConst binding's class is NoAlias singleton.

### Stress / property tests

* `alias_engine_stress_1000_candidates` — 1000 random candidate edges; deterministic output across 2 runs.
* `alias_engine_no_cycle_in_union_find` — invariant maintained.
* `alias_engine_no_orphan_dense_id` — every class has a unique dense id ∈ [0, n_classes).

## Logging Plan

Spans:
* `f_b8::alias_construction` — root span of the alias engine pass.

Events:
* `f_b8.alias.candidate_edge_collected` (TRACE) — per pair predicate match: `v_a, v_b, intent`.
* `f_b8.alias.component_constructed` (DEBUG) — per emitted class: `fingerprint, intent, member_count, dense_id`.
* `f_b8.alias.mixed_intent_rejected` (WARN) — per STORE-031 emission: `component_members, intents_seen`.
* `f_b8.alias.cardinality_rejected` (WARN) — per STORE-032: `intent, members`.
* `f_b8.alias.fingerprint_collision` (ERROR) — per STORE-035: both payloads.
* `f_b8.alias.singleton_emitted` (TRACE) — per NoAlias singleton: `value_id`.

`assert_traced!` for the STORE-031 regression:

```rust
let inputs = sc_violations::store_031_mixed_intent_component();
let result = build_storage_plan_core(inputs);
assert!(matches!(result.outcome, Outcome::Failed));
assert_traced!([
  { event: "f_b8.alias.candidate_edge_collected", intent: "ScratchReuse" },
  { event: "f_b8.alias.candidate_edge_collected", intent: "PingPong" },
  { event: "f_b8.alias.mixed_intent_rejected" },
  { event: "f_b8.diagnostic.emitted", code: "STORE-031" }
]);
```
notes:
## Regression checklist

1. PP-ScratchReuse requires `AbstractLiveRange` disjointness (T12), NOT byte-range disjointness, NOT lifetime-class disjointness.
2. PP-PingPong is WramHot-only and Activation/FfnIntermediate-only. RouterDecision and Accumulator are NOT candidates.
3. PP-PersistRotation reads `SP.persist_pages` — so persist pages must exist before alias edges are collected (driver T15 step 4 before step 6).
4. Union-find edges are intent-tagged; mixed-intent components fire STORE-031.
5. ScratchReuse disjointness is checked pairwise across the whole component, not just along edges.
6. Cardinality constraints enforced: PingPong (2 members), PersistRotation (rotation pair). Violations fire STORE-032.
7. Dense `AliasClassId` assigned by sorting on `(AliasClassFingerprint, CanonicalJson({members, intent}))`.
8. Fingerprint is full `Hash256` — no truncation; on hash collision over distinct payloads, fire STORE-035.
9. Every singleton class has `intent = NoAlias`. No exceptions.
10. Recompute and RomConst bindings are ALWAYS in NoAlias singletons.
close_reason: Completed alias-class engine: seed singleton NoAlias classes, union candidate edges by typed intent, reject mixed-intent components with STORE-031, enforce PingPong/PersistRotation cardinality with STORE-032, validate ScratchReuse pairwise AbstractLiveRange disjointness with STORE-014, sort by full AliasClassFingerprint/canonical payload before dense ids, and detect fingerprint collisions with STORE-035. Evidence: cargo fmt --check --all; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -p gbf-codegen storage_plan --lib (69 passed); CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -p gbf-policy diagnostics --lib (20 passed); SC11 rg static scan over gbf-codegen/src/storage_plan returned zero hits; policy/staged-LUT/kernel rg static scan returned zero hits; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo clippy -p gbf-policy -p gbf-codegen -p gbf-report --all-features -- -D warnings; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo build --workspace.

title: F-S7 v0.2: Outcome algebra & closure contract (Fail-bytes, Pass-with-warning removal, §21)
description:
## Description

The pre-review outcome algebra had three structural problems: (a) a `Pass-with-warning` variant in `S7Outcome` that the combination rules never returned (dead algebra); (b) bytes-mismatch was folded into `Fail-parity`, and `Fail-parity` dispatches to `ProceedToS8-DenseOnly` — meaning an invalid experiment (bytes weren't actually matched) would close bd-2v9r with a successful-scientific-falsification verdict; (c) the §21 "Final concise contract" item 12 admitted DenseOnly closure for any Fail-parity cause, not just true per-seed bpc misses. v0.2 separates `Fail-bytes` (Halt: invalid-experiment) from `Fail-parity` (DenseOnly: scientific falsification), removes `Pass-with-warning`, and tightens §21 item 12 so DenseOnly closure is reachable only when per-seed bpc parity fails under valid matched-deployed-byte accounting.

## Design

- `S7Outcome` gains `Fail-bytes` and drops `Pass-with-warning`.
- `AggregateParityVerdict` is `{Pass-clean, Fail-parity, Fail-bytes}`; §11.2 routes `|bytes_diff| > tolerance` straight to `Fail-bytes`.
- §12 dispatch inserts `elif aggregate_parity_verdict = Fail-bytes ⇒ Fail-bytes` before the H3 Refuted check.
- Decision dispatch: `Fail-bytes → Decision::Halt(matched-bytes-invalid; comparison-not-scientific)`.
- §21 closure rule 12 explicitly enumerates the invalid-experiment outcomes that MUST NOT close as DenseOnly: bytes mismatch, missing artifacts, gradient-provenance failure, oracle failure, emulator failure, guardrail failure.
- H3 falsification: `|B_deployed_total(MoE) - B_deployed_total(Dense)| > tolerance ⇒ NotEvaluable; S7Outcome = Fail-bytes`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `S7Outcome` enum has no `Pass-with-warning`.
- §11.2 AggregateParityVerdict produces `Fail-bytes` distinct from `Fail-parity`.
- §12 dispatch routes `Fail-bytes` to `Decision::Halt`.
- §21 item 12 lists the invalid-experiment outcomes verbatim and forbids DenseOnly closure for any of them.
- H3 falsification rule for bytes mismatch is `NotEvaluable; S7Outcome = Fail-bytes` (not `Refuted`).

## Notes

- Depends on F1: `Fail-bytes` only makes sense once `B_deployed_total` is the gate measure.
- Depends on F5: `InconclusiveDiverged` guardrail verdict participates in the outcome chain.
- Implementation crate: `gbf-experiments::s7::report` (outcome-algebra dispatcher).
close_reason: Completed outcome algebra/closure contract audit; Claude reason-tag concerns fixed and Gemini/Claude delta reviews passed.

title: T-B3.1: QG core + tensors + ResolvedBlobIndex + provenance (absorbs T-B3.2/2a/11)
description:
## What
Define the public `QuantGraph` struct and `QuantGraphIdentity` substruct
in `gbf-codegen::s1::quant_graph`, including `ModelSpecSummary` and
`lowering_manifest_hash`. This is the central type that every other
Wave 1 task hangs sub-fields off. See RFC §8.1.

## Why
Pinning the *shape* of `QuantGraph` once — with `identity`, `tensors`,
`norm_plans`, `layer_norms`, `routing_table: Option`, `expert_sections`,
`ffn_plans`, `decode_spec`, `sequence_semantics`, `provenance`,
`classify_head`, `residual_plan` as the closed top-level field set —
prevents the 10 sibling Wave 1 tasks from mutating top-level shape.

`QuantGraphIdentity` carries every hash that K1 keys off
(`artifact_core_hash`, `policy_resolution_self_hash`,
`artifact_validation_self_hash`, `semantic_core_hash`,
`lowering_manifest_hash`) plus `determinism` and `model_spec_summary`.
`semantic_core_hash` enables QG-Ok-4; `lowering_manifest_hash` enables
cache invalidation on lowering drift; `determinism` flows from
`ArtifactCore.numeric_profile` (NOT from policy — see Ambiguity A20 and
§9.10).

`ModelSpecSummary` is summary-only (Ambiguity A39): `n_layers`,
`d_model`, `d_ff`, `vocab_size: u32`, per-layer `n_experts: u16`,
per-layer `ffn_kind ∈ { Routed, Dense }`. Per-layer FFN
`activation_kind` / `intermediate_format` lives in `ffn_plans`, NOT in
the summary (T-B3.10) — preventing duplication that A39 calls out as
"redundant duplication invites drift".

## Inputs
- T-B3.0 envelope (`bd-23xt`) — provides the schema/hash conventions.
- `gbf-foundation::Hash256`, `DeterminismClass`, `LayerId`, `ExpertId`.
- Already-existing `gbf-artifact` types referenced by sub-tasks.

## Outputs
- `pub struct QuantGraph { identity, tensors, norm_plans, layer_norms,
  routing_table: Option<RoutingTable>, expert_sections, ffn_plans,
  decode_spec, sequence_semantics, provenance, classify_head,
  residual_plan }`. Sub-fields use placeholder types that later tasks
  refine.
- `pub struct QuantGraphIdentity { artifact_core_hash,
  policy_resolution_self_hash, artifact_validation_self_hash,
  semantic_core_hash, lowering_manifest_hash, determinism,
  model_spec_summary }`.
- `pub struct ModelSpecSummary { n_layers, n_experts: BTreeMap<LayerId, u16>,
  d_model, d_ff, vocab_size: u32, ffn_kind: BTreeMap<LayerId, FfnKindTag> }`.

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT put per-layer `activation_kind` / `intermediate_format` into
  `ModelSpecSummary` (Ambiguity A80). They go in `ffn_plans` (T-B3.10).
- DO NOT add a `quant_graph_self_hash` field on `QuantGraph` — the hash
  lives only on `QuantGraphProduct` (Ambiguity A77). Without this rule
  self-hashing becomes circular or needs ad-hoc zeroing.
- DO NOT add `residency_hint` anywhere on the struct (§2.3 storage-free
  + Ambiguity A27). Residency is HintBundle-only.
- DO NOT add `SemanticCheckpointId` or `TraceProbeId` (§2.12 / Ambiguity
  A16). Anchors are F-B5 territory; checkpoints are F-B6 territory.

## Acceptance
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_struct_top_level_shape_is_closed` (compile-
  time field-set check).
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_identity_carries_lowering_manifest_hash`.
- `gbf-codegen::quant_graph_identity_does_not_contain_self_hash`.
- `gbf-codegen::model_spec_summary_excludes_per_layer_ffn_plan_fields`.

## Refs
- RFC §8.1 type-level contract; §8.5 SC-19 (no storage metadata);
  §11 (K1 inputs); §9.10 (determinism inheritance).
- Ambiguity ledger: A20, A27, A39, A77, A80.
- Blocks: T-B3.2..T-B3.11 (sub-field definitions), T-B3.12 (IdentityBinding).
close_reason: Implemented QuantGraph core/tensor/blob/provenance public surface with storage-free shape, identity/model summary, ResolvedBlobIndex canonical hashing, provenance injectivity, and serde/canonical regressions. Gates: cargo test -p gbf-codegen --lib s1::quant_graph::tests:: (123 passed); cargo test -p gbf-codegen stage_cache_key_quant_graph (9 passed); cargo check -p gbf-codegen. Reviews: Gemini PASS, Claude PASS after proof-test fixes. Pure build_quant_graph_core split remains owned by open bd-ou73.

### Scope (full public surface; absorbs T-B3.2 / T-B3.2a / T-B3.11)

- `pub struct QuantGraphIdentity { artifact_core_hash, policy_resolution_self_hash, artifact_validation_self_hash, semantic_core_hash, lowering_manifest_hash, determinism: DeterminismClass, model_spec_summary }`.
- `pub struct ModelSpecSummary { n_layers, n_experts: BTreeMap<LayerId, u16>, d_model, d_ff, vocab_size: u32, ffn_kind: BTreeMap<LayerId, FfnKindTag> }`.
- `pub struct QuantTensorRef { tensor_id, layout, quant_format, role: QuantTensorRole, blob: ResolvedBlobRef, aux_blob_refs: Vec<QuantAuxBlobRef> }`.
- `pub enum QuantTensorRole { EmbeddingTable, NormScale { norm_plan }, NormBias { norm_plan }, RouterWeight { layer }, RouterBias { layer }, ExpertWeight { layer, expert, slot }, ExpertBias { layer, expert, slot }, ClassifyWeight, ClassifyBias }` (closed; SharedDense* deliberately absent per A63).
- `pub struct ResolvedBlobRef { blob_ref, content_hash, encoded_size_bytes, decoded_size_bytes, codec }`.
- `pub struct QuantAuxBlobRef { kind: QuantAuxKind, layout, format: AuxFormat, blob: ResolvedBlobRef, export_tensor_id }`.
- `pub enum QuantAuxKind { Scale, Threshold, SparseMeta }` (closed).

title: F-B13: GbSchedIR + ResourceStateValidation (Stages 10, 10.5)
description:
# F-B13 — GbSchedIR + ResourceStateValidation (Stages 10 and 10.5)

**Source RFC:** `history/rfcs/F-B13-sched-ir-resource-state.md`.

## Why these stages exist (paired as 10 and 10.5)

The Game Boy LR35902 has strict timing and banking constraints: ISR latency must be bounded, ROM banking is hardware-multiplexed, SRAM paging is invisible to ISR (ISR must execute from Bank0/HRAM/fixed WRAM), interrupt-policy regions must not hold non-resumable leases, and overlays are evicted on yield or interrupt entry. F-B5..F-B12 leave the pipeline with values, effects, persistent residencies, ROM banks, overlay reservations, and arena addresses — but **the schedule** (how slices execute on a cooperative scheduler, what leases bracket each op, what residency each slice runs from) is still implicit. F-B13 makes the schedule explicit and proves it is interrupt-safe, lease-balanced, and residency-consistent.

Stages 10 and 10.5 are paired (single RFC, single bead) because the certificate has exactly one input (the Stage 10 product) and one output (the proof), and every downstream consumer — F-B14 cost analyzer, F-B15 backend, F-C3 ScheduleOracle, F-D1 cooperative kernel — requires both. Splitting them would create a synthetic boundary with no contract value.

## Pipeline context

**Inputs (consumed by hash, not redefined):**
- F-B5 `GbInferIR` — value/effect ids; reachability.
- F-B6 `ObservationPlan` — semantic checkpoint pins, trace probe pins.
- F-B7 `RangePlan` — tile sizes, reduction-loop structure.
- F-B8 `StoragePlan` — Materialization per ValueId, LifetimeClass, AliasClassId.
- F-B9 `SramPagePlan` — SramPageBinding, commit boundaries, page-switch budgets.
- F-B10 `RomWindowPlan` — RomWindowBinding, KernelResidency.
- F-B11 `OverlayPlan` — OverlayId, OverlayInstall events, OverlayLeaseShape.
- F-B12 `ArenaPlan` — ArenaSlot byte ranges, NamedArena families.
- F-B2 `ResolvedCompilePolicy` — requested_runtime_modes, knobs.mode, knobs.drift.
- F-B4 `RuntimeChromeBudget` — per-token caps.

**Outputs:**
- `sched_ir.json` — SchedulePack report (modes, slices, leases, epochs, policy, drift monitor).
- `slice_report.json` — per-slice histograms.
- `certs/resource_state.cert.json` — ResourceStateCertificate.
- In-memory `SchedulePack` — consumed by F-B14, F-B15, F-C3, F-D1.

## Core data types (closed surface)

- **SchedSlice** — `{ id, ops: Vec<SchedOp>, hard_cycles_to_safe_point, soft_target_cycles, max_interrupt_latency, resources: ResourceVector, live_wram, live_sram, yield_kind: Micro|Frame|NeedInput|TokenReady|Finished|Fault, yield_check: OnceAtEnd|EveryNTiles{n}|EveryLoadStore|NoPoll, entry_residency: Bank0|Common(BankId)|Expert(ExpertId,BankId), interrupt_policy: Enabled|ShortCriticalSection|Disabled, required_leases, exit_kind: SaveContinuationAndYield|TailCall|EnterIsr|Halt|Fault, semantic_checkpoint_pins, trace_probe_pins, successors }`.
- **ResourceVector** — static tally: bank_switches, sram_page_switches, trace_bytes, persist_bytes, overlay_installs.
- **ResourceLease** — `{ id, kind: RomWindow|SramPage|Overlay|InterruptMask, acquired_in, released_in, yield_safe: bool }`. yield_safe derived from (kind × yield_kind) matrix: RomWindow/SramPage → false; Overlay → conditional; InterruptMask(Disabled|ShortCS) → false.
- **ResidencyEpoch** — `{ id, rom_window, overlay, residency, slices }` — partition of slices by (RomWindow, Overlay, Residency) triple.
- **SchedOp** (variants) — `AcquireLease`, `ReleaseLease`, `OverlayInstall`, `BankSwitch`, `SramPageSwitch`, `KernelCall { spec, tile_index }`, `Load`/`Store`, `Effect`, `TraceProbe`, `SemanticCheckpoint`, `PersistCommit`, `Yield { kind }`, `TailCall`, `EnterIsr`, `Halt`, `Fault`.
- **SchedulePack** — `{ modes: BTreeMap<RuntimeMode, GbSchedIR>, epochs, leases, checkpoint_schema_hash, continuation_abi_hash, switch_policy: ModeSwitchPolicy, drift_monitor: RuntimeDriftMonitor }`.
- **RuntimeMode** — `InteractiveTyping | SteadyStateGeneration | TraceHeavyDebugging | SafeMode`. All modes share checkpoint schema + continuation ABI; differ in tile granularity, yield cadence, trace density.
- **ModeSwitchPolicy** — `{ legal_switch_points, legal_epoch_boundaries, ui_pressure_thresholds, safe_mode_triggers, drift_triggers }`.
- **RuntimeDriftMonitor** — `{ expected: DriftEnvelope, observed: DriftEnvelope (all_none at compile time), consecutive_violations: 0, window_frames }`.
- **DriftEnvelope** — `{ slice_cycles_p95, ui_commit_cycles_p95, trace_drop_rate_pct, persist_overrun_rate_pct }`.
- **DriftTrigger** — `{ metric: SliceCyclesP95|UiCommitCyclesP95|TraceDropRatePct|PersistOverrunRatePct, threshold, action: ShrinkSlices|DropTrace|DemoteMode(mode) }`.
- **ResourceStateCertificate** — body: `{ identity, schedule_pack, lease_balance, yield_safety, isr_visible_residency, overlay_bank_shadow, diagnostics }`.

## Stage 10 construction (deterministic pure function)

1. ResidencyEpoch construction from (RomWindow, Overlay, Residency) triples; canonical sort → EpochIds.
2. Slice formation: walk GbInferIR topologically; cut at tile-loop boundaries crossing `hard_cycles_to_safe_point`, residency transitions, ObservationPlan pins, ModeSwitchPolicy switch points. Canonical SliceIds.
3. Lease binding: per (dominator, dominated) slice pair, derive resource set (RomWindow, SramPage, Overlay, InterruptMask). LeaseIds canonical-sorted.
4. Acquire/Release op insertion (start of acquired_in / end of released_in; nested acquires by LeaseId ascending).
5. Checkpoint pinning from ObservationPlan.
6. Per-mode pack assembly (repeat 2–5 for each requested RuntimeMode with per-mode tile sizes + yield spacing).
7. ModeSwitchPolicy assembly.
8. Drift envelope binding from knobs.drift.
9. Self-consistency.
10. Hash schemas (checkpoint_schema_hash, continuation_abi_hash).

## Stage 10.5 proof (typed lease-flow analysis, NOT runtime simulation)

- **F-LeaseBalance**: per lease, traverse slice graph; per-path acquire_count/release_count counters; terminal slices must have count == 0.
- **F-YieldSafety**: at every `SaveContinuationAndYield` exit, all outstanding leases must have yield_safe == true.
- **F-IsrVisibleResidency** (annotation-driven; F-B15 ReachabilityValidation is the whole-program computed counterpart): slices with `interrupt_policy == Enabled` must (a) have entry_residency ∈ {Bank0, Common(_)} and (b) hold no RomWindow/SramPage leases.
- **F-OverlayBankShadowConsistency**: entry_residency matches epoch; OverlayInstall ops reference epoch's overlay; BankSwitch ops bracketed by lease release+acquire.

## Invariants (named codes)

**Stage 10** — SCHED-*: LiveSlotLifetimeMismatch, HardLatencyBelowInterruptLatency, SoftTargetExceedsHardBound, EpochCoverageGap, EpochOverlap, StorageClassDrifted, OpSequenceMalformed, TerminalOpInconsistentWithExitKind, LoadStoreSlotNotInLiveSet, KernelCallResidencyMismatch, OverlayInstallLeaseShapeUnsatisfied, TailCallEntryResidencyMismatch, TailCallLeaseSetMismatch, EnterIsrInNonIsrSlice, IsrEntrySliceNotBank0, FaultPathResidencyMismatch, CycleBudgetOverflow, IrRealizationMissing, CheckpointPinNotRealized, OverlayInstallNotRealized.

LEASE-*: RequiredLeaseNotAcquired, YieldSafetyTableViolation, Unbalanced, DoubleAcquire, ReleaseWithoutAcquire, PathDivergent, YieldCrossesNonResumable, AcquireReleaseScopeViolation, LeaseIdCollision, LeaseKindMismatchAgainstUpstream.

RES-*: EntryResidencyEpochMismatch, OverlayInstallEpochMismatch, BankSwitchUnbracketed, IsrEnabledHoldsRomWindowLease, IsrEnabledHoldsSramPageLease, IsrEnabledInExpertBank, FaultPathInExpertBank, ResidencyClassMismatchAgainstRomWindowPlan.

**Mode-pack** — MODE-*: KeysMismatch, CheckpointSchemaMismatch, ContinuationAbiMismatch, EntrySliceMissing, PackEmpty, SwitchPointNotInObservationPlan, SwitchEpochBoundaryMissing, RequestedModeNotEmitted, EmittedModeNotRequested, CheckpointPinDivergence.

**Drift** — DRIFT-*: V1MinimumViolated, MetricNotInClosedSet, ActionNotInClosedSet, ObservedNotAllNoneAtCompileTime, ConsecutiveViolationsNonZeroAtCompileTime, DemoteModeTargetNotInPack.

**Liveness** — LIVENESS-*: NoProgressPerToken, CheckpointPinHasNoSemanticCheckpointOp, MaxNoProgressFramesNotInRuntimeChromeBudget.

All Hard. No Soft.

## Cache keys (K10 + K10.5)

```
K10 := DomainHash(..., 'sched_ir.v1', CanonicalJson({
  infer_ir_self_hash, observation_plan_self_hash, range_plan_self_hash,
  storage_plan_self_hash, sram_page_plan_self_hash, rom_window_plan_self_hash,
  overlay_plan_self_hash, arena_plan_self_hash,
  policy_resolution_self_hash, runtime_chrome_budget_self_hash,
  feature_set_hash, ...
}))

K10_5 := DomainHash(..., 'resource_state.cert.v1', CanonicalJson({
  sched_ir_self_hash, feature_set_hash, ...
}))
```

K10 and K10.5 are independent; K10 hit does NOT imply K10.5 skip.

## Interaction with F-B16 (BLOCKED on oracle)

F-B13 v1 emits NO repair proposals; schema reserves forward-compat hooks (`Diagnostic.provenance` may reference `RepairProposalId` in v2; `CompileKnobsSection` provenance entries may reference RepairProposalId in v2). When F-B16 unblocks, expected proposals: `SetSliceCoarsening`, `NarrowTileClasses`, `UpdatePressureThreshold` (slice cycles, interrupt latency, persist bytes).

## Open questions / risks

1. F-D6 multi-mode cadence runtime BLOCKED on oracle question; F-B13 lands schema only.
2. F-B15 ReachabilityValidation is the whole-program computed counterpart to F-IsrVisibleResidency; if F-B15 finds violations, the loop (when F-B16 lands) is the repair path. Until F-B15, annotation-driven check is the upper bound on detection.
3. Calibration NOT consumed at Stage 10; F-B14 charges actual cycles. Intentional separation.
4. `feature_set_hash` placeholder in v1 if F-B17 hasn't landed — acceptable for single-feature-set profiles but may over-share otherwise.

## Test surface (closure gate)

- Fixtures: single-mode (Default), multi-mode (Bringup), multi-mode with legal switch point.
- Rejection-class tests: one synthetic fixture per diagnostic code (60+ fixtures).
- Schema round-trip: sched_ir.v1, slice_report.v1, resource_state.cert.v1; canonical JSON, deny_unknown_fields, self-hash round-trip.
- Determinism: byte-identical regeneration.
- Independent verifier in `gbf-verify` re-runs Stage 10.5 proof obligations (defense-in-depth PO).
- Resource-state forgery: modified certificate fails hash verification.

## How this serves the overarching goal

F-B13 turns "what the program means" (GbInferIR) into "how the cooperative kernel runs it on real hardware with bounded interrupt latency, balanced leases, residency-honest slices, and observable runtime drift" — and emits a typed certificate that proves it. Without F-B13, every later stage (cost analysis, backend codegen, oracle agreement, runtime drift monitoring) is operating on faith.
design:
# F-B13 Implementation design (Stages 10 + 10.5, shipping together)

## Crate / module structure
- **Owner crate:** `gbf-codegen`
- **Modules:** `gbf-codegen::sched_ir` (Stage 10 — construction), `::resource_state` (Stage 10.5 — proof), shared `::types`, `::diagnostics`, `::cache` (K10 + K10.5).
- **Public types (Stage 10):** `SchedSlice`, `SchedOp` (enum), `ResourceVector`, `ResourceLease`, `ResourceLeaseKind`, `ResidencyEpoch`, `EpochId`, `SliceId`, `LeaseId`, `SchedulePack`, `GbSchedIR`, `RuntimeMode`, `ModeSwitchPolicy`, `RuntimeDriftMonitor`, `DriftEnvelope`, `DriftTrigger`.
- **Public types (Stage 10.5):** `ResourceStateCertificate`, `LeaseBalanceSection`, `YieldSafetySection`, `IsrVisibleResidencySection`, `OverlayBankShadowSection`, `ResourceStateIdentitySection`.
- **Public entries:** `build_schedule_pack(inputs) -> SchedulePackProduct` (Stage 10); `validate_resource_state(pack) -> ResourceStateCertificateProduct` (Stage 10.5). Cache wrappers: `run_sched_ir_cached`, `run_resource_state_cached`.

## Implementation phases (ordered; pairs cannot ship separately)

1. **Phase 1 — Type surface (Stage 10).** All public types above. Closed enums for `RuntimeMode`, `YieldKind`, `YieldCheckClass`, `Residency`, `InterruptPolicy`, `ExitKind`, `ResourceLeaseKind`, `SchedOp` variants. Gate: serde round-trip; canonical ordering.
2. **Phase 2 — Input bundle + K10.** Pin 11 upstream hashes per RFC §K10. Gate: F-B17 §9.6.2 injectivity tests (forward/backward/negative).
3. **Phase 3 — Residency epoch construction.** Enumerate `(RomWindowBinding, Option<OverlayId>, Residency)` triples; canonical sort; assign `EpochId`. Gate: epoch coverage total + no overlap.
4. **Phase 4 — Slice formation.** Walk GbInferIR topologically; cut at tile-loop boundaries (RangePlan), residency transitions, ObservationPlan pins, ModeSwitchPolicy switch points. Assign canonical `SliceId`. Gate: terminal-op grammar conformance (pre_ops* tile_loop? post_ops* terminal_op).
5. **Phase 5 — Lease binding.** Per (dominator, dominated) pair, derive resource set; mint canonical `LeaseId`. Gate: every required_lease is acquired by a dominating slice; no LeaseId collision.
6. **Phase 6 — Acquire/Release op insertion.** Start-of-acquired_in, end-of-released_in; nested by LeaseId ascending. Gate: every `AcquireLease` has matching `ReleaseLease`; acquire op present in acquired_in.ops.
7. **Phase 7 — Checkpoint + trace probe pinning.** Walk ObservationPlan; insert `SemanticCheckpoint` / `TraceProbe` ops at aligned slices. Gate: every pin realized.
8. **Phase 8 — Multi-mode pack assembly.** Repeat phases 4–7 per requested `RuntimeMode` (InteractiveTyping, SteadyStateGeneration, TraceHeavyDebugging, SafeMode) with per-mode tile sizes + yield spacing. Gate: shared `checkpoint_schema_hash` + `continuation_abi_hash` across modes.
9. **Phase 9 — ModeSwitchPolicy + RuntimeDriftMonitor.** Assemble switch points, epoch boundaries, UI pressure thresholds, safe-mode triggers, drift triggers from knobs. `observed = DriftEnvelope::all_none()`, `consecutive_violations = 0` at compile time. Gate: DRIFT-* invariants checked.
10. **Phase 10 — Stage-10 self-consistency (SCHED-*/LEASE-*/RES-*/MODE-*/DRIFT-*/LIVENESS-*).** ~60 named codes. Gate: each code has reject fixture.
11. **Phase 11 — Report emission (sched_ir.json + slice_report.json).** Per-slice cycle/resource histograms. Gate: schema round-trip byte-identical.
12. **Phase 12 — Stage-10.5 lease-flow analysis (F-LeaseBalance).** Per lease, per-path acquire/release counter walk. Gate: balance proved or LEASE-* diagnostic.
13. **Phase 13 — Stage-10.5 yield-safety analysis (F-YieldSafety).** At every `SaveContinuationAndYield`, outstanding leases yield_safe == true. Gate: LEASE-YieldCrossesNonResumable on violation.
14. **Phase 14 — Stage-10.5 ISR-visible residency (F-IsrVisibleResidency).** Annotation-driven; F-B15 ReachabilityValidation is the whole-program counterpart. Gate: RES-IsrEnabled* on violation.
15. **Phase 15 — Stage-10.5 overlay/bank-shadow consistency (F-OverlayBankShadowConsistency).** Gate: RES-EntryResidencyEpochMismatch, RES-OverlayInstallEpochMismatch, RES-BankSwitchUnbracketed.
16. **Phase 16 — ResourceStateCertificate emission + K10.5.** Pins all upstream self-hashes. Gate: cert self-hash matches re-validation by `gbf-verify`.
17. **Phase 17 — Cache integration (K10 + K10.5 independent).** K10 hit ≠ K10.5 skip. Gate: cache hit/miss + failure memo for both keys.
18. **Phase 18 — Cross-stage integration.** F-B14 cost analyzer consumes SchedulePack; F-B15 backend reads slice op sequences; F-C3 ScheduleOracle binds emulator state.
19. **Phase 19 — E2E verify-packet.** `scripts/review/f-b13/verify-packet.sh`.

## Structured tracing catalog

**Top-level spans:**
- `gbf.compile.stage10_sched_ir` — fields: `stage_id=10`, `build_id`, `input_identity_hash`, `cache_status`, `outcome`, `mode_count`, `slice_count_per_mode: map`, `epoch_count_per_mode: map`, `lease_count_per_mode: map`, `self_hash`.
- `gbf.compile.stage10_5_resource_state` — fields: `stage_id=10.5`, `sched_ir_self_hash`, `cache_status`, `outcome`, `lease_balance_passes: u32`, `yield_safety_passes: u32`, `isr_residency_passes: u32`, `overlay_bank_shadow_passes: u32`, `self_hash`.

**Events:**
- Common stage start/cache/complete.
- `gbf.compile.sched.epoch_constructed` — fields: `epoch_id`, `mode`, `rom_window`, `overlay`, `residency`, `slice_count`.
- `gbf.compile.sched.slice_formed` — fields: `slice_id`, `mode`, `epoch_id`, `entry_residency`, `interrupt_policy`, `hard_cycles`, `soft_cycles`, `max_interrupt_latency`, `op_count`, `live_wram_count`, `live_sram_count`, `exit_kind`.
- `gbf.compile.sched.lease_bound` — fields: `lease_id`, `kind` (RomWindow|SramPage|Overlay|InterruptMask), `acquired_in`, `released_in`, `yield_safe`.
- `gbf.compile.sched.mode_pack_assembled` — fields: `mode`, `entry_slice`, `slice_count`, `epoch_count`, `lease_count`.
- `gbf.compile.sched.mode_switch_policy` — fields: `legal_switch_point_count`, `legal_epoch_boundary_count`, `safe_mode_trigger_count`, `drift_trigger_count`.
- `gbf.compile.sched.drift_envelope_bound` — fields: `slice_cycles_p95`, `ui_commit_cycles_p95`, `trace_drop_rate_pct`, `persist_overrun_rate_pct`.
- `gbf.compile.resource_state.lease_balance_path_proved` — fields: `lease_id`, `path_terminal_slice`, `acquire_count`, `release_count`, `balanced`.
- `gbf.compile.resource_state.yield_safety_checked` — fields: `slice_id`, `yield_kind`, `outstanding_lease_count`, `all_yield_safe`.
- `gbf.compile.resource_state.isr_residency_checked` — fields: `slice_id`, `entry_residency`, `outstanding_lease_count`, `all_safe`, `computed_reachability_confirmed: false` (v1).
- `gbf.compile.resource_state.overlay_bank_shadow_checked` — fields: `slice_id`, `epoch_id`, `entry_residency_matches`, `overlay_installs_aligned`, `bank_switches_bracketed`.
- `gbf.compile.stage.diagnostic` — closed-enum code emission with detail.

## Test plan

### Unit tests (`crates/gbf-codegen/tests/`)
- `stage10_types_round_trip.rs` — all public types.
- `stage10_op_grammar.rs` — `pre_ops* tile_loop? post_ops* terminal_op`.
- `stage10_residency_epoch_construction.rs` — (RomWindow, Overlay, Residency) triple enumeration + canonical sort.
- `stage10_slice_formation.rs` — boundary cuts at tile + residency + pin + switch point.
- `stage10_lease_binding.rs` — canonical LeaseId assignment + nested acquire ordering.
- `stage10_yield_safety_table.rs` — yield_safe matrix per (kind × yield_kind).
- `stage10_multi_mode_pack.rs` — shared checkpoint_schema_hash + continuation_abi_hash across modes.
- `stage10_mode_switch_policy.rs` — switch points ⊂ ObservationPlan pins; epoch boundaries ⊂ epochs.keys().
- `stage10_drift_envelope.rs` — observed=all_none + consecutive_violations=0 at compile time.
- `stage10_self_consistency.rs` — one test per SCHED-*/LEASE-*/RES-*/MODE-*/DRIFT-*/LIVENESS- code.
- `stage10_5_lease_balance.rs` — per-path counter walk on synthetic graphs.
- `stage10_5_yield_safety.rs` — outstanding-lease check at yield.
- `stage10_5_isr_visible_residency.rs` — Enabled-policy slices reject RomWindow/SramPage leases.
- `stage10_5_overlay_bank_shadow.rs` — bank switch bracketing + epoch alignment.
- `stage10_k10_injectivity.rs` + `stage10_5_k10_5_injectivity.rs` — F-B17 §9.6.2.

### Fixture tests (`fixtures/sched_ir/` + `fixtures/resource_state/`)
- `pass/single_mode_default.json`, `pass/multi_mode_bringup.json`, `pass/multi_mode_with_switch_point.json`.
- `pass/lease_balance_basic.json`, `pass/yield_safe_overlay.json`, `pass/isr_residency_bank0.json`.
- `reject/sched_<code>.json` × ~20 SCHED- codes.
- `reject/lease_<code>.json` × 10 LEASE- codes.
- `reject/res_<code>.json` × 7 RES- codes.
- `reject/mode_<code>.json` × 9 MODE- codes.
- `reject/drift_<code>.json` × 6 DRIFT- codes.
- `reject/liveness_<code>.json` × 3 LIVENESS- codes.

### Property tests
- `prop_slice_id_canonical_order` — topological + canonical.
- `prop_lease_balance_path_invariance` — every reachable path balanced.
- `prop_yield_safe_matrix_consistent` — kind × yield_kind always agrees.
- `prop_mode_pack_keys_match` — modes/epochs/leases keys equal.

### Determinism + cache tests
- `determinism_two_runs_byte_identical` — Stage 10 + Stage 10.5 both byte-identical.
- `cache_hit_path_byte_identical` — both keys independently.
- `k10_hit_k10_5_independent` — K10 hit does NOT imply K10.5 skip.
- `cache_invalidation_on_upstream_change` — change any of 11 input hashes → K10 miss → K10.5 miss.
- `cache_failure_memo_replay` — both keys.

### Cross-stage integration
- `tests/stage10_from_arena_plan.rs` — slot ids resolve.
- `tests/stage10_to_cost_analysis.rs` — F-B14 consumes SchedulePack without modification.
- `tests/stage10_5_to_backend.rs` — F-B15 reachability annotation-vs-computed disagreement detection.
- `tests/stage10_5_independent_verifier.rs` — `gbf-verify` re-runs §9.1 proof obligations; certificate self-hash matches.

### E2E verify-packet (`scripts/review/f-b13/verify-packet.sh`)
1. Run all stage-10 + stage-10.5 unit + fixture tests.
2. Compile sample LM through Stage 10 + 10.5 in single-mode (Default).
3. Repeat in multi-mode (Bringup) with legal switch point.
4. Determinism: 2x build byte-identical (both keys).
5. K10 hit + K10.5 miss scenario verified (independent caching).
6. Independent verifier (`gbf-verify`) re-runs §9.1 proofs; certificate matches.
7. Resource-state forgery test: modify cert; verifier rejects.
8. Cross-stage smoke: F-B14 cost roll-up uses SchedulePack; F-B15 readiness check.
9. Emit `f_b13_packet.json` with per-mode slice/lease/epoch counts, cert hashes, verifier agreement, diagnostics.
10. Exit 0 on green.

## CLI / debug integration
- `gbf compile --stage=sched_ir --inputs=<dir>` and `--stage=resource_state`.

## F-B11: GbSchedIR + ResourceStateValidation (Stages 10, 10.5)

### What this is

`GbInferIR` says **what**; `GbSchedIR` says **how** (planv0.md line 1361). Slices with `hard_cycles_to_safe_point`, `max_interrupt_latency`, `ResourceVector` (bank_switches/sram_page_switches/trace_bytes/persist_bytes/overlay_installs), `live_wram` / `live_sram`, `YieldKind`, `InterruptPolicy`, `required_leases`, `exit_kind`. A `CompiledBuild` may carry a `SchedulePack` keyed by `RuntimeMode` (multi-mode is the future-self switch question).

`ResourceStateValidation` (Stage 10.5) proves leases are balanced, no yield crosses a non-resumable lease, no ISR-visible path depends on leased switchable state, overlay/bank-shadow assumptions match declared residency.

### Why this matters

This is where coroutine ABI realism becomes fact. Slices have proven worst-case interrupt latency, proven liveness properties (`progress_epoch` advances at semantic-checkpoint granularity), proven lease lifecycle.

Emits `certs/resource_state.cert.json`.

### Design sketch

```rust
pub struct SchedSlice {
    pub id: SliceId,
    pub ops: Vec<SchedOp>,
    pub hard_cycles_to_safe_point: CycleBudget,
    pub max_interrupt_latency: CycleBudget,
    pub resources: ResourceVector,
    pub yield_kind: YieldKind,
    pub interrupt_policy: InterruptPolicy,
    pub required_leases: Vec<LeaseId>,
    pub exit_kind: ExitKind,
}

pub struct SchedulePack {
    pub modes: BTreeMap<RuntimeMode, GbSchedIR>,
    pub epochs: BTreeMap<RuntimeMode, Vec<ResidencyEpoch>>,
    pub checkpoint_schema_hash: Hash256,
    pub switch_policy: ModeSwitchPolicy,
}
```

### Cross-feature deps

- F-B10 ArenaPlan
- F-A3.5 ResourceLease + InterruptPolicy
- F-B14 FeasibilityRefinementLoop (consumes proposals from here)

### Confidence: HIGH on shape, MEDIUM on multi-mode (oracle question pending)

title: Generalize FrontierRecommendation B and add FrontierLeaderVariant
description:
# Goal

Make FrontierRecommendation B reachable whenever any LinearState variant beats BoundedKv, not only when L_MT4 specifically wins. Record which variant won via a new \`frontier_leader_variant\` field.

# Background / Why

The RFC trains both L_FIX1 and L_MT4. H5 explicitly allows L_FIX1 to become the LinearState representative if L_MT4 disappoints. But the original FrontierRecommendation definition fixed B = "LinearState-MultiTimescale-leading" tied to L_MT4. If L_FIX1 beat BoundedKv but L_MT4 lagged, the rubric collapsed to Tie even though LinearState clearly led — an inaccurate frontier verdict.

# Change

In gbf-artifact (FrontierReport schema) + gbf-policy (§8.5 algorithm):

  - Add type FrontierLeaderVariant = Null | VariantId.
  - Add field \`frontier_leader_variant: FrontierLeaderVariant\` to FrontierReport.
  - Redefine B:
      \"at least one LinearState variant beats BoundedKv strictly on
       val_bpc_ternary by >= 0.05 bpc, passes v0_success, and has
       shadow_compile_ok_at_end = true.\"
  - Tie-break for frontier_leader_variant when B holds:
      1. val_bpc_ternary asc
      2. encoded_rom_byte_cost asc (when present)
      3. VariantId lex asc
  - Update §8.5 dispatcher to compute and emit the leader.

# Why this matters

H8 already permits LinearState to win in the surprise direction; the FrontierRecommendation rubric must reflect that without baking in a specific variant identity.

# Considerations

  - Pass-with-B-frontier consumers (downstream Act II selection, reporting) must read frontier_leader_variant; otherwise they default to L_MT4 wrongly.
  - Schema: do not break Pass-with-A-frontier / Pass-with-tie — those keep frontier_leader_variant = Null.
  - The B predicate keeps BoundedKv as Act II primary (D8); B is a license, not a winner.

# Verification

  - Three fixture FrontierReports: A (BoundedKv leads), B with L_MT4 leader, B with L_FIX1 leader.
  - Tie path: neither LinearState wins by >= 0.05 -> frontier_leader_variant=Null.
  - JSON canonical round-trip.

# Related RFC sections

  §1 (FrontierRecommendation, FrontierLeaderVariant), §D5, §8.5, §13.7 FrontierReport.

# Blocks

  B17 (F14 pareto-broken falsifier expects FrontierRecommendation B semantics).

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## F3: TernaryWeightPlan — Explicit Ternary Numeric Semantics

### Background

The plan defines WeightEncoding::Ternary2 as "2-bit packed ternary, four weights per byte." This is correct for storage but insufficient for specifying the deployed numeric behavior. Ternary quantization involves more than just {-1, 0, +1} packing:

1. **Scale granularity**: Are scales per-tensor, per-output-row, or per-group? This changes quality, byte cost, and accumulator behavior dramatically.
2. **Scale format**: Q8_8, Q4_4, or Pow2? This determines scale tensor size and accumulator precision requirements.
3. **Threshold schedule**: How are the ternary boundaries chosen? Fixed, globally annealed then per-row refined, or learned per group?

### The byte math

For a concrete example with the plan's default (d_model=128, d_ff=224, PerOutputRow scales, Q8_8):
- Expert up projection (128→224): ceil(128*224/4) = 7168 ternary bytes + 224*2 = 448 scale bytes = 7616 bytes
- Expert down projection (224→128): ceil(224*128/4) = 7168 ternary bytes + 128*2 = 256 scale bytes = 7424 bytes
- Total two-matrix expert: 7616 + 7424 = 15040 bytes + metadata
- This fits in a 16 KiB bank with ~1.3 KiB margin — but ONLY because we specified PerOutputRow Q8_8, not PerGroup(16) Q8_8 which would cost more

If you used per-tensor scales instead: 7168 + 2 = 7170 per projection, total ~14342 bytes — more margin but worse quality.
If you used per-group(16) Q8_8 scales: additional (128*224/16)*2 = 3584 scale bytes per projection — won't fit in one bank.

The TernaryWeightPlan makes these choices explicit so the byte formula is computable and the compiler can verify fit without guessing.

### Why this must be in the artifact, not just the compiler

The scale tensors and threshold parameters are part of the deployed model's identity. Two models with identical ternary weight bits but different scale granularity/format produce different inference results. Therefore TernaryWeightPlan must be referenced by QuantSpec inside ArtifactCore.

### Confidence: VERY HIGH

This is a mathematical necessity, not a design preference. Without it, the byte formulas are uncomputable and the export/compile agreement is unverifiable.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## F-G3: Decode

### What this is

`DecodeMode`, `DecodePolicy`, `DecodeCapabilitySet`, `DecodeTransformSet`, `SessionProfile`. Decode policy is **session-level** declared in `SessionProfile`; `ArtifactCore` only declares supported modes via `DecodeCapabilitySet`.

### Why this matters

Per planv0.md line 703: oracles, compiler, runtime, and harness all need the same decode + RNG semantics at session/run level. `DecodeCapabilitySet` keeps `ArtifactCore` mode-agnostic.

### Design sketch

```rust
pub enum DecodeMode {
    Greedy,
    TopK { k: u16 },
    TopP { p: f32 },
    Temperature { t: f32 },
}

pub struct DecodePolicy { ... }
pub struct DecodeCapabilitySet { pub modes: BTreeSet<DecodeMode> }
pub struct SessionProfile {
    pub decode: DecodePolicy,
    pub rng_seed: u64,
    pub max_tokens: Option<u32>,
}
```

### Cross-feature deps

- gbf-artifact (DecodeCapabilitySet in core, SessionProfile in aux/session)
- F-C1, F-C2 oracles (need shared decode semantics)
- F-D2 harness (SetSession sets SessionProfile)

### Confidence: HIGH

title: T6.1: Implement MoE-on-FFN-path-only with shared sequence-state
description: In gbf-model, the model topology struct should have a per-block config: MoeBlockConfig { has_moe_ffn: bool, shared_sequence_block: SharedSequenceConfig }. When has_moe_ffn is false, the block uses a shared dense FFN (non-expert). The sequence-state update path (attention/recurrent/linear) is always shared, never routed. This keeps routing complexity to one router call per MoE block and avoids doubling bank-switch cost.
acceptance_criteria: cargo check -p gbf-model exits 0; cargo test -p gbf-model -- block passes; MoE only on FFN path; Sequence-state always shared
close_reason: Implemented topology/config contract with review fixes; see closure comment.

## Agent Instructions

```rust
pub struct MoeBlockConfig {
    pub has_moe_ffn: bool,
    pub shared_sequence_block: SequenceBlockConfig,
}
```
- Key architectural rule: **Sequence-state update path is ALWAYS shared, NEVER routed.**
  - The attention/state-mixing block is shared across all experts
  - Only the FFN path goes through MoE routing
- Block structure: `input -> shared_sequence_block -> [MoE FFN | dense FFN] -> output`
- Blocks without MoE (`has_moe_ffn: false`) use a standard dense FFN.


Implemented bd-a8k as a model-topology/configuration bead.

Scope owned by this bead:
- Backend-independent topology structs for per-block shared sequence state plus FFN-only routing.
- Dense-vs-MoE FFN selection through an enum-backed config, with `has_moe_ffn()` as a derived query.
- A topology oracle that emits `SharedSequence -> DenseFfn` for dense blocks and `SharedSequence -> Router -> MoeFfn` for MoE blocks.
- Constructor validation for nonzero dimensions, nonempty model block lists, matching sequence/FFN `d_model`, and consistent model `d_model` across blocks.

Scope explicitly not claimed:
- No tensor forward implementation or Burn module path.
- No actual LinearState or BoundedKv sequence-state math; `SharedSequenceKind` is a topology marker only.
- No block-selection policy for alternating/middle MoE blocks; that remains with bd-31r.
- No default expert MLP implementation; that remains with bd-x75.
- No optional shared dense branch inside MoE expert blocks; that remains separate from the dense fallback path here.
- No artifact/export serialization contract.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Why this bead exists

F-S1.21..24 + F-S1.27..29 each define scripts and gates, but those
scripts must be INVOKED somewhere. Without an actual CI workflow file,
the "closure-blocking CI gates" of §16.6 are aspirational — they never
run on PRs.

This bead wires the F-S1 CI gates into actual GitHub Actions (or
equivalent) workflows. CI is the *only* layer that blocks closure of
bd-12pl in practice; everything else is a local-developer convenience.

## Scope

Three workflow files under `.github/workflows/`:

  - `s1-pr.yml` — runs on every PR touching s1 paths:
      jobs (in parallel where possible):
        - cargo-fmt + cargo-clippy --workspace -- -D warnings
        - cargo build -p gbf-experiments
        - cargo build -p gbf-experiments --no-default-features --features ablation
        - cargo build -p gbf-train --features qat,qat-ablation  (must FAIL)
        - cargo test -p gbf-experiments
        - cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features falsify --test falsification
        - cargo test -p gbf-experiments --test oracle
        - cargo test -p gbf-experiments --test canonical_json
        - cargo test -p gbf-experiments --test integration
        - cargo test -p gbf-experiments --test e2e
        - scripts/s1_preregistration_check.sh
        - scripts/s1_determinism_check.sh --fast    (tiny fixture)
        - scripts/s1_isolation_check.sh   --fast    (tiny fixture)
      Job timeout: 30 min total per matrix entry.
      Concurrency group: cancel-in-progress on rebases.
      Trigger paths: gbf-experiments/**, gbf-train/**, gbf-policy/**,
        gbf-data/**, gbf-artifact/**, gbf-foundation/**, gbf-cli/**,
        scripts/s1_*.sh, fixtures/corpora/tinystories.toml,
        docs/experiments/S1-report.md.

  - `s1-nightly.yml` — runs at 03:00 UTC daily on main:
      jobs:
        - Full S1 protocol (F-S1.28): 5-seed Phase A run + ablation
          seed 0 + score + baseline + neg-test + oracle + ablation.
        - Run scripts/s1_determinism_check.sh (full TinyStories)
        - Run scripts/s1_isolation_check.sh   (full TinyStories)
        - Upload safetensors checkpoints + run-logs as workflow artifacts
          (retention 90 days).
        - Post a brief summary comment (or status check) with per-seed
          val_bpc + outcome.
      Job timeout: 12 hours.

  - `s1-on-demand.yml` — workflow_dispatch trigger (manual):
      Same as nightly but can target an arbitrary git ref. Used to
      reproduce historical reports against their pinned rfc_revision.

- Workflow secrets / env handling:
    Each step that runs a binary uses `env -i` + the F-S1.04 env_exact
    to satisfy env_forbidden_unless_listed.
- Concurrency:
    s1-nightly and s1-on-demand share a concurrency group; only one
    full pipeline runs at a time to avoid disk contention.
- Artifact retention:
    PR run-logs: 7 days
    Nightly checkpoints + run-logs + reports: 90 days
    On-demand: 30 days

## Considerations

- Avoid hidden CI-specific behavior (Rep-8). Workflows must call the
  same scripts a developer runs locally; no inline divergent logic.
- Document the workflow file structure in F-S1.34's implementation guide.
- Future-self: if migrating away from GitHub Actions, this bead is the
  only place a translation is needed; everything below is shell scripts.

## Testing

- `act` (or the equivalent) dry-run of s1-pr.yml on a sample PR.
- Dummy "broken" PR test: introduce a deliberate failure (e.g., un-pin
  a sha256 in the manifest) and verify s1-pr.yml fails the
  appropriate job.

## RFC anchors

- §16.6 CI gates that block bd-12pl closure
- §16.5 Pre-registration CI
- §13 O1, O2, O5, O9

title: F-S2.01: gbf-experiments s2::* scaffolding + s2-full feature + core notation types
description:
Goal
====
Establish the gbf-experiments::s2 module subtree, the s2-full / s2-ablation
Cargo features, and ALL core S2 notation types (PhaseKind*, GlobalStep,
PhaseLocalStep, HardnessTriple, RouterTrainMode incl. NoRouter,
PhaseEffectiveLambda, S2BuildKind, HypothesisStatus, FailureKindS2,
Q8_8Scale, DistillTemperature/DistillLossNats/GapBpc aliases). Per F-S2
RFC §1 + §15.1 + §16.6.

Why this matters
================
This is the root of every F-S2 bead. The s2-full feature is the ONLY
S2 closure-relevant Cargo feature on gbf-experiments: s2_fp_full and
s2_ternary_nodistill are RUNTIME BuildKinds inside the same compiled
binary (RFC §16.2/§16.3 + AS2-9). The s2-ablation feature is the only
compile-time alternate identity because it forwards qat-ablation. The
notation types here are the load-bearing vocabulary of D1, D2, D5,
D10, D13 and every artifact schema in §9.

IMPLEMENTER START-HERE NOTE: F-S2.01 and F-S2.23 (test scaffolding) have
NO deps on each other and BOTH gate everything else. Land them in
parallel.

Scope
=====
- Cargo features on gbf-experiments:
    s2-full: forwards burn-adapter + gbf-train/qat (S1 inheritance from
      bd-2hze, now closed);
    s2-ablation: forwards gbf-train/qat-ablation + gbf-train/burn-adapter,
      with the gbf-train dep declared default-features = false on this
      feature path (RFC §16.6) so gbf-train/qat is not enabled accidentally.
    compile_error! at gbf-experiments crate root when s2-full ⊕ s2-ablation
      are simultaneously enabled.
- Module declarations (empty, filled by later beads): s2::run, s2::distill,
  s2::score, s2::ablation, s2::gap, s2::loss_grad_flow, s2::linearstate_smoke,
  s2::phase_transition_integ, s2::oracle_re_run, s2::schema, s2::report,
  s2::cli, s2::manifest, s2::rng, s2::device_profile.
- Types in gbf-experiments::s2::schema:
    enum PhaseKindS2 { PhaseA, PhaseB, PhaseC, PhaseD }
    enum PhaseKindFixture { PhaseA, PhaseB, PhaseC, PhaseD, PhaseE }
    type GlobalStep = u64; type PhaseLocalStep = u64; type PhaseStep = GlobalStep
    enum QuantHardness { Off, Soft, Hard }  (re-export gbf-model)
    enum RouterTrainMode { NoRouter, SoftTop1, HardTop1 }
    struct HardnessTriple { expert_qat, activation_qat, norm_qat }
    struct PhaseEffectiveLambda { 8 lambda fields }
    type DistillTemperature = f32; type DistillLossNats = f32;
    type DistillLossNats64 = f64; type GapBpc = f64; type Q8_8Scale = u16;
    enum S2BuildKind {
      s2_ternary_full, s2_fp_full, s2_ternary_nodistill, s2_ablation
    }
    enum HypothesisStatus { Confirmed, Refuted, NotEvaluatedDueToPriorGate(String) }
    enum FailureKindS2 (full set per F-S2 RFC §1)
    NO s2_phase_a build variant — Phase A teacher checkpoints belong to
    their parent build kind.
- All types serde-deriveable, S1CanonicalJson round-trip byte-equal
  (inherits the canonical encoder from bd-5lrn, now closed).

Logging contract
================
This bead is mostly type-only and emits no per-step events at runtime.
The only required tracing event is module load:

  tracing::info!(event="s2::module_loaded", schema_count=<N>,
    type_count=<M>, s2_full_enabled=<bool>, s2_ablation_enabled=<bool>)
  emitted once from a #[ctor]-style mod init or from the first call to
  any s2::* function.

This event is captured by gbf-test::tracing_capture so the integration
smoke can assert the s2 module was wired in correctly.

Unit tests
==========
- File: gbf-experiments/tests/canonical_json_s2.rs (extends bd-3kqp pattern)
  Scenarios:
    * Each enum variant round-trips through S1CanonicalJson byte-equal.
    * HardnessTriple field order is stable (expert / activation / norm)
      regardless of input struct field order.
    * PhaseEffectiveLambda has all 8 lambda fields present in canonical
      JSON; reordering field declarations does not change canonical bytes.
    * S2BuildKind round-trips as kebab-case strings:
        s2_ternary_full → "s2-ternary-full" (etc).
    * HypothesisStatus::NotEvaluatedDueToPriorGate(String) round-trips
      with reason preserved byte-equal.

- File: gbf-experiments/tests/types_proptest_s2.rs
  Property tests (proptest, using arb_* strategies from F-S2.23):
    * arb_phase_kind_s2 → canonical JSON round-trip.
    * arb_hardness_triple → field-order stability.
    * arb_phase_effective_lambda → no NaN serialization (rejects at
      construction with explicit error per CLAUDE.md
      "Training Loss Beads" finite-validation rule).
    * arb_s2_build_kind → no unknown variants.

- File: gbf-experiments/tests/feature_compile_s2.rs (trybuild)
  Compile-fail cases:
    * cargo build --features s2-full,s2-ablation → expected
      compile_error! with stable diagnostic "S2 feature mutex violated".

Golden artifacts (insta snapshots, regenerable via `cargo insta accept`):
  gbf-experiments/tests/snapshots/types_s2__hardness_triple_off.snap
  gbf-experiments/tests/snapshots/types_s2__phase_effective_lambda_default.snap
  gbf-experiments/tests/snapshots/types_s2__build_kind_serialization.snap
These golden files are checked into the repo and form the regression
oracle for the S2 ABI surface.

E2E verification
================
- CLI invocation: not applicable (no CLI surface).
- Cargo gate (s2-pr workflow):
    cargo build -p gbf-experiments --features s2-full              succeeds.
    cargo build -p gbf-experiments --no-default-features --features s2-ablation
                                                                    succeeds.
    cargo build -p gbf-experiments --features s2-full,s2-ablation   fails
      at compile time with the expected diagnostic.
    cargo check -p gbf-experiments --features s2-full exercises every
      s2::* module declaration without orphan-module warnings.
    cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s2-full --test canonical_json_s2
      passes.
- Structured log assertion: the integration_s2 e2e smoke (F-S2.22)
  captures stderr and asserts at least one
  event="s2::module_loaded" event appears with s2_full_enabled=true.

Considerations
==============
- Do NOT introduce gbf-train/qat-fp-only, gbf-experiments/s2-fp-only,
  or gbf-experiments/s2-nodistill features. Those identities are runtime
  BuildKinds.
- Future build-kind additions require a pass_version_S2 bump (Rep-S2-5).
- Future enum variant additions require golden artifact regeneration +
  pass_version_S2 bump.

References
==========
F-S2 RFC §1 Core notation, §15.1 Crate map, §15.5, §16.1-§16.6.
Inherits from F-S1 closed beads: bd-1pnu (workspace scaffolding),
bd-2hze (qat features), bd-5lrn (canonical JSON), bd-3kqp (schema test
patterns), bd-2i00 (test scaffolding).
Merges (former separate beads): F-S2.01 (scaffolding) + F-S2.02 (types).

title: F-B8 T19: Overlay-eligibility lens IsOverlayEligible(sp, b) for F-B11 (reads provenance op_output_role, not GbInferIR)
description:
# Overlay-eligibility lens for F-B11

## Why a lens

F-B11 OverlayPlan is the next-but-one downstream stage. It needs to enumerate candidate overlay objects without re-reading `GbInferIR` (the IR is large; re-reading would defeat the cache). The lens is a typed predicate over `StoragePlan.bindings ∪ StoragePlan.provenance.bindings`.

v2 review caught that the v1 lens called `ValueRoleOf(b.value)`, but `StorageBinding` does not carry role. Role appears only in `BindingProvenance.op_output_role`. So the lens must take the whole plan, not just a binding.

## Deliverable

```rust
pub fn is_overlay_eligible(sp: &StoragePlan, b: &StorageBinding) -> bool {
    matches!(b.materialization,
             Materialization::Materialize {
                 class: StorageClass::RomConst, ..
             })
    && sp.provenance.bindings.get(&b.value)
        .and_then(|p| p.op_output_role.as_ref())
        .map_or(false, |r| matches!(r,
            ValueRole::LutFragment
          | ValueRole::ExpertWeight
          | ValueRole::RouterWeight))
}
```

Note the absence of `OverlayRegionSizeCeiling(policy)` or `overlay_excluded_set(policy)` — those policy fields are intentionally not in T5's available surface (v2 cleanup). If a later RFC adds them, this lens grows; F-B11 cannot filter on them today.

## Acceptance

* Unit test: an expert weight binding returns true; a router score binding returns false; a `Materialize{class:WramHot, ..}` binding returns false even with `op_output_role = LutFragment`.
* Unit test: when provenance is missing `op_output_role`, the lens returns false (not panics).

## Anti-patterns

* Do not call `ValueRoleOf(b.value)` — that requires re-reading `GbInferIR`.
* Do not reference unavailable policy fields.

Depends on: T15, T16.
design:
## Test Plan

### Lens admits the right RomConst roles

* `lens_admits_expert_weight_rom_const` — synthetic plan with ExpertWeight + RomConst binding → lens returns true.
* `lens_admits_lut_fragment_rom_const` — same shape.
* `lens_admits_router_weight_rom_const` — same.
* `lens_rejects_norm_param_rom_const` — NormParam is RomConst but NOT in the overlay-eligible role set. Lens returns false.
* `lens_rejects_embedding_table_rom_const` — same; EmbeddingTable not in the set.
* `lens_rejects_non_rom_const_materialization` — Materialize{WramHot, ..} → false.
* `lens_rejects_recompute_binding` — Recompute → false.
* `lens_rejects_persist_binding` — Persist → false.

### Provenance source path (the v2 fix)

* `lens_reads_op_output_role_from_provenance` — synthetic binding whose `StoragePlan.provenance.bindings[v].op_output_role = Some(ExpertWeight)` → lens returns true. Confirms the lens does NOT call `ValueRoleOf(b.value)` (which would require re-reading GbInferIR).
* `lens_handles_missing_provenance_role` — if `op_output_role = None` → lens returns false (not panic).
* `lens_does_not_re_read_gb_infer_ir` — trybuild compile-fail if anyone refactors the lens to take `&GbInferIR`.

### Unavailable policy fields (v1 cleanup)

* `lens_does_not_reference_overlay_region_size_ceiling` — compile-fail if `OverlayRegionSizeCeiling(policy)` appears in the lens source.
* `lens_does_not_reference_overlay_excluded_set` — same for `overlay_excluded_set(policy)`.

### Defensive

* `lens_returns_false_when_provenance_map_missing_entry` — gracefully handles a binding without an associated provenance entry; returns false.

### Cumulative on routed-FFN fixture

* `routed_ffn_overlay_candidates_match_expected` — drive `synth::tiny_routed_ffn()`; enumerate `bindings.iter().filter(|b| is_overlay_eligible(sp, b))`; assert the result matches a checked-in golden list of ValueIds.

title: T-A1.6: Layout + branch relaxation + structured-op lowering
description: Implements layout.rs (interval allocator, reserved ranges, alignment_padding, StrictOneExpertPerBank profile), relax.rs (iterative-monotone JR→JP / per-target far-call thunks via ThunkMaterializer; CallReachability::NearOnly is the default and rejects cross-bank), and the new lowering.rs module (PreLayoutOpLowering / LegalizationOpLowering, LoweredFragment, LegalizedFragment, ResolvedThunkRequest, link::resolve_runtime_externals, stubs gated by cfg(feature=stub-runtime)). Encoder consumes the legalized output; relax sizes via Instr::byte_len(), not the encoder.
design:
## T-A1.6: Layout + branch relaxation + lowering

**Target crate**: `gbf-asm`
**Target file(s)**: `gbf-asm/src/layout.rs`, `gbf-asm/src/relax.rs`, `gbf-asm/src/lowering.rs` (new)
**Reference**: `history/rfcs/F-A1-gbf-asm.md` §3.1, §4, §6, §7.

### Background

Layout assigns concrete CPU-visible addresses to sections within ROM banks; relaxation legalizes branches once placement is known and lowers placement-dependent `LegalizationOp` values inside the same fixed-point loop. The new `lowering.rs` module owns the seam between authoring intent (`PreLayoutOp`, `LegalizationOp`) and concrete `Instr`s.

This task replaces the prior pseudo-op story with the RFC's typed split:

- **`PreLayoutOp`** — placement-independent intent; lowered before layout in `lowering.rs`.
- **`LegalizationOp`** — placement-dependent intent; lowered inside `relax::relax_and_legalize` after final bank/address facts are known.
- **Encoder is downstream and rejects nothing**: it consumes `&LegalizedSection`, which physically does not have `pre_layout_ops`, `legalization_ops`, or `branches` arrays.

### `lowering.rs`

```rust
pub trait PreLayoutOpLowering {
    fn lower(&self, op: &PreLayoutOp, ctx: &LoweringContext<'_>)
        -> Result<LoweredFragment, LoweringError>;
}
pub trait LegalizationOpLowering {
    fn lower(&self, op: &LegalizationOp, ctx: &LegalizationContext<'_>)
        -> Result<LegalizedFragment, LoweringError>;
}

pub struct LoweredFragment {
    pub labels:           Vec<FragmentItem<Label>>,
    pub instrs:           Vec<FragmentItem<Instr>>,
    pub data_blocks:      Vec<FragmentItem<DataBlock>>,
    pub alignments:       Vec<FragmentItem<Align>>,
    pub legalization_ops: Vec<FragmentItem<LegalizationOp>>,
    pub branches:         Vec<FragmentItem<SymbolicBranch>>,
}

pub struct LegalizedFragment {
    pub labels:         Vec<FragmentItem<Label>>,
    pub instrs:         Vec<FragmentItem<Instr>>,
    pub data_blocks:    Vec<FragmentItem<DataBlock>>,
    pub alignments:     Vec<FragmentItem<Align>>,
    pub branches:       Vec<FragmentItem<SymbolicBranch>>,
    pub thunk_requests: Vec<ResolvedThunkRequest>,
}

pub struct ResolvedThunkRequest {
    pub thunk_symbol:    SymbolName,
    pub target:          SymbolName,
    pub callee_bank:     BankIndex,
    pub target_cpu_addr: u16,
    pub policy:          ThunkPolicy,
}
```

`LoweredFragment` MUST NOT carry a thunk-request field — pre-layout lowering
runs before bank assignment and cannot know `callee_bank`. Stubs ship as
`StubPreLayoutOpLowering` / `StubLegalizationOpLowering`, gated by
`cfg(feature = "stub-runtime")`. Stub lowerers emit `SymbolicBranch::Call`,
not concrete `Instr::Call` (operand resolution belongs to relax).

Every fragment is revalidated against the source section's
`SectionPrivilege` before splice; `LoweredSection` and `LegalizedSection`
both retain `privilege`.

### `layout.rs`

```rust
pub fn layout_into_banks(
    sections: Vec<LoweredSection>,
    profile: PlacementProfile,
    target: &TargetProfile,
    pinned: &[PinnedPlacement],
) -> Result<LayoutPlan, LayoutError>;

pub enum PlacementProfile {
    StrictOneExpertPerBank,                 // renamed from StrictOnePerBank
    Budgeted { reserve_bytes_per_bank: u16 },
    PackedExperts,
}

pub struct PlacedSection {
    pub id: SectionId,
    pub space: AddressSpace,
    pub bank: BankIndex,
    pub cpu_start: u16,                     // CPU-visible, NOT a ROM file offset
    pub final_size: u16,
    pub estimated_size: u16,
    pub alignment_padding: BTreeMap<ItemOrder, u16>, // concrete; encoder reads, never recomputes
}

impl PlacedSection {
    pub fn cpu_end_exclusive(&self) -> u32; // u32 arithmetic everywhere
    pub fn rom_file_offset(&self) -> Result<Option<usize>, LayoutError>;
}

pub struct ReservedRange {
    pub bank: BankIndex,
    pub start: u16,
    pub end_inclusive: u16,
    pub reason: ReservedRangeReason,
}

pub enum ReservedRangeReason {
    CartridgeHeader, ResetVector, InterruptVector, ThunkPool, UserPinned,
}
```

Layout uses an **interval allocator**, not a single cursor per bank. Bank 0
is seeded with reserved ranges (`$0100..=$014F` cartridge header,
reset/interrupt vectors not occupied by pinned sections, downward-growing
thunk pool). Pinned vs. unpinned placements are inserted in order; the
allocator records concrete padding into `PlacedSection::alignment_padding`.

`LayoutPlan` JSON serialization handles `BTreeMap<BankIndex, _>` via a
canonical string key form (`"rom:0"`, `"sram:1"`, `"wram"`, etc.) — see RFC
§11.4. `serde_json` rejects non-string map keys at runtime, so this is gated.

### `relax.rs`

```rust
pub fn relax_and_legalize(
    sections: Vec<LoweredSection>,
    plan: LayoutPlan,
    legalizer: &dyn LegalizationOpLowering,
    materializer: &dyn ThunkMaterializer,
) -> Result<(Vec<LegalizedSection>, LayoutPlan, SymbolTable), RelaxError>;

pub trait ThunkMaterializer {
    fn estimated_thunk_size(&self, request: &ResolvedThunkRequest) -> u16;
    fn materialize_thunk(
        &self,
        request: &ResolvedThunkRequest,
        ctx: &ThunkMaterializationContext<'_>,
    ) -> Result<LegalizedSection, LoweringError>;
}
```

- Initial assumption: every `JR` is in range, every `CALL` is intra-bank.
- Each branch rechecks legality after symbol resolution against the current `LayoutPlan`.
- **`SymbolicBranch::Call` carries `CallReachability`**:
  - `NearOnly` (default for `Builder::call`): cross-bank → `RelaxError::CrossBankBranchUnsupported`.
  - `AutoFar { lease_chain }` (only via `Builder::far_call` / `LegalizationOp::FarCall`): may rewrite to `CALL <thunk>` and allocate one thunk per cross-bank target symbol (`runtime.banking.thunk.<target_symbol>`).
- **One thunk per target symbol** — the thunk body bakes in `(callee_bank, target_cpu_addr)` because a 3-byte `CALL` carries only one 16-bit operand. Two call sites that share a target share a thunk.
- Relax owns thunk allocation; `ThunkMaterializer` owns thunk body bytes/ABI. The materializer must report any size dependence on its own assigned address; otherwise the fixed-point bound is invalid.
- Relax uses `Instr::byte_len()` and explicit sizing policies — **not** the encoder — for size queries.
- Iteration cap: `1 + relaxable_branch_count + unique_cross_bank_call_target_count`.

### Forward-declared runtime externals (§2.7.10, §4.4)

`SymbolKind::ExternalRuntime` represents stub-runtime placeholders. A new
linking step is owned by `lowering.rs` (RFC §2.7.10):

```rust
pub fn resolve_runtime_externals(
    sections: Vec<LoweredSection>,
    symbols: SymbolTable,
    runtime: &dyn RuntimeMaterializer,
) -> Result<(Vec<LoweredSection>, SymbolTable), LinkError>;
```

Every required external must be replaced with a `Defined` symbol before
final relax. A surviving external is `LinkError::UnresolvedExternalRuntime`,
not a relax or encode error.

### Errors

```rust
pub enum LayoutError {
    SectionTooBig { id, size, bank_capacity },
    NoBankFits { id, role },
    Bank0ThunkOverflow { requested, available },
    PinnedPlacementCollision { section_a, section_b },
    PinnedPlacementOutOfRange { section_id, start, bank_capacity },
    DuplicatePinned { section_id },
    InvalidBankCount { requested, max_for_mbc5 },
    AlignmentOutOfRange { section_id, align },
    ReservedRangeCollision { section_id, range },
    BankSpaceMismatch { section_id, space, bank },
    CpuAddressOutOfRange { section_id, space, cpu_start },
}

pub enum RelaxError {
    NoFixedPoint { iters: u8 },
    ThunkPoolExhausted { requested, capacity },
    UnresolvedSymbol { name, used_in },
    InvalidRelativeOffset { offset: i32 },
    CrossBankBranchUnsupported { used_in, source_bank, target, target_bank },
}

pub enum LinkError {
    UnresolvedExternalRuntime { name: SymbolName, used_in: SectionId },
}
```

comments.text:
## T-A1.6: Layout + branch relaxation

**Target crate**: `gbf-asm`
**Target file(s)**: `gbf-asm/src/layout.rs`, `gbf-asm/src/relax.rs`
**Reference**: `planv0.md` §"PlacedRom" (line 1536), §"Assembly eDSL".

### Background

Layout assigns concrete addresses to sections within ROM banks; relaxation rewrites branches when the chosen layout pushes targets out of range. On LR35902:
- `JR` is a signed 8-bit relative jump (`±127` bytes).
- `JP` is absolute 16-bit.
- Cross-bank calls require a far-call thunk because `CALL` is intra-address-space.

This task implements that legalization. The full PlacedRom pass (with placement profiles, bank packing, etc.) is Epic B; this is the gbf-asm-level mechanism.

### Implementation Notes

`layout.rs`:

```rust
pub struct LayoutPlan {
    pub sections: Vec<PlacedSection>,
}

pub struct PlacedSection {
    pub id: SectionId,
    pub bank: u16,                           // 0 for fixed, 1..=N for switchable
    pub start: u16,                          // address within bank
    pub size: u16,
}

pub fn layout_into_banks(
    sections: Vec<Section>,
    profile: PlacementProfile,
) -> Result<LayoutPlan, LayoutError>;
```

`PlacementProfile` is `StrictOnePerBank | Budgeted | PackedExperts` (`planv0.md` line 1540). The Bringup default is `StrictOnePerBank`.

`relax.rs`:

```rust
pub enum RelaxAction {
    KeepRelative,
    UpgradeToAbsolute,                       // JR -> JP
    InsertFarCallThunk { thunk_id: SymbolId, lease_chain: SmallVec<[LeaseId; 2]> },
}

pub fn relax_branches(plan: &LayoutPlan, sections: &mut [Section]) -> Vec<RelaxAction>;
```

The relaxation is iterative-monotone: each pass can only grow the encoded size. Iterate until fixed point or a configurable max iteration count.

### Acceptance Criteria

```bash
cargo check -p gbf-asm
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- layout::no_section_crosses_bank      # Hard invariant
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- layout::strict_one_per_bank           # Profile semantics
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- relax::out_of_range_jr_becomes_jp     # JR upgrade
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- relax::cross_bank_becomes_far_call    # Far-call thunk insertion
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- relax::reaches_fixed_point             # Iteration converges
```

### Constitution Checkpoints

- §I.1: `LayoutError` enumerates exact failure modes (section too big, no fitting bank, etc.).
- §IV.3: Layout is deterministic for the same inputs.
