comments.text:
## Why this bead exists

§2 Rule Falsification: "This RFC is correct only if a deliberately-broken
implementation produces the expected Refuted verdict on the appropriate
hypothesis. Falsification sensitivity is a first-class proof obligation."

§13 O5 enumerates SIX broken substitutes that must each produce a specific
Refuted verdict. This is the load-bearing proof that the framework would
catch real bugs — without it, a Confirmed verdict on a real run could be
unfounded (the hypothesis algebra might be too loose to reject ANY input).

## Scope

In `gbf-experiments/tests/falsification/`, gated by the test-only `falsify`
feature so broken substitutes CANNOT leak into a release build:

  Required test files (paths normative per §13 O5):
    f1_nan_forward.rs
    f2_zero_grad.rs
    f3_no_reset_scorer.rs
    f4_phase_a_leaks_ternary.rs
    f5_toytiny_undersized.rs
    f6_modulo_biased_shuffle.rs

  - F1 NaN-injecting forward → H1 Refuted (non-finite loss; FailSubstrate).
  - F2 gradient-zeroing hook → H1 Refuted (loss flat over windows;
       mean_train_loss(91..100) NOT < mean_train_loss(1..10) − 0.5).
  - F3 scorer fails to reset at 128-byte boundary OR consumes byte before
       scoring → H5 Refuted via O-metric-3 spy (recorded context lengths
       diverge from [0,1,...,127,0]).

title: F-S2.22: CI workflows (s2-pr / s2-nightly / s2-on-demand) + integration_s2 end-to-end smoke
description:
Goal
====
Implement the GitHub Actions workflows .github/workflows/{s2-pr,
s2-nightly, s2-on-demand}.yml AND the integration_s2 end-to-end CI smoke
test (5-seed × 3-build s2_train_run + seed-0 s2_ablation on a TINY in-
repo fixture corpus, exercising O2 / O9 in seconds rather than hours).
Per F-S2 RFC §15.2 + §16.9.

Why this matters
================
- The CI workflow is the operational gate. Without workflow definitions,
  closure scripts cannot enforce §16.9.
- integration_s2 is the per-PR smoke: catches scheduler bugs, divergence
  regressions, isolation violations, basic determinism failures in
  seconds (not hours).

Scope
=====
CI workflows (.github/workflows/):

s2-pr.yml (per-PR, fast):
  - cargo fmt --check --all
  - cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings
  - cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s2-full
  - cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features falsify --test falsification_s2
  - cargo test -p gbf-experiments --test loss_grad_flow_s2
  - cargo test -p gbf-experiments --test linearstate_smoke_s2
  - cargo test -p gbf-experiments --test phase_transition_integ_s2
  - cargo test -p gbf-experiments --test canonical_json_s2
  - cargo test -p gbf-experiments --test integration_s2
  - cargo test -p gbf-experiments --test oracle_re_run_s2
  - cargo test -p gbf-experiments --test outcome_totality_s2
  - cargo test -p gbf-train --features burn-adapter --
       linear_state::gradient phase::linear_state_hardness
       distillation loss::config teacher::freeze
  - cargo build -p gbf-experiments --features s2-full
  - cargo build -p gbf-experiments --no-default-features --features s2-ablation
  - scripts/s2_preregistration_check.sh
  - scripts/s2_determinism_check.sh
  - scripts/s2_isolation_check.sh
  - scripts/s2_api_drift_check.sh
  - scripts/s2_distill_determinism_check.sh
  - Upload: experiments/S2/** + /tmp/s2-*.json + stderr NDJSON as CI
    artifacts (for forensic reproduction).

s2-nightly.yml (full TinyStories): 5-seed × 3-build + ablation; regenerate
  S2-report.md; comment outcome on commit.

s2-on-demand.yml: parameterized.

integration_s2 (gbf-experiments/tests/integration_s2.rs):
- Tiny fixture corpus path: fixtures/corpora/tinystories-stub.toml.
- 5 seeds × 3 full builds + s2_ablation seed 0 = 16 runs.
- Walk full state machine path through Decided.
- Assertions:
    - All 16 runs complete (no DivergedAt).
    - At least two seeds produce distinct final shas.
    - Re-running seed 0 of s2_ternary_full byte-equal.
    - Decision = ProceedToS3 OR PassWithDistillWarn.
- Timeout: < 60s on CI hardware.

Structured-log capture in CI
============================
Every workflow step captures BOTH stdout and stderr.
The s2-pr workflow tee-collects stderr (NDJSON when --log-format=json)
into a single file per step: artifacts/s2-pr/<step_name>.ndjson.
On failure, the workflow uploads:
  - artifacts/s2-pr/**/*.ndjson
  - /tmp/s2-*.json (script structured outputs)
  - experiments/S2/** (any partial run artifacts)
This gives a forensic trail covering every event emitted during the
failed CI run.

Unit tests
==========
- File: gbf-experiments/tests/integration_s2.rs (the master e2e):
  Scenarios:
    * 16-run happy path → Decided(ProceedToS3 | PassWithDistillWarn).
    * Each phase log produces exactly 10000 PhaseEntry events for full
      builds; 4000 for ablation.
    * Phase transition events at exactly steps 4001/5001/8001 for full
      builds.
    * teacher_freeze event at step 4001 (full builds only).
    * Re-running seed 0 of s2_ternary_full produces byte-equal
      phase_log_self_hash + final_checkpoint_sha.
    * Synthetic NaN injection at any step → Decided(Halt(...)) via
      Fail-substrate.
    * Synthetic shared-state leak between builds → integration_s2
      detects in step-2 of isolation check.

- File: gbf-experiments/tests/workflow_lint_s2.rs (syntax-only):
  Verify each .github/workflows/s2-*.yml is well-formed YAML and each
  CI step references a valid script / cargo command.

Golden artifacts (insta):
  tests/snapshots/integration_s2__happy_path_summary.snap
    (state-transition sequence + decision)
  tests/snapshots/integration_s2__nan_injection_recovery.snap

E2E verification
================
- s2-pr workflow passes on a clean main branch.
- s2-nightly produces full report + uploads artifacts.
- s2-on-demand accepts seed-list parameter.
- cargo test -p gbf-experiments --test integration_s2 passes locally
  in <60s.
- Forensic capture verified: a deliberately-broken commit's CI run
  uploads sufficient artifacts to reproduce the failure offline.

Considerations
==============
- The tiny corpus is NOT TinyStories. Stable in-repo fixture pinned by
  sha256.
- integration_s2 mocks ONLY external-state verifier records.
- Per CLAUDE.md "Beads Workflow Integration": commits run pre-commit
  hook; workflows mirror but don't replace.

References
==========
F-S2 RFC §15.2 Test layout, §16.9 CI gates, §13 O2 + O9.
Inherits from F-S1 closed beads: bd-ah6o (F-S1.32 GitHub Actions
workflows), bd-2364 (F-S1.27 tiny-fixture integration smoke pattern),
bd-16mx (F-S1.36 E2E test harness with structured logs + golden
artifacts).
Merges (former separate beads): F-S2.49 (CI workflows) + F-S2.51
(integration_s2 smoke).

title: T-B6T7.A: Five report schemas + canonical-JSON for complex-key maps + R-NoReportHashCycles
description:
## What
Land the five report schemas (bodies + envelope wiring) plus canonical-JSON
encoding for complex-key maps:

1. `build_active_semantic_checkpoint_schema.v1` — body
   `SemanticCheckpointSchemaReEmitBody` carrying `ReEmittedCheckpointEntry`
   (with `original_checkpoint_metadata`, `source`, `attachment_node_id`,
   `attachment_anchor`, `canonical_provenance_tuple`).
2. `operational_probe_schema.v1` — body `OperationalProbeSchemaBody` with
   probes, metrics, `per_class_probe_weight_total`,
   `per_class_metric_weight_total`, `per_class_total_weight`.
3. `observation_plan.v1` — body `ObservationPlanReportBody` referencing
   the embedded `ObservationPlan` + the three ancillary report hashes.
4. `range_plan.v1` — body `RangePlanReportBody` with histograms.
5. `range.cert.v1` — body `RangeCertBody` with `Option<Hash256>` identity.

Each body wraps in `ReportEnvelope<R>` at the driver boundary.

## Canonical-JSON encoding for complex-key maps

JSON object keys must be strings. Many of our maps use complex types
(`SemanticCheckpointId`, `ProbeInstanceId`, `ReductionSelector`,
`ReductionSiteId`, etc.). The RFC §4 mandates the sorted-list rule:

```text
CanonicalMap<K, V> JSON encoding:
  [{ "key": K, "value": V }, ...]
  sorted by CanonicalJson(key), bytewise lex order.
  Duplicate keys after canonicalization are rejected.
```

`ReductionSiteId(pub String)` from `gbf-policy::diagnostics` is a
transparent newtype so it can use native string keys — flag in code which
maps fall under which rule.

## Hash definitions

```text
observation_plan_self_hash             = DomainHash(.., "ObservationPlan",          "observation_plan.v1",                              CanonicalJson(plan))
build_active_checkpoint_schema_hash    = DomainHash(.., "BuildActiveCheckpointSchema", "build_active_semantic_checkpoint_schema.v1",  CanonicalJson(schema))
operational_probe_schema_hash          = DomainHash(.., "OperationalProbeSchema",   "operational_probe_schema.v1",                      CanonicalJson(schema))
range_plan_self_hash                   = DomainHash(.., "RangePlan",                 "range_plan.v1",                                    CanonicalJson(range_plan))
range_cert_body_hash                   = DomainHash(.., "RangeCertBody",             "range.cert.v1",                                    CanonicalJson(range_cert))
```

Plus `report_self_hash` for each `ReportEnvelope<R>` (inherited from F-B2/F-B4 §7.2).

## Subtasks
- [ ] Define five body types as `gbf-report` schemas.
- [ ] All five register as `ReportSchemaId` variants.
- [ ] Implement CanonicalMap<K,V> sorted-list rule.
- [ ] `Option<Hash256>` failure-capable identity fields (Patch 8 of
      30-patch).
- [ ] Cross-report invariants: `R-Stage4-Triple`, `R-Stage5-Pair`,
      `R-NoReportHashCycles`.
- [ ] `R-NoPartialProduct` discipline: no successful product field in
      failed reports.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Round-trip canonical JSON byte-stable for each body.
- [ ] Report self-hashes stable.
- [ ] R-NoReportHashCycles enforced at compile time (where possible).
- [ ] `Option<Hash256>` `range_plan_self_hash` exercised in failure
      fixtures.
- [ ] BTreeMap<SemanticCheckpointId, ...> serializes via sorted-list rule.

## How this serves the project
The reports + cert are the deliverable downstream of F-B6/F-B7. F-C2,
gbf-debug, F-F1 gbf-verify, gbf-bench, and the build manifest all read
these JSON files. They must round-trip byte-stably or `cargo test
--workspace` will flap.

## RFC anchors
§4 CanonicalMap rule, §7 envelope, §10.1-5 schema bodies, §16 obligations
O11-O17.

## History
- 41-patch Patches 38, 39, 40: ReportEnvelope/diagnostic discipline + hash naming
- 30-patch Patch 8: Option<Hash256> on failure paths
- 30-patch Patch 21: define range_cert_body_hash, build_active_checkpoint_schema_hash
- 30-patch Patch 26: R-NoReportHashCycles
- 30-patch Patch 9: complex-key map encoding rule
- 41-patch Patch 33: build_active schema id rename

## Blocked by
T-B6.F (ObservationPlanCoreProduct), T-B7.B (RangePlanCoreProduct).

Evidence: cargo test -p gbf-report passed (98 tests); cargo fmt --check -p gbf-report passed. Caveat: cargo fmt --check --all fails in untracked gbf-codegen/src/s4/observation_plan.rs, outside bd-ja69 ownership.

title: T-B2.15: Stage 0.5 lock/bound enforcement
description:
## What
Implement lock/bound enforcement in the merge resolver: locked knobs
reject overrides; out-of-bounds values are hard rejected; bounds are
monotone-tighter through resolution.

## Why
The `CompileKnobs` surface F-B16 will eventually mutate must be locked
where the profile says "this is non-negotiable for this build class."
Without enforcement, F-B16's loop could silently widen bounds the profile
intended to cap.

## Inputs
- T-B2.13 resolver scaffolding.
- T-B2.12 CompileProfileSpec fixtures (for `KnobLockSet`).
- T-B2.1 diagnostic taxonomy.

## Outputs
- `PolicyKnobLockedAndOverridden { knob: CompileKnobId }` Hard diagnostic.
- `PolicyKnobOutOfBounds { knob, requested, bounds }` Hard diagnostic.
- Bounds-monotonicity check: every `bounds` field at least as tight after
  resolution as before. Violation is an internal-error-class panic in tests
  (a resolver bug, not user input).

## Pitfalls
- Locks apply AFTER profile frames, BEFORE compile-request overrides
  (RFC §7.4 merge rules).
- Out-of-bounds is detected against the *post-merge* bounds, not the
  initial bounds.
- Test with both single-knob locks and lock sets that include nested
  paths (e.g. `ScheduleResourcePressure → wram_hot.hard`).

## Acceptance
- gbf-codegen::f_b2_resolve_policy_rejects_locked_knob_override
- gbf-codegen::f_b2_resolve_policy_rejects_out_of_bounds_value

## Refs
- RFC §7.4 lock/bound rules.
- Depends on: T-B2.13.
- Blocks: T-B2.19.
close_reason: Completed with gates and review wave

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## RFC amendments (2026-05-07)

Two additions to lock/bound enforcement:

**1. Unsatisfiable bound meet → `PolicyConstraintUnsatisfiable` (§7.4)**

When the bound-meet operation produces an empty intersection (e.g., target
allows `[A, B, C]` and profile tightens to `[D, E]`), emit
`PolicyConstraintUnsatisfiable { knob, left, right }` — a typed Hard
diagnostic, NOT a generic `String` error. The `ValidationCode` variant lives
in T-B2.1's enum.

**2. Stronger lock semantics (§7.4)**

Locks apply after profile frames and before ALL later frames (not just
compile-request overrides). Any later frame — hint, compile-request, OR
calibration — that attempts to change a locked knob to a non-identical
value is a hard `PolicyKnobLockedAndOverridden` diagnostic.

Identical-value re-affirmation is allowed (idempotent).

New acceptance tests:
- `f_b2_resolve_policy_rejects_unsatisfiable_bound_meet`
- `f_b2_resolve_policy_lock_blocks_calibration_change`
- `f_b2_resolve_policy_lock_allows_identical_re_affirmation`

(The merge rules themselves live in T-B2.13; this task implements the
enforcement and emits the typed diagnostics.)

Cross-refs: §7.4 merge rules, §7.1 PolicyConstraintUnsatisfiable variant.

title: T-B3.7: FfnTopologyKindTag + Mixed-as-some-dense-some-routed (no shared dense branch)
description:
## What
Define `FfnTopologyKindTag { Dense, Routed, Mixed }` for the report
identity field. Mixed means *some layers are Dense, some are Routed*
— and **nothing else**. Pin that no-shared-dense-branch rule in v1.
See RFC §8.1 / §10.1 / Ambiguity A63.

## Why
Earlier drafts overloaded "Mixed" with two senses:
  (a) some layers dense / some routed; and
  (b) routed layers with a *shared dense branch alongside experts*.
Only (a) was actually defined. Sense (b) — `SharedDenseMatVec`,
`SharedDenseWeight`, `SharedDenseBias` — is **out of scope for v1** and
requires explicit RFC amendment.

This task pins the v1 meaning. `FfnTopologyKind` lives only on
`QuantGraphReportBody.input_identity`, NOT on `QuantGraph` itself
(Ambiguity A39: full topology is derivable from
`ModelSpecSummary.ffn_kind` per layer; the tag is a cheap
report-level branching aid). QG-10 (§10.1) defines the cross-check:
- Dense  ⇒ routing_layers_count = 0
- Routed ⇒ routing_layers_count > 0 ∧ all layers Routed
- Mixed  ⇒ at least one Dense and at least one Routed layer

## Inputs
- T-B3.6 (`ExpertSection` shape) — informs how Mixed is computed.
- T-B3.1 (`ModelSpecSummary.ffn_kind` per layer).

## Outputs
- `pub enum FfnTopologyKindTag { Dense, Routed, Mixed }`.
- Helper `compute_ffn_topology_kind(model_spec: &ModelSpecSummary) ->
  FfnTopologyKindTag`.
- The QG-10 cross-check predicate (used by report semantic-validator,
  T-B3.24).

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT add `MixedWithSharedDense` or any variant that implies a
  shared-dense branch. Adding such a variant requires a separate RFC
  amendment that defines op shape, semantics, and `QuantTensorRole`
  variants for the shared-dense path (Ambiguity A63).
- DO NOT compute the tag from anything other than `ModelSpecSummary`;
  that lets Stage 0 → Stage 1 chain validate without re-reading
  `ArtifactCore`.

## Acceptance
- `gbf-codegen::ffn_topology_kind_tag_three_variants_only`.
- `gbf-codegen::compute_ffn_topology_kind_matches_qg_10_predicate`
  (table-driven test over dense / routed / mixed model specs).

## Refs
- RFC §8.1 (Mixed-topology note), §10.1 (QG-10 invariant), Ambiguity
  ledger: A39, A63.
- Depends on: T-B3.1, T-B3.6.
- Blocks: T-B3.24 (report schema), T-B3.22 (SC checks consume the tag).

title: T-B4.12: StageCache key for Stage 2
description:
## What
Wire the Stage 2 StageCache key in `gbf-codegen::stage_cache`, including
failure-memo cell. See RFC §7.8.

## Why
Cache invalidation must be tight enough that schema/feature-flag changes
invalidate, but not so loose that legitimately-cacheable repeat runs miss.
Stage 2's reads are `policy_resolution_self_hash`, `quant_graph_hash`,
`runtime_chrome_budget_hash` (Optional), `target_profile_hash`, plus
versioning.

## Inputs
- T-B4.11 static_budget.v1 schema (for failure memos).
- T-B2.20 StageCache pattern.
- T-B2.13 ResolvedPolicyProduct (for policy_resolution_self_hash).
- T-B4.1 QuantGraphBudgetView (for quant_graph_hash).

## Outputs
- Stage 2 cache key inputs: `policy_resolution_self_hash`, `quant_graph_hash`,
  `runtime_chrome_budget_hash`, `target_profile_hash`, `pass_version_budget`,
  `crate_feature_set_hash`, `static_budget_schema_hash`.
- Success cell: `StaticBudgetReport` + report bytes.
- Failure memo: `static_budget.json` JSON bytes + diagnostics, replayed
  only on exact input-hash match.
- Cache-hit materializes cached canonical bytes (no recanonicalization).

## Pitfalls
- `runtime_chrome_budget_hash` is Optional in the *report*, but in the
  *cache key* a `None` value still hashes to a stable representation
  distinct from `Some(...)`.
- `pass_version_budget` bumps when Stage 2 logic changes; treat like an ABI version.
- `static_budget_schema_hash` changes whenever static_budget.v1's schema
  or canonicalization rules change.

## Acceptance
- gbf-codegen::stage_cache_key_budget_is_deterministic
- gbf-codegen::stage_cache_failed_pass_does_not_enter_success_cache (already from T-B2.20; reaffirmed for Stage 2)
- gbf-codegen::stage_cache_failure_memo_replays_only_on_exact_input_match (Stage 2 variant)

## Refs
- RFC §7.8 keys.
- Depends on: T-B2.20, T-B4.11.
- Blocks: T-B4.13.

No changes to Stage 2 cache key inputs. The `runtime_chrome_budget_hash`

the key records explicit `None`, never an all-zero sentinel. For Stage 2

No new acceptance tests required.

title: T-B3.6: ExpertSection (no residency_hint) + dense-as-one-expert encoding rule
description:
## What
Define `ExpertSection { layer: LayerId, expert: ExpertId, tensor_refs:
Vec<TensorId> }`. Pin the dense-FFN encoding rule: dense layers are
encoded as exactly one ExpertSection with `expert == 0` and no
RoutingTable entry. See RFC §8.1.

## Why
Two structural decisions land together:

1. `tensor_refs` (renamed from `weight_refs` in earlier drafts) carries
   both weights and biases, in the canonical order
   `FfnGate? → FfnUp → FfnDown` with each weight's optional bias
   immediately following (§8.5 SC-6, Ambiguity A23). The schema
   property is enforced; runtime cannot reorder.

2. **No `residency_hint`** (Ambiguity A27). Residency is downstream
   storage/scheduling territory and conflicts with the storage-free
   boundary (§2.3). HintBundle remains the only carrier of residency
   hints; F-B10 reads them directly from there.

The dense-as-one-expert encoding (Ambiguity A2) lets `QuantGraph`'s
shape stay uniform across dense and routed layers without forcing a
separate `DenseFFN` field. Mathematically, dense FFN = routed FFN with
hard probability 1.0 on expert 0; structurally, the shape is one
section per (layer, expert). Per-IR, dense layers emit no router/select
nodes (§9.8 dense-direct-shape rule, Ambiguity A61).

## Inputs
- T-B3.1 (`QuantGraph` skeleton).
- T-B3.2 (`TensorId`, `QuantTensorRole`).

## Outputs
- `pub struct ExpertSection { layer: LayerId, expert: ExpertId,
  tensor_refs: Vec<TensorId> }`.
- A documented invariant on `tensor_refs` ordering used by SC-6 in
  T-B3.22.

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT add `residency_hint`, `placement_hint`, or any storage
  metadata field (Ambiguity A27, §2.3).
- DO NOT allow `expert` values outside `0..n_experts(layer)` for routed
  layers, or anything other than `0` for dense layers — these are
  enforced by SC-4 (T-B3.22).
- `tensor_refs` ordering rule is a *schema* property, not a runtime
  property — F-B3 enforces; tests pin (Ambiguity A23).

## Acceptance
- `gbf-codegen::expert_section_struct_has_no_residency_field`.
- `gbf-codegen::expert_section_tensor_refs_canonical_order_pinned`.
- `gbf-codegen::dense_layer_uses_single_expert_section_with_expert_zero`
  (test fixture in T-B3.26).

## Refs
- RFC §8.1 (ExpertSection), §8.5 SC-5/SC-6, §2.3 (storage-free), §9.8
  (dense-direct shape).
- Ambiguity ledger: A2, A23, A27, A61.
- Depends on: T-B3.1, T-B3.2.
- Blocks: T-B3.7 (mixed topology summary uses ExpertSection counts),
  T-B3.17 (ExpertBinding), T-B3.22 (SC-5/SC-6).

title: F-S7 v0.2: §21 closure rule 12 restriction (DenseOnly only for valid Fail-parity)
description:
## Description

Tighten §21 "Final concise contract" item 12 so `ProceedToS8-DenseOnly` is reachable only when `S7Outcome = Fail-parity caused by per-seed bpc parity failure under valid matched-deployed-byte accounting`. Explicitly enumerate the invalid-experiment outcomes that MUST NOT close as DenseOnly: bytes mismatch, missing artifacts, gradient-provenance failure, oracle failure, emulator failure, guardrail failure. The pre-review text allowed any Fail-parity (including from bytes mismatch) to close DenseOnly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- §21 item 12 reads: "Decision is one of {ProceedToS8, ProceedToS8-DenseOnly}; any other Decision blocks bd-2v9r closure. ProceedToS8-DenseOnly is permitted iff S7Outcome = Fail-parity caused by per-seed bpc parity failure under valid matched-deployed-byte accounting. Bytes mismatch, missing artifacts, gradient-provenance failure, oracle failure, emulator failure, or guardrail failure are invalid-experiment outcomes and MUST NOT close bd-2v9r as DenseOnly."
- §15 decision protocol cross-references this restriction.
- bd-2v9r predicate is updated (in a separate patch series) to align with v0.2.

## Notes

- This tightens the contract; it does not change the §12 dispatch table (which already routes Fail-bytes → Halt). §21 item 12 is the prose summary that closes the loop — without the explicit enumeration, a reviewer could plausibly interpret "any Fail-parity" as admitting DenseOnly closure.
- Depends on T_F2_1 (Fail-bytes must exist before §21 can exclude it).

## REVISION PASS — RFC §8.5 hard-gate patch (2026-05-03)

The L4 hard-gate suite gains three new gate items and a gated-frame-interval clarification.

### Updated hard-gate block

```text
frame_service_misses == 0
widget_update_count == gated_frame_count
scheduler_service_count == gated_frame_count
max_no_progress_frames <= 1
max_unyielded_compute_mcycles <= 17_556 - soft_deadline_margin_mcycles                  <-- new
max_bank_lease_hold_mcycles <= 17_556 - soft_deadline_margin_mcycles                    <-- new
byte_exact_match == true
yield_while_bank_lease_active_count == 0
harness_pause_while_bank_lease_active_count == 0                                        <-- new (T-B1.3.4 revision)
```

All count equality gates are computed over the gated frame interval only — i.e. excluding startup, shutdown, and host-paused tile-dump intervals. The interval is `[gated_frame_start, gated_frame_end_exclusive)` from the realism report's `scheduling` block (T-B1.6.1 revision).

### Why these three additions

* `max_unyielded_compute_mcycles` directly bounds how long compute can run without giving the cooperative scheduler a chance to fire. The widget+scheduler counters can pass even with a single multi-frame compute spike if the spike happens to straddle exactly one frame; this gate removes the loophole.
* `max_bank_lease_hold_mcycles` bounds scheduler starvation caused by long bank-lease holds. A panel copy under lease is non-yieldable; a runaway copy could starve service even if the post-copy code yields normally.
* `harness_pause_while_bank_lease_active_count` extends the no-yield-under-lease invariant to harness pauses (see T-B1.3.4 revision).

### New tests

```rust
#[test]
#[ignore = "Heavy"]
fn f_b1_l4_max_unyielded_compute_within_frame_budget() { /* ... */ }

#[test]
#[ignore = "Heavy"]
fn f_b1_l4_max_bank_lease_hold_within_frame_budget() { /* ... */ }

#[test]
#[ignore = "Heavy"]
fn f_b1_l4_no_harness_pause_while_banklease_active() { /* ... */ }
```

These join the existing three `#[ignore]`d tests; T-B1.6.9 (ignored discipline) requires all six to remain `#[ignore]`d.

### Logging discipline

When a gate fails, `FB1TraceEvent::ValidatorRejected { rule, evidence }` records which gate fired, with concrete evidence (the `mcycle` window, the lease ID, the frame index). T-B1.6.11's run-log capture surfaces these in the post-mortem summary.

### What did NOT change

- The hard-gate-or-RFC-amendment escalation rule (RFC §0, §9.4) is unchanged.
- `byte_exact_match` is still the headline correctness gate.
- The original three gates (`frame_service_misses`, `widget_update_count`, `scheduler_service_count`) are unchanged.

## T-B1.6: L5 — Realism report + review packet + closure skill

### Background

L5 freezes the M0.5 empirical baseline. The deliverable is `docs/review/f-b1/artifacts/realism_report.v1.json`, bit-reproducible from pinned inputs, plus the review packet (scope, architecture, claim-to-gate, reviewer-checklist, known-debt, reproducibility, generated-artifacts).

### Why the report is the deliverable, not the kernel

The kernel is a means to an end. The thing M1 actually inherits is the **measured cost of bringup compute** — cycles per product-accumulate, ROM bandwidth, bank-switch frequency, frame budget consumption, WRAM/HRAM/SRAM peaks. M1's `QuantSpec` and `D_model` choices are data-driven by these numbers.

### Reproducibility — load-bearing

The report records only emulated cycle counts and emulator-deterministic outputs. **No host wall-clock fields**. `wall_clock_seconds_at_gb_clock_f64` is derived from the DMG clock, not the host. Two consecutive `regen.sh` runs must diff to zero.

`git_dirty` is evaluated before artifact writes in a fresh checkout. Regeneration is valid only if the final worktree diff is clean after the script completes.

`report_self_hash` is computed over canonical JSON with the field zeroed; the emitter writes the final hash afterward.

### Schema fields — load-bearing decisions baked in

- **No `artifact_core_hash`.** F-B1 has no `ArtifactCore`; including the field would violate the milestone's own non-goals.
- **`compute_bringup_request_hash`** (not `compile_request_hash`) — F-B1 does not have the real `CompileRequest`.
- Identity fields: `build_hash`, `runtime_nucleus_hash`, `compute_bringup_request_hash`, `asm_ir_hash`, `rom_sha256`, `operand_fixture_hash`, `quarter_square_table_hash`.
- Memory bandwidth split: `rom_bank0_table_bytes_read` vs `romx_operand_bytes_read` (different traffic classes).
- Banking split: `logical_bank_switches_*` vs `mbc_rom_bank_register_write_count` (these are different things).
- Banking includes `max_active_bank_leases` and `yield_while_bank_lease_active_count` (the safety invariant).
- `rom_layout` block reports `bank0_used_bytes`, `bank0_free_bytes`, `romx_operand_bank_size_bytes`.
- Scheduling: `frame_service_misses` (renamed from `vblank_misses`), `scheduler_service_count`, `cycles_remaining_at_widget_tick`, `cycles_remaining_at_scheduler_service` (distinguishing ISR-update from cooperative service).
- Conformance hashes split: `reference_source_hash`, `fixture_hash`, `expected_output_hash`.
- Compute costs use `cycles_per_product_accumulate` (not `cycles_per_multiply`) — the measured step includes table lookup, product reconstruction, accumulator update, and loop overhead.

### Companion artifacts

- `cycle_attribution_n128.json` — per-metric attribution rules so M1 can interpret the report.
- `matmul_n128.map.json` — machine-readable Bank0 layout, table placement, symbol sizes.

### Subtask plan

- **T-B1.6.1** `realism_report.v1` schema in `gbf-report` + self-hash convention + acceptance/rejection tests.
- **T-B1.6.2** `gbf-bench::MatmulI8Bringup` workload runner + sweep over N ∈ {32, 64, 96, 128}.
- **T-B1.6.3** Report aggregation logic + cycle attribution per `cycle_attribution rule`.
- **T-B1.6.4** Companion artifacts (`cycle_attribution_n128.json`, `matmul_n128.map.json`).
- **T-B1.6.5** Review packet scripts (`regen.sh`, `verify-packet.sh`).
- **T-B1.6.6** Review packet markdown documents.
- **T-B1.6.8** Frozen baseline check-in + reproducibility verification.

### Acceptance gates

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-report -- realism_report_v1_schema_accepts_fixture
cargo test -p gbf-report -- realism_report_v1_rejects_missing_required_fields
cargo test -p gbf-report -- realism_report_v1_self_hash_round_trip
cargo test -p gbf-bench -- f_b1_report_aggregation_known_fixture
./scripts/review/f-b1/regen.sh
./scripts/review/f-b1/verify-packet.sh
```

### RFC reference

`history/rfcs/F-B1-compute-bringup.md` §10, §14.

### Dependencies

- T-B1.5 (L4) — cooperative gate working at N=128 (or waiver path active).

## REVISION PASS — Two structural-counts and dev-loop beads added

Two new sub-beads close gaps that were latent in the original L5 plan:

| Bead       | Purpose                                                                                  |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| T-B1.6.12  | Runtime structural-counts hard gate per N — products / output_tiles / panel_copies match formula |
| T-B1.6.13  | F-B1 dev-loop smoke entrypoint script (`scripts/review/f-b1/smoke.sh`) with verbose tracing |

### Why T-B1.6.12

RFC §10.5 lists structural counts ("products = N³, output tiles = (N/16)², panel copies = (N/16)³ × 2") as **sanity bands, not gates**. That framing is too loose for the runtime side. Cycle counts are measurement-defined, but structural counts are exact integer functions of N and tile shape. Putting them under a hard gate means a silent miscount (kernel skipped a tile, aggregator double-counted, runtime trace missed an event) fails immediately with a precise diagnostic — instead of surfacing as an opaque byte-exact mismatch in T-B1.4.6 / T-B1.5.6.

The bead is dynamic and complements T-B1.4.5 (static tile-schedule validator). T-B1.4.5 walks the lowered AsmIR; T-B1.6.12 watches the runtime trace.

### Why T-B1.6.13

The original L5 plan has two heavy-side scripts (`regen.sh`, `verify-packet.sh`) and one fast-side gate (the pre-commit hook). There is no dedicated F-B1 fast entrypoint with verbose tracing. New contributors hit the friction first; existing developers fall back to remembering individual `cargo test -p <crate> -- <pattern>` invocations. The smoke script gives F-B1 a named, layered, RUST_LOG=info-by-default dev-loop entrypoint.

Three-tier model after the addition:

| Script | When to run | Wall clock |
|--------|-------------|------------|
| `cargo test --workspace --all-features` (pre-commit hook) | every commit | seconds |
| `scripts/review/f-b1/smoke.sh` (T-B1.6.13) | every dev iteration | tens of seconds |
| `scripts/review/f-b1/regen.sh` (T-B1.6.5) | before opening PR; nightly via T-B1.6.10 | minutes |
| `scripts/review/f-b1/verify-packet.sh` (T-B1.6.5) | before merge | 2× regen.sh |

T-B1.6.9 (ignored discipline) protects the boundary: smoke.sh must not run any `#[ignore]`d test name listed there.

- **T-B1.6.12** blocks on T-B1.6.3 (aggregation surfaces counts), T-B1.0.9 (typed trace vocabulary), T-B1.0.8 (synthetic-trace fixtures for formula tests), T-B1.6.2 (bench runner provides the trace).

### What did NOT change

- L0 → L1 → L2 → L3 → L4 → L5 layered structure is unchanged.
- The hard 60 Hz cooperative-frame-service gate is unchanged.
- The "no silent close, escalate via RFC amendment" rule is unchanged.

title: T-B5.8: NodeAnchorMap + SemanticAnchor (serialized DomainHash; opaque to F-B5; F-B6 attaches later)
description:
## What
Define `NodeAnchorMap` and the serialized `SemanticAnchor` shape:

```rust
pub struct NodeAnchorMap(pub BTreeMap<NodeId, SemanticAnchor>);

pub struct SemanticAnchor(pub Hash256);    // serialized DomainHash id
```

The anchor id is computed as
`DomainHash("gbf-codegen", "SemanticAnchor", "v1",
  CanonicalJson({ quant_graph_self_hash, node_id, op_tag,
                  canonical_provenance_tuple }))`.

See RFC §9.1, §2.12.

## Why
Anchors are the F-B6 handshake (Ambiguity A16, §13.3). F-B5 emits
`NodeAnchorMap` so F-B6 can attach `SemanticCheckpointId` and
`TraceProbeId` references to canonical IR nodes WITHOUT altering IR
shape.

Three rules:
1. The anchor map is **part of the IR product** (so a StageCache hit
   replaying the IR produces the same anchors). Putting it outside
   the product would mean a cache hit invalidates anchor identity.
2. **No `SemanticCheckpointId` / `TraceProbeId` in v1 F-B5**
   (Ambiguity A7, §2.12). F-B6 owns those. The anchor is opaque from
   F-B5's perspective.
3. The anchor id is a **DomainHash** over a tuple including
   `quant_graph_self_hash` so anchors are stable per QG (a different
   QG produces different anchor ids). This is what F-B6 will rely on
   when binding checkpoints.

## Inputs
- T-B5.2 (`GbNode`, `NodeId`, `InferOpTag`).

## Outputs
- `pub struct NodeAnchorMap(BTreeMap<NodeId, SemanticAnchor>)`.
- `pub struct SemanticAnchor(Hash256)`.
- `fn compute_semantic_anchor(quant_graph_self_hash: &Hash256,
  node_id: NodeId, op_tag: InferOpTag, canonical_provenance_tuple:
  &CanonicalProvenanceTuple) -> SemanticAnchor`.

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT include `SemanticCheckpointId` or `TraceProbeId` in the
  anchor or anywhere in the IR (§2.12 / Ambiguity A16).
- DO NOT compute the anchor id over anything other than a tuple that
  includes `quant_graph_self_hash` — anchors must be stable across
  cache hits but distinguishable across QGs.
- DO NOT make `NodeAnchorMap` unordered; canonical hashing requires
  `BTreeMap`.

## Acceptance
- `gbf-codegen::node_anchor_map_is_btree_map_canonical`.
- `gbf-codegen::semantic_anchor_id_uses_domain_hash_with_qg_self_hash`.
- `gbf-codegen::node_anchor_map_excludes_semantic_checkpoint_ids`.

## Refs
- RFC §9.1, §2.12 (no semantic checkpoints in this chunk), §13.3
  (F-B6 handshake), Ambiguity ledger A7, A16.
- Depends on: T-B5.2.
- Blocks: T-B5.14 (AnchorBinding).
close_reason: Consolidated 2026-05-10: scope absorbed into bd-i19q. This bead's body remains as detailed prose for the absorbed sub-scope; bd-i19q is the implementation anchor with combined coverage.

title: RV-3: close BlockExport hole when nucleus hashes differ and any delta exceeds D9-tol
description:
# Goal

Extend RV-3 (BlockExport predicate) to cover the case where runtime_nucleus_hashes do NOT match AND any |delta_bytes(s)| > D9-tol, even when fits_envelope is true. The previous RV-2 \"Warn\" predicate had a gap that effectively neutered the D9 tolerance gate.

# Background / Why

D18 defines:
  RV-1 Pass:  hashes_match AND fits_envelope AND (forall s. |delta| <= D9-tol).
  RV-2 Warn:  !hashes_match AND fits_envelope AND (forall s. |delta| <= D9-tol).
  RV-3 Block: fits_envelope fails OR synthetic-vs-real mismatch (D10).

The gap was: !hashes_match AND fits_envelope AND any |delta| > D9-tol. Under RV-1 that fails (not equal); under RV-2 that fails (delta exceeds tolerance); under RV-3 that fails (fits_envelope passes). So the run dispatched to ... nowhere, or by default to Warn. That makes D9-tol an advisory string, not a gate.

# Change

In gbf-policy re-validation logic:

  - Update RV-3:
      outcome = BlockExport iff
        any fits_envelope check fails
        OR synthetic-vs-real mismatch (D10)
        OR (!runtime_nucleus_hashes_match AND any |delta_bytes(s)| > D9-tol).
  - Make sure the per-slot delta diagnostic surfaces the offending slot id (RV-4 already covers this for BlockExport).

# Why this matters

Without this, D9-tol is advisory. A drift in chrome budget that exceeds tolerance but still keeps the ROM within envelope would Warn instead of Block, and shippable closure PRs could include incorrect budgets.

# Considerations

  - Reviewer P7 (Numerical / Determinism) explicitly checks gate effectiveness; this closure removes a known false-negative.
  - Tolerance value D9-tol is pinned in §D9.

# Verification

  - Fixture: !hashes_match, fits_envelope true, max delta = D9-tol -> Warn.
  - Fixture: !hashes_match, fits_envelope true, max delta = D9-tol + 1 -> BlockExport.
  - Fixture: !hashes_match, !fits_envelope -> BlockExport (existing case).

# Related RFC sections

  §D18 RV-1..RV-5, §D9 tolerance, §D10 synthetic-vs-real.

# Depends on

  B03 (RuntimeNucleusHash union type -- the comparison is on this typed field).
close_reason: Completed RV-3 BlockExport predicate and review fix preserving matching-hash Pass semantics. Gemini and Claude ACPX reviews PASS; re_validation tests passed.

title: F-S2.25: FrozenTeacher + teacher storage/weight fingerprinting (at step 4000 boundary)
description:
Goal
====
Implement gbf-train::teacher::FrozenTeacher — the contract that detaches
the teacher at step 4000, sets teacher_requires_grad = false thereafter,
and records storage + weight fingerprints into s2_distillation_log.v1.
Per F-S2 RFC §3 D3.

Why this matters
================
The teacher provenance is intra-S2 (the seed-matched Phase A end
checkpoint inside the SAME S2 run — not S1 — per RFC §0 intro update).
Without a fingerprint, a corrupted or wrong-seed teacher could silently
pollute distillation gradients and break H2/H3.

Scope (in gbf-train::teacher)
=============================
- struct FrozenTeacher {
    teacher_storage_fingerprint: String,   // hex of safetensors-canonical
                                            // storage byte digest
    teacher_weight_fingerprint:  String,   // hex of CanonicalTensorPayloadHash
    teacher_checkpoint_sha:      Hash256,
    requires_grad: bool,                   // always false after freeze
  }
- fn detach_for_teacher(model_after_step_4000: &Model, seed: Seed,
                       build_kind: S2BuildKind) -> FrozenTeacher
- Invariants:
    detach_for_teacher invoked EXACTLY ONCE per run, at the step-4000
    boundary (the bead F-S2.06 fires the event; this bead implements
    the actual detach).
    teacher_requires_grad = false thereafter; assertion held at every
    subsequent step.
- Fingerprints recorded into s2_distillation_log.v1 by F-S2.17 at
  finalize.

Acceptance
==========
- Unit test: calling detach_for_teacher twice in a row panics (single-
  fire invariant).
- Unit test: teacher_storage_fingerprint deterministic across replays.
- Unit test: teacher_weight_fingerprint = CanonicalTensorPayloadHash of
  the teacher trainable tensor set at step 4000.
- Unit test: any forward pass through FrozenTeacher after detach has
  zero gradient w.r.t. teacher parameters (Burn autodiff feature-gated).
- Unit test: ablation builds do NOT freeze a teacher (no detach_for_teacher
  call) — Ok-8 holds only for full builds.

Considerations
==============
- The teacher is the SEED-MATCHED Phase A end snapshot from THIS S2 run.
  It is NOT an S1 checkpoint. See RFC §3 D3 + the round-4 intro
  amendment.
- Storage fingerprint covers safetensors bytes; weight fingerprint covers
  CanonicalTensorPayloadHash. They serve different audit purposes; both
  are recorded.

References
==========
F-S2 RFC §3 D3, §5 S2-Run-Ok-8, §9.3 DL-1.
Depends on: F-S2.24 (train run boundary), F-S2.06 (event fire),
F-S2.17 (distill log writer).

title: F-S7 v0.2 T3.1: AggregateParityVerdict + Fail-bytes routing
description:
## Goal

Implement §11.2 AggregateParityVerdict (Pass-clean | Fail-parity | Fail-bytes) with the bytes-check-first semantics. Wire Fail-bytes into the §12 dispatch table so it routes to Decision::Halt, not Decision::ProceedToS8-DenseOnly.

## Background

Pre-review §12 collapsed bytes-mismatch into Fail-parity. Fail-parity → DenseOnly closes bd-2v9r AND amends S8's epic to drop MoE. So an unfair byte allocation (dense too small, MoE 'wins' parity but the byte gate fires Refuted) would close S7 with a DenseOnly mandate based on an invalid comparison. v0.2 says: bytes mismatch is an invalid experiment (Halt), not a scientific falsification (DenseOnly).

The bytes check fires FIRST: if |B_deployed_total(MoE) − B_deployed_total(Dense)| > D6_tolerance, the verdict is Fail-bytes regardless of per-seed bpc parity. This protects bd-2v9r closure from an accidentally-too-small dense baseline silently producing a DenseOnly verdict.

## Files

- gbf-experiments/src/s7/parity.rs (s7_parity_aggregate)
- gbf-experiments/src/s7/outcome.rs (S7Outcome enum + §12 dispatch table)
- gbf-experiments/tests/outcome_totality.rs (O7 — enumerates all observable verdict combinations)

## Acceptance

- s7_parity_aggregate returns Fail-bytes when bytes_diff > tolerance, regardless of per-seed verdict.
- §12 dispatch sends Fail-bytes to Decision::Halt(matched-bytes-invalid; comparison-not-scientific).
- §21 closure rule rejects ProceedToS8-DenseOnly when S7Outcome = Fail-bytes (compile-time enum match).
- O7 totality test passes (every observable verdict combination maps to exactly one S7Outcome).
- F-bytes-mismatch test fixture (dense d_ff_dense scaled to violate tolerance) produces Halt, not DenseOnly.

## Reasoning chain

T1.3 (MatchedBytesPin) produces the byte totals; T3.1 reads tolerance_bytes from the pin and the per-seed scores from the scoring phase. T3.1 unblocks T3.2 (Pareto verdict comes after parity verdict in the §11 pipeline).
notes:
## Test Plan & Logging (AGENTS.md addendum)

### O7 totality enumeration (the keystone test)

`gbf-experiments/tests/outcome_totality.rs` enumerates every observable input combination and asserts unique S7Outcome dispatch:

- H1 verdict ∈ {Confirmed, Refuted(divergence), Refuted(collapse), Refuted(loss)} (4)
- H2 verdict ∈ {Confirmed, Refuted} (2)
- H3 verdict ∈ {Confirmed, Refuted} (2)
- H4 verdict ∈ {Confirmed, Refuted(tied), Refuted(incomparable), Refuted(dense-wins)} (4)
- H5-H10 each ∈ {Confirmed, Refuted} (2^6 = 64)
- bytes_within_tolerance ∈ {true, false} (2)
- median_val_bpc < 0.5 (suspicious) ∈ {true, false} (2)

→ 4*2*2*4*64*2*2 = 16384 input cells. Each maps to exactly one S7Outcome variant; the test runs the dispatch table and asserts (a) no panic, (b) no two cells map to a 'Pass-clean OR Fail-X' ambiguity, (c) Pass-clean only arises when all gates Confirmed.

### Specific cell tests (called out for the §21 line-12 protection)

- bytes_mismatch_with_all_other_pass: bytes_within_tolerance=false, all H_i=Confirmed → S7Outcome MUST be Fail-bytes (not Pass-clean; not Fail-parity).
- parity_fail_under_valid_bytes: bytes_within_tolerance=true, H3=Refuted, H1/H2/H4..H10=Confirmed → S7Outcome MUST be Fail-parity.
- parity_fail_under_invalid_bytes: bytes_within_tolerance=false, H3=Refuted → S7Outcome MUST be Fail-bytes (Fail-bytes takes precedence; this protects bd-2v9r from a poisoned DenseOnly closure).

### Logging

- s7.outcome.dispatch INFO event for every verdict computation: { input_verdicts: HashMap<H_i, Verdict>, bytes_within_tolerance, suspicious_median, dispatched_outcome }.
- s7.outcome.invariant_failure ERROR event on any totality violation (the test surfaces the specific input cell that broke uniqueness).
- A test-end summary: s7.outcome.totality_summary { cells_dispatched, unique_outcomes, dispatch_table_version }.

### Reviewer Personas

P5 Detective (always-on), P6 Scope Sentinel (always-on), P1 Architecture & Boundary Steward (outcome algebra is the system boundary between experiment and closure), P8 Public Contract / Schema Stability (S7Outcome is the §15 closure-time contract), P4 QA / Test Engineer.

### Project Skills

`.agents/skills/qat-bead-closure/SKILL.md` (claim-to-gate matrix; outcome variants ARE the gates).

## Context

The F-S3 RFC (`history/rfcs/F-S3-v0-success-tinystories.md`) was rewritten on 2026-05-13 to inherit the landed F-S2 contracts (main commit `ca21eb4`, "F-S2 QAT survives closure" PR #19). Per F-S1 R-Predictions discipline (re-affirmed by F-S2 Rep-S2-6), the "Pre-registered predictions" section of the RFC must appear in git history strictly BEFORE any S3 result-artifact commit.

This bead pre-registers the RFC and runs the preregistration script for the first time. **Critically, this bead is independent of every other F-S3 bead** — the pin lives in a standalone TOML fixture (NOT inside the s3 module that B7 creates), so B1 closes without crate-level dependencies.

## Why this matters

R-Predictions is the project's main defense against post-hoc hypothesis adjustment. F-S1 enforced it; F-S2 inherited it (Rep-S2-6 + O1). Without this bead closing FIRST, every later F-S3.* bead's result-artifact commit will fail the preregistration ancestry gate at S3 closure (bd-3k8o), and the closure itself produces `Fail-preregistration` per the RFC §10 dispatcher.

## Deliverables

1. A git commit on `main` capturing the F-S3 RFC at the rewritten state (commit `predictions_commit` = this commit's `GitCommitId`).
2. **`experiments/S3/preregistration.toml`** (standalone — no crate dependency; readable by the prereg script and by later beads):
   ```
   schema = "s3_preregistration.v1"
   predictions_commit = "<sha>"
   predictions_section_hash = "sha256:..."     # over S1CanonicalJson normalization of the markdown block
   pass_version_S3 = "<unique-string>"          # independent of S1/S2 versions per AS2-19
   rfc_revision = "<sha of HEAD>"
   first_result_commit = ""                     # sentinel; set when first result artifact lands
   ```
3. First run of `scripts/s3_preregistration_check.sh --dry-run` (script itself comes from F-S3.24): exits 0, NDJSON `{passed: true, first_result_commit: null}`.
4. A reference `docs/experiments/S3-preregistration.md` explaining the convention to future contributors.

## Test scaffolding

1. `gbf-experiments/tests/preregistration_pin_s3.rs` — unit test asserting the TOML round-trips through serde and that `predictions_section_hash` is deterministic across replays (10 invocations).
2. `gbf-experiments/tests/preregistration_idempotence_s3.rs` — re-running the prereg script twice in a row produces byte-identical NDJSON output (`captureEvents` sink check).
3. **Negative test**: edit the RFC's "Pre-registered predictions" section (any character); assert `predictions_section_hash` changes, AND assert `scripts/s3_preregistration_check.sh` exits non-zero.

## Logging discipline (subscriber-level capture)

The prereg pin module emits a single tracing event:
```
event_name = "s3::preregistration_pin_loaded"
fields: { predictions_commit, predictions_section_hash, pass_version_S3, rfc_revision }
target = "gbf_experiments::s3::preregistration"
```
Subscriber-level test `gbf-experiments/tests/preregistration_logging_s3.rs` drives the loader and asserts the event fires once with the expected field set (per CLAUDE.md "Logging helper closure must cite subscriber-level capture for event shape").

## Inheritance / non-duplication

- DOES NOT redesign the three-stage preregistration check (it mirrors `scripts/s2_preregistration_check.sh` exactly). F-S3.24 implements it; B1 is the first invocation against an empty result-artifact set.
- DOES NOT introduce S3CanonicalJson; reuse S1CanonicalJson per RFC §3.
- DOES NOT touch the `gbf-experiments/src/s3/...` tree (that comes in B7); B1 lives only at the workspace root in `experiments/` + `docs/experiments/` + `scripts/`.

## Acceptance

```
git log -1 --format=%H -- history/rfcs/F-S3-v0-success-tinystories.md   # matches predictions_commit in TOML
scripts/s3_preregistration_check.sh --dry-run                            # passed: true
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test preregistration_pin_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test preregistration_idempotence_s3
cargo test -p gbf-experiments --features s3 --test preregistration_logging_s3
```

## E2E acceptance

The end-to-end script `scripts/s3_preregistration_check.sh` (B24) is invoked here against an empty result-artifact set; expected NDJSON:
```
{"event":"s3_preregistration_check_stage_start","stage":1,"description":"verify predictions_section_hash"}
{"event":"s3_preregistration_check_stage_done","stage":1,"passed":true,"detail":"hash matches"}
{"event":"s3_preregistration_check_stage_start","stage":2,"description":"verify ancestry"}
{"event":"s3_preregistration_check_stage_done","stage":2,"passed":true,"detail":"first_result_commit is sentinel"}
{"event":"s3_preregistration_check_stage_start","stage":3,"description":"verify earliest result-artifact commit"}
{"event":"s3_preregistration_check_stage_done","stage":3,"passed":true,"detail":"no result artifacts yet"}
```

## Considerations

- If the RFC is amended after B1 closes, **bump `pass_version_S3` AND re-run B1** (or open a follow-up B1' bead). Stale pins silently invalidate later result artifacts.
- The TOML location (`experiments/S3/`) mirrors the F-S2 convention (`experiments/S2/preregistration.toml`); reuse the same parser pattern.

## Out of scope

- Implementing `scripts/s3_preregistration_check.sh` itself (owned by F-S3.24).
- Any S3 training or result artifacts (those begin with B18 / B19 / B21).
- The `gbf-experiments/src/s3/...` module tree (B7).

## References

- RFC §17.6 "Pre-registration CI" (F-S3 instance of F-S1 O1)
- F-S2 RFC §13 O1 (template that B1 mirrors)
- `scripts/s2_preregistration_check.sh:1-485` (existing implementation template)
- F-S2 Rep-S2-5 / Rep-S2-6 / AS2-19 (independent pass_version + RFC revision discipline)

title: T5.1: Implement temporal switch penalty (L_switch)
description: Implement L_switch = (1/LT) sum_{l,t} (1 - dot(p_{l,t}, p_{l,t-1})) where p_{l,t} is the soft expert distribution. Requires access to consecutive token positions within a training batch. ## Agent Instructions

**Target crate**: `gbf-train`
**Target file(s)**: `gbf-train/src/loss/switch.rs`

**Reference**: `history/planv0.md` — search for "temporal switch penalty", "L_switch", "consecutive tokens", "bank-switch cost".

### Implementation Notes
- Temporal switch penalty: `L_switch = (1/LT) Σ_{l,t} (1 - ⟨p_{l,t}, p_{l,t-1}⟩)`
- Where p_{l,t} is the soft routing distribution at layer l, token t.
- Inner product between consecutive-token routing distributions penalizes switching.
- Must handle sequence boundaries: reset at start of each sequence (no penalty for first token).
- `pub fn temporal_switch_loss(routing_probs: &Tensor, sequence_mask: &Tensor) -> Tensor`
  - routing_probs shape: [batch, seq_len, n_layers, n_experts]
  - sequence_mask: marks sequence boundaries

### Acceptance Criteria
```bash
cargo check -p gbf-train                       # Compiles
cargo test -p gbf-train -- loss::switch         # Tests pass
cargo clippy -p gbf-train -- -D warnings        # No warnings
# Verify: identical consecutive distributions -> loss = 0
# Verify: orthogonal consecutive distributions -> loss = 1
# Verify: sequence boundaries correctly handled (no cross-sequence penalty)
# Verify: gradient flows correctly
```

### Constitution Checkpoints
- §I.2: Pure function — tensor in, scalar out
- §III.2: Property test — loss is in [0, 1] range

bd-m7q closure packet: differentiable temporal switch penalty.

QAT Closure Checklist

Artifact contract
- This bead has no artifact serialization contract. It owns the gbf-train Burn training-loss helper for S7 L_switch.
- The public helper is gbf_train::loss::switch::burn_temporal_switch_loss over routing_probs shaped [batch, seq, n_layers, n_experts], plus flattened [batch, seq] sequence_mask and optional boundary-before mask.
- Pair selection delegates to gbf_model::loss::temporal_smoothness::s7_temporal_smoothness_with_boundaries, preserving the reviewed D10/§7.3 model contract as the single source of truth for full-window pairs.

differentiable Burn path
- burn_temporal_switch_loss slices differentiable routing_probs rows, computes per-pair dot products, accumulates 1 - dot penalties, normalizes by n_layers * n_pairs(b) per batch, and returns the batch mean.
- The helper validates tensor/mask shape before tensor math and only host-copies the detached final scalar loss for finite validation; it does not host-copy the full differentiable routing tensor for routine validation.

Tests proving it
- cargo test -p gbf-train --features burn-adapter --lib loss::switch passed: 5 tests covering oracle value, boundary exclusion, gradient flow, invalid masks, and window-one rejection.
- cargo clippy -p gbf-train --features burn-adapter --lib -- -D warnings passed.
- Existing bd-122/bd-1kkf gates cover the shared model pair-set and O13 every-valid-u provenance.

| Public behavior or variant | Scalar/model core | Burn training path | Export/artifact path | Guard |

| Explicit sequence boundary exclusion | supported | supported | not applicable | burn_temporal_switch_loss_excludes_explicit_boundaries; cargo test -p gbf-train --test L_switch_boundary |
| smoothness_window=1 | rejected | rejected | not applicable | burn_temporal_switch_loss_rejects_window_one; gbf-model smoothness_window tests |
| Empty-pair batch rows | supported | supported | not applicable | Implemented as zero contribution via routing_probs.sum() * 0.0; this matches first-token/no-valid-pair semantics without creating NaN. |
| Full run-loop L_total caller adoption and switch-loss structured logging | moved | moved | not applicable | owned by bd-1ryn / final S7 closure owners; this bead supplies the raw helper. |

title: T-B3.3: NormPlanRecord + NormSite + LayerNorms (absorbs T-B3.4)
description:
## What
Define `NormPlanRecord { norm_plan_id, site, plan, input_format,
output_format }` and `NormSite { LayerSequence { layer }, LayerFfn
{ layer }, Final }`. See RFC §8.1.

## Why
`NormSite` makes every `NormPlanRecord` self-locating: the evaluator
does not need positional indices into a flat array (Ambiguity A56).
`q.norm_plan(site)` is a *named* lookup keyed by `NormSite`, used by
`eval_canonical_qg` (RFC §8.7) and by `eval_canonical_ir` Norm{plan}
resolution (§9.6 SC-6).

Three sites cover v1: pre-sequence-block (per layer), pre-FFN (per
layer), and final pre-classify. Adding a new site is a schema-version
bump.

`input_format` and `output_format` are pinned per record so the IIR
Norm op-signature (§9.7a / IIR-SC-6) can validate against producer/
consumer ValueDecl formats without re-deriving them.

## Inputs
- T-B3.1 (`QuantGraph` skeleton).
- `gbf-artifact::NormPlan` (carries variants like `TileRmsThenAffineClip`).
- `gbf-foundation::LayerId`, `QuantFormat`.

## Outputs
- `pub struct NormPlanRecord { norm_plan_id: NormPlanId, site: NormSite,
  plan: NormPlan, input_format: QuantFormat, output_format: QuantFormat }`.
- `pub enum NormSite { LayerSequence { layer: LayerId }, LayerFfn
  { layer: LayerId }, Final }`.
- `pub struct NormPlanId(u32)` newtype.
- A `q.norm_plan(site: NormSite) -> Option<&NormPlanRecord>` resolver
  helper (used by §8.7 reference semantics; tests pin it).

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT make the second norm optional (Ambiguity A56). Standard
  transformer requires both pre-sequence and pre-FFN; architectures
  omitting one require explicit RFC amendment.
- DO NOT key norm-plan lookup positionally — always by `NormSite`.
- `NormSite::Final` is a single record per QG (§8.5 SC-20: exactly one
  Final). It is *not* part of `LayerNorms` (T-B3.4) — it stands alone.

## Acceptance
- `gbf-codegen::norm_site_is_closed_enum_with_three_variants`.
- `gbf-codegen::norm_plan_record_carries_input_and_output_format`.
- `gbf-codegen::norm_plan_lookup_is_named_not_positional`.

## Refs
- RFC §8.1 (NormPlanRecord), §8.7 (named lookup in eval_canonical_qg),
  §9.6 SC-6 (IIR Norm format consistency), §8.5 SC-20 (final norm
  uniqueness).
- Ambiguity ledger: A5 (Norm carries id, not full plan, in the IR),
  A56 (per-layer pre_sequence + pre_ffn).
- Depends on: T-B3.1.
- Blocks: T-B3.4 (LayerNorms), T-B3.13a (NormPlanIdPreBinding), T-B3.15
  (NormPlanBinding), T-B3.22 (SC checks).
close_reason: Implemented NormPlanRecord/NormPlanId/NormSite/LayerNorms, named q.norm_plan lookup, canonical norm id assignment, final norm exclusion, and bind_norm_plans tracing. Gates: cargo test -p gbf-codegen --lib s1::quant_graph::tests:: (124 passed after adding skipped LayerSequence regression). Reviews: Gemini PASS; Claude PASS with concerns addressed by norm_plan_id_pre_binding_skipping_layer_sequence_is_rejected and closure scope note. Co-located binding helpers remain reviewed/closed under bd-o3jg/bd-2yye as applicable.

title: F-S2.06: Training-run schemas — s2_phase_log.v1 + s2_score.v1 + s2_distillation_log.v1
description:
Goal
====
Implement the three training-run artifact schemas + emitters:
s2_phase_log.v1 (header + JSONL per-step with train_loss + grad_norm),
s2_score.v1 (renamed from s2_ternary_score; ThresholdStatsSummary +
ScaleStatsSummary with scale_count), s2_distillation_log.v1
(teacher fingerprints + LossTermEvalPoint + phase_log_self_hash link).
Per F-S2 RFC §9.1 / §9.2 / §9.3.

Why this matters
================
- s2_phase_log.v1 is the SOLE substrate for H1 verification. Round 4
  review added train_loss + grad_norm per step; PL-0 covers header +
  JSONL canonical byte sequence (tamper-evident).
- s2_score.v1 was renamed from s2_ternary_score.v1 (round 2 review)
  because it scores ternary AND fp AND nodistill. ScaleStatsSummary
  gained scale_count.
- s2_distillation_log.v1's LossTermEvalPoint + phase_log_self_hash
  linkage (round 2 review) fixed DL-3 claim that 'phase-effective
  lambdas are recorded in the embedded PhaseEntry' (the embedded
  PhaseEntry didn't exist).

JSONL durability strategy (NEW — addresses crash recovery)
==========================================================
The s2_phase_log.v1 JSONL writer uses:
  - Buffered writes via std::io::BufWriter with explicit flush() at
    every phase boundary (steps 4000, 5000, 8000, 10000) and at run
    completion / divergence.
  - fsync (File::sync_all) after each flush so a crash between writes
    leaves at most one partial line.
  - On reader open, the loader walks lines; if the last line has
    incomplete JSON (no closing brace), it truncates back to the last
    complete line and emits WARN. The header phase_log_self_hash is
    recomputed and checked at load.
  - If the header's recorded entry-count does not match the loaded
    entry-count, return PhaseLogIntegrityError::EntryCountMismatch.
This contract makes partial-write divergence transparent without
allowing silent corruption.

Scope (gbf-experiments::s2::schema)
====================================
s2_phase_log.v1:
  Paths: experiments/S2/runs/{build_kind}/seed-{seed}/phase-log.json (header)
                                                     /phase-log.jsonl (entries)
  Header: PhaseLog { schema, seed, build_kind, train_config_hash,
    full_s2_phase_boundaries: [4000,5000,8000,10000],
    executed_checkpoint_steps: List[u64],
    hardness_ramp_id: 'PhaseCRampD2+PhaseDRampD2',
    teacher_freeze_step: 4000, phase_log_self_hash }
  JSONL entry: PhaseEntry { step, phase, hardness, router_mode,
    lambda_effective, teacher_frozen, train_loss: f32 (finite),
    grad_norm: f32 (finite, >=0), distill_loss: DistillLossNats|null,
    events: List[PhaseEvent] }
  PhaseEvent: PhaseTransition{from,to} | TeacherFreeze{teacher_checkpoint_sha}
  Invariants PL-0..PL-8:
    PL-0 phase_log_self_hash covers (canonical header JSON, with self
         hash field omitted) + (ordered canonical JSONL bytes) + domain
         separator 's2_phase_log.v1/header+entries'.
    PL-1 entry count = optimizer_steps (10000 full / 4000 ablation).
    PL-2 PhaseTransition event count = 3 full / 0 ablation.
    PL-3 teacher_frozen false 1..=4000; true 4001..=10000 (full).
    PL-4 HardnessTriple matches D2 for ternary builds; (Off,Off,Off) for
         s2_fp_full and s2_ablation.
    PL-5 distill_loss finite 5001..=10000 in ternary/fp; finite in
         nodistill Phase C/D (raw); null 1..=5000; null every step
         for ablation.
    PL-6 transition events on first step of new phase (4001/5001/8001).
    PL-7 train_loss finite every entry.
    PL-8 grad_norm finite + >=0 every entry.

s2_score.v1:
  Path: experiments/S2/scores/{build_kind}/seed-{seed}/score.json
  S2ScoreReport { schema, seed, build_kind, checkpoint_sha,
    corpus_val_sha, chunk_size:128, token_count, log2_sum, bpc,
    threshold_stats: Null | ThresholdStatsSummary{matrices,
      threshold_min/max/mean, threshold_count},
    scale_stats: Null | ScaleStatsSummary{matrices, scale_count,
      scale_min/max, scale_mean_f32},
    score_self_hash }
  Stats non-null only for s2_ternary_full + s2_ternary_nodistill.

s2_distillation_log.v1:
  Path: experiments/S2/distillation/{build_kind}/seed-{seed}/distill-log.json
  DistillationLog { schema, seed, build_kind, teacher_checkpoint_sha,
    teacher_weight_fingerprint, teacher_storage_fingerprint,
    teacher_freeze_step:4000, distill_temperature,
    lambda_distill_default, distill_loss_per_eval_point:
      List[(EvalStep, DistillLossNats|null)],
    phase_log_self_hash, loss_terms_per_eval_point:
      List[LossTermEvalPoint], distill_log_self_hash }
  LossTermEvalPoint { eval_step, lambda_effective,
    raw_losses + weighted_losses per term: f32|null per
    InertLossDiscipline trichotomy }
  Invariants:
    DL-1 teacher_checkpoint_sha matches s2_phase-A-end at step 4000.
    DL-2 nodistill: lambda_distill_default=0.0; pre-Phase-C distill null;
         Phase C/D distill finite (raw). ternary/fp: lambda_distill_default=1.0.
    DL-3 records BOTH configured lambda_distill_default AND phase-
         effective lambdas per eval point. Links to authoritative
         per-step phase log via phase_log_self_hash.

Logging contract
================
Per-emitter open INFO:
  event="phase_log_writer_open" build_kind=<S2BuildKind> seed=<Seed>
    header_path=<Path> jsonl_path=<Path>
Per-flush DEBUG (every phase boundary):
  event="phase_log_flush" entries_flushed=<u32> last_step=<u64>
    fsync=true
Per-finalize INFO:
  event="phase_log_finalized" entries=<u32> transition_event_count=<u32>
    teacher_freeze_event_count=<u32> phase_log_self_hash=<hex>
Per-validate ERROR if PL-* invariant fails:
  event="phase_log_invariant_failed" pl_id=<&str>
    expected=<json> observed=<json> step=<u64|null>
Score emitter INFO:
  event="score_emitter_finalized" build_kind=<S2BuildKind>
    seed=<Seed> bpc=<f64> score_self_hash=<hex>
Distill emitter INFO:
  event="distill_log_finalized" build_kind=<S2BuildKind>
    seed=<Seed> teacher_checkpoint_sha=<hex>
    distill_log_self_hash=<hex>

Unit tests
==========
- File: gbf-experiments/tests/canonical_json_s2.rs
  Scenarios (per-schema round-trip + PL-* / score / DL-* invariants):
    * Canonical-JSON round-trip byte-equal for all three artifacts.
    * Each invariant PL-0..PL-8 / DL-1..DL-3 / score nullability rule
      has a dedicated unit test (positive + fail).
    * Tampering a JSONL byte after finalize changes recomputed
      phase_log_self_hash (PL-0 tamper evidence).
    * A truncated JSONL (partial last line) is recovered by the loader
      with a WARN event; entry-count mismatch triggers
      PhaseLogIntegrityError::EntryCountMismatch.
    * s2_score.v1 produces non-null threshold/scale stats with matrices=2
      for Toy0 ternary builds; scale_count = sum-of-rows.

- File: gbf-experiments/tests/phase_log_emitter_s2.rs
  Scenarios:
    * Emit a complete s2_ternary_full phase log for seed 0 on the smoke
      fixture (using F-S2.03 scheduler + F-S2.09 train run) and verify
      10000 JSONL entries + 3 PhaseTransition events + 1 TeacherFreeze
      event at correct steps.
    * Re-running the emitter on the same inputs produces byte-equal
      header + JSONL (Rep-S2-1).
    * Inject a synthetic non-finite train_loss at step 100 → PL-7 invariant
      fails at validate-time with diagnostic identifying step 100.

  Property tests:
    * arb_phase_log_header + arb_phase_entry_sequence → round-trip
      byte-equal + PL-0 hash stability across re-canonicalization.

- File: gbf-experiments/tests/distillation_log_s2.rs
  Scenarios:
    * nodistill build: pre-Phase-C distill = null; Phase C/D distill =
      finite raw.
    * Toy0 router-side terms: raw=null + weighted=null (StructurallyInert).
    * phase_log_self_hash field round-trips correctly.

Golden artifacts (insta):
  tests/snapshots/phase_log_s2__header_ternary_seed0.snap
  tests/snapshots/phase_log_s2__jsonl_first_100_steps.snap
  tests/snapshots/score_s2__ternary_seed0_tiny.snap
  tests/snapshots/distill_log_s2__nodistill_phase_c.snap

E2E verification
================
- integration_s2 (F-S2.22) tail-asserts the produced phase log golden
  artifact matches tests/snapshots/phase_log_s2__header_ternary_seed0.snap.
- scripts/s2_determinism_check.sh (F-S2.21):
    1. cargo run replay-full --seed-list 0 --builds s2_ternary_full (run 1)
    2. Repeat (run 2)
    3. Assert byte-equality of phase_log_self_hash + distill_log_self_hash
       + score_self_hash + safetensors at 4000/5000/8000/10000.
- Structured log assertions: exactly one event="phase_log_finalized"
  per run; exactly one event="score_emitter_finalized" per (build,seed);
  exactly one event="distill_log_finalized" per (build,seed) for
  full builds.

Considerations
==============
- Producer is F-S2.09 (s2_train_run). This bead is schema + emitter
  only.
- InertLossDiscipline (F-S2.05) governs whether each lambda field
  serializes as null vs 0.0.
- s2_ternary_score.v1 → s2_score.v1 rename is one-time; once result
  artifacts exist they pin the schema name in pass_version_S2.
- JSONL durability: see "JSONL durability strategy" block above. The
  recovery rule is essential because a divergent run still WANTS its
  partial phase log preserved for forensics.

References
==========
F-S2 RFC §9.1 / §9.2 / §9.3, §2 Rule InertLossDiscipline.
Inherits from F-S1 closed beads: bd-3kqp (s1_*.v1 schema patterns +
canonical JSON round-trip tests), bd-3kje (s1_score.v1 emitter
patterns).
Merges (former separate beads): F-S2.15 (phase log) + F-S2.16 (score)
+ F-S2.17 (distillation log).
close_reason:

Score reports pin QAT stats nullability by build kind. Distillation logs link to the authoritative `phase_log_self_hash` and carry aligned distillation/loss-term eval points.

title: T-A6.5: gbf-migrate scaffolding (deferred to F-A6b)
description: DEFERRED per RFC history/rfcs/F-A6-gbf-store-migrate.md §0.0.0 and §§11-13. F-A6 must not modify gbf-migrate/src/{dag.rs,epochs.rs,report.rs}, gbf-migrate/Cargo.toml, or create gbf-migrate/tests. This bead is no longer on bd-3ll closure path; it reopens only when the first real schema bump justifies F-A6b.

comments.author: bkase
bkase
comments.text:
**DEFERRED — see RFC F-A6 §0.0.0** (2026-05-03)

Per RFC F-A6's deferral notice, this entire task is moved out of F-A6 and into a new follow-up feature bead (provisional **F-A6b: gbf-migrate scaffolding**) that opens when the first real schema bump in the workspace demands it.

### Why deferred

As of 2026-05-03, the workspace has shipped zero versioned schemas in production: no real artifacts, no measured calibration bundles, no captured failure capsules, no run reports. The cost of "wipe and rebuild from sources on schema bump" is therefore essentially zero today, while the cost of carrying ~600 LOC of unused scaffolding plus a permanent maintenance surface (DAG planner, loss-class enum, family scoping, tests) is paid every day F-A6 onward.

The first real trigger that re-opens this bead is, by family:
- `calibration` — costliest because regenerating means physical lab access to the target Game Boy hardware (`gbf-bench` measures on real DMG/MBC5). The first calibration bundle that needs to survive a schema bump is the bead that re-opens migration work.
- `artifact` — cost = recompile time. May be acceptable to wipe-and-rebuild for the lifetime of M0/M1; decide at the first artifact-schema bump.
- `abi` / `reports` — cost = lost replay/audit data. Likely acceptable to wipe; revisit if external users start preserving these across schema bumps.

### What this bead does NOT do under F-A6

- Does not modify `gbf-migrate/src/{dag.rs, epochs.rs, report.rs}` — they stay exactly `//! Module stub.`
- Does not modify `gbf-migrate/Cargo.toml` — the wrong-direction `gbf-abi`/`gbf-artifact` deps stay until F-A6b lands
- Does not create any `gbf-migrate/tests/` files
- Does not ship any migrator (real or fixture, including `IdentityBytesMigrator` / `BumpMinorMigrator`)
- Does not add `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` to `gbf-migrate/src/lib.rs` — F-A6b adds it along with the rest of the crate's contents

### Source of truth

RFC F-A6 §§ 11, 12, 13 (Compatibility epochs / Migrator trait + DAG / Migration report) are preserved as design notes for F-A6b. They carry inline `DEFERRED` banners. F-A6b will inherit those sections as its starting design rather than starting from a blank page.

### Relationship to bd-3ll

bd-3ll (parent feature bead) is re-scoped to `gbf-store` only — closing F-A6 closes T-A6.0..T-A6.4 and `bd-3ll`. This bead (`bd-n9i`) is `br defer`-red and is **no longer** a closure-blocker for `bd-3ll`. A new feature bead `F-A6b` will open in the future and will own the `gbf-migrate` work.

description: gbf-bench produces real measurements that populate the calibration schema from F-A2.7. PlatformCalibrationBundle (bank_switch_cost, sram_page_cost, timer_isr_cost), KernelCalibrationBundle (per-kernel measured profiles), RuntimeCalibrationBundle (scheduler_overhead, overlay_install_cost, trace_event_cost). Cycle-model drift reports + constrained autotune over tile/residency/slice knobs.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Epic E: Calibration & Bench (`gbf-bench`)

### What this is

`gbf-bench` per `planv0.md` line 318: workload manifests, cycle calibration, layered calibration bundle production (`PlatformCalibrationBundle`, `KernelCalibrationBundle`, `RuntimeCalibrationBundle`), constrained autotuning, cycle-model drift reporting.

The schema for these types lands in M0 (F-A2.7). This epic produces real *measurements* that populate them.

### Why this matters

`ScheduleCostAnalysis` (Epic B F-B12) is the only objective-facing cost producer in the compiler. Its inputs are calibration bundles. Without real measurements, cost estimates are heuristics with no `EvidenceClass::Measured` data, and `RiskPolicy::require_confidence_at_least` always fails.

`HardCap` switch budgets in `CompileProfile` (F11 / `bd-1i8`) graduate from hand-picked numbers to calibration-derived values once Epic E's `PlatformCalibrationBundle` exists with measured `bank_switch_cost`.

### Scope (six features)

- **F-E1 — Workload manifest pipeline**: `WorkloadManifest`, `WorkloadClass`, `AcceptanceMatrix`, `ExecutionMatrix`, `ObservationPolicy` types in `gbf-workload` plus the bench runner that consumes them.
- **F-E2 — `PlatformCalibrationBundle` production**: measure `bank_switch_cost`, `sram_page_cost`, `timer_isr_cost` against a target via emulator or hardware.
- **F-E3 — `KernelCalibrationBundle` production**: per-kernel measured profiles tied to `kernel_impl_hash` + `runtime_nucleus_hash`.
- **F-E4 — `RuntimeCalibrationBundle` production**: `scheduler_overhead`, `overlay_install_cost`, `trace_event_cost`.
- **F-E5 — Cycle-model drift reports**: compare `gbf-asm` cycle model predictions to measured kernel runs; produce drift reports.
- **F-E6 — Constrained autotune**: explicit knob set (tile sizes, kernel residency, slice ceilings); Pareto frontier; objective-driven selection.

### Out of scope

- Producing the artifacts themselves → Epic B.
- Running oracles in calibration mode → Epic C + this epic interface.

### Critical path

```
F-A2.7 (calibration schema) ──→ F-E1..F-E4
F-A1 (gbf-asm cycle model) ──→ F-E5 drift reports
F-H3 (emulator adapters) ────→ F-E2..F-E4 (bench runs against emulator)
```

### Confidence: MEDIUM

Bench infrastructure is straightforward. The risk is "what's a good baseline measurement context" — emulator vs hardware vs both, and how MeasurementContext encodes that.

title: T-B3.12: Identity + SequenceSemantics + NormPlanIdPre + TensorBinding (Wave 2 classes 1–4; absorbs T-B3.13/13a/14)
description:
## What
Implement `IdentityBinding` (QGClass 1 in §8.3): bind
`artifact_core_hash`, `policy_resolution_self_hash`,
`artifact_validation_self_hash`, `semantic_core_hash`,
`lowering_manifest_hash`, `determinism`, and `model_spec_summary` from
the F-B2 inputs into `QuantGraphIdentity`.

## Why
This is the first construction class because it both (a) carries the
hashes K1 will key off (RFC §11), and (b) provides the fields that
later classes cross-reference. Specifically:
- `semantic_core_hash` = `i.validated.input_hashes.artifact_effective_core_hash`
  (QG-Pre-2 / QG-Ok-4). Drift triggers
  `QuantGraphIdentityHashMismatch`.
- `lowering_manifest_hash` is bound from
  `validated.input_hashes.lowering_manifest_hash` so cache
  invalidation responds to lowering drift (§8.1).
- `determinism` is read from `ArtifactCore.numeric_profile`, NOT from
  `ResolvedCompilePolicy` (Ambiguity A20, §9.10). This keeps the data
  flow strictly linear: F-B3 binds determinism from artifact, F-B5
  inherits from F-B3.

`ModelSpecSummary` carries summary-only fields per Ambiguity A39:
`n_layers`, `n_experts(layer)`, `d_model`, `d_ff`, `vocab_size`, and
per-layer `ffn_kind`. Per-layer `activation_kind` /
`intermediate_format` belong in `ffn_plans` (T-B3.10), not here.

## Inputs
- T-B3.1 (`QuantGraphIdentity`, `ModelSpecSummary` shape).
- F-B2 outputs: `ValidatedInputs`, `ResolvedCompilePolicy`,
  `ArtifactCore`.

## Outputs
- `fn bind_identity(i: &QuantGraphInputs) -> Result<QuantGraphIdentity,
  Vec<ValidationDiagnostic>>` (collects hard diagnostics; this is the
  canonical accumulate-within-class pattern from QG-Accumulate).
- Diagnostic mappings: `QuantGraphIdentityHashMismatch` (Stage 0
  binding drift), `QuantGraphRequiredFeatureUnsupported`.

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT read `determinism` from policy (Ambiguity A20). It comes from
  artifact's `numeric_profile`.
- DO NOT compute the summary by walking `ArtifactCore.tensors`; that
  invites drift. Read it from authoritative artifact metadata.
- IdentityBinding may collect diagnostics but must NOT fail-fast — the
  later classes need to attempt their work to surface as many issues
  as possible (QG-Accumulate / QG-ShortCircuit only when *invalidated*).

## Acceptance
- `gbf-codegen::identity_binding_pulls_determinism_from_artifact_not_policy`.
- `gbf-codegen::identity_binding_records_lowering_manifest_hash`.
- `gbf-codegen::identity_binding_emits_hash_mismatch_diagnostic_typed`.

## Refs
- RFC §8.3 (Construction order class 1), §8.1 (Identity fields),
  Ambiguity ledger A20, A39.
- Depends on: T-B3.1.
- Blocks: T-B3.13 (next class), T-B3.22 (cross-class checks consume
  identity), T-B3.25 (K1 keys off identity hashes).

title: F-B8 T20: RepairProposal emission (PromoteRecompute, ForceRecompute) — proposal-only handshake with F-B16
description:
# RepairProposal emission for F-B16

## Why proposal-only

F-B8 never accepts a repair proposal — that is F-B16 FeasibilityRefinementLoop's authority. F-B8 only *emits* proposals when:

* `DR-13` fires for a value that would have been admitted by `DR-11 RecomputeForPureSliceValue` under a higher promotion level, **and**
* WRAM/HRAM/SRAM pressure summarized in `StoragePlanSummary.abstract_pressure` exceeds its soft threshold (T5's `soft_pressure_threshold_bytes`).

The proposal is emitted with `source = PlanningStage::StoragePlan`, `reason = RepairReason::PromoteRecompute`, and a typed `ConstraintDelta`. The driver records proposals in `StoragePlan.repair_proposals: Vec<RepairProposal>`. In v1 (pre-F-B16), proposals are emitted but never fed back — the wired-but-not-driven state is intentional, to let us verify the typed handshake before F-B16's acceptance logic exists.

## Knob bounds and locks (RFC §2.10)

Every emitted proposal must respect:

* `CompileKnobBounds.max_recompute_promotion` — proposed level cannot exceed bound. Violation: STORE-027.
* `CompileKnobId::StorageRecomputePromotion ∈ KnobLockSet.locked` — no proposal advances the level. F-B8 emits zero proposals.

For value-localized cases, emit `KnobDelta::ForceRecompute { values }` instead of a bulk `PromoteRecomputeLevel` advance.

## Proposal shape

```rust
RepairProposal {
    source: PlanningStage::StoragePlan,
    reason: RepairReason::PromoteRecompute,
    tighten: ConstraintDelta {
        changes: vec![KnobDelta::PromoteRecomputeLevel { to: PureSliceValues }],
        // or:
        changes: vec![KnobDelta::ForceRecompute { values: ... }],
    },
    estimated_cost: EstimatedCostDelta {
        cycles: Some(sum_of_recompute_cost_estimate(v).cycles),
        bytes:  Some(sum_of_logical_byte_size(v)),
        ...
    },
}
```

`EstimatedCostDelta.cycles` and `.bytes` are dimensioned (T11 fixed the v1 cycles-vs-bytes confusion); they must stay typed as separate fields.

## Note on v1 promotion ladder

v2 narrowed v1 to `{None, PureSliceValues}`. Do not emit `PromoteRecomputeLevel { to: PureResumeWindowValues }` or `PureTokenValues` — those levels are reserved. STORE-027 fires if the proposal violates the bound.

## Acceptance

* Unit test: M1 degenerate fixture under `recompute_promotion = None` and pressure above soft threshold produces a proposal to advance to `PureSliceValues`; no further proposals fire.
* Unit test: with `KnobLockSet.locked` set on `StorageRecomputePromotion`, zero proposals emit.
* Unit test: a proposal advancing beyond `max_recompute_promotion` fires STORE-027.
* Unit test: PO-23 — every emitted proposal has `source = StoragePlan` and `tighten.changes ⊆ {PromoteRecomputeLevel, ForceRecompute}`.

## Anti-patterns

* Do not let F-B8 accept its own proposal. That is F-B16's job.
* Do not propose advances beyond the v1 ladder (`None, PureSliceValues`).
* Do not emit a proposal when the knob is locked.

Depends on: T15, T5.

### Knob bounds (RFC §2.10)

* `proposal_respects_max_recompute_promotion` — `CompileKnobBounds.max_recompute_promotion = None` → zero proposals (cannot advance).
* `proposal_violation_fires_store_027` — synthetic proposal that would advance past max → STORE-027 with `proposal_id, ConstraintDelta, max_recompute_promotion`.

* `no_proposal_when_knob_locked` — `KnobLockSet.locked` contains `CompileKnobId::StorageRecomputePromotion` → zero proposals.

### Proposal id stability (PO-23)

* `proposal_id_stable_across_two_runs` — same inputs → identical proposal ids in identical order. Critical for cache replay.

### Cost dimensions (regression for v1 cycles-vs-bytes confusion)

* `proposal_cost_carries_cycles_and_bytes_separately` — `EstimatedCostDelta.cycles: Option<u64>` and `bytes: Option<u64>` are separate fields. Trybuild compile-fail if collapsed.

### Promotion ladder (v1 narrowing)

* `proposal_advances_to_pure_slice_values_only` — v1's only legal advance is None → PureSliceValues. Any proposal to advance to PureResumeWindowValues fires STORE-027.

* `proposals_recorded_in_repair_proposals_field` — `StoragePlan.repair_proposals: Vec<RepairProposal>` populated.

Events:
* `f_b8.proposal.emitted` (INFO) — per proposal: `reason ("PromoteRecompute"), tighten_summary (e.g. "PromoteRecomputeLevel→PureSliceValues"), estimated_cost (cycles, bytes)`.
* `f_b8.proposal.suppressed_by_lock` (DEBUG) — when knob lock prevents emission.
* `f_b8.proposal.bound_violation` (ERROR) — preceding STORE-027.
