title: Epic H: Kernel — gbf-kernel
description: gbf-kernel owns kernel contracts and the first-wave kernel implementations (matvec, residual, norm, route, decode) as AsmIR builders tied to KernelSpecId + KernelCalibrationBundle. Per planv0.md (revised) lines 2715-2720, the previously-sketched two-backend SameBoy+BGB emulator model is dropped; gbf-emu has moved to Epic A (F-A7) as an M0 deliverable, and gbf-debug joins it (F-A8). Epic H now scopes only to gbf-kernel.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Epic H: Kernel & Emulator (`gbf-kernel`, `gbf-emu`)

### What this is

Two crates that are infrastructure for the core compiler/runtime work:

- `gbf-kernel` per `planv0.md` line 189: "owns kernel contracts and kernel-family implementations; `gbf-codegen` selects them and `gbf-runtime` links them, but neither redefines kernel signatures." A kernel here is e.g., `matvec_int8`, `residual_add`, `top1_router`, `softmax_clipped`, etc. — the actual compute primitives.
- `gbf-emu`: emulator adapters (SameBoy / BGB), breakpoint orchestration, trace normalization, harness mode. Per planv0.md line 2552: "emulator accuracy solved by adapters around SameBoy/BGB rather than re-implementation."

### Why this matters

Without `gbf-kernel`, every compile request reinvents matvec. Without `gbf-emu`, every test that runs a ROM is bespoke shell-out to an emulator.

### Scope (three features)

- **F-H1 — `KernelSpec` + signatures + compatibility ids**: schema types only. `KernelSpec`, `KernelSpecId`, signatures, calling conventions, `KernelCompatSpec`, autotune dimensions.
- **F-H2 — Kernel implementations**: AsmIR builders for the first kernel families (matvec, residual, norm, route, decode). Each tied to a `KernelSpecId` and a `KernelCalibrationBundle`.
- **F-H3 — Emulator adapters**: SameBoy + BGB adapters with shared trait, breakpoint orchestration, normalized trace event format, harness command/result block plumbing.

### Critical path

```
F-A1 (gbf-asm builders) ──→ F-H2 (kernels are AsmIR sections)
F-A3 (gbf-abi traces)   ──→ F-H3 (adapters parse traces)
F-H1 ───→ F-B (compiler kernel selection in stages)
F-H3 ───→ F-E (bench needs adapters to run measurements)
```

### Confidence: MEDIUM

Adapters are real engineering — the harness-mode plumbing (breakpoints, memory inspection, trace dumping) varies between SameBoy and BGB. F-H2 kernel implementations are the steady-state work that gets refined over many milestones.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## Epic H scope reduced (2026-04-30): gbf-emu moved out

### What changed

`history/planv0.md` was revised to drop the two-backend SameBoy+BGB model in favor of a single Rust-native gameroy adapter (planv0.md lines 2715-2720). At the same time, the M0 milestone added an agent-facing scripted debugger (`gbf-debug`) layered on top. Both crates are now M0 deliverables (planv0.md line 2901).

The result: `gbf-emu` belongs in **Epic A (M0)**, not here. Epic H now scopes only to `gbf-kernel`.

### What stays in Epic H

- **F-H1** (`bd-2f32`): `KernelSpec` + signatures + compatibility ids
- **F-H2** (`bd-3se9`): Kernel implementations (matvec, residual, norm, route, decode)

That's it. Two features.

### What moved out

- **F-H3** (`bd-1aqc`): "Emulator adapters (SameBoy + BGB) in gbf-emu" — **closed as superseded** by F-A7 (`bd-3mxe`) in Epic A. The two-backend model is dropped entirely; gameroy is the single backend.

### What replaces F-H3 in Epic A

- **F-A7** (`bd-3mxe`): `gbf-emu` — gameroy adapter, DeterminismPolicy, breakpoint/watchpoint primitives, snapshot-restore, framebuffer, joypad-injection, registry-driven trap dispatcher.
- **F-A8** (`bd-1o08`): `gbf-debug` — agent-facing scripted debugger CLI (rquickjs scripting host + zstd-compressed session files).

### Why dropping the two-backend model is correct

planv0.md lines 2715-2720 spell it out:

> The emulator strategy is single-backend on purpose: gameroy as the sole Rust-native core, used by both bulk CI and nightly/trust runs; `gbf-debug` layered on top to give agents a programmable, stateless machine-interface debugger. The previously-sketched two-backend split (separate accuracy backend wrapping an external emulator/debugger) is dropped: gameroy already passes most mooneye-test-suite accuracy gates, and maintaining two adapters and two calibration bundles in a Rust-only project did not pay for itself. The differential ladder still has its bites — `ScheduleOracle` ↔ harness, `ArtifactOracle` ↔ `ScheduleOracle`, conformance vs `DenotationalOracle` — we just stopped pretending two emulator cores were the load-bearing safety net.

### Milestone retiming

Epic H was M1-M3. Now M2-M3 — F-H1 (KernelSpec types) is roughly when M2's first kernel ships; F-H2 (kernel implementations) drives into M3 alongside the routed FFN MoE work.

### Dependency cleanup

Beads outside Epic H that previously blocked on F-H3 (`bd-1aqc`):

- **F-E2** (`bd-2ww0`, PlatformCalibrationBundle production) — dependency redirected to F-A7 (`bd-3mxe`).

No other beads referenced F-H3 inbound.

title: T-B3.27: build_quant_graph_core (pure) / run_stage1 (driver) split; ResolvedBlobIndex as pure input
description:
## What
Split Stage 1 into pure core and IO driver:

```
fn build_quant_graph_core(i: QuantGraphInputs)
   -> Result<QuantGraphProduct, QuantGraphStageFailure>;
   // pure; no IO; no StageCache writes; no JSON emission

fn run_stage1(i: QuantGraphInputs, env: PassEnvironment)
   -> Result<QuantGraphProduct, QuantGraphStageFailure>;
   // driver; emits quant_graph.json; may write StageCache
   //   success entry + failure memo
```

`ResolvedBlobIndex` is a *pure input* (T-B3.2a): the driver
(`run_stage1`) builds it using IO; the core never opens a file.

## Why
This is the single most-cited proof obligation of the chunk: O22
(pure-function shape). Without it, `build_quant_graph_core` is not a
pure function of typed inputs and:
- Caching cannot guarantee determinism (a hidden FS read could change
  output).
- Tests cannot construct stub artifacts and hit the core directly.
- F-C2 cannot evaluate `QuantGraph` reproducibly across builds.

`run_stage1` is the only function that touches:
- Filesystem (to build `ResolvedBlobIndex`).
- StageCache (to write success entries / failure memos).
- JSON sink (to emit `quant_graph.json`).

The same `Result` is returned by both — the driver simply wraps the
core with IO. This is identical to the F-B2/F-B4 driver pattern.

## Inputs
- T-B3.26 (fixtures cover both happy + reject paths).
- F-B2's `PassEnvironment` machinery.

## Outputs
- `fn build_quant_graph_core(i: QuantGraphInputs) ->
  Result<QuantGraphProduct, QuantGraphStageFailure>` — invokes the
  full QGClass 1..14 chain in order.
- `fn run_stage1(i: QuantGraphInputs, env: PassEnvironment) ->
  Result<...>` — wraps `build_quant_graph_core`, builds
  `ResolvedBlobIndex` from artifact storage, emits report,
  reads/writes StageCache.
- `gbf-codegen::pure_core_signature_takes_resolved_blob_index_not_resolver`
  compile-time check (Ambiguity A71).

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT have `build_quant_graph_core` accept a `dyn ArtifactResolver`
  (Ambiguity A71). Pure cores never do IO.
- DO NOT have `run_stage1` rebuild `ResolvedBlobIndex` differently
  from cache hits — both must produce identical metadata for the
  same inputs (proof obligation O1).
- Audit-parent fields (`policy_resolution_self_hash`,
  `compile_request_hash`) must be re-wrapped on cache hit even though
  the embedded product is byte-identical — this is the same
  C-ReportRewrap rule used by Stage 3 (Ambiguity A76).

## Acceptance
- `gbf-codegen::build_quant_graph_core_is_pure_function`.
- `gbf-codegen::run_stage1_emits_report_and_writes_cache`.
- `gbf-codegen::run_stage1_cache_hit_replays_byte_identical_product`.

## Refs
- RFC §8.2 (Operation contract), §11 (StageCache laws), Proof
  obligations O22, O13, O1, Ambiguity ledger A71.
- Depends on: T-B3.26.
- Blocks: T-B5.1 (F-B5 type binding can begin), T-B3.28 (review
  packet), all Wave 3+ T-B5.* tasks (per RFC §14: "F-B3 must merge
  before F-B5").
close_reason: Implemented Stage 1 pure core / driver split with ResolvedBlobIndex pure input, report emission, StageCache success/failure memo handling, and cache-hit byte-identical replay. Forced only over malformed imported empty dependency / parent-rollup bookkeeping, not over a real open prerequisite. Reviews: Claude CONCERN addressed by bd-2juw then Claude PASS; Gemini PASS. Gates: cargo test -p gbf-codegen --lib s1::quant_graph::tests:: (141 passed); cargo test -p gbf-codegen --lib stage_cache::tests::stage_cache (30 passed earlier); bash scripts/e2e/stage1.sh PASS; cargo clippy -p gbf-codegen --all-features -- -D warnings passed. A76 decision documented: Stage 1 keys on full policy_resolution_self_hash and does not use Stage 3-style audit rewrap.

## F-F1: Build reports

### What this is

Emit the structured JSON + binary report set per `planv0.md` line 1577: `map.json`, `provenance.json`, `budget.json`, `slice_report.json`, `trace_schema.json`, `oracle_vectors.bin`, `semantic_checkpoint_schema.json`, `operational_probe_schema.json`, `artifact_lineage.json`, `workload_manifest.json`, `hint_consumption.json`, `compiler_feedback.json`, `reachability_report.json`. Every regression in the system gets caught by diffing reports between builds. Without structured reports, debugging a regression is bisecting + cycle-counter staring.

### Design sketch

One JSON schema per report. Reports go into `artifacts/builds/<build_id>/`. CI tests round-trip each schema. Schema versioning via `gbf-migrate`.

- All compiler stages (F-B0..F-B13) emit their reports
- F-A6.1 gbf-store for archival
- F-A6.5 gbf-migrate for schema evolution

title: F-B14: ScheduleCostAnalysis (Stage 11)
description:
# F-B14 — ScheduleCostAnalysis (Stage 11)

**Source RFC:** `history/rfcs/F-B14-F-B17-schedule-cost-stagecache.md` (paired RFC with F-B17).

## Why this stage exists

F-B13 leaves the pipeline with spatial + scheduling decisions final, but no oracle for "will this artifact satisfy the compile objective on the target hardware?" F-B14 is the **single load-bearing producer of objective-facing cost envelopes** in the pipeline. It consumes the `SchedulePack` and the resolved `CompileObjective`, dereferences calibration bundles by hash, and produces a per-`RuntimeMode` `EstimatedCostDelta` map — each estimate carrying an `EvidenceClass`, an `UncertaintyEnvelope`, and an `EvidenceRef` chain back to the calibrated source, transferred source, or heuristic fallback that produced it.

This is the fourth shift-left filter (after `gbf-train preflight`, `ArtifactValidationAndUpgrade`, and cache-correctness): it catches "this schedule won't satisfy the objective" before F-B15 pays the cost of codegen, placement, and encoding. It is also the only stage that delivers per-mode cost envelopes — without which M4 SchedulePack mode switching cannot decide which mode satisfies the active objective at which quantile.

## Pipeline context

**Inputs (pinned, hash-bound into K14):**
- `SchedulePackProduct` (F-B13) — per-mode slice schedules, epochs, checkpoint schema.
- `ResolvedCompilePolicy` (F-B2) — CompileObjective + RuntimeModeSet.
- `CalibrationBundleSet` (Epic E) — measured cycle costs keyed by KernelSpecId.
- `RuntimeChromeBudget` — memory/budget constraints.
- `TargetProfile` — hardware target identity.
- `KernelSpecRegistry` (Epic H) — available kernel implementations.

**Outputs:**
- `schedule_cost.json` with `ScheduleCostReport` body (canonical JSON with self-hash).
- Per-mode `EstimatedCostDelta` map keyed by RuntimeMode.

**Downstream consumers:**
- F-B16 FeasibilityRefinementLoop — reads per-mode EstimatedCostDelta to evaluate RepairProposal acceptance.
- F-B15 Backend — embeds per-mode envelopes in budget.json, map.json, compiler_feedback.json.

## Core data types

- **EvidenceClass** — `Calibrated < Transferred < Heuristic < Fallback` (lower = tighter; ordering is REVERSED from everyday strength).
- **UncertaintyEnvelope** — `{ p50_q16_16, p95_lower_q16_16, p95_upper_q16_16, p99_upper_q16_16? }` — Q16.16 fixed-point (±2^47 cycles, 16-bit fractional precision; NO floating point anywhere). Invariant: `p95_lower ≤ p50 ≤ p95_upper ≤ p99_upper`.
- **CostEstimate** — `{ evidence_class, envelope, refs: Vec<EvidenceRef>, fallback_reason: Option<FallbackReason> }`. Invariant: Calibrated/Transferred ⇒ refs nonempty ∧ fallback_reason None; Heuristic/Fallback ⇒ fallback_reason Some.
- **EstimatedCostDelta** (per mode) — required: cycles_per_token, bank_switches_per_token, yields_per_token, scheduler_headroom_utilization, max_no_progress_estimate, time_to_first_token, sustained_throughput_tokens_per_megacycle. Optional: sram_page_switches_per_token (if persistent pages), video_commit_cost_margin (if UI nucleus), frame_jitter (if objective requires). Each field independently classed.
- **EvidenceRef** variants — `CalibrationBundle { bundle_kind, bundle_hash, record_path, confidence } | CycleModel { kernel_spec, cycle_model_hash } | HeuristicPolicy { policy_id, version } | TransferPolicy { id, from_target, to_target, hash } | Composition { component_refs }`.
- **FallbackReason** — `NoBundleForTarget | ConfidenceBelowRequirement(declared, required) | KernelSpecNotCalibrated | BundleStale(field, declared, observed) | MeasurementShapeMismatch | UpstreamFallback(Box<...>)`. `stale_field ∈ {TargetProfileHash, KernelSetHash, PackerVersion, CalibrationSchemaHash, ValidityEnvelope}`.
- **ScheduleCostReport** — `{ objective, per_mode: BTreeMap<RuntimeMode, EstimatedCostDelta>, satisfaction: ObjectiveSatisfactionMatrix, refs (union), identity }`.
- **ObjectiveSatisfactionMatrix** — entries keyed by `{ mode, axis, quantile: P50|P95|P99 }` with value `Satisfied | Borderline | Violated`.

## Algorithm sketch (deterministic pure function)

1. **Per-slice cost projection** (per mode, per slice): resolve KernelSpecId → CycleModelRef from CalibrationBundleSet by hash; compute per-op cycle estimate with EvidenceClass; sum bank/page switch contributions.
2. **Per-token rollup** (per mode): cycles_per_token = sum(slice cycles in token frame); compute scheduler_headroom_utilization = predicted/FrameBudget; compute video_commit_cost_margin / frame_jitter if objective requires.
3. **Per-objective satisfaction** (per mode × axis × quantile): Satisfied if pessimistic ≤ target; Borderline if predicted ≤ target but pessimistic > target; Violated if optimistic > target.
4. **Fallback marking**: Heuristic/Fallback ⇒ fallback_reason Some; composed-from-upstream-fallback ⇒ UpstreamFallback.
5. **Assemble ScheduleCostReport**; build envelope with `report_self_hash` (canonical JSON hash with self-hash field zeroed).

**Evidence composition rules (per-slice sum):**
- Calibrated if every component Calibrated; Transferred if all ∈ {Calibrated, Transferred} and ≥1 Transferred; Heuristic if all ∈ {Calibrated, Transferred, Heuristic} and ≥1 Heuristic; Fallback if any Fallback.
- Envelope sum: p50 := Σp50; p95_lower := Σp95_lower (best-case); p95_upper := Σp95_upper (worst-case); p99_upper := Σp99_upper if all present, else None.
- Conservative composition (no independence assumption); future RFC may add `IndependenceClaim` for quadrature.

**Calibration resolution** `lookup_record(CB, m, kspec, r, tc)`:
- Exact match → Calibrated
- Transfer-eligible match → Transferred
- Else → Heuristic from policy

## Invariants

- COST-* codes (see Diagnostics) enforce hash integrity, freshness gates, confidence tiers, refs consistency, envelope ordering, satisfaction matrix consistency, refs union completeness.
- Risk policy confidence tiers: Bringup (NoMinimumConfidence) allows Heuristic; Default/Trace/Recovery (Measured/Transferred) hard-fail on missing.
- Self-consistency (§8.3): per_mode.keys() == requested_runtime_modes; all estimates classed; every EvidenceRef resolves through `gbf-store::BlobStore` with canonical-JSON round-trip hash match; optional fields gated by SramPagePlan/UI nucleus presence; NO floating-point fields; satisfaction recomputable from per_mode + objective.

## Cache invariants (§11.2)

- K14-Success: passed → cache stores product + report.
- K14-FailureMemo: failed → cache memos canonical failure report under exact input-hash match.
- K14-ReadValidate: on hit, cached self_hash must equal computed; mismatch poisons + recomputes.
- K14-PolicyProjection: only `compile_objective, risk_policy.calibration_confidence_requirement, requested_runtime_modes` affect K14 (NOT observability mode, decode policy, etc.).

## Diagnostic algebra (closed, all Hard, origin `ScheduleCostAnalysis`)

CostScheduleCostInputHashMismatch, CostCalibrationBundleHashMismatch, CostCalibrationBundleStale, CostCalibrationMissingForRequirement, CostKernelSpecNotInRegistry, CostPerModeMissing, CostPerModeUnexpected, CostEvidenceClassRefsInconsistent, CostFallbackReasonMissing, CostFallbackReasonPresentForCalibrated, CostUncertaintyEnvelopeMalformed, CostUncertaintyEnvelopeNegative, CostObjectiveSatisfactionMatrixIncomplete, CostObjectiveSatisfactionMatrixInconsistent, CostHeuristicPolicyUnknown, CostTransferPolicyUnknown, CostFloatingPointFieldDetected, CostScheduleCostSchemaUnknown, CostOptionFieldMissing, CostOptionFieldPresentUnexpectedly, CostRefsUnionInconsistent, CostScheduleCostReportRoundTripFailed, CostFinalNonNegativityViolation.

## Cache key (K14)

```
K14 := DomainHash('gbf-codegen', 'StageCacheKey', 'schedule_cost.v1', '1.0.0',
                  CanonicalJson({
                    schedule_pack_self_hash,
                    policy_resolution_self_hash,
                    calibration_bundle_set_hash,
                    runtime_chrome_budget_hash,
                    target_profile_hash,
                    kernel_spec_registry_hash,
                    schedule_cost_policy_projection_hash, // projection, not full policy
                    pass_version: 'stage11/v1',
                    crate_feature_set_hash,
                    schedule_cost_schema_hash,
                  }))
```

K14-K10 cascade: `K14.schedule_pack_self_hash` must equal the SchedulePack hash produced under K10.

## Interaction with F-B16

F-B14 is **passive**: it produces estimates + evidence classes. F-B16 owns comparison logic and policy. Flow: F-B16 proposes ConstraintDelta → re-runs F-B7..F-B13 to produce candidate SchedulePack → re-runs F-B14 → compares `candidate.per_mode[m]` vs `current.per_mode[m]` → accept/reject per active RepairPolicy.

## Open questions / risks

1. CalibrationConfidenceClass taxonomy inherited from Epic E; refinements there force F-B14 amendment.
2. Conservative-sum composition; future `IndependenceClaim` may tighten quadrature.
3. Oracle-loop cost-delta comparison semantics owned by F-B16 RFC; F-B14 only guarantees envelope determinism + evidence classing.

## Test surface (closure gate)

- RC-COST-1..9 fixtures (one per major diagnostic code).
- Determinism: byte-identical regeneration.
- Round-trip: serialize → deserialize → structural equality.
- Cache-miss-vs-hit equivalence: byte-identical outputs.

## How this serves the overarching goal

Compiling an LM to a Game Boy ROM under a `CompileObjective` (max latency, throughput, frame jitter) needs a stage that says "this schedule, at this mode, will hit your targets with this confidence." F-B14 is the only stage that delivers this. Without it, M3 closes the IR pipeline but the cost surface is missing, and M4 mode switching has no oracle to choose modes.
design:
# F-B14 Implementation design

## Crate / module structure
- **Owner crate:** `gbf-codegen`
- **Modules:** `gbf-codegen::schedule_cost` (public), `::core` (rollup), `::evidence` (composition), `::satisfaction` (objective matrix), `::diagnostics`, `::cache` (K14).
- **Public types:** `EvidenceClass`, `UncertaintyEnvelope`, `CostEstimate`, `EvidenceRef`, `FallbackReason`, `EstimatedCostDelta`, `ScheduleCostReport`, `ObjectiveSatisfactionMatrix`, `SatisfactionKey`, `ObjectiveSatisfaction`.
- **Public entry:** `build_schedule_cost(inputs) -> ScheduleCostReportProduct` (pure, deterministic).

## Critical engineering rule: Q16.16 fixed-point only

ALL cycle / cost / throughput / utilization fields are `i64` Q16.16 fixed-point. **Floating-point fields are a hard reject (`CostFloatingPointFieldDetected`).** Rationale: hash determinism + cross-platform reproducibility.

Helpers in `gbf-codegen::schedule_cost::q1616`:
- `q1616_from_u32_cycles(u32) -> i64`
- `q1616_add_saturating(a, b) -> i64`
- `q1616_mul_saturating(a, b) -> i64`
- `q1616_le(a, b) -> bool`
- `q1616_ratio(num, den) -> i64`

## Implementation phases (ordered, gated)

1. **Phase 1 — Type surface + Q16.16 utilities.** All public types + Q16.16 helpers + arithmetic property tests (no overflow, monotone). Gate: round-trip; envelope ordering invariant (`p95_lower ≤ p50 ≤ p95_upper ≤ p99_upper`).
2. **Phase 2 — Input bundle + K14.** Pin 10 fields including `schedule_cost_policy_projection_hash` (projection: only `compile_objective`, `risk_policy.calibration_confidence_requirement`, `requested_runtime_modes`). Gate: F-B17 conformance; K14→K10 cascade (K10 miss ⇒ K14 miss).
3. **Phase 3 — Calibration resolution.** `lookup_record(CB, mode, kspec, residency, tile_class)`: exact → Calibrated; transfer-eligible → Transferred; else → Heuristic. Gate: every kernel spec resolves; missing under non-Bringup profile → `CostCalibrationMissingForRequirement` Hard.
4. **Phase 4 — Per-slice cost projection.** Per SchedOp: resolve KernelSpecId → CycleModelRef by hash; compute per-op cycle estimate with EvidenceClass; tally bank/page switch contributions. Gate: per-op evidence class composes correctly.
5. **Phase 5 — Evidence composition rules.** Per-slice sum: Calibrated if all C; Transferred if all ∈ {C,T} ∧ ≥1 T; Heuristic if all ∈ {C,T,H} ∧ ≥1 H; Fallback if any F. Envelope sum: conservative (no independence assumption). Gate: per-mode rollup composition correctness.
6. **Phase 6 — Per-token rollup per mode.** cycles_per_token = Σ slice cycles in token frame; scheduler_headroom_utilization = predicted/FrameBudget; video_commit_cost_margin / frame_jitter conditional. Gate: required fields always present; optional gated by upstream presence (SramPagePlan, UI nucleus).
7. **Phase 7 — Objective satisfaction matrix.** Per (mode, axis, quantile): Satisfied if pessimistic ≤ target; Borderline if predicted ≤ target but pessimistic > target; Violated if optimistic > target. Gate: matrix is total over `requested_runtime_modes × objective.axes × {P50, P95, P99}`.
8. **Phase 8 — Fallback marking.** Heuristic/Fallback ⇒ fallback_reason Some; composed-from-fallback ⇒ `UpstreamFallback`. Gate: cross-product CostEstimate validator.
9. **Phase 9 — ScheduleCostReport assembly + `report_self_hash`.** refs := union of all CostEstimate.refs (deduplicated). Gate: refs union completeness check.
10. **Phase 10 — Diagnostic algebra.** 23 closed codes. Gate: each has reject fixture.
11. **Phase 11 — Cache integration (K14).** Success → product + report cached; failure → memo. Gate: K14-Success, K14-FailureMemo, K14-ReadValidate, K14-PolicyProjection.
12. **Phase 12 — Cross-stage integration.** F-B15 backend embeds per-mode envelopes in budget.json + compiler_feedback.json. Gate: serde compatibility test.
13. **Phase 13 — E2E verify-packet.** `scripts/review/f-b14/verify-packet.sh`.

## Structured tracing catalog

**Top-level span:** `gbf.compile.stage11_schedule_cost` with `stage_id=11`, `build_id`, `input_identity_hash`, `cache_status`, `outcome`, `mode_count`, `evidence_class_distribution: {calibrated, transferred, heuristic, fallback}`, `satisfaction_summary: {satisfied, borderline, violated}`, `self_hash`.

**Events:**
- Common start/cache/complete.

### Unit tests
- `stage11_q1616_arithmetic.rs` — saturating add/mul; monotone; no overflow; ordering invariants.

- `reject/RC-COST-8_evidence_class_refs_inconsistent.json`.

- All 23 closed codes covered.

### Property tests
- `prop_envelope_sum_monotone` — adding a component never decreases p95_upper.
- `prop_evidence_class_join_associative` — composition is order-independent.
- `prop_satisfaction_matrix_total` — every (mode, axis, quantile) populated.

### Determinism + cache tests
- `determinism_two_runs_byte_identical`.

### E2E verify-packet (`scripts/review/f-b14/verify-packet.sh`)
1. Run all stage-11 tests.
2. Compile sample LM through Stage 11 with calibration bundle (Calibrated path).
3. Re-run with calibration removed under Bringup profile (Heuristic path); verify fallback_reason chain.
4. Re-run with calibration removed under Default profile (hard fail with `CostCalibrationMissingForRequirement`).

## Performance budget
- Wall-clock target: < 100 ms on M3 sample LM (per-mode rollup over ~200 slices).
- Memory ceiling: < 16 MiB peak.
- Cache hit: < 10 ms.

comments.text:
## F-B12: ScheduleCostAnalysis (Stage 11)

### What this is

The single load-bearing producer of objective-facing cost envelopes (`planv0.md` line 1484). Runs over `GbSchedIR` / `SchedulePack`, uses calibration bundles, produces per-mode cost envelopes that predict objective satisfaction and feed the refinement loop.

### Why this matters

Every other stage produces structural facts; F-B12 produces *predicted cost*. Centralizing keeps repair logic testable: a `RepairProposal::estimated_cost: EstimatedCostDelta` is meaningful only if there's a single oracle for cost.

### Design sketch

```rust
pub struct ScheduleCostReport {
    pub objective: CompileObjective,
    pub per_mode: BTreeMap<RuntimeMode, EstimatedCostDelta>,
    pub refs: Vec<EvidenceRef>,
}

pub struct EstimatedCostDelta {
    pub cycles: Option<CostEstimate>,
    pub bank_switches: Option<CostEstimate>,
    pub sram_page_switches: Option<CostEstimate>,
    pub bytes: Option<CostEstimate>,
}
```

Each `CostEstimate` carries `EvidenceClass::{Measured, Transferred, Heuristic}` + `sample_count` + `refs` so risk policies can reject low-confidence estimates.

### Cross-feature deps

- F-B11 GbSchedIR
- Epic E calibration bundles (`PlatformCalibrationBundle` etc.)

### Confidence: HIGH

title: F-S2.21: s2_ablation.v1 schema + emitter (AB-1 / AB-2)
description:
Goal
====
Implement s2_ablation.v1 — the seed-0 H4 comparator artifact recording
the two checkpoint shas, the canonical tensor payload shas, the equality
flag, and the first_mismatch diagnostic. Per F-S2 RFC §9.7.

Why this matters
================
H4 is a closure gate: the s2_ternary_full Phase A end checkpoint MUST
have a CanonicalTensorPayloadHash equal to the s2_ablation Phase A end
checkpoint for seed 0. This proves Phase A under the S2 binary is
uncontaminated by Phase B/C/D code. The comparison is over the dense
Toy0 trainable tensor set inherited from S1 — QAT-only buffers must be
excluded.

Scope (in gbf-experiments::s2::schema)
======================================
Path: experiments/S2/ablation/seed-0/ablation-report.json

S2AblationReport (JSON) := {
  schema:                       "s2_ablation.v1"
  seed:                         0
  s2_ternary_phase_a_checkpoint_sha:  Hash256   // step 4000
  s2_ablation_phase_a_checkpoint_sha: Hash256   // step 4000
  s2_ternary_tensor_payload_sha:      Hash256
  s2_ablation_tensor_payload_sha:     Hash256
  phase_a_eq_ablation:                Bool
  first_mismatch:                     Null |
                                      { tensor: String, byte_offset: u64 }
  ablation_self_hash:                 Hash256
}

Invariants:
  AB-1 phase_a_eq_ablation = (s2_ternary_tensor_payload_sha =
                              s2_ablation_tensor_payload_sha).
  AB-2 Closure requires phase_a_eq_ablation = true.

Acceptance
==========
- Canonical-JSON round-trip byte-equal.
- AB-1 / AB-2 each tested.
- first_mismatch is non-null when shas differ; null when equal.
- Whole-file safetensors byte equality is NOT part of the equality
  decision (non-normative; RFC §3 H4).

Considerations
==============
- The comparison op lives in F-S2.31 (H4 verifier). This bead is schema
  + emitter only.
- Per RFC update: thresholds + scales after Phase C init are EXCLUDED
  from this payload comparison even though they appear in
  later-phase checkpoints.

References
==========
F-S2 RFC §9.7 s2_ablation.v1, §3 H4.
Depends on: F-S2.02.

No artifact bytes, export facts, or ReferenceModelBundle behavior are claimed here.
- Differentiable Burn path: not implemented in this bead. This is schema/config validation only. Executable training-loop phase selection is moved to bd-cmf, and per-module Off/Soft/Hard application is moved to bd-2uw.

## T-B14.3: Define `ConstraintDelta` + `KnobDelta` + `ResourcePressureUpdate`

**Target crate**: `gbf-policy`
**Target file(s)**: `gbf-policy/src/knobs/delta.rs`
**Reference**: F-B14 oracle resolution. T-B14.1 (knobs), T-B14.2 (overrides) must land first.

### Background

`RepairProposal::tighten: ConstraintDelta` — the typed mutation a pass proposes. The loop controller (T-B14.6) decides admissibility and applies. Each `KnobDelta` variant maps 1:1 to one repair lever; no untyped extension points.

### Implementation Notes

```rust
pub struct ConstraintDelta {
    pub changes: Vec<KnobDelta>,
}

pub enum KnobDelta {
    AdvancePlacementProfile { to: PlacementProfile },
    SetTraceDemotion { to: TraceDemotionLevel },
    DisableOptionalProbes { probes: BTreeSet<TraceProbeId> },
    RaiseReductionCeiling { selector: Option<ReductionSelector>, to: ReductionPlanCeiling },
    PromoteRecomputeLevel { to: RecomputePromotionLevel },
    ForceRecompute { values: BTreeSet<ValueSelector> },
    AdvanceSramPageAggression { to: SramPageAggression },
    AdvanceKernelResidencyBias { to: KernelResidencyBias },
    AdvanceKernelDuplicationBias { to: KernelDuplicationBias },
    ForceKernelResidency { selector: KernelSelector, to: KernelResidency },
    PromoteOverlay { to: OverlayPromotionLevel },
    NarrowTileClasses { selector: TileSelector, remaining: BTreeSet<TileCandidateClass> },
    SetSliceCoarsening { to: SliceCoarseningLevel },
    UpdatePressureThreshold { update: ResourcePressureUpdate },
}

pub enum ResourcePressureUpdate {
    WramHot(PressureLimit<ByteBudget>),
    HramHot(PressureLimit<ByteBudget>),
    Bank0Rom(PressureLimit<ByteBudget>),
    SwitchableRomWindow(PressureLimit<ByteBudget>),
    SramWindow(PressureLimit<ByteBudget>),
    SliceCycles(PressureLimit<CycleBudget>),
    InterruptLatency(PressureLimit<CycleBudget>),
    TraceBytesPerFrame(PressureLimit<u16>),
    PersistBytesPerFrame(PressureLimit<u16>),
    OverlayInstallsPerFrame(PressureLimit<u8>),
    BankSwitchesPerToken(PressureLimit<u16>),
    SramPageSwitchesPerToken(PressureLimit<u16>),
}
```

### Admissibility-check primitives

Provide pure functions that the loop controller (T-B14.6) calls — they don't mutate state, they answer "is this delta legal against current `CompileKnobs` + `RepairPolicy`?".

```rust
pub fn check_delta_admissible(
    delta: &KnobDelta,
    current: &CompileKnobs,
    policy: &RepairPolicy,
    observability: ObservabilityMode,
) -> Result<(), DeltaRejection>;

pub enum DeltaRejection {
    KnobLocked { knob: CompileKnobId },
    PolicyToggleDisabled { knob: CompileKnobId, toggle: &'static str },
    BeyondBounds { knob: CompileKnobId, attempted: String, max: String },
    NotMonotone { knob: CompileKnobId, current: String, attempted: String },
    InvariantObservabilityViolation { knob: CompileKnobId },
    EffectfulRecompute { value: ValueSelector },     // recompute promotion of an effectful value
}
```

`DeltaRejection::EffectfulRecompute` is the special case: the loop controller validates that `ForceRecompute` targets are pure (no RNG, no sequence write, no persistence commit, no trace effect). T-B14.6 wires this against `GbInferIR` effect edges.

### Acceptance Criteria

```bash
cargo check -p gbf-policy
cargo test -p gbf-policy -- delta::serde_round_trip
cargo test -p gbf-policy -- delta::admissibility_locked          # Locked knob -> KnobLocked
cargo test -p gbf-policy -- delta::admissibility_policy_toggle    # allow_* false -> PolicyToggleDisabled
cargo test -p gbf-policy -- delta::admissibility_bounds           # Beyond max -> BeyondBounds
cargo test -p gbf-policy -- delta::admissibility_monotone         # Backward step -> NotMonotone
cargo test -p gbf-policy -- delta::invariant_blocks_demotion      # Invariant + SetTraceDemotion -> InvariantObservabilityViolation
```

### Constitution Checkpoints

- §I.1: `KnobDelta` enum is closed; new repair levers require new variants.
- §V.3: `DeltaRejection` carries actionable diagnostic info.

## T-A1.8: Listing emitter

**Target crate**: `gbf-asm`
**Target file(s)**: `gbf-asm/src/listing.rs`
**Reference**: `planv0.md` §"EncodedRom" (line 1565: emits `.gb`, `.sym`, `.lst`).

### Background

A `.lst` file is human-readable annotated assembly listing — one line per encoded instruction with address, bytes, mnemonic, source-stage provenance. It exists for debugging compiler/runtime output without reverse-engineering the ROM. Listings must be byte-stable across runs so a diff between two listings is meaningful.

### Implementation Notes

```rust
pub struct ListingOptions {
    pub show_provenance: bool,
    pub show_cycle_costs: bool,
    pub show_bytes: bool,
}

pub fn emit_listing(
    section: &Section,
    encoded: &EncodedSection,
    placed: &PlacedSection,
    symbols: &SymbolTable,
    opts: &ListingOptions,
) -> String;
```

Format:

```
; section: kernel.matvec.tile_8x8 (CommonBank)
; bank=03 origin=$4000 size=0x123
$4000: CD 34 80    call $8034            ; provenance: stage=Backend op=far_call_thunk
$4003: 21 00 C0    ld   hl, $C000        ; provenance: stage=ArenaPlan op=load_input_tile
...
```

Listings concatenate naturally per build into one `.lst` blob. Tests assert: same `(Section, EncodedSection, ListingOptions)` produces the same string twice in a row.

### Acceptance Criteria

```bash
cargo check -p gbf-asm
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- listing::byte_stable                     # Same input -> same output bytes
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- listing::all_options_render               # Each ListingOptions flag changes output
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- listing::provenance_visible               # Stage labels appear in output
```

### Constitution Checkpoints

- §IV.3: Listing determinism asserts at test level.
- §V.3: Listings carry provenance so a failing slice's listing is self-explaining.

comments.text:
## T-B1.0.8: Test fixture infrastructure — synthetic AsmIR, frame traces, emu cycle traces

**Target paths**:
- `crates/gbf-codegen/tests/fixtures/synthetic_asmir/` (validator negative-test inputs)
- `crates/gbf-emu/tests/fixtures/synthetic_frame_traces/` (frame-event ordering tests)
- `crates/gbf-emu/tests/fixtures/synthetic_cycle_traces/` (cycle-attribution unit tests)
- `crates/gbf-verify/tests/fixtures/expected_outputs/` (committed reference outputs for cross-build sanity)

### Background

Many tests in F-B1 need fixtures that are *not* the output of a full ROM run:

- **Validator negative tests** (T-B1.3.3, T-B1.3.4) need synthetic AsmIR that contains a violation, to assert the validator rejects it. Without these fixtures, the validator can silently regress to a no-op.
- **Frame-event ordering tests** (T-B1.5.5) need synthetic traces with controlled timing: a "good" trace, a "missed widget" trace, a "missed scheduler" trace, an "edge-frame-only" trace.
- **Cycle-attribution unit tests** (T-B1.6.3) need a synthetic per-frame mcycle stream that lets us verify the aggregator excludes dump pause and includes ISR correctly.
- **Reference output cross-build sanity**: a tiny pinned blob of the expected i32 output for `N = 16` matmul, so a failing host system (broken sign-extension, wrong endianness) is caught in plain `cargo test` without needing the full ROM build path.

This bead owns those fixtures as a single coherent layer.

### Fixture catalogue

#### 1. Synthetic AsmIR fixtures

```text
synthetic_asmir/
├── well_typed_panel_copy.bin        # baseline: passes all validators
├── violation_raw_mbc_write.bin      # contains a write to $2000; T-B1.3.3 rejects
├── violation_yield_under_lease.bin  # yields with a held BankLease; T-B1.3.4 rejects
├── violation_kernel_in_romx.bin     # kernel section in switchable ROM; rejected
├── violation_isr_in_romx.bin        # ISR section in switchable ROM; rejected
└── README.md                        # human-readable description of each fixture
```

Each fixture is a small, hand-constructed AsmIR blob (or a Rust function that builds one). The README documents *why* each violation is in scope.

#### 2. Synthetic frame-event traces

```text
synthetic_frame_traces/
├── good_n128_60_frames.json         # ordered VBlankFired/WidgetTick/SchedSrv triples
├── missed_widget_frame_42.json       # widget tick for frame 42 occurs after VBlank(43)
├── missed_scheduler_frame_55.json    # scheduler service for frame 55 missing
├── edge_only_first_last.json         # only first/last frames have ticks; gated frames empty
└── overlong_isr_frame_19.json        # widget tick happens; scheduler service crosses VBlank(20)
```

Stored as deterministic JSON with explicit cycle counts.

#### 3. Synthetic emu cycle traces

```text
synthetic_cycle_traces/
├── known_8_products_per_window.json  # mcycle deltas + product counts; aggregator must compute cycles_per_product_accumulate exactly
├── dump_pause_excluded.json          # contains a dump-pause window; aggregator must NOT include those mcycles
├── isr_window_marked.json            # contains a VBlank ISR span; aggregator must include only in cycles_per_full_matmul
└── empty_run.json                    # zero products; aggregator must produce 0/0 = NaN-safe distribution
```

#### 4. Reference output fixtures (committed)

```text
expected_outputs/
├── matmul_n16.i32_le.bin             # 1024 bytes, output of matmul_reference_i8 on canonical N=16 fixtures
├── matmul_n16.sha256                 # sha256 of the .bin file
└── README.md                         # how to regenerate (just run the reference)
```

The pinned bytes catch host-system bugs (wrong endianness, sign-extension regressions) faster than a full ROM run. They are regenerated by a single command:

```bash
cargo run -p gbf-verify --bin emit_reference_fixture -- --n 16 --out tests/fixtures/expected_outputs/
```

### Logging discipline

Each fixture-loading helper emits a structured trace event when loaded:

```rust
tracing::debug!(
    target = "gbf_codegen::test_fixtures",
    name = "violation_yield_under_lease",
    bytes = bytes.len(),
    "loaded synthetic AsmIR fixture"
);
```

Tests that consume fixtures use a subscriber-capture helper (T-B1.0.9) so a failing test prints which fixture it loaded, when, and what assertion fired.

### Acceptance gates

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- test_fixtures::synthetic_asmir_fixtures_load
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- test_fixtures::all_violation_fixtures_actually_violate
cargo test -p gbf-emu -- test_fixtures::synthetic_frame_traces_parse
cargo test -p gbf-emu -- test_fixtures::synthetic_cycle_traces_parse
cargo test -p gbf-verify -- test_fixtures::n16_expected_output_hash_pinned
```

The "actually violate" test sanity-checks each named violation fixture by attempting (in a controlled way) to verify it *would* be rejected by some validator — protects against the fixture set drifting away from the violations they claim to encode.

### RFC reference

`history/rfcs/F-B1-compute-bringup.md` §11 (validation strategy — implies fixture infrastructure).

### Dependencies

- T-B1.0.2 (reference function — used to generate `expected_outputs/`).
- T-B1.0.3 (deterministic fixtures — operands feeding the reference).
- F-A1 (`gbf-asm` AsmIR builders — synthetic AsmIR fixtures use them).

### Forward links

Consumed by:
- T-B1.3.3 (no-raw-MBC validator)
- T-B1.3.4 (no-yield-under-lease validator)
- T-B1.5.5 (frame-trace ordering tests)
- T-B1.6.3 (aggregation cycle-attribution unit tests)

title: F-S7 v0.2: LowRankRouter rank rationale (D7 honesty)
description:
## Description

D7 claimed `router_rank = 4` "provides the parameter-count savings vs a dense d_model -> n_experts projection." The math in §3.2 immediately showed the delta is *negative* (64*4 + 4*4 = 272 > 256 = 64*4). The "rationale" was therefore false. §3.2's own delta line called it "negative; low-rank with rank = n_experts adds bias." The contradiction would have been a review-time embarrassment. v0.2 rewrites D7's rationale honestly: rank = n_experts saturates the factorized linear map to the full router matrix while preserving the LowRankRouter abstraction used by later slices; the load-bearing claim is the abstraction/regularization behavior, not parameter savings. The default formula is also corrected (the old `min(n_experts/4, 8)` gives rank=0 for n_experts=2, which is degenerate).

## Design

- D7 rationale: pins router_rank to 4 for n_experts=4 production lane, 2 for n_experts=2 ablation lane. Explicitly notes "this is not a parameter-saving choice" and quotes the 272 vs 256 numbers.
- Default formula (preserved for non-S7 callers): `max(1, min(ceil(n_experts / 4), 8))`. Old formula was `min(n_experts/4, 8)` which evaluates to 0 for n=2 (`floor(2/4) = 0`).
- §3.2 LowRankRouter parameter-count block stays as-is — its math was right; only D7's prose was wrong.

## Acceptance Criteria

- D7 prose does not claim parameter savings as the rationale.
- D7 pins router_rank = 4 for n_experts=4 and router_rank = 2 for n_experts=2.
- Default formula in `gbf-model::LowRankRouter::default_rank` is `max(1, min(ceil(n_experts / 4), 8))`.
- Construction test asserts default_rank(2) = 1, default_rank(4) = 1 (default; S7 OVERRIDES), default_rank(16) = 4, default_rank(32+) = 8.
- S7 pinning test asserts router_rank = 4 for MoeTiny n=4 and = 2 for MoeTiny n=2.

## Notes

- The "implicit regularization" claim from the pre-review remains the load-bearing rationale: factorizing the router matrix imposes a rank-K structure on routing weights that is hypothesized to generalize better than the dense version at MoeTiny scale. Whether this hypothesis bears out is observed in H1-H4, not pre-asserted.
- The abstraction survives to S8 with larger n_experts where rank = n_experts/4 starts saving real parameters.
- Implementation crate: `gbf-model::LowRankRouter`.
close_reason:
Closed after parent audit and Gemini/Claude inspection-only review.

Parent evidence:
- Child `bd-1yu6` is closed and covers the concrete D7 LowRankRouter rationale/default-rank/pin changes.
- RFC D7 no longer claims S7's rank override is parameter-saving; it explicitly states the MoeTiny rank override costs 272 vs 256 parameters and names abstraction/regularization as the rationale.
- D7 pins `router_rank = 4` for `n_experts = 4` production and `router_rank = 2` for `n_experts = 2` ablation.
- `gbf-model::qat::default_router_rank` implements the non-S7 formula as `ceil(n_experts / 4)` clamped to `[1, 8]`.
- `gbf-policy::ModelSizeProfile::s7_router_rank` exposes the S7 MoeTiny rank pin without claiming runtime/topology adoption.

Reviewer results:
- Gemini: PASS. Confirmed RFC honesty, rank pinning, default formula equivalence, and honest deferral of downstream construction/runtime/export scope.
- Claude: PASS. Confirmed the same parent acceptance and noted no overclaim beyond the scalar/policy contract.

Non-blocking notes:
- A3 is production-lane focused and relies on D7 for the ablation pin; D7 itself is unambiguous.
- `s7_router_rank()` currently relies on the rank-equals-n_experts pin for MoeTiny; future profiles that diverge from that equality will need explicit per-lane pins.

Moved/not claimed:
- S7 executable router construction consuming the pin remains downstream topology/router integration work.
- Burn/export/runtime behavior is not claimed by this parent.

title: T-B7.G: Static budget reduction-site-facts trait (Stage 2 amendment for F-B7)
description:
## What
**Stage 2 surface amendment.** Add a trait
`StaticBudgetReductionSiteFacts` on `StaticBudgetReport` (in
`gbf-codegen/src/budget.rs`) exposing per-site full projection facts to
F-B7 Stage 5:

```rust
pub trait StaticBudgetReductionSiteFacts {
    fn reduction_site_projection(&self, site: &ReductionSiteId)
        -> Option<&ReductionSiteProjection>;
}
```

`ReductionSiteProjection` carries `term_count, input_max_abs_q,
weight_max_abs_q, bias_max_abs_q: Option<u32>, accumulator_domain`. The
landed `StaticBudgetReportBody.projections.accumulator_maxima:
Vec<AccumulatorBound { site, projected_max_abs, i16_safe, i32_safe }>`
does **not** carry these fields — they live only inside
`QuantGraphBudgetView.reduction_sites` in Stage 2 internals.

## Why
F-B7 must copy `term_count, input_max_abs_q, weight_max_abs_q,
bias_max_abs_q, accumulator_domain` per site to compute
`AccumulatorCertificate`s. Without this surface, Stage 5 cannot construct a
certificate from typed Stage 2 inputs without crossing into Stage 1
internals (a layering violation).

## Two implementation paths
1. **Side channel (preferred)**: attach `Vec<ReductionSiteProjection>` to
   `StaticBudgetReport` as a non-report field; trait reads from it.
   Backward-compatible with the `static_budget.v1` report schema.
2. **Schema bump**: embed `Vec<ReductionSiteProjection>` in
   `StaticBudgetReportBody.projections`. Requires bumping
   `static_budget.v1 -> static_budget.v2` and re-emitting `static_budget.json`.

Pick (1) unless an oracle/external consumer demands the projection appear in
the published report.

## Subtasks
- [ ] Define the trait in `gbf-codegen` alongside the existing
      `StaticBudgetReductionSites` trait.
- [ ] Decide between (1) side channel and (2) schema bump; record decision.
- [ ] If (1): add a non-report `pub reduction_site_facts:
      Vec<ReductionSiteProjection>` field to `StaticBudgetReport`.
- [ ] If (2): coordinate a `static_budget.v2` schema bump with F-B4 owner.
- [ ] Fixture wiring so F-B7 tests can stub the trait against canned
      projections without booting the whole pipeline.
- [ ] Round-trip property test: re-binding from `QuantGraphBudgetView`
      reproduces identical facts byte-for-byte.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `StaticBudgetReductionSiteFacts` trait imports cleanly in `gbf-codegen`.
- [ ] T-B7.C `SiteFactsBinding` reads from it (not from internals).
- [ ] No new public access to `QuantGraphBudgetView` is required from F-B7.

## How this serves the project
This is the **hard layering invariant** for Stage 5: F-B7's pure core must
not touch `QuantGraph.tensors` directly. The trait pattern is the only way
to preserve that invariant while giving Stage 5 the per-site facts the
certificate math requires.

## RFC anchors
§13.2a (Static budget access trait — required Stage 2 amendment),
§9.3 SiteFactsBinding (Stage 5 construction class 3),
§9.1 ReductionSiteFacts type.

## History
- F-B3/F-B5 alignment audit (2026-05-14) surfaced this gap.
- Earlier RFC drafts assumed `StaticBudgetProduct.reduction_sites[e.site]`
  worked verbatim; the landed type only exposes `AccumulatorBound`.

## Blocks
T-B7.C (SiteFactsBinding) directly.

## T-B1.2.3: `MatmulI8Node` IR in `gbf-ir::infer`

**Target crate**: `gbf-ir`
**Target file**: `gbf-ir/src/infer.rs`

### Background

`gbf-ir::infer` is the inference IR that M1 will eventually populate with norm, activation, router, expert dispatch, embed, unembed, etc. F-B1 introduces the IR with exactly **one** node variant — `MatmulI8` — plus a terminator. The single-node graph forecloses any premature commitment to an effect-edge model M1 has not yet designed.

### Types

```rust
pub enum InferNode {
    MatmulI8(MatmulI8Node),
    End,
}

pub struct MatmulI8Node {
    pub a: TensorBinding,
    pub b: TensorBinding,
    pub out: TensorBinding,
    pub dim: SquareDim,
    pub tile_size: TileSize,
}
```

### Invariants F-B1 enforces

- The graph contains exactly one `MatmulI8` and one `End`.
- A and B are read-only.
- The output is harness-streamed (not written to a tensor binding M1 would observe).
- No effect-edge graph yet.
- No range annotations.
- No observation hooks.
- No quantization metadata.

### Deferred to M1 (do NOT add in F-B1)

- All other op kinds (`Norm`, `Activation`, `RouterTopK`, `ExpertDispatch`, `Embed`, `Unembed`, ...).
- Effect edges. F-B1's single-op IR has trivial effect ordering; M1 introduces the graph.
- `ObservationPlan` visitor hooks.
- `RangePlan` annotation slots.
- `LifetimeClass` on `TensorBinding`.

The type body must contain a clear `// M1: deferred` comment naming each missing field.

### Anti-pattern to refuse

- Generalizing `MatmulI8` to `Matmul<T>`. M1's quantized kernel is a different node type with a different effect profile (rescale, requantise, possibly fuse with norm). Generalising prematurely commits to the wrong axis.

### Acceptance gates

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-ir -- f_b1_matmul_ir_single_node_shape
cargo test -p gbf-ir -- f_b1_matmul_ir_rejects_multi_op_graph
cargo test -p gbf-ir -- f_b1_matmul_ir_a_b_are_read_only
cargo test -p gbf-ir -- f_b1_matmul_ir_no_effect_edges
```

### RFC reference

`history/rfcs/F-B1-compute-bringup.md` §7.4.

### Dependencies

- T-B1.0.1 (`SquareDim`).
- T-B1.2.1 (`TileSize`).

title: T-B5.13: ReductionSiteBinding + Provenance/Anchor + CanonicalSort + SelfConsistency (Wave 4 classes 6–10; absorbs T-B5.14/15/16)
description:
## What
Implement `ReductionSiteBinding` (IIRClass 6): set
`GbNode.reduction_site = Some(...)` for every node satisfying
`ReductionSiteBearing(op, q)` (i.e. RouterMatVec, ExpertMatVec,
Norm{plan ∈ TileRms*}, Classify); other nodes get `None`. The
`Some(ReductionSiteId)` values match Stage 2's
`ReductionSiteProjection`.

## Why
F-B7 (`RangePlan`) consumes `GbInferIR` reduction sites. The Stage 2
↔ Stage 3 join key is canonical and typed (RFC §13.4):

```
ReductionSiteKey :=
  RouterMatVec  { layer, router_weight }
  | ExpertMatVec { layer, expert, slot, expert_weight }
  | Norm        { norm_plan, norm_site }
  | Classify    { classify_weight }

ReductionSiteId =
  StaticBudgetReport.reduction_sites[ReductionSiteKey].reduction_site_id
```

F-B5 does **not** mint new `ReductionSiteId`s (Ambiguity A82). It
computes the `ReductionSiteKey` for every reduction-bearing node and
looks it up in `i.static_budget`. Missing or duplicate keys fail
with `InferIrReductionSiteMissing`.

## Inputs
- T-B5.12 (NodeBuilding output).
- T-B5.12a (op signature predicate).
- F-B4's `StaticBudgetProduct` (existing bd-2ps + sub-beads).

## Outputs
- `fn bind_reduction_sites(nodes, quant_graph, static_budget) ->
  Result<Vec<GbNode>, Vec<ValidationDiagnostic>>` (mutates
  `node.reduction_site` in place).
- Diagnostic: `InferIrReductionSiteMissing`.

## Pitfalls
- DO NOT mint a new `ReductionSiteId` (Ambiguity A82); look up Stage
  2's value.
- DO NOT set `reduction_site = Some(...)` on non-bearing nodes.
- DO NOT skip the lookup when Stage 2's projection is missing — that
  must fail loudly.

## Acceptance
- `gbf-codegen::reduction_site_binding_uses_static_budget_keys`.
- `gbf-codegen::reduction_site_binding_emits_missing_typed_diagnostic`.
- `gbf-codegen::reduction_site_only_some_on_bearing_ops`.

## Refs
- RFC §9.3 (Class 6), §13.4 (ReductionSiteKey, F-B7 handshake),
  IIR-Ok-18, Ambiguity ledger: A58, A82.
- Depends on: T-B5.12, T-B5.12a.
- Blocks: T-B5.14 (ProvenanceBinding/AnchorBinding).

comments.text:
## §20 amendments (post-PR-#14) — handshake reframe RFC §20.2 reframes the F-B7 handshake. The deployed `ReductionSiteProjection` shape: ```rust pub struct ReductionSiteProjection { pub site: ReductionSiteId, // pub struct ReductionSiteId(pub String) pub layer: Option, pub expert: Option, pub term_count: u32, pub input_max_abs_q: u32, pub weight_max_abs_q: u32, pub bias_max_abs_q: Option, pub accumulator_domain: AccumulatorDomain, } ``` There is **no `*_weight: TensorId` field** in the deployed projection and no separate `ReductionSiteKey` schema type. Authority moved: F-B3 mints `ReductionSiteId(String)` using a canonical scheme; F-B4 records and validates ordering / uniqueness; F-B5 reconstructs the same scheme to perform a string lookup. Canonical scheme F-B5 reconstructs (matches what F-B3 mints): ```text RouterMatVec{layer = ℓ} -> "router.<ℓ>" ExpertMatVec{layer = ℓ, expert = e, slot} -> "expert.<ℓ>.." where slot_tag ∈ {gate, up, down} Norm{plan = NormPlanId(p)} -> "norm.

" Classify -> "classify" ``` `ReductionSiteKey` from RFC §13.4 is **F-B5's internal correlation predicate** — not a schema type. Use it only to assert `canonical_reduction_site_id_string(key) == projection.site` during binding, and (optionally) include `*_weight: TensorId` in `InferIrReductionSiteMissing` diagnostics for actionability. Ambiguity A82 amended: F-B5 still does not mint independently; the canonical scheme is the source of truth, and F-B3 implements it on the producer side.

title: F-S7 v0.2: Lambda sweep cadence & H3 decoupling
description:
## Description

D19 said the lambda_switch sweep happens "every 1000 steps." §9.3 said sweeps run once at the end of training, each lambda retrained for 1000 extra steps from the same base checkpoint. These are different experiments — one in-loop and one post-Phase-D. The cadence-mismatch confusion bled into H5's falsification ("lambda_switch_sweep_log cadence is not every 1000 steps") which was testing the wrong axiom. v0.2 makes the sweep explicitly post-Phase-D-local and stops H3 from depending on sweep-local bpc.

## Design

- D19 wording: "In the post-Phase-D sweep harness, each lambda_switch grid point adds: quality_delta_per_lambda_switch." Drops "Periodically (every 1000 steps)."
- H5 falsification: "lambda_switch_sweep_log does not contain exactly one 1000-extra-step record per grid point ⇒ Refuted."
- H3 vs sweep decoupling: D11 explicitly says "The sweep-local production-lambda bpc is used only for H6 guardrail comparisons. H3 uses the final production training run's validation bpc, not the sweep-local retrain."
- §9.3 retains the harness-level cadence pin (1000 extra steps per grid point from end-of-Phase-D checkpoint).

## Acceptance Criteria

- D19 no longer says "every 1000 steps" as if it were in-loop cadence.
- H5 falsification names "one 1000-extra-step record per grid point" as the cadence axiom.
- D11 (and H3 statement) explicitly say H3 uses production-run bpc, not sweep-local bpc.
- §9.3 still pins the 1000-extra-step retrain semantics.
- RouterCollapseSweepReport's `RCS-Cadence` invariant verifies the 1000-extra-step delta per grid point.

## Notes

- Pre-review confusion likely arose from logging-bead reuse (the per-step structured tracing emits every 1000 steps in S2-S5 spirit). The sweep is fundamentally a different cadence and lives in a separate harness.
- Implementation crate: `gbf-experiments::s7::collapse_sweep`.
close_reason:
Closed after parent audit and Gemini/Claude inspection-only review.

Parent evidence:
- Child `bd-d1h1` is closed and covers the concrete D19/H3 cadence proof.
- RFC D19 now uses post-Phase-D sweep semantics rather than an in-loop every-1000-steps sweep claim.
- H5/§13.5 pin exactly one 1000-extra-step record per lambda grid point.
- D11/§11.1 decouple H3 from sweep-local bpc by using production `S7ScoreReport` inputs for parity.
- `gbf-experiments::s7::collapse_sweep` and `gbf-experiments/tests/collapse_sweep_s7.rs` provide the schema/helper/test proof without loading checkpoints or emitting artifacts.

Reviewer results:
- Gemini: PASS. Confirmed D19 cadence, H3 decoupling, H5/§13.5 axiom, and honest parent scope.
- Claude: PASS. Confirmed the same RFC/helper/test coverage and no overclaim of the real sweep harness, checkpoint retraining, producers, artifact emission, or end-to-end logging.

Non-blocking caveat:
- Divergent record semantics are still owned by the H6/producer lane. In particular, `LambdaSwitchSweepRecord::from_parts` currently enforces a 1000-step delta for all records, while §9.3 allows `completion = DivergedAt(step)` with null bpc. That reconciliation is assigned to `bd-34f3` / `bd-xlqf` and real producer emission to `bd-6w8m`.

Moved/not claimed:
- Real post-Phase-D sweep harness, checkpoint retraining, `LambdaSwitchSweepStep` producer/log emission, and `s7_router_collapse_sweep.v1` artifact emission remain `bd-6w8m`.
- End-to-end structured logging adoption remains `bd-1ryn`.

title: T-B3.19: ClassifyHeadBinding (Tied weight equals embedding; logit_format named boundary)
description:
## What
Implement `ClassifyHeadBinding` (QGClass 11 in §8.3): bind
`ClassifyHead { kind, weight, bias, logit_format }`. If `kind = Tied`,
assert `weight = embedding_table.tensor_id`. Pin `logit_format` from
`ArtifactCore`.

## Why
The Tied/Untied rule (SC-15) is asserted here because TensorBinding
has already produced the EmbeddingTable tensor and ClassifyWeight
tensor (when Untied). Specifically:
- `Tied` ⇒ `classify_head.weight` references the `EmbeddingTable`
  tensor's `TensorId` (Ambiguity A11).
- `Untied` ⇒ `classify_head.weight` references a tensor with role
  `ClassifyWeight`.

`logit_format` is read from `ArtifactCore.classify_head` (Ambiguity
A79): a Tied head may legitimately declare a different logit format
than the embedding format (Ambiguity A41), so SC-15 only constrains
weight identity, not format. SC-15a constrains `logit_format` ∈
{ I8, I16, Q8_8, Q4_4 }.

Bias is independent of kind (Ambiguity A24): a Tied head with its
own bias is allowed.

## Inputs
- T-B3.18 (DecodeBinding).
- T-B3.9 (`ClassifyHead`, `ClassifyHeadKind`).

## Outputs
- `fn bind_classify_head(tensors, artifact_core) ->

comments.text:
## Agent Instructions

**Target crate(s)**: `gbf-train` (loader + fixture path), `gbf-policy` (helper to construct), `fixtures/calibration/` (the actual JSON).
**Target file(s)**: `fixtures/calibration/synthetic_reference_budget.json` (new), `gbf-policy/src/synthetic.rs` (new — constructs / validates), `gbf-train/src/preflight.rs` (uses).

**Reference**: bd-1hv 2026-04-26 session ("Pre-runtime: synthetic budget path"), T2.2 refinement (bd-1g9), T2.4 (bd-37r).

### Implementation Notes

This task lets training begin at M1–M2, before a real `gbf-runtime` shell exists, by providing a deterministic synthetic `RuntimeChromeBudget`.

1. **Schema parity with real emission.**
   - The synthetic budget MUST round-trip through the same `serde` types as the real one (no parallel struct).
   - `reference_shell_modules` is populated with the minimal+UI set from `pinned_reference_shell()` (T2.4).
   - `runtime_nucleus_hash` uses a stable, explicitly-marked sentinel:
     ```
     0x53594E54__48455449435F5345544348__... // "SYNT" "HETI" "C_SE" "TCH..."
     ```
     Or simpler: `Hash256::from_str("synthetic-reference-shell-v1").into_marked()`. The point is that the value is recognizable in logs and impossible to confuse with a real hash.

2. **Concrete byte estimates.**
   - Bank0Free: estimate 8 KiB after minimal+UI nucleus (Bank 0 is 16 KiB; UI/scheduler/etc. estimated at 8 KiB).
   - CommonBank: 1 slot × 16 KiB usable_bytes − reserved_slack=512.
   - ExpertBank: 8 slots × 16 KiB usable_bytes − reserved_slack=384 each.
   - WramReserved: overlay=512, hot_arena_floor=4096, total=1536 (overlay + continuation + stack + small runtime slack).
   - sram_reserved: 1024 (sequence-state + commit metadata reservation under T2.4).
   - Future-module reservations from T2.4 are subtracted from the relevant slots and recorded.

   These numbers must be reviewed and updated as the real shell forms; they are CONSERVATIVE starting points so a model trained against them likely fits the eventual real shell.

3. **Loader.**
   - `gbf-train::preflight` falls back to the synthetic budget when no real `RuntimeChromeBudget` is available.
   - Trainer emits a structured log line at run start: `{ "synthetic_reference_budget": true, "hash": "0x...", "fixture": "fixtures/calibration/synthetic_reference_budget.json" }`.
   - If the user explicitly passes a real budget path, the synthetic is ignored (real wins).

4. **Marked nature.**
   - The CI drift gate (T2.5) MUST treat synthetic-marked hashes as a separate cohort — drift in synthetic is a fixture update (low ceremony), drift in real is a release-note-required promotion.

### Acceptance Criteria

```bash
cargo check -p gbf-train                                            # Compiles
cargo test -p gbf-policy -- synthetic::round_trip                    # JSON round-trips
cargo test -p gbf-train -- preflight::synthetic_fallback             # Trainer uses synthetic when no real budget present
cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings                              # No warnings
# Verify: synthetic budget passes the same preflight as a real one (schema parity)
# Verify: `runtime_nucleus_hash` for synthetic is detectably synthetic (a structured check, not a string match)
# Verify: trainer log line clearly indicates synthetic-mode at run start
```

### Constitution Checkpoints

- §I.1: Same `RuntimeChromeBudget` type for synthetic and real eliminates "two paths" drift.
- §IV.3: Reproducible — checked-in JSON fixture means every run sees the same synthetic budget.
- §V.1: Structured log indicates synthetic-mode (machine-readable for CI).
- §VI.1: Fixture is in-repo at `fixtures/calibration/`.

title: F-S2.44: O1 pre-registration check script (predictions_section_hash + strict-ancestor + first_result_commit non-null rule)
description:
Goal
====
Implement scripts/s2_preregistration_check.sh — the O1 pre-registration
proof script that asserts predictions_section_hash matches the markdown
section in predictions_commit, predictions_commit is a strict ancestor
of first_result_commit, and first_result_commit is the earliest commit
introducing any non-null S2 result artifact self-hash / completed run-
product field / score value / hypothesis verdict. Schema templates,
null placeholders, and pre-registration-only report drafts do NOT count
as result artifacts. Per F-S2 RFC §13 O1 + §10 R-S2-Predictions + §16.8.

Why this matters
================
Pre-registration is the load-bearing scientific commitment: predictions
must exist in git history BEFORE any result artifact, with no edits
after. Without the strict-ancestor + non-null result definition, a
schema-template commit could be mis-classified as the first result, and
a prereg edit could go undetected.

Scope (in scripts/s2_preregistration_check.sh)
==============================================
- Inputs: predictions_commit, first_result_commit (from
  s2_report.v1 front-matter).
- Step 1: extract the "## Pre-registered predictions" markdown section
  from docs/experiments/S2-report.md at predictions_commit; normalize
  via S1CanonicalJson body-bytes rule; sha256 it; compare against
  predictions_section_hash in current report.
- Step 2: git merge-base --is-ancestor predictions_commit first_result_commit
  (strict — they may not be equal).
- Step 3: scan every commit C ∈ git log predictions_commit..HEAD; for
  each C, check whether C introduces any:
    - non-null S2 result artifact self-hash (phase_log / score /
      distill_log / ablation / loss_grad_flow / linearstate_smoke /
      phase_transition_integ / oracle_re_run / report) ,
    - completed/diverged run-product field,
    - score value,
    - hypothesis verdict derived from an S2 result.
  The earliest such commit must equal first_result_commit.
- Schema templates, null placeholders, and pre-registration-only report
  drafts are SKIPPED.

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## T-B1.3.3: No-raw-MBC-writes static checker

**Target crate**: `gbf-asm` (effect classification) and `gbf-codegen` (consumer)
**Target file**: `gbf-asm/src/effect_class.rs` (extends), `gbf-codegen/src/validators/no_raw_mbc.rs`

### Background

The audited runtime banking implementation is the **only** code allowed to write MBC5 registers (`$0000`, `$2000`, `$3000`, `$4000`). Any direct write from generated code violates the BankLease discipline and would let the kernel and the HRAM bank shadow drift apart.

This bead implements two complementary checks:

1. **At the AsmIR effect-classification layer**: a write to any address in the MBC range is classified as an MBC effect. Sections without privilege to perform MBC effects fail validation if they emit one.
2. **At the F-B1 codegen-validator layer**: the matmul kernel's emitted sections are explicitly checked to contain no MBC effects.

### Why two layers

The effect classifier (`gbf-asm`) is the structural mechanism. The F-B1-specific validator is the narrow *F-B1* assertion that the matmul kernel in particular contains no raw MBC writes. They serve different correctness questions and either alone is insufficient.

### Acceptance gates

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- effect_classification_flags_direct_mbc_writes
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- f_b1_l2_generated_code_has_no_raw_mbc_writes
cargo test -p gbf-codegen -- f_b1_l2_validator_rejects_synthetic_raw_mbc_write
```

The third test deliberately constructs a synthetic AsmIR section that performs a raw MBC write and asserts the validator rejects it. This guards against the validator silently regressing to a no-op.

### Anti-pattern

- Implementing the validator as a string match against generated bytes. The validator must operate on the typed AsmIR, not on encoded bytes.

### RFC reference

`history/rfcs/F-B1-compute-bringup.md` §3 (goals: narrow validator), §7.8.

### Dependencies

- T-B1.3.2 (lowering uses BankLease) — checker validates *that* output.
- F-A1 (`MachineEffect`/`PrivilegeClass` from gbf-asm).

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## F-A1: `gbf-asm` — Typed LR35902 eDSL + Encoder + Cycle Model + Layout

### Background

`gbf-asm` is the Rust eDSL that authors **all** generated executable code in the system. Per the constitution-grade rule from `planv0.md` line 2492 ("All generated executable code originates from `AsmIR` / `Instr` / audited runtime builders, never from ad hoc byte pushes"), there is no other path to bytes-on-cartridge. `Raw(Vec<u8>)` exists only as a tightly audited escape hatch.

This feature fills the ten module stubs in `gbf-asm/src/`: `isa`, `section`, `provenance`, `symbols`, `builder`, `cycle_model`, `layout`, `relax`, `encoder`, `listing`, plus a small ROM-builder wrapper.

### How this serves overarching project goals

- Compiler-generated code (Stage 12 backend in Epic B) emits `AsmIR` and **must not** make raw MBC writes — the legal path is `BankLease` pseudo-ops that go through F-A4.
- The runtime nucleus (F-A5) is itself authored as Rust builders that emit `AsmIR` sections (`planv0.md` line 305: "this is the key interpretation of 'end-to-end Rust' on Game Boy").
- `ReachabilityValidation` (Epic B, deferred) computes residency / privilege classes by walking `AsmIR`'s `MachineEffect` and `PrivilegeClass` annotations. Without those types here, the validation pass can't be written later.
- `gbf-bench` (Epic E) reads cycle annotations from `AsmIR` to ground its calibration.

### The problem this solves

Without `gbf-asm`:
1. Anyone emitting bytes invents their own ad hoc encoder, which silently disagrees with anyone else's encoder.
2. There is no single place where "is this MBC write legal here?" can be asked.
3. Cycle models live as comments in random files.
4. Provenance — which compiler stage emitted which byte — is lost the moment bytes leave the compiler.

### Design

Module-level layout (matching the existing scaffold):

```
gbf-asm/src/
  isa.rs          # legal LR35902 instruction shapes, registers, addressing modes
  section.rs      # SectionRole, SectionId, MachineEffect, PrivilegeClass
  provenance.rs   # InstrProvenance — which compile stage emitted what
  symbols.rs      # symbol table, label resolution, .sym output
  builder.rs      # typed Builder eDSL emitting Instr + Db/Dw + pseudo-ops
  cycle_model.rs  # per-instruction M-cycle costs (taken/not-taken branches)
  layout.rs       # section placement, address assignment
  relax.rs        # branch relaxation (rel-jump <-> jp <-> far-call thunk)
  encoder.rs      # the only thing that turns Instr into bytes
  listing.rs      # human-readable .lst emitter
```

Plus a small `rom.rs` (or a top-level helper) that takes encoded sections + cartridge header and produces a `.gb` blob.

### Pseudo-ops the eDSL must support (planv0.md line 1511)

- `BankLease { bank, mode }` → consumed by F-A4.
- `BankRelease { lease }`
- `FarCall { target, lease_chain }`
- `Yield { kind: YieldKind }` — consumed by Epic B's slice scheduler.
- `TraceProbe { id, level }` — consumed by Epic D's trace pipeline.
- `AssertBank { expected }` — debugging assertion.
- `Db(u8)`, `Dw(u16)` — data directives. `Raw(Vec<u8>)` exists but is a code smell.

### Children (T-A1.1 ... T-A1.9)

1. **T-A1.1** ISA types + register/operand modeling.
2. **T-A1.2** SectionRole + SectionId + symbol table + provenance.
3. **T-A1.3** Builder eDSL (instructions + pseudo-ops + Db/Dw).
4. **T-A1.4** `MachineEffect` + `PrivilegeClass` typing on instructions/sections.
5. **T-A1.5** Cycle model.
6. **T-A1.6** Layout + branch relaxation.
7. **T-A1.7** Encoder.
8. **T-A1.8** Listing (.lst) emitter.
9. **T-A1.9** ROM builder (.gb assembler with cartridge header).

### Confidence: HIGH

Pure types and a deterministic encoder. The hardest part is getting `MachineEffect` / `PrivilegeClass` right because they are consumed by ReachabilityValidation later — the typing must be expressive enough that "this MBC write is privileged" / "this load is bank-dependent" can be asked locally.

## Agent Instructions (Feature)

**This is a feature bead.** Implement via child tasks T-A1.1–T-A1.9. Tasks should land roughly in the dep order; T-A1.7 (encoder) is the integration point.

### Feature Definition of Done

```bash
cargo test -p gbf-asm                                       # All module tests pass
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- encoder::round_trip                 # Encode then decode (where decoders exist) round-trips
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- cycle_model::known_instructions     # Cycle costs match Pan Docs for a curated set
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- layout::branch_relaxation           # Out-of-range rel-jump becomes jp; cross-bank becomes far-call thunk
cargo test -p gbf-asm -- listing::stable                     # Listings are byte-stable across runs (no nondeterminism)
cargo run -p gbf-asm --example tiny_rom                      # Produces a 32 KiB .gb that boots in an emulator
```

close_reason:
## QAT Closure Checklist

**Artifact contract:** F1 establishes that `gbf-model` owns deployable QAT numerics and artifact-facing export contracts. The implemented artifact boundary is `ExportVisitor` producing `ArtifactCore`, `QuantSpec`, `ExportFacts`, artifact metadata, and canonical tensors where applicable for ternary weights/scales, dense weights/biases, embeddings, classifiers, router/shared-dense branches, and norm LUTs. Activations export as range/quant facts, not tensors. Sequence-state semantics are owned by F12; F1 only ensures the QAT/export boundary composes with model-owned artifact types. Target compiler/runtime lowering and ArtifactOracle agreement are not claimed by F1; those remain downstream validation.

**differentiable Burn path:** Burn is contained in `gbf-train` behind the adapter boundary. Implemented Burn-backed paths cover finite-input ternary linear, activation fake-quant for fixed ranges, norm approximation, router, and expert block adapters with finite owned adapter state. The supported adapters use Burn tensors/autodiff for training while exporting back through model-owned scalar cores and `ExportVisitor`. Global non-finite error-boundary parity with scalar code is not claimed by F1 except where focused tests exist. Learned/EMA activation range state is intentionally not accepted on the Burn path yet; constructors reject it and `bd-1zv` owns that future behavior.

**Tests proving it:**

- `cargo test -p gbf-model -- qat`
- `cargo test -p gbf-train --features burn-adapter -- qat`

comments.author: bkase
comments.text:
## F1: Reframe Burn as Training Front-End

### Background

The original plan said "Burn-fronted with custom fake-quant / STE layers because built-in QAT is currently not supported." This is true but incomplete — it doesn't say WHERE those custom modules live or WHO owns the numeric contracts that cross the training/artifact boundary.

Burn's docs position it as a Rust training framework with swappable backends. Its value is: autodiff, optimizer implementations (Adam, AdaFactor, etc.), checkpoint serialization, metric logging, and backend portability (wgpu, tch, ndarray, candle). What Burn does NOT currently offer is QAT, ternary/binary projection, or hardware-aware fake quantization.

### The problem this solves

Without this reframing, the first implementer faces an ownership ambiguity: does `gbf-model` contain Burn `Module` types that happen to have quantization, or does `gbf-train` contain quantization logic that wraps Burn modules? The answer matters because:

1. The export boundary (what goes into ArtifactCore) must be defined by whoever owns the quantization modules
2. The fake-quant forward pass (used during training) must match the real quantization (used during export) — if they live in different crates, drift is inevitable
3. The ExportVisitor pattern (walk the model, extract canonical tensors + scales + metadata) is tightly coupled to the quantization module structure

### Design decision

`gbf-model` owns a `qat` module namespace containing:
- `TernaryLinearQat` — wraps a Burn Linear, adds learnable/annealed thresholds and per-row scales, provides both a fake-quant forward (for training) and an export method (for artifact generation)
- `ActFakeQuant` — activation clipping/quantization at expert input/output boundaries
- `NormApproxQat` — deployable norm approximation (AffineClipLut or TileRmsThenAffineClip)
- `Top1RouterQat` — low-rank top-1 router with z-loss and export support
- `ExpertBlockQat` — composes the above for a complete MoE expert block
- `ExportVisitor` — walks a trained model, extracts all canonical tensors, scales, metadata, and emits ArtifactCore + TernaryWeightPlan

Burn stays as the training host: you derive `Module` on your model struct, Burn gives you `.forward()`, `.backward()`, `.step()`, `.save()`. But the numeric semantics of what gets exported are defined in gbf-model's qat modules.

### Why Burn-native PTQ is kept as ablation path

Even though QAT is the production path, Burn's native PTQ (post-training quantization, if/when available) should remain as a baseline for:
- Shared modules (embedding, router, classifier) that may stay at higher precision
- Ablation experiments comparing PTQ vs QAT quality
- Quick iteration when you want to test a model architecture change without running the full QAT schedule

### The adapter layer

`gbf-train` should contain a thin adapter layer that:
- Pins the exact Burn version (e.g., `burn = "=0.16.0"`)
- Wraps any Burn API that might change between versions
- Provides a stable internal interface that gbf-model's QAT modules program against
- Includes a CI check that warns on Burn version bumps

### Confidence level: VERY HIGH

This is the single best framing correction in the whole patch. The ownership ambiguity it resolves would otherwise cause real implementation paralysis.

comments.text:
## T-A5.5: Keyboard input + layout

**Target crate**: `gbf-runtime`
**Target file(s)**: `gbf-runtime/src/keyboard.rs`
**Reference**: `planv0.md` line 1626 + `KeyboardLayoutSpec` (line 703).

### Background

The on-screen keyboard is how users input prompts. It's a grid of glyphs with a cursor; D-pad moves the cursor, A presses, B backspaces, Start submits. The layout is data-driven from `LexicalSpec.charset` (Epic G) so character set changes don't touch keyboard code.

### Implementation Notes

```rust
pub fn build_keyboard_section() -> Section;

pub struct KeyboardLayoutSpec {
    pub rows: u8,
    pub columns: u8,
    pub characters: &'static [u8],                  // grid laid out row-major
    pub special_keys: &'static [SpecialKey],
}

pub enum SpecialKey {
    Backspace,
    Submit,
    Shift,                                          // toggles charset slice (e.g., letters <-> punct)
    Cancel,
}

pub struct KeyboardState {
    pub cursor_row: u8,
    pub cursor_col: u8,
    pub charset_slice: u8,
}

/// Emit AsmIR: read joypad cached state, advance cursor / commit character.
pub fn emit_keyboard_step<B: Builder>(b: &mut B);
```

Keyboard state lives in WRAM. Each step:
1. Read joypad (T-A5.3 cached state).
2. If just-pressed direction: move cursor (text re-render via T-A5.4).
3. If just-pressed A: emit current character into the prompt buffer.
4. If just-pressed B: backspace.
5. If just-pressed Start: signal `HarnessOp::SetSession` or whatever the prompt protocol is.

### Acceptance Criteria

```bash
cargo check -p gbf-runtime
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- keyboard::default_layout            # Sane DMG-sized layout exists
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- keyboard::cursor_movement            # D-pad moves cursor; bounds clamp
cargo test -p gbf-runtime -- keyboard::special_keys               # Backspace/Submit work
```

### Constitution Checkpoints

- §I.1: SpecialKey is enumerated.

## F-G1: Corpus pipeline

### What this is

### Why this matters

### Design sketch

pub struct CorpusManifest {
    pub id: CorpusId,
    pub sources: Vec<CorpusSource>,
    pub normalization: NormalizationPolicy,
    pub dedup_policy: DedupPolicy,
    pub split: TrainValTestSplit,
    pub canary_prompts: Vec<PromptCase>,
}

pub fn check_contamination(corpus: &CorpusManifest, workloads: &[WorkloadManifest])
    -> ContaminationReport;
```

### Cross-feature deps
