title: F-S2.20: Pre-train state machine (T1b..T1g + AblationAttempted) + gbf-cli s2 subcommand
description:
Goal
====
Implement two coupled pieces: the F-S2 pre-train state machine that runs
H6 / H5 / D8 / falsification / oracle re-run / api drift BEFORE the
15-train-run budget (with explicit failure transitions + AblationAttempted)
AND the gbf-cli s2 subcommand surface (replay-full / replay-ablation /
verify-determinism / grad-flow / linearstate-smoke / phase-integ /
oracle-re-run) with gbf-cli/s2-full + gbf-cli/s2-ablation feature
forwarding. Per F-S2 RFC §4 + §15.4 + §16.6.

Why this matters
================
- The state machine is the run orchestrator. The prior state machine
  had no failure transitions from early gates; round 3 review fixed it.
- Reproducibility requires a CANONICAL replay command. The state machine
  + verifiers all need a single CLI surface for closure scripts.

Scope
=====
State machine (gbf-experiments::s2::run::state_machine):
  enum State { Configured | LoadedBaselines | LinearStateSmokeRun |
    LossGradFlowRun | PhaseTransitionIntegRun | OracleReRun |
    ApiDriftChecked | FalsificationChecked | TrainAttempted | Trained |
    Scored | GapComputed | AblationAttempted | AblationCompared |
    Reported | Decided }
  Transitions T0..T7 + failure branches (T1b..T1g) per RFC §4 +
  round-3/4 review.

CLI (gbf-cli):
  Cargo features s2-full ⊕ s2-ablation, both forwarding to
  gbf-experiments features with default-features=false on the ablation
  path.
  Subcommands: replay-full / replay-ablation / verify-determinism /
  grad-flow / linearstate-smoke / phase-integ / oracle-re-run / report.

CLI logging configuration (NEW — round 5 review)
=================================================
Global CLI flags:
  --log-format <pretty|json>   (default: pretty for terminals, json for CI)
  --log-level <off|error|warn|info|debug|trace>  (default: info)
  --log-file <path>             (additional sink; default: stderr only)
  --capture-events <path>       (writes a NDJSON file with structured
                                  events for test assertions)

Each subcommand emits a uniform pair:
  event="cli_subcommand_start" name=<&str> args=<json>
  event="cli_subcommand_done" name=<&str> exit_code=<i32>
    artifacts_written=<list<Path>>

When --log-format=json, ALL events emit as NDJSON to stderr — making
CI capture trivial (the workflow tee-collects stderr to artifact).
When --log-format=pretty, the same events render in human-readable
tracing-tree format.

State machine transitions log INFO with structured event:
  event="state_transition" from=<state_tag> to=<state_tag>
    elapsed_ms=<u64> success=<bool>
On state failure:
  event="state_transition_failed" state=<state_tag> reason=<&str>
    will_emit_report=<bool>

Unit tests
==========
- File: gbf-experiments/tests/state_machine_s2.rs
  Scenarios:
    * Each state transition + failure branch has a unit test with a
      synthetic state in / expected next state out.
    * Early H6 failure → build_fail_linearstate_report path; never
      enters TrainAttempted.
    * AblationAttempted runs ONLY after GapComputed.
    * Complete happy path on tiny fixture → Decided(ProceedToS3).
    * Each Tx transition logs the expected state_transition event.

- File: gbf-cli/tests/s2_cli_s2.rs
  Scenarios (using assert_cmd):
    * `gbf s2 replay-full --manifest stub --pass-version 0.0.0
       --seed-list 0 --builds s2_ternary_full
       --device-profile S1CpuDeterministic` exits 0.
    * `gbf s2 replay-ablation --manifest stub --pass-version 0.0.0
       --seed-list 0 --device-profile S1CpuDeterministic` exits 0.
    * `gbf s2 grad-flow` runs F-S2.13 + bd-1j7 fixtures; exit 0.
    * `gbf s2 linearstate-smoke` runs F-S2.14; exit 0.
    * `gbf s2 phase-integ` runs F-S2.15; exit 0.
    * `gbf s2 oracle-re-run` runs F-S2.17 O3; exit 0.
    * `gbf s2 verify-determinism` replays seed 0 twice + byte-compares.
    * `--log-format=json --capture-events /tmp/events.ndjson` produces
      a NDJSON file with at least the expected start/done events.
    * Mutually exclusive features: enabling both s2-full and s2-ablation
      on gbf-cli fails compile.

Golden artifacts (insta):
  tests/snapshots/state_machine__happy_path_tiny.snap (sequence of
    state_transition events for one canonical run)
  tests/snapshots/cli__replay_full_seed0_tiny.snap (stdout summary)

E2E verification
================
- cargo run --release -p gbf-cli --features s2-full -- s2 replay-full
  --manifest fixtures/corpora/tinystories-stub.toml --pass-version 0.0.0
  --seed-list 0 --builds s2_ternary_full --device-profile
  S1CpuDeterministic
  succeeds.
- cargo run --release -p gbf-cli --no-default-features --features
  s2-ablation -- s2 replay-ablation --seed-list 0 --pass-version 0.0.0
  --manifest fixtures/corpora/tinystories-stub.toml
  --device-profile S1CpuDeterministic
  succeeds.
- integration_s2 (F-S2.22) invokes the state machine end-to-end.
- Structured log assertion: every CI workflow stores stderr (NDJSON
  format) as a build artifact.

Considerations
==============
- State machine does NOT itself train; it sequences s2_train_run
  (F-S2.09) and verifiers.
- I-S2-2: T2 issues 15 full runs (5 seeds × 3 builds); T5 issues one
  additional ablation run. Run isolation per S1 Rep-7.
- replay-full does NOT take feature overrides — runtime BuildKind is
  the only switch.

References
==========
F-S2 RFC §4 Experiment state machine, §15.4 replay commands, §16.6
gbf-cli features.
Inherits from F-S1 closed beads: bd-7ljt (F-S1.25 `gbf s1` subcommand
pattern — same logging / exit-code conventions).
Merges (former separate beads): F-S2.45 (state machine) + F-S2.46 (CLI).

title: T-B4.6: Projected WRAM/SRAM/HRAM peaks
description:
## What
Project static peak-byte requirements for WRAM, SRAM, and HRAM. Each
peak carries a `ProjectedSizeSource` recording how it was derived
(static graph projection, hint-bundle constraint, or
calibration-sampling closed form). See RFC §7.6 / §7.7.

## Why
DMG WRAM is 8 KiB; HRAM is 127 bytes; SRAM is target-dependent. Stage 2
must answer "does any of these scarce resources blow up before lowering
even tries to allocate?" before downstream stages waste cycles.

## Inputs
- T-B4.1 QuantGraphBudgetView, especially `sequence_state` and
  `reduction_sites`.
- T-B4.2 byte-math helpers.
- T-B2.13 ResolvedPolicyProduct (some peaks come from hint constraints
  or calibration data).
- T-B4.10 RuntimeChromeBudget caps.

## Outputs
- `pub struct ProjectedSize { peak_bytes: u32, source: ProjectedSizeSource }`.
- `pub enum ProjectedSizeSource { StaticGraphProjection, HintBundleConstraint, CalibrationSamplingClosedForm }`.
- `RuntimeMemoryCapSection` per RFC §7.7 — caps live with the chrome budget.
- Hard rejects: `BudgetWramPeakExceeds { peak, cap }`,
  `BudgetSramPeakExceeds { peak, cap }`, `BudgetHramPeakExceeds { peak, cap }`.

## Pitfalls
- Zero is a valid peak when the resource is unused (RFC §7.7 invariant).
  But when a resource IS used, `source` must be explicit.
- DO NOT use floats. Express any fractional input via `_q8_8`/`_q16_16`.

title: T-B6.H: Probe instantiation + metric selection + probe+metric budget cap (construction 7-12)
description:
## What
Implement construction classes 7-12 of `build_observation_plan_core`
(probe + metric paths):

7. **ProbeRegistryInstantiation** — read templates
   (`ProbeSourceSelector`) from `ProbeRegistrySnapshot`; instantiate
   against `GbInferIR`/`NodeAnchorMap`; produce concrete `OperationalProbe`s
   with `ProbeInstanceId { probe_id, source_fingerprint }`.
8. **ProbeBudgetGovernance** — enforce floor, demotion, and
   `disabled_optional_probes`. Required-importance probes MUST NOT be
   disabled — emit `OBSERVATION-REQUIRED-PROBE-DISABLED` if so.
9. **ProbeOrdering** — sort by `(TraceProbeId, source_fingerprint)`.
10. **MetricRegistryFilter** — read from `MetricRegistrySnapshot`. Reject
    `MetricSource::PerSliceReserved` with
    `OBSERVATION-METRIC-SOURCE-RESERVED-V1`.
11. **MetricSelection** — same floor/demotion rules as probes; Histogram
    bucket_count > 0.
12. **PerClassWeightCap** — enforce
    `F-B6-ObservationBudgetCapTotal`:
    `sum_over_probes(weight | class==c) + sum_over_metrics(weight |
    class==c) <= profile_observation_caps[c]`. Required class is uncapped
    (`required_max: None`).

## Why
The 45-patch review's Patch 5 (Registry templates), Patch 7 (Metrics
count against caps), and the 30-patch Patch 5 (metric weight) shape this
pass. Required-probe-disable rejection (30-patch Patch 6) closes the only
way `disabled_optional_probes` could break the Required guarantee.

## Subtasks
- [ ] Implement `probe_instance_source_fingerprint` as
      `DomainHash("gbf-codegen", "ProbeInstanceSource",
      "operational_probe_schema.v1", CanonicalJson({probe_id, source}))`.
- [ ] Disabled-required probe pre-check (fail before instantiation).
- [ ] Probe budget cap = probes + metrics combined.
- [ ] Reject zero-bucket histograms.
- [ ] Reserved-effect probe diagnostic precedence
      (`SequenceState { .. }` → SEQUENCE-STATE-PROBE-RESERVED,
      `FaultBoundary` → FAULT-BOUNDARY-PROBE-RESERVED, otherwise
      RESERVED-EFFECT-PROBE).

## Acceptance
- [ ] All four importance classes (Required, Important, Diagnostic,
      BestEffort) have at least one fixture probe and one fixture metric.
- [ ] Cap math hits the failure mode under each class.
- [ ] OP-SC-2a confirmed: two instances with same TraceProbeId allowed iff
      ProbeInstanceId differs.

## How this serves the project
This pass enforces the build-active observation surface contract that
gbf-debug, gbf-bench, and gbf-runtime trace all rely on. Without correct
governance the same build emits a different probe set on different runs.

## RFC anchors
§8.3 classes 7-12, §8.7 OP-SC-2/2a, OP-SC-5..7, §2.4 (effect probe v1 set),
§2.7 (probe budget governance).

## History
- 45-patch Patch 4: ProbeInstanceId + source fingerprint
- 45-patch Patch 5: registry templates instead of concrete entities
- 45-patch Patch 7: metrics count against caps
- 30-patch Patch 5: weight on MetricProbe
- 30-patch Patch 6: required-probe-disable rejection
- 41-patch Patch 36: Histogram bucket_count > 0

## Blocked by
T-B6.E (probe/metric types), T-B6.B (registry snapshots).

## Audit amendment — landed-code reconciliation (2026-05-14)

### ProbeImportanceClass replaces ProbeBudgetClass in policy paths
Per RFC §20.4 + T-B6.A, all policy-side governance uses the new
`gbf-policy::probe::ProbeImportanceClass` (Required/Important/
Diagnostic/BestEffort). Update tests + telemetry accordingly:

- Tracing event fields: `importance_class:
  "required"|"important"|"diagnostic"|"best_effort"`
- Cap accounting: `profile_observation_caps[ImportanceClass]`

### Probe carries both `level` (ABI) and `importance` (policy)
Each `OperationalProbe` has two orthogonal classifications:
- `level: gbf_abi::trace::ProbeLevel { Always, OnError, Verbose }`
  (runtime semantic — when does it fire)
- `importance: gbf_policy::probe::ProbeImportanceClass`
  (build-time governance — how is it budgeted)

Tests must exercise both axes.

### `TraceProbeId` conversion at the trace-install boundary
`OperationalProbe.probe_id: gbf_policy::diagnostics::TraceProbeId`
(build-time selection) converts to `gbf_abi::trace::TraceProbeId`
(runtime trace event) via the From impl introduced by T-B6.A.

### Frequency bound + max payload bound vs the ABI 16-byte slot
Each `TraceEventShape.max_payload_bytes` must be `<= 16` (per
`gbf-abi::trace::TraceEvent.data: [u8; 16]`). Add an invariant test:

- `trace_event_shape_payload_bytes_within_abi_slot`

### Acceptance addition
- [ ] All probe tests verify `importance` and `level` independently
- [ ] `TraceProbeId` From impls round-trip in tests
- [ ] `max_payload_bytes <= 16` enforced at type construction

title: F-S2.02: Runtime BuildKind dispatch + QuantHardnessOverride + TrainConfigS2 + train_config_hash + RNG streams
description:
Goal
====
Implement runtime S2BuildKind dispatch + QuantHardnessOverride::AllOff so
s2_ternary_full / s2_fp_full / s2_ternary_nodistill share one compiled
binary. Implement TrainConfigS2Full + TrainConfigS2PhaseAOnly +
train_config_hash + PhaseAEffectiveConfigHash. Declare ThresholdInitRng as
a disjoint RNG stream alongside InitRng/BatchRng/ShuffleRng. Per F-S2 RFC
§3 + §5 + §10 Rep-S2-4 + §16.6.

Why this matters
================
- The matched-protocol comparator hinges on s2_ternary and s2_fp running
  the SAME compiled code with only runtime config differing. A compile-
  time qat-fp-only feature would break that property (AS2-9).
- Reproducibility (Rep-S2-1) requires that EVERY field that perturbs
  training is hashed. Rep-S2-4 binds D1+D3+D5+D10+D13 plus the loss-unit
  choice from §1.
- The TrainConfigS2 split (Full vs PhaseAOnly) avoids ablation-vs-full
  ambiguity in I-S2-5: H4 needs the Phase-A-effective hash, not the full
  A→D plan.
- ThresholdInitRng is declared even though v1 consumes 0 draws so a
  future randomized init does not silently expand the RNG domain set
  (Rep-S2-9, AS2-22).

Scope
=====
Runtime BuildKind dispatch (gbf-experiments::s2::run + gbf-model::qat):
- enum QuantHardnessOverride { None, AllOff }
- Phase scheduler consults override before computing effective HardnessTriple.
- BuildKind → override mapping at s2_train_run entry:
    s2_ternary_full       → None
    s2_fp_full            → AllOff
    s2_ternary_nodistill  → None
    s2_ablation           → N/A (separate binary via qat-ablation feature)
- BuildKind → loss-config override (lambda_distill_default = 0.0 for
  nodistill; raw distill still computed per RFC §S2-Run-Ok-7 + DL-2).

TrainConfigS2 (gbf-experiments::s2::schema):
  struct TrainConfigS2Full {
    optimizer_steps:        10000      // S1 inheritance
    batch_size:             32; sequence_length: 128;
    eval_every_steps:       1000; eval_subset_size: 4096;
    optimizer:              AdamW { lr=1e-3, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999,
                                     eps=1e-8, weight_decay=0.0 };
    phase_plan: [PhaseA(1..=4000), PhaseB(4001..=5000),
                 PhaseC(5001..=8000), PhaseD(8001..=10000)];
    hardness_ramp:           PhaseCRampD2 + PhaseDRampD2;
    distill_temp:            2.0;
    lambda_distill_default:  1.0;
    lambda_range:            0.01;     // hardened, no [ESTIMATE]
    lambda_zero:             0.0001;   // hardened, no [ESTIMATE]
    range_safe_lo:          -1.0;
    range_safe_hi:           1.0;
    threshold_init_multiplier: 0.7;
    teacher_freeze_step:     4000;
    rng_kind:                Pcg64Mcg;
    device_profile:          S1CpuDeterministic;
    training_loss_unit:      Nats;     // explicit unit pin
  }
  struct TrainConfigS2PhaseAOnly { optimizer_steps = 4000; phase_plan =
    [PhaseA only]; same other fields. }
  fn train_config_hash(cfg, build_kind) -> Hash256 (domain separator
    's2_train_config.v1/<build_kind>') — covers Rep-S2-4 full field set.
  fn phase_a_effective_config_hash(cfg) -> Hash256 — Phase A fields only,
    used ONLY by H4 ablation comparator.

RNG streams (gbf-experiments::s2::rng):
- ThresholdInitRng(seed) = Pcg64Mcg(seed128('threshold_init', seed))
- Disjointness audit asserts no collision among {init, batch, shuffle,
  threshold_init, linearstate_smoke/*} seed128 domains.

Logging contract
================
At config construction:
  tracing::info!(event="train_config_built", build_kind=<S2BuildKind>,
    train_config_hash=<hex>, phase_a_effective_hash=<hex>,
    training_loss_unit="nats")
At dispatch time (per s2_train_run entry):
  tracing::info!(event="buildkind_dispatch", build_kind=<S2BuildKind>,
    quant_hardness_override=<None|AllOff>,
    lambda_distill_default=<f32>)
At RNG stream initialization (per stream):
  tracing::debug!(event="rng_stream_init",
    domain="<init|batch|shuffle|threshold_init>",
    seed=<u64>, seed128=<hex>)
On disjointness audit:
  tracing::debug!(event="rng_disjointness_audit_pass",
    domains=<list>, collision_count=0)
  WARN if a collision is ever observed (a SHOULD-be-zero condition).

Unit tests
==========
- File: gbf-experiments/tests/buildkind_dispatch_s2.rs
  Scenarios:
    * Same seed + same model + ternary_full → HardnessTriple ramps per D2.
    * Same seed + same model + fp_full → HardnessTriple = (Off,Off,Off)
      at every step (verified by PL-4 in F-S2.06).
    * Same seed + same model + nodistill → lambda_distill_effective = 0.0
      every step BUT distill_loss_raw is still computed and recorded.
    * Compile-only assertion: gbf-train dep for s2-ablation feature path
      uses default-features = false (trybuild + dependency walk).

- File: gbf-experiments/tests/train_config_hash_s2.rs
  Scenarios:
    * train_config_hash is deterministic across replays.
    * Changing ANY of the Rep-S2-4 fields changes the hash (table-driven

title: F-S7 v0.2: §6.2 dense solver fairness + O11 standalone CI test
description:
## Description

Two-part task: (1) §6.2 D-Ok-1 dense solver fairness — old solver picked the *smallest* d_ff_dense within tolerance, biasing toward MoE; v0.2 minimizes `abs(B_deployed_total(Dense[d_ff]) - B_deployed_total(MoE))` with explicit tie-breaks. (2) O11 standalone CI test — verifies the pinned d_ff_dense matches the formula end-to-end, including bias bytes, without requiring any training artifact.

## Design

Solver:
- §6.2 D-Ok-1 selects `d_ff_dense = argmin_{d_ff} |B_deployed_total(Dense[d_ff]) - B_deployed_total(MoE)|`, subject to D6 tolerance.
- Tie-break order: prefer Dense ≥ MoE; if still tied, smaller d_ff.
- D-Ok-2 tolerance check uses `B_deployed_total`, not `B_experts_total`.

CI test (O11):
- `gbf-experiments/tests/matched_bytes_formula.rs` reads matched_bytes.json, recomputes every byte total from the canonical formula, asserts equality within tolerance.
- Verifies `b_deployed_total_moe = B_experts_total + B_router_overhead_total + B_common_total`.
- Verifies `b_deployed_total_dense = B_common_total + B_dense_ffn_total`.
- Asserts `|moe - dense| <= tolerance_bytes`.
- Fails CI if `bias_policy = "<PIN_ME>"` still appears at first-result commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- §6.2 D-Ok-1 prose: "the d_ff that minimizes abs(B_deployed_total(Dense[d_ff]) - B_deployed_total(MoE))."
- Tie-break documented (Dense ≥ MoE; then smaller d_ff).
- `gbf-experiments/tests/matched_bytes_formula.rs` validates all byte totals end-to-end.
- Test runs WITHOUT training artifacts (O11 standalone contract).
- Crafted-candidate test validates the tie-break order with two d_ff values straddling the MoE byte count.

## Notes

- The "Dense ≥ MoE" tie-break is conservative — it gives the dense baseline a slight byte budget edge on ties, making the parity claim harder to win.
- Depends on bd-3ex4: solver and CI test consume `B_deployed_total` and the MatchedBytesPin fields.

title: State machine: single FrontierEmitted; rename PickFrontierEmitted->PickFrontierInputsFrozen
description:
# Goal

Collapse PickFrontierEmitted and FitFrontierEmitted into a single FrontierEmitted state that owns the one final s5_frontier.v1 artifact. Rename the pre-Fit state to PickFrontierInputsFrozen to make clear that Pick-side inputs are locked but no frontier has been written yet. Clarify the seed-0 emulator harness as a one-shot inside the seed loop.

# Background / Why

§13.7 specifies a single combined s5_frontier.v1, and H7 says exactly one frontier instance is emitted per PR. The original state machine had:

  PickFrontierEmitted    (binds H7 + Pick side of H5/H8/H10)
  ...Fit per-seed loop...
  FitHarnessRun(0)
  FitFrontierEmitted

Two emit-states produce two artifacts (or one is overwritten), violating H7 and creating replay ambiguity. The seed-0 harness was tangled into the seed loop as \"repeat per seed 1..4 for cadence + export; seed-0 also runs FitHarnessRun\", which is hard to read and easy to implement wrong.

# Change

In gbf-experiments::s5 state machine + gbf-policy state-to-hypothesis traceability:

  - States:
      PickFrontierInputsFrozen   (was PickFrontierEmitted; binds H7 inputs)
      FitPreflightDone(seed), ..., FitEncodedRomEmitted(seed)
      FitHarnessRun(seed=0)
      FrontierEmitted            (single state writing s5_frontier.v1)
  - Per-seed loop body: FitPreflight -> FitShadowReal cadence -> FitFeedback -> FitExport -> FitRevalidation -> FitEncodedRom for seeds 0..4.
  - Emulator harness is seed-0 only and runs exactly once after seed 0's pipeline.
  - Transition table updated; documentation rewritten for clarity.

# Why this matters

A single FrontierEmitted state cleans up:
  - Artifact uniqueness (H7).
  - Replay chain hash binding (one frontier_self_hash, one artifact write).
  - Reader comprehension (seed loop is a flat loop, harness is a clear one-shot).

# Considerations

  - Existing consumers must not pattern-match on \`FitFrontierEmitted\`; grep for the old name and remove or rename references.
  - Hypothesis traceability: H7 binds to PickFrontierInputsFrozen for input freezing AND to FrontierEmitted for emission; document both.
  - Re-validation and EncodedRom bindings remain per-seed; only the final frontier write is the single shared event.

# Verification

  - State machine enumeration test: exactly one FrontierEmitted transition per run.
  - End-to-end run emits exactly one s5_frontier.v1 file.
  - Replay determinism: identical hash chain across two runs of the same seed set.

# Related RFC sections

  §5 state machine, §13.7 s5_frontier.v1, H7.

# Depends on

  B09 (pick_points / fit_points shape -- determines what the single FrontierEmitted writes).
close_reason: Completed: single FrontierEmitted state, PickFrontierInputsFrozen rename, seed-0 harness ordering, logging handoff, and rehearsal-order fix landed; Gemini and Claude ACPX reviews passed.
